title: Larry Fitzgerald refuses to call himself "retired"
summary: Larry Fitzgerald will be inducted into the Pro Football Hall of Fame today, and he'll turn 43 years old this month.
full_text: ''' Larry Fitzgerald will be inducted into the Pro Football Hall of Fame today, and he'll turn 43 years old this month. It seems safe to say he's done playing professional football. But don't call Fitzgerald "retired." Fitzgerald told the Cardinals' website that he never plans to use that word to describe where he is in life. " I have not committed to retirement ," Fitzgerald said. Fitzgerald recalls hearing his grandfather talk with friends about how when people retire, they give up. And giving up is not something Fitzgerald ever wants to do. "They'd talk about retirement killing more people in our country than anything," Fitzgerald said. "It always stuck with me. I just don't believe in retirement. I just think you transition into different phases, especially as an athlete. I was done at 38. Retire? There is no retirement in sight. I protest the word more than the actual thing. So I just won't acknowledge that." When Fitzgerald confirmed after his 17th season with the Cardinals that he wouldn't be back for an 18th, he studiously avoided the word "retirement." It's still not a word he'll use. Fitzgerald knows he has a lot more to do with his life.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Matt LaFleur bans backflips after Christian Watson and MarShawn Lloyd celebrations
summary: The Packers' head coach said he doesn't want to see any more backflips after two oft-injured players did them.
full_text: When Giants running back Cam Skattebo did a backflip while recovering from an injury, coach John Harbaugh joked that he should have stuck the landing . When a couple of oft-injured Packers players did backflips, coach Matt LaFleur took a harder line. Packers running back MarShawn Lloyd and wide receiver Christian Watson, both of whom have been injury-prone, both did backflip celebrations, and LaFleur told them to knock it off. Lloyd said after a training camp practice that LaFleur told him to stop. "I've always been able to do it," Lloyd told reporters. "Coach LaFleur doesn't want me to do it no more. . . . He said it was cool, but he said, 'Let's not do that.'" Lloyd said LaFleur told Watson to stop the backflips, too. "He told him the same thing: Stop doing them," Lloyd said. Lloyd said he was trying to bring some energy to the running back group, which hadn't been celebrating the way the receivers were. "The running backs weren't doing any celebrations when we were scoring," Lloyd said. "The whole offense wasn't liking that. The receivers came into the running back room, and said you guys need to start celebrating more. So that was the first thing that came to my mind. I can't dance. I don't know how to do the dance they're doing. But I know how to do a backflip." In two years since the Packers selected him in the third round of the 2024 NFL draft, Lloyd has been plagued with injuries and played in only one game. Lloyd understands that LaFleur wants him to stay healthy, and accepts that the no backflips rule is a part of that. "I've been doing them for a long time, but it's fine," Lloyd said. "If he said it's over, it's over."
author: Michael David Smith

title: Josh Allen still feels guilty about Sean McDermott's firing
summary: The last of 10 head-coaching vacancies in the 2026 cycle arose when the Bills surprisingly fired Sean McDermott after a divisional-round overtime loss to the Broncos.
full_text: The last of 10 head-coaching vacancies in the 2026 cycle arose when the Bills surprisingly fired Sean McDermott after a divisional-round overtime loss to the Broncos. Quarterback Josh Allen, who was heavily involved in the search for McDermott's successor, still feels guilty about McDermott's demise, seven months later. “ I think about that all the time ," Allen told Mike Silver of The Athletic . "There are certain plays throughout the game — and that’s going to be every game — where you’re like, ‘I could have done more.’ And I always feel like I can do more." Allen had four turnovers in the 33-30 loss at Denver. If the Bills had returned to the AFC Championship and won, McDermott would still be there. Even if the Bills had lost in the AFC title game, advancing to the final four likely would have been enough to keep it from being McDermott's final season. The end result — a pink slip for McDermott and promotions for G.M. Brandon Beane and offensive coordinator Joe Brady — sends mixed signals to the Bills Mafia. And it puts even more pressure on Allen and the rest of the organization to finish the job of getting back to the Super Bowl for the first time since 1993, and winning it for the first time ever.
author: Mike Florio

title: Mark Wilf: Our family intends to be part of the Vikings for a "very, very long time"
summary: The Wilfs have owned the Vikings for 21 years.
full_text: The Wilfs have owned the Vikings for 21 years. They don't plan to end their tenure any time soon. Earlier this year, local speculation emerged that the Wilfs could sell based on a massive drop in spending from 2025 to 2026. The team quickly got the word out that it’s not, and won’t be, for sale . "The business side of it is not what got us into the Minnesota Vikings," co-owner Mark Wilf told reporters on Thursday. "We love football. We're honored and privileged to be stewards of an incredible franchise, and our ultimate goal is to bring championships to the fans of the Minnesota Vikings, who really deserve it. And that's what we're about, and that's the excitement, and we're long term, we're a family that is going to hopefully be part of the Minnesota Vikings for a very, very long time." Wilf also said that the Vikings "aren't focused on" the possibility of selling a piece of the team to any of the approved private-equity funds. The Wilfs have successfully built a new stadium, one that has hosted a Super Bowl. By all indications, the Vikings continue to make plenty of money, each and every year. The on-field success has been limited, to say the least. Since the Wilfs bought the team from the late Red McCombs in 2005, the Vikings have won only three playoff games: one in 2009, one in 2017, and one in 2019. The Vikings have made it to the playoffs only eight times in the 21 seasons that the Wilfs have owned the team, with back-to-back playoff years only once (2008 and 2009). "Ultimately, it's about not just playoff wins, but championships," Wilf said. "And that is the ultimate measure. We know that. We try to be patient as an ownership, and that's what our — that we know is the ultimate success. But, of course, patience isn't infinite. We understand that, but I feel really good about the direction of this football club, and we're going to get those benchmarks checked off here." The biggest benchmark — winning a Super Bowl — has never been checked off by the Vikings. Since the team's last Super Bowl appearance 50 years ago, the Vikings have gone 0-6 in the NFC Championship. While the Wilfs aren't cheap, talk is. Yes, Mark Wilf said the right things on Thursday. It all comes down to whether the organization can find a way to consistently contend, and whether it can ever get back to a Super Bowl and finally win one. For most Vikings fans who lived (and died) with a team that did very well, but not well enough, in the 1970s, the dream has been to witness the confetti fall of purple helmets just once in their lifetimes. For those who are still alive, the realization has begun to creep in that it's not going to happen before they're blowing the great Gjallarhorn in the sky.
author: Mike Florio

title: Broncos DL Matt Henningsen tears Achilles
summary: Broncos defensive lineman Matt Henningsen, who was carted off at Friday's practice, was diagnosed with a torn Achilles, Mike Klis of 9News reports.
full_text: Broncos defensive lineman Matt Henningsen, who was carted off at Friday's practice, was diagnosed with a torn Achilles , Mike Klis of 9News reports. Henningsen's injury came exactly one year to the day when he tore his other Achilles in a joint practice against the 49ers. It means Henningsen will miss a second consecutive season. The Broncos selected Henningsen in the sixth round of the 2022 draft, and he played in every game in his first two seasons. He spent all of 2024 on the team's practice squad and then was on injured reserve all of last season. The Broncos also saw wide receiver Marvin Mims go down, but Klis reports that the Broncos are hopeful that Mims' injury is not serious. Tight end Nate Adkins also left practice early.
author: Charean Williams

title: John Harbaugh on Cam Skattebo leaving practice: Just working through the football shape part of it
summary: Running back Cam Skattebo made an early exit from Friday's practice, but Giants head coach John Harbaugh didn't show much concern about his condition after the workout.
full_text: Running back Cam Skattebo made an early exit from Friday's practice, but Giants head coach John Harbaugh didn't show much concern about his condition after the workout. Skattebo left practice after a collision with rookie linebacker Arvell Reese and reporters at the session said he remained on the sideline stretching out his left leg. Skattebo's rookie season ended when he dislocated his right ankle and Friday's issue doesn't appear to be in the same ballpark. "It's natural. I think he's working through the football shape part of it," Harbaugh said at a press conference. "You know, he's coming off of rehab, so that's what that was. It won't be a serious injury at all." Center John Michael Schmitz and defensive end Brian Burns also left practice. Harbaugh said Schmitz got his bell rung and will be evaluated while Burns is managing a minor ankle injury.
author: Josh Alper

title: Jahmyr Gibbs: The contract process was extremely stressful
summary: There was reason to believe that Lions running back Jahmyr Gibbs was close to signing a contract extension on Thursday morning when he suited up for practice for the first time at training camp and those thoughts became a reality when news of an agreement broke later in the day.
full_text: There was reason to believe that Lions running back Jahmyr Gibbs was close to signing a contract extension on Thursday morning when he suited up for practice for the first time at training camp and those thoughts became a reality when news of an agreement broke later in the day. Gibbs remained limited to individual work at Friday's practice, but made it clear that even a limited workload was better than how it felt sitting on the side to watch his teammates go through the first week of camp without him. "This process has been extremely stressful ," Gibbs said, via the team's website. "I just wanted to play ball. I missed being out there with my teammates and my coaches and it's just fun being out there now with my pads. It feels a lot better." The Lions will likely continue to ramp Gibbs up with caution to make sure that there's no more missed time in the future because, as his three-year, $67.5 million deal makes clear, they have a lot riding on him.
author: Josh Alper

title: Report: Giants agree to terms with C Brenden Jaimes
summary: The Giants are signing free agent center Brenden Jaimes, Dan Duggan of TheAthletic.com reports.
full_text: The Giants are signing free agent center Brenden Jaimes, Dan Duggan of TheAthletic.com reports. The team needed help at the position with John Michael Schmitz likely headed to concussion protocol and backup center Lucas Patrick hobbling during Friday's practice. Jaimes, 27, worked out for the Giants earlier this week. He has appeared in 50 games over five seasons, mostly with the Chargers. Jaimes was with the Patriots last season and played 22 offensive snaps and 28 on special teams in four games.
author: Charean Williams

title: DeMarcus Lawrence returns for 13th season after considering retirement
summary: Seahawks defensive end DeMarcus Lawrence capped his 12th NFL season with his first Super Bowl ring.
full_text: '' Seahawks defensive end DeMarcus Lawrence capped his 12th NFL season with his first Super Bowl ring. He considered calling it quits after that. Only when Lawrence's wife told him "it was OK" did he decide to return for a 13th season. "I kind of had my mind made up that if I won, I was done," Lawrence said, via Brady Henderson of ESPN. "But I kind of had a bittersweet feeling in my heart, understanding that with the type of team that we had, we should have been where we were last year. This is where the hard part begins, staying on top." Lawrence, 34, also considered retiring in the 2025 offseason after his 11-year run with the Cowboys ended. He instead signed with the Seahawks as a free agent. Now, he returns to help the Seahawks attempt a repeat. "They say it's no fun when the rabbit has the gun," Lawrence said. "We're the ones with the dot on our backs. I just want to see how that feels, see the different obstacles that we can overcome. Are we going to stay together in those tough moments throughout a season? And just be a part of this brotherhood."
author: Charean Williams

title: Dolphins sign S Tanner Wall, claim CB Ahmari Harvey off waivers
summary: The Dolphins doubled down on defensive back moves on Friday.
full_text: The Dolphins doubled down on defensive back moves on Friday. They announced that they have signed Tanner Wall to the active roster and they also claimed cornerback Ahmari Harvey off of waivers. Harvey was with the Steelers prior to being cut on Thursday. Wall was undrafted out of BYU this year and signed by the Raiders. He remained with Vegas until he was cut loose earlier this week. Harvey also entered the league as an undrafted free agent this spring. He signed with the Broncos and spent a little over a month in Denver before moving on to the Steelers. The Dolphins waived quarterback Mark Gronowski and safety Omar Brown to open spots for the new members of the team.
author: Josh Alper

title: Bears sign DB Xavier Woods, place DB Dallis Flowers on IR
summary: The Bears signed defensive back Xavier Woods, the team announced Friday.
full_text: ' The Bears signed defensive back Xavier Woods, the team announced Friday. In a corresponding move, the Bears placed defensive back Dallis Flowers on injured reserve. Flowers needed help getting off the field during Thursday's practice after injuring his right leg. He appeared in one game for the Bears last season. Woods, 31, spent last season with the Titans. He played 526 defensive snaps in 11 games, 10 of those starts, and totaled 39 tackles, two interceptions and three passes defensed. The Cowboys selected Woods in the sixth round in 2017, and he spent four seasons in Dallas. Woods also played for the Vikings and Panthers before landing in Tennessee last season.
author: Charean Williams

title: Browns claim DT Patrick Jenkins off of waivers
summary: The Browns plucked a defensive lineman off of the waiver wire on Friday.
full_text: The Browns plucked a defensive lineman off of the waiver wire on Friday. They announced the addition of defensive tackle Patrick Jenkins to the roster. They had opened up a roster spot earlier in the day by placing offensive lineman Kendrick Green on injured reserve. Jenkins was let go by the Jets on Thursday and he was in training camp with the Cardinals last summer. He also spent some time on the Falcons' practice squad late in the regular season. Jenkins played for Columbus in the UFL this spring. He had 22 tackles, six tackles for loss and 1.5 sacks in 10 games.
author: Josh Alper

title: Patriots sign S Eric Butler
summary: The Patriots have made a pair of roster moves on Friday.
full_text: '' The Patriots have made a pair of roster moves on Friday. New England announced the team has signed safety Eric Butler. Butler, 23, is an undrafted rookie out of San Diego State. He previously worked out for the Patriots in late July. As a corresponding move, the Patriots have waived rookie defensive tackle David Blay Jr.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Cowboys sign RB Jashaun Corbin
summary: The Cowboys made a change in their running back room on Friday.
full_text: ' The Cowboys made a change in their running back room on Friday. They announced that they have signed Jashaun Corbin to the 90-man roster. Dominic Richardson was waived in a corresponding move. Corbin most recently played for Orlando in the UFL. He ran 131 times for 466 yards and three touchdowns during the 2026 regular season. He also caught 21 passes for 118 yards. Corbin played in six games for the Giants in 2023 and ran for one yard. He also caught three passes for 12 yards. Corbin has also spent time with the Panthers, Falcons and Patriots. Richardson was undrafted out of Tulsa this year.
author: Josh Alper

title: Boye Mafe on Cashius Howell: He's gonna be a dog in this league
summary: Bengals rookie defensive end Cashius Howell has spent most of training camp playing with the second team behind Myles Murphy and Boye Mafe.
full_text: '' Bengals rookie defensive end Cashius Howell has spent most of training camp playing with the second team behind Myles Murphy and Boye Mafe. But he earned a promotion Thursday, getting more first-team snaps. According to Jay Morrison of SI.com, Howell twice beat starting left tackle Orlando Brown Jr. “I’ve had a few [first-team] reps here and there, but today was the first real day that I’ve gotten good, solid, quality reps,” Howell said. “It gives me a little bit of confidence . But regardless of who lines up in front of me, I want to make sure I’m coming out and bringing the same competitive performance, the same energy.” Howell went 41st overall despite being the SEC's Defensive Player of the Year in 2025 with 11.5 sacks. His 30 1/4-inch arm measurement — the shortest of any edge rusher since at least 1999 — was the reason. The Texas A&M product has had no problem getting separation in camp. “It’s very hard to do what he’s doing so early,” Mafe said. “It’s been exciting to see. I’ve been saying he’s going to be a great player. I’ve always known that. He has it in him. It’s just a matter of getting comfortable. “Once he does, he's gonna be a dog in this league, and I can’t wait to see it.”
author: Charean Williams

title: Ravens to sign LB Jamon Johnson
summary: The Ravens will close out the week by adding a linebacker.
full_text: The Ravens will close out the week by adding a linebacker. Jeff Zrebiec of TheAthletic.com reports that they are going to sign Jamon Johnson to their active roster. Johnson tried out for the team on Thursday. Johnson signed with the Packers after going undrafted last year. He had 10 tackles and a pass defensed in two appearances. The Packers released Johnson during their offseason program. Ravens linebacker Teddye Buccanan remains on the physically unable to perform list and Zrebiec notes that Carl Jones has also missed practice time recently, so the Ravens were in need of a healthy body at linebacker as they head toward their first preseason game.
author: Josh Alper

title: Inside the Zay Flowers deal
summary: Earlier this week, the Ravens and receiver Zay Flowers agreed to terms on a new deal that, by way of new money, put him in the Justin Jefferson tax bracket at $35 million annually.
full_text: Earlier this week, the Ravens and receiver Zay Flowers agreed to terms on a new deal that, by way of new money, put him in the Justin Jefferson tax bracket at $35 million annually. The full details of the Flowers contract are now available. Here they are, per a source with knowledge of the terms: 1. Signing bonus: $24.855 million, $18.855 million of which will be paid within 10 days, and the remaining $6 million of which will be paid by October 31, 2026. 2. 2026 base salary: $1.145 million, fully guaranteed. 3. 2027 option bonus: $26.74 million, fully guaranteed; $20 million will be paid my March 31, 2027, and the remaining $6.74 million will be paid by October 31, 2027. 4. 2027 base salary: $1.26 million, fully guaranteed. 5. 2028 base salary: $26.5 million, guaranteed for injury and fully guaranteed in March 2027. 6. 2029 base salary: $27.5 million, guaranteed for injury and fully guaranteed in March 2028. 10. 2030 offseason roster bonus: $2 million. 11. 2030 base salary: $28 million. 12. 2031 offseason roster bonus: $2 million. 13. 2031 base salary: $29.962 million. The four-year extension has a new-money average of $35 million. Factoring in the existing money owed in 2026 and 2027, the full six-year deal has an average value of $28.327 million at signing. The deal includes $54 million fully guaranteed at signing, $80.5 million fully guaranteed by March 2027, and $108 million fully guaranteed by March 2028.
author: Mike Florio

title: Colts CB Cam Taylor-Britt suspended one game
summary: The Colts won't be able to put cornerback Cam Taylor-Britt in the lineup for their season opener against the Ravens.
full_text: The Colts won't be able to put cornerback Cam Taylor-Britt in the lineup for their season opener against the Ravens. The NFL announced on Friday that Taylor-Britt has been suspended one game. The suspension is for violating the league's Personal Conduct Policy. Taylor-Britt pleaded guilty to reckless driving and driving without a valid license in January to resolve charges from a pair of 2025 traffic stops. He was sentenced to five days in jail as a result. Both of those traffic stops took place while Taylor-Britt was playing for the Bengals. He signed with the Colts as a free agent this offseason. Taylor-Britt will not be with the team for the first week of the regular season, but can practice this summer and play in the team's preseason games.
author: Josh Alper

title: Nick Sirianni on Makai Lemon: Working like crazy to get him healthy
summary: Eagles rookie wide receiver Makai Lemon was out of practice on Tuesday due to a hamstring injury and he has missed the rest of the week's work as well.
full_text: ''' Eagles rookie wide receiver Makai Lemon was out of practice on Tuesday due to a hamstring injury and he has missed the rest of the week's work as well. Lemon also dealt with a hamstring injury this spring and head coach Nick Sirianni was asked at a Friday press conference whether he was recalibrating early expectations for the first-round pick because of the missed time. Sirianni said the only thing the team is concerned with right now is getting Lemon healthy enough to play. "It's just, right now, how do we get him healthy? How do we get him as healthy as we can and get him back rolling? He's doing the things in the meeting rooms," Sirianni said, via a transcript from the team. "He's watching the walkthrough portions of it and being diligent there. This isn't new. This happens, right? You've got guys that are out for some time, or an extended period of time, or a short period of time, and they've got to make sure that they're doing the right things. Us as coaches, getting that extra meeting time with them as well when they miss some of the time on the field. Excited about him, and we'll continue to work like crazy to get him back." DeVonta Smith has also been out with a hamstring issue this week. His experience means there's less reason to be concerned about how ready he'll be for the Commanders on September 13, but the Eagles will be better off when both wideouts are able to do more than observe during practices.
author: Josh Alper

title: Inside the Jahmyr Gibbs deal
summary: The Gibbs deal is virtually identical in structure to the Bijan Robinson deal.
full_text: A week of bank-breaking running back contracts was capped by Lions running back Jahmyr Gibbs breaking the bank by the biggest margin. Gibbs, now the highest-paid running back in the league, signed his new contract on Friday. Here are the full and complete details, per a source with knowledge of the terms: 1. Signing bonus: $15 million. 2. 2026 90-man roster bonus: $2.038 million, fully guaranteed. 3. 2026 base salary: $1.145 million, fully guaranteed. 4. 2027 option bonus: $10.033 million, fully guaranteed. 5. 2027 base salary: $1.26 million, fully guaranteed. 6. 2028 offseason workout bonus: $250,000, fully guaranteed but must be earned. 7. 2028 base salary: $10.25 million, fully guaranteed. (The full 2028 compensation package is guaranteed for injury at signing. Of that amount, $8.25 million is fully guaranteed. The remaining $2.25 million becomes fully guaranteed in March 2027.) 8. 2029 offseason workout bonus: $250,000. 9. 2029 base salary: $22.25 million, $11.5 million of which is guaranteed for injury at signing. Of that amount, $8 million becomes fully guaranteed in March 2028. The remaining $3.5 million becomes fully guaranteed in March 2029. 10. 2030 offseason roster bonus: $1 million. 11. 2030 offseason workout bonus: $250,000. 12. 2030 base salary: $21.25 million. The contract also includes $4.125 million in available escalators for 2029 and 2030 each. For 2029, Gibbs gets $562,500 for each year from 2026 through 2028 in which he generates 800 or more receiving yards. He gets another $562,500 for each year in which he generates 800 or more receiving yards and the team gets to the divisional round of the postseason. For 2030, Gibbs gets $421,875 for each year from 2026 through 2029 in which he generates 800 or more receiving yards. He gets another $421,875 for each year in which he generates 800 or more receiving yards and the team gets to the divisional round of the postseason. Gibbs also gets $750,000 in each year for winning the MVP award a single time. If the escalator package sounds familiar, it should. It’s identical to the Bijan Robinson incentive package. In fact, the overall structure of the two deals is virtually identical. It appears that the Lions and/or Gibbs took the Bijan deal and used it as the template for the Gibbs deal, with more total money for Gibbs. The biggest difference is the amount. The Robinson new-money APY is $22.25 million, and the maximum value is $25 million. For Gibbs, the new-money APY is $22.5 million, with a maximum value of $25.25. From signing, the Gibbs deal has a five-year average of $16.995 million. Robinson's deal has a five-year average of $16.36 million. That may not seem like much, but it works out to a difference of more than $3 million.
author: Mike Florio

title: Peter Skoronski signs four-year extension with Titans
summary: The Titans have made a significant commitment to one of their key offensive players.
full_text: The Titans have made a significant commitment to one of their key offensive players. Guard Peter Skoronski has signed a contract extension, the team announced on Friday. Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports the deal is for four years and $100 million, with $88 million guaranteed, which makes him the league's highest-paid guard. "We couldn't be happier to keep Peter in Nashville. The goal will always be to retain people and players who are cornerstones of our organization, and Peter is certainly that for us ," General Manager Mike Borgonzi said in a statement from the team. "He has the work ethic to match his talent and a perpetual desire to win that we want permeating throughout our building. We're excited to enter the season knowing he and his family will remain Titans for years to come.” "This is a tremendous blessing. It's a reflection of the work, sacrifice and support that has helped me get to this point, and I don't take any of it for granted," Skoronski said in a statement released by the team. "Thank you to Ms. Amy [Adams Strunk], Mike Borgonzi and coach [Robert] Saleh for believing in me. From the moment I got here, this is where I wanted to be. I love this organization, I love this city, and I'm grateful for the opportunity to continue representing this franchise. I appreciate the faith they've shown in me, and now it's my job to earn it every day. I'm excited for what's ahead, but more than anything, I'm ready to get back to work.” The No. 11 overall pick of the 2023 draft, Skoronski has started 48 games over the last three seasons, including all 17 in each of the last two. The Titans had picked up his fifth-year option in the spring, which put him in line to earn $19.072 million guaranteed in 2027.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Rams sign DE Daniel Rickert
summary: The Rams have added a defensive lineman.
full_text: The Rams have added a defensive lineman. No, not that one . Los Angeles announced the club has signed defensive end Daniel Rickert on Friday. Rickert enters the league as an undrafted free agent out of Virginia. He spent last season there after five with Tennessee Tech. In 14 games in 2025, he tallied 6.5 sacks. He totaled 25.5 sacks in his 57-game collegiate career.
author: Myles Simmons

title: A.J. Brown: Nothing but respect for Christian Gonzalez
summary: Wide receiver A.J.
full_text: Wide receiver A.J. Brown and cornerback Christian Gonzalez tussled at Patriots training camp on Thursday, but there was no reprise of the fireworks on Friday. Brown and Gonzalez were on the same team for the Patriots' intrasquad scrimmage, so the 1-on-1 drills that led to Thursday's explosion were off the table. Gonzalez said after Thursday's practice that he and Brown were "just battling and getting each other better," and Brown went similar places when he was asked about Gonzalez on Friday. “Every day’s a battle with him," Brown said. "It’s nothing but respect. Ultimately, it’s not about me and him. We’re out here competing. All of us are challenging each other. And, ultimately, for the greater of the team . It's nothing. Guys who are going back and forth, guys who are trying to play hard, and compete. That’s all." Brown and Gonzalez are both crucial to the Patriots' hopes in 2026, so everyone will likely be on board with anything that raises their ceilings as long as it stops short of a full-blown fight.
author: Josh Alper

title: Eric Bieniemy is watching Chiefs practice live streams as Mia Bieniemy continues to recover
summary: Chiefs offensive coordinator Eric Bieniemy is staying involved with the team while continuing to support his wife, Mia Bieniemy, as she recovers from a shooting.
full_text: ''' Chiefs offensive coordinator Eric Bieniemy is staying involved with the team while continuing to support his wife, Mia Bieniemy, as she recovers from a shooting. "Mia continues to improve," Chiefs head coach Andy Reid said today. "We're heading in the right direction and we'll just see when he gets back, he gets back here. He's champing at the bit and Mia is probably wanting to get him out of there too." Bieniemy is remaining involved with the team. According to the Kansas City Star , he is watching live streams of training camp practices and calling Reid when he sees something that needs to be addressed. Elijah Bieniemy, Eric and Mia's son, is accused of shooting his mother in the family home. He is charged with malicious wounding, use of a firearm in commission of a felony, and discharge of a firearm inside a dwelling. Elijah Bieniemy's attorney told a judge that Elijah “appears to suffer from significant mental health issues” and “does not appear able to assist in his own defense at the present time.”
author: Michael David Smith

title: Broncos DL Matt Henningsen carted off at Friday's practice
summary: Broncos defensive lineman Matt Henningsen had to be carted off the field during Friday's training camp practice.
full_text: Broncos defensive lineman Matt Henningsen had to be carted off the field during Friday's training camp practice. There's been no word from the team yet about the nature of his injury, but reports from media members at the team's facility painted a grim picture of the scene. Henningsen went down during a drill and players took a knee around him before he was helped to a cart by medical personnel. It's an all too familiar course of events for Henningsen. He tore his Achilles during a joint practice with the 49ers last August and missed the entire season. Henningsen was a 2022 sixth-round pick and he played in every game over his first two seasons. He had 40 tackles and a sack, but spent all of 2024 on the team's practice squad.
author: Josh Alper

title: Saints agree to sign LB Deion Jones
summary: Deion Jones is completing the cycle.
full_text: Deion Jones is completing the cycle. Jones has agreed to sign with the Saints, according to ESPN’s Adam Schefter, which means he will have played for all four teams in the NFC South. A second-round pick in 2016, Jones starts this career with the Falcons, playing six seasons for the club before heading to Cleveland in 2022. He then played for the Panthers in 2023 before spending the last two seasons with the Buccaneers. Jones is not only completing the NFC South cycle, but he’s also coming home. A New Orleans native, Jones also played his college ball at LSU. In his 128 career games with 91 starts, Jones has tallied 12.0 sacks, 50 tackles for loss, 24 QB hits, 13 interceptions, and 53 passes defensed.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Report: Commanders to sign OL Max Scharping
summary: The Commanders are adding a player to their offensive line.
full_text: The Commanders are adding a player to their offensive line. According to Matt Zenitz of CBS Sports, Washington is expected to sign Max Scharping. Scharping, 29, spent most of the last two seasons with the Steelers. But before that, he was on the Commanders’ practice squad for about a month. A second-round pick in 2019, Scharping has appeared in 81 games with 33 starts for Houston, Cincinnati, and Pittsburgh. He has also spent time with the Eagles.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Klint Kubiak on scuffle between Maxx Crosby and Kirk Cousins: "That's training camp"
summary: It sounds like the end of Friday’s Raiders practice brought out a little fire between Kirk Cousins and Maxx Crosby.
full_text: '' It sounds like the end of Friday’s Raiders practice brought out a little fire between Kirk Cousins and Maxx Crosby. Per Sam Warren of TheAthletic.com, Crosby tipped a pass from Cousins in the backfield during team drills. Cousins got in Crosby’s face with one grabbing the other’s collar before a shouting match ensued . Warren notes Cousins then performed well in a two-minute situation, which was a rebound for the QB who had thrown two interceptions during the session. Afterward, head coach Kilnt Kubiak didn’t seem concerned about two of the team’s most critical players mixing it up. “Yeah, that’s training camp ,” Kubiak said in his press conference. “Those are two leaders of our team going at it. So, that is part of camp. Obviously, you fight in a game, you throw a punch in the game, especially, then you’re out of the game. So, we’ve got to be smart, treat it like a game.” As Kubiak said, teammates getting into it is a part of camp, particularly once guys have been going against each other for over a week. But the Raiders need to make sure they channel that energy the right way as camp continues.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Seahawks sign LB Power Echols
summary: The Seahawks have made a roster move.
full_text: '' The Seahawks have made a roster move. Seattle announced the club has signed linebacker Power Echols on Friday. Echols, 23, entered the league last year as an undrafted free agent out of North Carolina. He spent time with the Bears and Texans in 2025, though he didn’t appear in a regular-season game. As a corresponding move, Seattle waived linebacker Joseph Vaughn.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Steelers OL Max Iheanachor OK after early practice exit
summary: The Steelers received some positive news on the injury front for one of their rookies.
full_text: The Steelers received some positive news on the injury front for one of their rookies. Head coach Mike McCarthy told reporters on Friday that offensive tackle Max Iheanachor will be out of practice for the next few days with an undisclosed injury. But, he is set to return early next week. “He won’t go today,” McCarthy said, via Brian Batko of the team’s website. “I think we might not see him until Monday, but he’s OK .” McCarthy did not go into specifics about the nature of Iheanachor’s injury after the 2026 first-round pick had to exit practice earlier this week. The Steelers first preseason game is set for next Thursday night against the Packers.
author: Myles Simmons

title: NFL training camp 2026: Kirk Cousins, Maxx Crosby have altercation during Raiders' practice
summary: Cousins took issue with Crosby hitting him multiple times
full_text:
Maxx Crosby and Kirk Cousins engaged in an altercation during the Las Vegas Raiders ' training camp practice on Friday. Both players exchanged words before they were ultimately separated.
The altercation began when Cousins took exception to Crosby hitting him on the arm twice during the team period. After the second hit, Cousins confronted Crosby and grabbed his jersey. The two players then exchanged words before being separated.
Crosby said prior to training camp that he had been warned by the team's new coaching staff about touching the quarterback during practice. He acknowledged at the time that his aggressiveness once led to his removal from practice during his time at Eastern Michigan.
"When you get out there and bullets are flying, I'm not thinking about not finishing the play," Crosby said prior to the start of camp, via ESPN . "That's just not in my nature. That's something I've been dealing with my whole career. It's not easy."
Friday's altercation was downplayed by Raiders coach Klint Kubiak.
"Those are two leaders on our team going at it," he said. "Obviously, fighting in a game [or] you throw a punch in a game, you are out of the game. So we got to be smart."
While Crosby's aggressive nature is well-documented, Cousins' actions on Friday were an insight into his competitive spirit. It may also serve as a rallying cry for a Raiders offense that was pushed around far too often in 2025.
"You want him to defend your team," tight end Michael Mayer said of Cousins. "He's always had [that edge] since the first day I met him when he came in here."
The Crosby-Cousins scuffle was one of two altercations that took place during Friday's practice. And while fighting during practice isn't always a good thing, it might be for a once proud franchise that is looking to turn things around.
"It's energy, man," Mayer said. "We don't want to be throwing punches, but I think on any padded day of camp there's going to be some [scuffles]."
author: Bryan DeArdo

title: 2026 Pro Football Hall of Fame ceremony: Where to watch, TV, live stream
summary: Five players are set to join pro football's most exclusive fraternity
full_text:
Five former NFL players are about to formally join the most exclusive fraternity in professional football. Drew Brees, Larry Fitzgerald, Roger Craig, Adam Vinatieri, and Luke Kuechly will become the newest members of the Pro Football Hall of Fame during Saturday's induction ceremony.
Located in Canton, Ohio, the Pro Football Hall of Fame was built in 1963. Since then, 387 former NFL players, coaches and executives have received gold jackets, bronze busts, a ring and a permanent place in pro football lore.
This year's class will include one of the most prolific passers in football history, an equally prolific receiver, one of the most versatile running backs in NFL history, the NFL's all-time leading scorer and the second-youngest player to receive Hall of Fame induction.
Here's how you can watch the ceremony, in addition to summaries of each member of this year's induction class.
Date: Saturday, Aug. 8 | Time: 12 p.m. ET Location: Tom Benson Hall of Fame Stadium (Canton, Ohio) TV: ESPN/NFL Network; Stream: Fubo
Brees retired as the NFL's career leader in both passing yards (80,353) and touchdown passes (571) and is currently second in both categories behind Tom Brady . Brees never won league MVP, but he did capture Super Bowl MVP honors after leading the Saints to their first championship at the end of the 2009 season.
One of the most efficient and prolific quarterbacks of all-time, Brees led the NFL in passing seven times, completion percentage six times and touchdown passes on four occasions.
Fitzgerald is second only to Jerry Rice in career catches (1,432) and career receiving yards (17,492). During the 2008 playoffs, Fitzgerald caught 30 passes for 546 yards and seven touchdowns while helping the Cardinals reach the franchise's first Super Bowl. He caught seven passes for 127 yards and two scores in Arizona's Super Bowl loss to Pittsburgh.
At 35, Kuechly is the second-youngest person to earn a Hall of Fame induction. The youngest was Gale Sayers, who was 34 when he was inducted back in 1977.
Kuechly was one of the NFL's premier defensive players before injuries cut his career short after eight seasons. After winning Defensive Rookie of the Year, Kuechly won Defensive Player of the Year the following season and was named to seven straight Pro Bowls and was a five-time All-Pro. He helped spearhead a successful period in Panthers history that included three straight division titles and an NFC title in 2015.
The NFL's all-time leading scorer, Vinatieri, ended two Super Bowls with winning field goals. In addition to his four Super Bowl wins, Vinatieri is also notorious for his two critical kicks in blizzard-like conditions against the Raiders during the Patriots' first championship run.
One of the most versatile running backs in NFL history, Craig became the first player in history to post 1,000-yard rushing and receiving campaigns in the same season in 1985. His versatility was on full display in the prior year's Super Bowl, when he scored a Super Bowl record three touchdowns in the 49ers ' win over the Dolphins .
Three years later, Craig amassed over 2,000 all-purpose yards during the regular season before becoming the first running back to have over 100 receiving yards in a Super Bowl. Craig won his third Super Bowl a year later while helping the 49ers win back-to-back Super Bowl titles.
author: Bryan DeArdo

title: Colts' Cam Taylor-Britt suspended by NFL for violating personal conduct policy
summary: Taylor-Britt served a five-day jail sentence earlier this year
full_text:
Cam Taylor-Britt has been suspended for one game by the NFL after he violated the league's personal conduct policy. Taylor-Britt, a veteran cornerback who signed a one-year deal with the Indianapolis Colts this offseason, will miss the team's Week 1 home matchup against the Baltimore Ravens .
In January, Taylor-Britt served a five-day jail sentence after he pleaded guilty to reckless driving and an unclassified no-license charge stemming from an incident in September of 2025. Taylor-Britt was driving recklessly following a Bengals game while pedestrians were still in the area, according to a Cincinnati police officer.
Taylor-Britt, 26, was the 60th overall pick in the 2022 NFL Draft . He cracked Cincinnati's starting lineup as a rookie and helped the Bengals advance to the AFC title game that season. He then had a career-high four interceptions in 2023 and three the following season, while being a central part of the Bengals' defense.
This 2025 was a setback for Taylor-Britt, however. He made two starts in eight games before he suffered a season-ending Lisfranc injury that was sustained during Cincinnati's Week 11 loss to the Pittsburgh Steelers .
Taylor-Britt has reunited in Indianapolis with Colts defensive coordinator Lou Anarumo, who served as the Bengals' defensive coordinator during Taylor-Britt's first three seasons in Cincinnati. During Anarumo's first season in Indianapolis, the Colts' defense ranked 21st in points allowed, 31st in passing yards allowed, 7th in rushing yards allowed, 26th in third-down efficiency, and 11th in red zone efficiency.
author: Bryan DeArdo

title: Highest-paid players at every NFL position: Jahmyr Gibbs joins top earners with historic RB contract
summary: A look at the markets by position for 2026
full_text:
NFL training camps are well underway, and not only does that mean that the season is fast approaching, but the paydays are coming in bunches, too, as teams look to lock in their top players long-term.
It's no secret that the NFL is a money-making machine: from merchandise, to commercials, streaming services, to tickets and more. Money is often a big hurdle between teams and players, with contract holdouts, hold-ins and trades giving each season plenty of drama on the sidelines.
The NFL salary cap has more than doubled in the last decade-plus and now sits at over $300 million per team heading into the 2026 season. Some teams are known to be more willing to spend money, while others like to be more cautious with the paycheck.
Some players choose to take less to be on the team they want or to rebuild a solid core around them, while others demand the highest value at their position. Just who is taking home the biggest bag?
We broke down the highest-paid players by position, based on average annual value, to gauge where the market stands. All values are via Spotrac .
Patrick Mahomes agreed this offseason to terms on a revised contract that adds two years to his existing deal and makes him the highest-paid quarterback in average annual value. The three-time Super Bowl MVP and two-time NFL MVP is the first player in NFL history to sign a contract worth more than $500 million. He passed Dak Prescott , who previously held the title at $60 million per year. Followed by Mahomes and Prescott are Josh Allen , Joe Burrow , Trevor Lawrence , Jordan Love and Matthew Stafford , who all hold $55 million AAV deals, according to Spotrac.
Gibbs replaced Bijan Robinson as the highest-paid running back in NFL history after he and the Detroit Lions agreed to a three-year, $67.5 million deal that could be worth up to $75.75 million, sources confirmed to CBS Sports' Matt Zenitz. The deal also includes $51.5 million guaranteed.
The 32-year-old went undrafted in 2017 before signing with the Baltimore Ravens . He signed with the Giants this offseason after earning Pro Bowl and second-team All-Pro honors in 2025.
Jaxon Smith-Njigba was essential to the Seahawks ' Super Bowl championship run last season and was named the NFL's Offensive Player of the Year. He had 119 receptions and 1,793 receiving yards, a league high, along with 10 touchdowns in the regular season. His breakout year came at the perfect time for Sam Darnold's offense and he has high expectations as he enters Year 4.
George Kittle is arguably the best tight end in the league right now and it shows in his contract. The seven-time Pro Bowler and two-time first-team All-Pro has spent his entire career with the 49ers . Kittle started and ended his season with injuries last year, missing five games due to a hamstring tear suffered in Week 1 and going down with an Achilles injury in their wild-card game against the Eagles . He still has goals of a Week 1 return for the 2026 season.
Laremy Tunsil was the No. 13 overall pick in 2016, selected by the Miami Dolphins . He then went to the Houston Texans before joining the Commanders in 2025. His resume includes five Pro Bowl honors and he has started all 139 games he's played in.
The Bears already picked up a fifth-year option on Wright for 2027, and they secured his future even further when they came to terms during training camp on a four-year extension . The $93 million guaranteed on that new deal is the most ever for an offensive lineman, and the $29 million per year makes Wright the highest-paid right tackle in league history.
Skoronski surpassed Tyler Smith and Matthew Bergeron after he came to terms on an historic extension that will includes $88 million guaranteed. By locking up Skoronski, the Titans have ensured that they will have one of the NFL's best offensive lineman under contract for the foreseeable future.
Tyler Linderbaum was drafted No. 25 overall in 2022 by the Ravens, where he remained until this offseason, when he joined the Raiders . The three-time Pro Bowler took 99% of offensive snaps last season, starting all 17 games.
Will Anderson Jr . became the highest-paid non-quarterback in NFL history with his massive three-year, $150 million deal. According to Next Gen Stats, he was seventh in run-stop rate (12.6%), third in run stuffs (13) and second in pressures (85) among defenders with at least 150 run defensive snaps in 2025. His performance put him second in NFL Defensive Player of the Year voting. He was named DPOY in 2023.
Jeffery Simmons briefly held the title of highest-paid interior defensive lineman this offseason before Jalen Carter took the throne with a huge extension on the eve of the first practice of training camp. Carter's extension doesn't kick in until after the 2027 season and includes $106 million guaranteed.
Fred Warner has spent his entire career with the Niners and the team has him under contract until 2030. He is a four-time first-team All-Pro and a four-time Pro Bowler, starting all 121 regular-season and 12 playoff games he's appeared in. The defensive leader was limited to six games last season due to an ankle fracture.
For the second time in his career, Ward tops the highest-paid defensive back list after signing a two-year, $62.2 million extension that ties him to Cleveland through 2029. Ward was already signed through 2027 on a five-year, $100.5 million extension in 2022. He's a five-time Pro Bowler with 18 career interceptions.
Derwin James has played for the Chargers since the team selected him No. 17 overall in 2018. He earned his fifth Pro Bowl and fourth second-team All-Pro honor last season. He had a career-best three interceptions last season, to go with 94 combined tackles, seven passes defended, two sacks and one forced fumble.
This marks the largest deal for a kicker in league history, earned in thanks to Pro Bowls in each of his three seasons in the NFL. Aubrey went undrafted in 2022 and joined the USFL, becoming a two-time champion in the league, before heading to the Cowboys in 2023. He has made 88.2% of field goals attempted and 96.9% of attempted extra points. He has six total field goals over 60 yards, an NFL record.
Jordan Stout led the league with a net average of 44.9 yards last season and earned a Pro Bowl spot due to his 2025 performance.
author: Zachary Pereles

title: Hall of Famer Larry Fitzgerald explains why he will never retire
summary: The Arizona Cardinals legend is protesting that word
full_text:
Arizona Cardinals legend Larry Fitzgerald will be enshrined into the Pro Football Hall of Fame this Saturday in Canton, Ohio. Players have to be retired for five straight seasons to qualify for the Hall of Fame, and while Fitzgerald hasn't played in the NFL since 2020, the wide receiver has never officially retired -- and maybe never will.
"I have not committed to retirement," Fitzgerald said this week, via the Cardinals' official website .
That doesn't mean Fitzgerald is actively pondering a return to the gridiron, but he avoids the word "retirement." When he was a young boy, Fitzgerald's grandfather would talk with his friend about how retirement was deadly. The 42-year-old is done with football, not with life.
"They'd talk about retirement killing more people in our country than anything," Fitzgerald said. "It always stuck with me. I just don't believe in retirement. I just think you transition into different phases, especially as an athlete. I was done at 38. Retire? There is no retirement in sight.
"I protest the word more than the actual thing. So I just won't acknowledge that."
Fitzgerald has spent his entire life around football, and it's fair to assume he will stay close the game in retir- ... his "next phase of life." As a youth, Fitzgerald was a ball boy for the Minnesota Vikings and head coach Dennis Green -- who would later coach Fitzgerald in Arizona. He found his way to the University of Pittsburgh for college, and after catching 161 passes for 2,677 yards and 34 touchdowns in just 26 games played, was selected by the Cardinals with the No. 3 overall pick in the 2004 NFL Draft .
It didn't take Fitzgerald long to establish himself as one of the premier wide receivers in the NFL . In his second NFL season, Fitzgerald led the league with 103 receptions. At 22-years-old, he was the youngest NFL player to catch 100 passes in a single season. Fitzgerald would go on to rack up nine 1,000-yard seasons, four 1,400-yard seasons and five seasons where he caught double-digit touchdowns. He was named to 11 Pro Bowls, led the league in receptions and receiving touchdowns twice, and earned the coveted Walter Payton NFL Man of the Year award in 2016.
Fitzgerald was a lifetime Cardinal, and saw more losses than wins in his NFL career. He played in just nine postseason matchups over 17 years, but did power an impressive run to Super Bowl XLIII in 2009 with Kurt Warner. In those four playoff games, Fitzgerald caught 30 passes for 546 yards and seven touchdowns. That's 136.5 receiving yards per game! He admitted there was a time where he considered leaving Arizona, but ultimately decided against it.
"I would be lying to you if it didn't cross my mind, I didn't think about it, maybe even had conversations about it, but never seriously tried to put it in motion," Fitzgerald said, per ESPN . "I loved where I was at. And quite frankly, I don't know if it would've meant the same for me if I went to somewhere where it was already some super team."
To this day, Fitzgerald ranks second all time in receiving yards (17,492) and receptions (1,432), trailing only the great Jerry Rice. Fitzgerald is looking forward to his induction into "Football Heaven" this weekend. But don't make the mistake of saying he's retired.
author: Jordan Dajani

title: Why the Cardinals should name Carson Beck their starting QB for 2026 after Hall of Fame Game performance
summary: Arizona should rip the Band-Aid off and give the starting QB job to Carson Beck
full_text:
Every year, I promise myself that I won't overreact to anything that I see during the NFL preseason , and every year, I end up overreacting to almost everything I see. That being said, I don't think what I'm about to say is an overreaction: The Arizona Cardinals should give their starting quarterback job to Carson Beck for the 2026 season.
I thought this before Arizona's 33-30 loss to Carolina in the Hall of Fame Game, and after watching Beck's performance on Thursday night, I'm even more convinced that it should happen.
When you throw a rookie QB into an actual game for the first time, you never know what you're going to get. As Ryan Wilson noted on Thursday night , some rookies have performed well in their first preseason game ( Dak Prescott finished 10 of 12 for 139 yards and two touchdowns in 2016), while other rookies have struggled ( C.J. Stroud completed just 2 of 4 passes for 13 yards with an interception in his first preseason game).
What Beck did was prove that he can play at the NFL level. When you have a rookie QB, you want to make sure he can command the huddle, that he knows the playbook and that he can make good throws. Beck did all of that on Thursday in a performance that saw him complete 15 of 19 passes for 188 yards and a touchdown. He completed two passes of at least 35 yards, including the 49-yarder below to Jalen Brooks .
Carson Beck to Jalen Brooks. WOW. @ProFootballHOF Game on NBC Stream on @NFLPlus + Peacock pic.twitter.com/VjnMEP2mIQ
New Cardinals coach Mike LaFleur didn't seem too shocked by Beck's performance, because that's apparently how he's been playing during training camp.
"The same thing that I keep seeing at practice where he just gets in and out of the huddle, and he doesn't make it too big," LaFleur said, via ESPN . "[Beck] worried about one play at a time and executing that play and going through your progressions, not making stuff up. If it's not there, checking it down. If we're in a bad play, a bad call, don't make it worse. ... I just thought he was steady all day."
Right now, Jacoby Brissett seems to be the leader in the clubhouse for the starting QB job. LaFleur hasn't officially named a starting quarterback just yet, but Arizona did just revise Brissett's contract . The new deal will give the veteran QB a raise of about $10 million over his old contract: He'll now be making about $15.5 million in 2026 with a chance to earn up to $21 million . You don't hand out a raise like that unless you're thinking about making that guy your starter.
Brissett is a 33-year-old veteran and he might make sense as a bridge quarterback in another situation, but not here. Let's start with the fact that Beck already knows the playbook better than Brissett. Usually, this would be an advantage for the veteran QB on the team, but with a new head coach, both quarterbacks had to start from scratch this year and both guys are in the process of learning the new playbook. However, Brissett skipped OTAs due to a contract issue, so he actually fell behind. After signing his new deal on July 26, Brissett was asked if he was up to speed on the new offense and he gave an extremely honest answer.
"Oh, hell no," Brissett said, via ESPN . "I got a long way to go. I mean, I'm willing to put the work in. Obviously, after this night of sleep that I do get, I'll go back to three hours of sleep for work purposes now. But it's training camp. We're all learning. It's first time in this offense."
So Brissett has no advantage there. Beck, who was taken in the third round of the draft back in April, has shown that he can competently run the offense and that's what matters.
The bigger reason to start Beck is because the Cardinals need to know what they have in him RIGHT NOW. There's simply no upside to giving the starting QB job to Brissett.
Let's look at three hypothetical scenarios for how Arizona's season plays out with Brissett and why Beck would make more sense in each case.
1. The Cards play bad and earn the top pick in the 2027 draft. The Cardinals are in the toughest division in football, so there's a real chance that they end up with the worst record in the NFL. If that happens, they'll have the top pick in the 2027 NFL Draft , which is theoretically a good thing, because the draft is expected to be loaded with talented quarterbacks like Dante Moore and Arch Manning. However, if Brissett starts in 2026, then the Cards won't know what they have in Beck. They'd likely take a QB in the 2027 draft, which essentially means they'd be giving up on Beck without ever actually knowing what they have in him. WHY BECK: If Beck were to start in 2026 and lead the team to the No. 1 overall pick, the Cardinals would know that they gave him a shot and that he came up short, and that would put them in a spot where they'd feel comfortable taking a QB with the top pick.
2. The Cardinals win five to eight games with Brissett. This would arguably be the worst-case scenario for Arizona this year. Brissett is a veteran who might be able to lead you to a handful of wins, but that does nothing for you this year. In this situation, you likely don't get a high pick in the 2027 draft and you STILL don't know what you have with Beck. You wouldn't have the top pick in the draft, so grabbing one of the top 2027 quarterbacks wouldn't be an option and signing a QB in free agency wouldn't make much sense, because you would once again hinder Beck's potential growth. WHY BECK: If Beck were to start and lead the team to five to eight wins, the organization would likely feel optimistic about its future. With a young QB under center, the Cards could use the 2027 draft to build around Beck.
3. Brissett somehow leads the Cardinals to the playoffs. This is a long shot, but if it did happen, it would actually put the Cardinals in an awkward spot. Brissett's contract expires after the 2026 season and if he led them to the playoffs, they would probably be tempted to sign him to a new deal in 2027, which would keep Beck on the bench for another year. WHY BECK: If Beck were to lead the Cardinals to the playoffs, he would probably get his own holiday in the state of Arizona. The Cards would also confidently be able to say that they've found their franchise QB.
Brissett is a 33-year-old journeyman quarterback who has never finished a season with a winning record as a starter. He's gone just 2-15 as a starter over the past two seasons and that includes going 1-11 last year in Arizona. Despite those numbers, Brissett still had the audacity to skip OTAs in hopes of getting a bigger contract, and for some reason, the Cardinals caved, even though the answer (Beck) was right in front of them all along.
Carson Beck could be the QB of the future in Arizona and the Cardinals need to figure out if the future is now.
author: John Breech

title: Hall of Fame locks: Active NFL players bound for enshrinement include Aaron Rodgers, Myles Garrett
summary: Football immortality awaits these legends
full_text:
The Pro Football Hall of Fame Class of 2026 will be inducted on Saturday as five all-time NFL legends become immortalized in Canton, Ohio. Every year when the next batch of greats goes down in history, it raises the question of which players will follow in their footsteps. The book is not fully written on the active players in consideration, but for a large handful, the Hall will come calling when it is all said and done.
Players like Aaron Rodgers who are synonymous with football are no-doubt future Hall of Famers regardless of the quality of their play between now and retirement. With Rodgers set to close his career this year, eligibility is just around the corner. He and the rest of next year's retirees (if he follows through on his pledge to hang up his cleats after the 2026 season) will be under consideration for Hall of Fame election in 2032.
The five-year period between retirement and eligibility exists to eliminate recency bias. For the active players who are virtual locks to receive a gold jacket, their legacies will be just as strong in five years as they are today. In fact, some might become even greater.
Below are the active NFL players who are locks to earn a spot in the Hall of Fame.
Not only is Aaron Rodgers a top 10 quarterback of all time, but he also ranks near the top of the 100 greatest players to ever grace an NFL field . With four MVP awards, a Super Bowl MVP honor and the league's career interception rate record in hand, there are hardly any more accolades for Rodgers to stack up in what he says will be his final year.
By age 30, Patrick Mahomes already stacked up two regular-season MVP trophies and three Super Bowl MVP crowns. The individual accolades speak for themselves, and the team success element puts him in rare air as one of just five quarterbacks to ever win at least three Super Bowls. Mahomes is as transcendent of a player as there is in the NFL right now -- a quarterback who quickly became the face of a dynasty and who redefined his position with unmatched improvisational skills.
Detractors will knock him for the lack of a Super Bowl title, but even without a ring, Lamar Jackson is a legend at the quarterback position. He is already the greatest rusher in the position's history with 6,522 yards, and anyone who doubted that his passing ability would ever match his athleticism outside the pocket has been silenced in the last couple of years. Jackson now also stands as the most efficient passer in league history with a 102.2 rating. He is a future Hall of Famer as both a rusher and passer , and history says that winning two MVP awards constitutes a lock to receive a gold jacket.
The case for Matthew Stafford to clinch a spot in Canton was strong but not airtight before the 2025 season. Now that he has an MVP on his ledger, it is hard to envision him falling short of Hall of Fame status . Quarterbacks with both an MVP and a Super Bowl victory are shoo-ins in the eyes of Hall of Fame voters, and Stafford joined that group when he led the league in passing yards, touchdowns and TD-INT ratio as a 37-year-old. If he delivers on expectations and wins another title this year, Stafford could go from a "likely inductee" to a potential first-ballot selection in a matter of two seasons.
The 12,000-yard club is the threshold for guaranteed Hall of Fame status. Every single eligible rusher to reach that landmark has been enshrined in Canton. Derrick Henry joined the group last season (and, in fact, became the 10th player to hit 13,000 yards) while also moving into fourth place on the all-time rushing touchdowns leaderboard with 122. What is most impressive about Henry's reign as the greatest ballcarrier of his generation is that he continues to dominate defenses into his 30s. He seems to have plenty left in the tank.
The gruesome knee injury Tyreek Hill sustained last year puts his career in jeopardy , but if he has already played his final snap, his career accolades are already Hall of Fame-worthy. Hill is the only receiver in NFL history to post two 1,700-yard seasons, and he did so in consecutive years in 2022 and 2023. He finished top 10 in MVP voting both times, and that was after he earned a Super Bowl title during his run with the Chiefs . At his peak, Hill's game-breaking speed made him one of the most dangerous vertical threats the game has ever seen.
Only six players have ever led the NFL in receiving touchdowns in three different seasons. Last year, Davante Adams did it with his third separate team. His 14 scores with the Rams placed him in elite company and proved that even at 33, he remains one of the toughest covers in the game. In his prime, Adams was a three-time first-team All-Pro who caught passes at will and racked up receptions en route to becoming the 18th player to crack the 1,000 career catch threshold.
If not for the hamstring and clavicle injuries that cost him more than half of last season, Mike Evans could have broken the NFL record for consecutive 1,000-yard seasons. The streak came to an end with him playing just eight games, but the 11 straight years of at least 1,000 yards were the most to start a career. That extended run of consistent, high-end production made Evans a Buccaneers legend, not to mention the Super Bowl he won with them in 2021. Anything Evans achieves with the 49ers is gravy on what is already a Hall of Fame-worthy résumé.
There are only 10 tight ends in the Hall of Fame, and Rob Gronkowski will become the 11th when he gains eligibility in 2027. In an era where the position is more active in the receiving game than ever before, Gronkowski and Travis Kelce could be the first part of a new wave of legends to be enshrined in the Hall. The latter is a no-doubter thanks to his three Super Bowl titles, seven consecutive All-Pro selections and the fact that in every year but one, he racked up at least 800 receiving yards. Kelce is also the most prolific pass-catcher in postseason history.
Only a couple of other active players are as surefire of a first-ballot Hall of Famer as Trent Williams . His longevity as an elite left tackle -- and the fact that he has essentially only become better with age, rather than the other way around -- is uncanny. All three of his first-team All-Pro selections came in his mid-30s, and even though he acknowledged that he may not play beyond his current contract (which runs through 2027), it does not take much imagination to foresee him remaining a league standard until his retirement.
It is practically unbelievable how much of an impact Lane Johnson has on the Eagles . With the legendary right tackle in the lineup, Philadelphia is 110-57-1. Without him, the record falls off a cliff to 18-27. He was integral in two Super Bowl runs and regularly ranks as the league's best active offensive lineman, if not one of the greatest right tackles to ever play.
As arguably the second-greatest defensive tackle of his generation, behind Aaron Donald , Chris Jones can expect to give an induction speech in Canton before too long. He has been one of the premier pass-rushing defensive tackles since his arrival in the league in 2016 and twice eclipsed 15 sacks in a season. Jones anchored the Chiefs' defense for all three Super Bowl runs since 2020 and is a six-time All-Pro honoree.
The trade that sent Myles Garrett from the Browns to the Rams this offseason reshaped the NFL's defensive power dynamic. Garrett is so impactful that Los Angeles' Super Bowl odds spiked aggressively with his arrival, and if he secures that first championship, his legacy will be complete. From his second professional season onward, Garrett has never posted fewer than 10 sacks or 18 QB hits in a campaign, and his legendary 2025 season, of course, went into the record books. The 23 sacks he racked up in his second Defensive Player of the Year campaign were the most in a single season and reflected Garrett's leveling up into a new echelon of backfield disruption. That is not to mention that he is also as…
