title: Crowning moment: Panthers' Haynes King headlines five standouts from the NFL Hall of Fame Game
summary: Undrafted quarterback Haynes King scored a walk-off touchdown to cap a thrilling 33-30 victory, highlighting the top standouts from a historic Hall of Fame Game
full_text:
We saw a likely NFC Championship preview on Thursday night between the Carolina Panthers and Arizona Cardinals . OK, maybe that's an exaggeration, but football is back, and it was fun. Shame on the NFL fans that didn't find time to watch the first preseason game of the year, because it was the best Hall of Fame Game ever.
Seriously, the Panthers defeated the Cardinals, 33-30. That's 63 total points scored -- 30 points more than expected. Cardinals quarterback Kedon Slovis threw a 1-yard touchdown to Bryson Green with 1:55 remaining in the fourth quarter to give Arizona a 30-27 lead, which gave Panthers quarterback Haynes King the opportunity to lead a game-winning drive. Undrafted yet undeterred, King led a 13-play, 65-yard drive -- and punched in the game-winning touchdown on a third-and-goal on the final play of the game. You could practically feel the golden busts in the next building over peeking outside for a look.
If that's the way the 2026 NFL season is going to start, it could be the best ever. Let's take a look at who stood out from the Hall of Fame Game.
In previewing the Hall of Fame Game, I pointed to undrafted Panthers quarterback Haynes King as one of the players I'm most excited to watch this preseason. Well, he was the star on Thursday night.
As we mentioned, King led a 65-yard game-winning drive with under two minutes remaining in the fourth quarter, which included three third-down conversions. That includes this third-and-14.
Haynes King showing off his speed! @ProFootballHOF Game on NBC Stream on @NFLPlus + Peacock pic.twitter.com/oqCTM8AkKu
Down at the 5-yard line with two seconds remaining on the clock, King decided to take the outcome of his first professional game in his hands, and run it in for the win.
HAYNES KING WINS IT FOR THE PANTHERS ‼️ pic.twitter.com/HESbUZGhBN
"Fine, I'll do it myself." 😤 pic.twitter.com/rnv5msqYwu
Knowing this player, I wonder how much he actually thought about throwing the ball. This is a legitimate dual-threat signal-caller who ran a 4.46 40-yard dash at the combine, and rushed for 37 touchdowns over his collegiate career. In his final two seasons at Georgia Tech, King averaged more than one touchdown a game on the ground!
What I will say about King is that he's not the most polished passer. As a prospect, you wouldn't describe him as a pinpoint deadeye that layers the ball with precision in zone coverage, but the dude is a gamer and he's fun ... obviously. The upside and athleticism is evident. You don't win ACC Player of the Year for nothing.
King replaced Panthers starter Kenny Pickett in the second quarter, and played out the rest of the game. He completed 21 of 34 passes for 180 yards and two touchdowns, and rushed for 39 yards, plus the game-winning score. King definitely missed a handful of throws, but made some, too.
This throw by Haynes King 😮‍💨 @ProFootballHOF Game on NBC Stream on @NFLPlus + Peacock pic.twitter.com/bKtIsO1ygy
Given his background and what happened on Thursday night, this is a preseason star in the making -- just like we predicted.
Cardinals rookie quarterback Carson Beck was one of the headliners of this matchup. The third quarterback selected in the 2026 NFL Draft got the start for Arizona, and he did not disappoint.
The Miami product completed 15 of 19 passes for 188 yards and a touchdown in his first NFL action, and looked comfortable commanding this Mike LaFleur offensive attack. Maybe that was to be expected from the quarterback who racked up the most wins, passing yards and passing touchdowns in the FBS from 2023-25, but the point is the moment was not too big for him.
In the first quarter while operating out of his own end zone, Beck found a streaking Jalen Brooks off a double move down the right sideline.
What a throw by Carson Beck! @ProFootballHOF Game on NBC Stream on @NFLPlus + Peacock pic.twitter.com/ai2A4lm7z0
In the second quarter, he found Brooks AGAIN down the left sideline for a 49-yard gain. Pretty solid ball, and shoutout to Brooks for holding onto the pigskin while taking the illegal hit.
Carson Beck to Jalen Brooks. WOW. @ProFootballHOF Game on NBC Stream on @NFLPlus + Peacock pic.twitter.com/VjnMEP2mIQ
That play set up Beck's first touchdown pass -- which went to Simi Fehoko on a throw to the right pylon. I love this toss, because it was to one-on-one coverage and only where his receiver could grab it.
. @carsonbeck01 drops it in a bucket 🪣 @ProFootballHOF Game on NBC Stream on @NFLPlus + Peacock pic.twitter.com/fZQpMPha1q
I'm not going to say there's a quarterback controversy in Arizona. Jacoby Brissett is probably going to start the season. But if he struggles, fans will be calling for Beck early.
He's coming off a season where he led the Hurricanes to the College Football Playoff National Championship. While not the most electric playmaker, Beck is effective from the pocket and was compared to Jared Goff by our CBS Sports analysts. I do see some Goff in Beck. From a clean pocket he's dangerous. But he's not the most creative quarterback when under pressure or forced from his progression. Beck was a big winner from Thursday night. It's worth watching him in Arizona's next three preseason matchups.
Every completion from @carsonbeck01 's preseason debut 👀 pic.twitter.com/0WI9ofkRYw
We can't just praise the quarterback for his throws, we have to point out the game's leading receiver as well! Jalen Brooks caught three passes for a whopping 99 yards, which includes this disgusting double move that toasted rookie cornerback Will Lee III .
. @LarryFitzgerald is liking what he is seeing from the @AZCardinals 😌 @ProFootballHOF Game on NBC Stream on @NFLPlus + Peacock pic.twitter.com/fh5NzdXELk
Imagine impressing Larry Fitzgerald in Canton.
We also posted the video of Brooks catching a 49-yard pass and surviving an illegal hit above. Gritty.
This is a former seventh-round pick of the Dallas Cowboys in 2023 out of South Carolina, but Brooks did spend five games with the Cardinals last season. In 27 career games played, he's caught 21 passes for 292 yards and a touchdown.
There are plenty of Panthers playmakers I could mention here. Miles Davis led the team in rushing with 53 yards on four carries, Jimmy Horn Jr . led the team in receiving with 44 yards on four receptions and AJ Dillon looks like a legitimate power back. But let's talk about Ja'seem Reed for a second.
The former undrafted wideout out of San Diego last year has been a training camp darling in Charlotte, and he caught two passes for 30 yards and a touchdown on Thursday. He was also working in on special teams, returning a kick for 26 yards. Keep an eye on this kid.
Haynes King and Ja'seem Reed get 6️⃣ more on the board for the @Panthers @ProFootballHOF Game on NBC Stream on @NFLPlus + Peacock pic.twitter.com/L9LtMbeYnx
This was an undrafted linebacker Brian Flores initially saw something in. Austin Keys landed in Arizona late last season, and is battling for a roster spot. He did his part on Thursday, leading all teams in tackles with 11, plus one tackle for loss on a screen he read well.
Keys also had a play in the second quarter where he stopped a would-be touchdown in one-on-one coverage downfield. Talk about perfect timing in reading the hands of the tight end.
#RiseUpRedSea Austin Keys coverage on the wheel route #AzCardinals #WarEagle pic.twitter.com/vycZ7pK05V
Keys appeared to be one of the best defenders for the Cardinals in their first outing of the season. I'm curious if he can work his way up the depth chart.
author: Jordan Dajani

title: Rams might not have to wait long for Aaron Donald's return: Predicting when former NFL star will unretire
summary: Don't be surprised if the three-time NFL Defensive Player of the Year makes a big announcement next week
full_text:
It has now been more than two months since rumors started that Aaron Donald might come out of retirement to play for the Rams this year, but that hasn't happened yet.
The speculation started in June after the Rams made a shocking trade to acquire Myles Garrett from the Cleveland Browns . Less than 24 hours after the deal went down, the Donald rumors started and the three-time NFL Defensive Player of the Year had a chance to shut them down, but instead, he added fuel to the fire. On June 2, Donald admitted that he was thinking about a possible comeback.
"I'm for sure flirting with the idea," Donald told Jordan Schultz . "Helluva an opportunity with the Super Bowl in SoFi this year. If I can find the fire, it's a possibility."
That comment came in June, but two months later, a Donald return seems like a lot more than "a possibility." Based on everything that's happened over the past two months, it sure feels like Donald is planning to make a comeback this year, so we're going to try and predict when he's officially going to come out of retirement. However, before we get to that, let's take a look at why a return seems imminent.
After announcing that he might return on June 2, the Donald chatter stopped for nearly a month, but then it shot back to life on July 10, so let's start here.
July 10: The TMZ workout. If you're wondering what happened on July 10, that's when TMZ caught Donald working out at the Rams' facility. Before this, it wasn't clear how serious Donald was about a return, but then TMZ managed to obtain a video of Donald working out on the Rams' practice field, which ramped up the speculation that he was going to come out of retirement after two years. At the beginning of training camp, Sean McVay actually cracked a joke about the fact that TMZ caught Donald at the team's facility. With the Rams holding camp at Loyola Marymount, McVay was asked if Donald might spend some time working out at the team's normal facility in Woodland Hills, Calif. "There's nobody at the Rams facility right now, but maybe TMZ knows the answer to that," McVay said.
July 31: McVay offers first big hint that Donald might be returning. The Rams held their first fully padded practice of training camp on July 31 and after the session was over, McVay said the possibility of a Donald return was "trending upwards." The Rams coach also gave the first hint of just when Donald might actually come out of retirement. McVay made it clear that Donald wouldn't be making his return while the team was still practicing at Loyola Marymount. "Once we get back to Woodland Hills, we'll have a better idea of what that timeline looks like," McVay said . "There won't be any decision and anything in terms of Aaron's situation while we're here. That's kind of already been set out when we've talked for the past couple weeks."
The Rams' final practice at LMU will be coming on Aug. 7, so a Donald decision could come at any point after that.
Aug. 1: McVay talks to CBS Sports HQ. During our CBS Sports HQ training camp tour this year, we stopped at Loyola Marymount and that's where two-time Super Bowl winner Bryant McFadden conducted an interesting interview with McVay. The Rams coach had to answer each question with a facial expression, and his response to a question about Donald's possible return made it seem like the 35-year-old will be making a comeback soon.
Did Sean McVay just ...? 😉 @BMac_SportsTalk pic.twitter.com/rdnbz6MfGO
Aug. 5: The NFL transaction wire gives a surprising Donald update. It's not clear how many times Donald has been at the Rams' facility since July 10, but he was definitely there on Aug. 5 and we know that thanks to the NFL transaction wire. Donald was there because he wanted to work out in a football helmet and he ended up going to the Rams' facility to use their equipment. Due to that fact, the Rams had to report the visit to the NFL and it was listed as a "tryout."
"Best tryout that we've ever had, I think he could make the team," McVay said Wednesday when asked about the situation . "That was honestly our way of getting to work with him in the parameters of what's necessary."
Two days after his "tryout" with the Rams, Donald was spotted on the practice field at UCLA doing another workout, and he was actually wearing a Rams helmet. In a video that was posted to social media , a young fan asks Donald if he will be "unretiring" and "going back to the Rams."
"I don't know yet, we're going to see," Donald replied.
Caught Aaron Donald @ UCLA training today this gives me a feeling he is definitely coming back. My lil nephews asked the question. Let’s go!! @AaronDonald97 #ramshouse #nfl pic.twitter.com/8sD0K4YVln
So what does all of this mean? That leads us to our next question.
Here's what we know: The Rams aren't looking for Donald to come out of retirement until they return home from training camp and their last practice at LMU is on Aug. 7, so it will be some point after that. We also know that the Rams had Donald in for a formal workout on Wednesday, which feels like one of the final steps both sides would want to take before a return.
Although Donald is definitely in good shape, he likely isn't in football shape. The only way to get into football shape is to get on the field, so it seems like it would be in Donald's best interest to return at some point in the next few weeks. All 32 NFL teams have to cut down their roster to 53 players by Aug. 30 and the Rams would likely want to know before that if Donald is going to play, so that feels like a soft deadline.
BREECH PREDICTION: With all of that in mind, this seems to set up a situation where Donald returns between Aug. 9-16. If he returns on Aug. 9, that would give him a chance to play in a preseason game to get his feet wet. If he's back on Aug. 16, he may not play in a preseason game, but he would get three full weeks of practice before the Rams' opener in Australia against the 49ers . If I were going to predict an exact date, I'd probably go with Aug. 10. The Rams will be back at their home practice facility in Woodland Hills at that point and having Donald at practice to open the week would be a fitting way to mark their return.
Donald is already under contract with the Rams, and after he makes the decision to return, his old deal will instantly become reactivated by the team. At that point, the Rams will be on the hook for about $30 million to Donald in 2026, so the team might have to restructure his deal so that it can fit under the salary cap.
PREDICTION FROM A FORMER NFL GENERAL MANAGER: Of course, there's always a chance that my prediction ends up being 100% wrong -- it wouldn't be the first time -- and if that happens, former Titans general manager Ran Carthon outlined a plan that might make sense for Donald.
Carthon spent five seasons as the Rams' director of player personnel (2012-2016) and he was with them when they drafted Donald in 2014. During a conversation about Donald on the "With the First Pick" podcast , Carthon predicted that Donald might wait to return until AFTER the season starts.
"I don't know that we see him early in September," Carthon said. "If you're Aaron Donald at this point and you came back and the team doesn't win the championship, then what did you come back for? I think we will see some games played so he can evaluate how the season is going for the team. I think, if the season is going well, we'll see him, let's call it the middle of September, early October. If the season is not going well, then I don't know that we see him at all."
With games against the 49ers, Giants and Broncos to start the season, Carthon thinks that Donald might wait to see how those play out before committing to anything. We don't know for sure when Donald will unretire, but at this point it seems almost certain to happen.
Before retiring, Donald won a Super Bowl ring in 2021 after the Rams beat the Bengals at SoFi Stadium. This year, the Super Bowl is once again being held at SoFi and that seems to be…

title: Beaks & Geeks: Cardinals Hall of Fame Game
summary: The Arizona Cardinals kicked off the NFL’s 2026 season by playing the Carolina Panthers in the annual Hall of Fame Game in Canton, Ohio. The contest is part of the Hall of Fame weekend, which includes various festivities with the conclusion of the induction of the 2026 Pro Football Hall of Fame class. Former Arizona […]
full_text: The Arizona Cardinals kicked off the NFL’s 2026 season by playing the Carolina Panthers in the annual Hall of Fame Game in Canton, Ohio. The contest is part of the Hall of Fame weekend, which includes various festivities with the conclusion of the induction of the 2026 Pro Football Hall of Fame class. Former Arizona great WR Larry Fitzgerald was part of this year’s class. With the Panthers, former linebacker Luke Kuechly was also a class member. RELATED: FIRST OFFICIAL DEPTH CHART And now for the game. For one, the expectations with any starters entering the game and getting snaps are pretty low. That should be true for all four exhibition competitions. Back in the day, every coach and player gave it their all to win just because it was a game and they were competitive. Also consider it was the first game for Mike LaFleur as an NFL head coach. A decade ago, the tradition was that the starters bypassed the first game and then played two series in the second preseason game, a full quarter in the third match, and then the first half in the final contest. Now, few starters make an appearance at all at the exhibition level. The reason for preseason games is numerous. First, the coaching staff needs to find out which players to cut. The training camp roster is 90 players, which has to be pared down to 53 plus a 17-member practice squad before Week 1. That is quite a few athletes to let go, and the last thing any head coach wants is to see a guy they had in camp become a star player elsewhere. Secondly, rookies need to get acclimated to the professional level, which is bigger, stronger, and faster. Thirdly, with new players signed from other teams, they know their former team’s schemes and playbook, but not the Cardinals’ stuff. Practice and classroom meetings are a great help, but seeing what these players have absorbed in a live game is critical. And finally, great practice players don’t necessarily translate into great talent on the field when there is live hitting and quick decision-making. Case in point, last year’s training camp darling was OG Isaiah Adams. He was named the starter at LG to start the season, then struggled mightily once he no longer faced second-and third-stringers. Who played well for the Cardinals against the Panthers in the Hall of Fame Game? Who did not? ————————————————————————— BEAKS QB Carson Beck – You have to admit – the kid delivered. He was poised, never became flustered, and did well while rolling out. Beck threw strikes and stepped up in the pocket when he felt it begin to collapse. His magic began early when he left the pocket and ran for four yards on a third-and-three. Debut numbers📈 @BetMGM pic.twitter.com/zjTPMx8930 — Arizona Cardinals (@AZCardinals) August 7, 2026 With 5:30 left in the first quarter, Beck hit WR Jalen Brooks for 35 yards after beating CB Will Lee down to the 42-yard line. After being pinned down at their own three, on second-and-six, Beck found Brooks again for 15 yards and then RB Corey Kiner for eight that was marked at the one. A very deep pass to Brooks in the second stanza gained 49 yards as CB Akayleb Evans attempted a pass breakup, but Brooks was able to cradle the long pass. Beck had another smart play when a short screen was upset by the defense and the signalcaller wisely tossed the ball into the turf instead of forcing the play. As well as Beck played, keep in mind he went up against second-teamers for his two-plus quarters. SIMI SIMI SIMI 📺: NBC pic.twitter.com/DOJ3YVzmvp — Arizona Cardinals (@AZCardinals) August 7, 2026 But watch the pass he sent flying into the back corner of the end zone that was caught by WR Simi Fehoko for the touchdown. Exact placement. Went 15-19 for 188 yards with one touchdown pass, zero interceptions, and was sacked just once. Two of the incompletions were touched by the receiver. K Chad Ryland – The experienced kicker connected on all three field goal attempts and converted 3-3 on PATs. He was also able to have two kickoffs land in the end zone for touchbacks. Ryland did what kickers are supposed to do. . @LarryFitzgerald is liking what he is seeing from the @AZCardinals 😌 @ProFootballHOF Game on NBC Stream on @NFLPlus + Peacock pic.twitter.com/fh5NzdXELk — NFL (@NFL) August 7, 2026 WR Jalen Brooks – A lot of noise from training camp on this kid, and he balled out. Has great speed and is elusive. Twice, Brooks juked his defender out of his Nikes to run free. Before kickoff, he was listed as the second backup behind Marv Harrison and Fehoko. If he continues, Brooks will be impossible to cut. Three receptions for 99 yards and a 33.0 yards per catch average. OT Josh Fryer – Listed on the depth chart as the backup to LT Paris Johnson, but lined up at RT while all of the second team offense was in the game. Held his own without any sacks allowed, but he did have a false start in the second quarter. Fryer looked good and did not allow any defender to get close to Beck. LB Austin Keys – Somehow, this guy needs to find a spot on this year’s defense. Every time you looked up, there was #53 making a tackle or swatting the ball away. Saved a touchdown in the second quarter when he was beaten a step by TE James Mitchell. Unable to see the pass, but not holding his man, Keys threw up his arms, and the ball hit him in the elbow and fell harmlessly to the turf. Led all Cardinals defenders with 11 total tackles. Find a spot for this guy. WR Reggie Virgil – The rookie looked very good once he started getting targets. With 5:46 before halftime, he caught a 14-yard pass. In the third quarter, Panthers S Isaiah Simmons was all over Virgil when the pass came as a bullet for nine yards early in Quarter 3. Nice 16-yard grab late in the game. This kid will push WR Kendrick Bourne for playing time, and maybe his job. S Isaiah Oliver – This kid was all over the field the entire time he got snaps. Eight total tackles. Solid game defensively. ——————————————————————— GEEKS Return game – First it was punt returner Harrison Wallace who, instead of moving towards the punt in flight, sorta waited around and instead of fielding the kick, let it bounce around until it was downed at the three-yard line. In the third quarter, Xavier Weaver muffed the kickoff in the end zone and had to fall on it. In all, one punt return for a 7.0 average and three kickoffs for a 24.7 yards per kick average. Yikes. Was surprised that Bam Knight wasn’t involved in kickoff returns. TD Tyus 📺 NBC pic.twitter.com/dC5gUdZKqP — Carolina Panthers (@Panthers) August 7, 2026 CB Elijah Culp – Playing way too much off his receiver all night. Then that stupid 15-yard penalty in the third quarter that not only gave Carolina a first down, but marched them down the field now in Arizona territory. Now keeping the drive alive, seven plays later, the Panthers scored a touchdown when, once again, Culp (#26) looked inside off the snap as the running back, Tyus, was in plain view flaring out. Culp came up but never looked at Tyus until he had snagged the short pass and was headed into the end zone. Culp finished with five tackles. A big run for Davis 📺 NBC pic.twitter.com/Ww0HDYBAL8 — Carolina Panthers (@Panthers) August 7, 2026 Stopping the run up the middle – When the game was second-teamers on both sides, the Cardinals had issues with sealing up gaps up the gut. The Panthers gashed the defense for a 36-yard run and a 26-yarder. Realize all the defensive tackle starters were standing along the sidelines in a Larry Fitzgerald #11 shirt, but most of these guys are fighting for the DT3 and DT4 roster spots. Arizona will only keep four DTs. This game showed some issues with the depth. Winning late, then losing – It’s just an exhibition game designed to show the coaches what they don’t know about the halfway point of the roster and down. The Panthers got the ball back with 1:55 remaining and losing by three as the defense couldn’t stop their progress. Last year’s version had seven games in which they were winning late in the contest…

full_text: The Cardinals did not win Thursday night’s Hall of Fame Game, but the team still came away with a phenomenal first look at rookie quarterback Carson Beck who got the start. Beck finished with 15 completions on 19 attempts, throwing for 188 yards and a touchdown pass to wideout Simi Fehoko. This performance is all the more impressive given just how underwhelming the initial football product has become in the year’s first preseason game. With three more preseason exhibitions to go, we’ll get to see a lot more of Beck in the weeks to come. Here’s to hoping the momentum continues. How did you enjoy the Hall of Fame Game? title: Atlanta Falcons training camp 2026: Day 8 news, notes, injuries, and updates
summary: FLOWERY BRANCH, Ga. — It was an overcast day at the Falcons’ training facility in Flowery Branch as Atlanta took the field for their eighth training camp practice of 2026. Kevin Stefanski spoke before practice, which consisted of team drills, some 7-on-7s and 11-on-11s, and some red zone work. The team will be in full […]
full_text: Jul 29, 2026; Atlanta, Falcons, USA; Atlanta Falcons head coach Kevin Stefanski on the field during the first day of training camp at IBM Performance Field. Mandatory Credit: Dale Zanine-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect FLOWERY BRANCH, Ga. — It was an overcast day at the Falcons’ training facility in Flowery Branch as Atlanta took the field for their eighth training camp practice of 2026. Kevin Stefanski spoke before practice, which consisted of team drills, some 7-on-7s and 11-on-11s, and some red zone work. The team will be in full pads for tomorrow’s Saturday Night Lights event at Lanier High School. Here’s my reporting from the day: Other notes and quotes from Friday’s practice: Kevin Stefanski did address Jalon Walker’s injury at the start of his availability, saying he was “disappointed,” but that Walker will be back. I wouldn’t expect that to be this season, unfortunately, but hopefully he’ll be 100% for 2027. Michael Penix Jr. was very limited on Friday, unsurprisingly. They aren’t going to push Penix and take risks with his long-term health and availability. He did get some work in 7-on-7s, hitting Drake London for a TD with excellent coverage from Xavier Watts, who almost turned it into a pick. Tua got quite a bit of work in 7s, 11s and red-zone drills. Assuming no setbacks with his lower back, I’d expect Tua to start next week’s preseason game. They’re rotating different players in and out, but in general Tua’s taking more snaps with the probable first team. Cooper Rush is getting more snaps than Jack Strand, who sailed a few passes today. The speed of the game is very different, but it does look like Strand is adjusting. I’m interested to see him in preseason action at closer to full speed. The kid has a serious arm. Matt Ryan ran some receiving drills with Drake London and Jahan Dotson during practice. “He always wants to throw,” London said after practice. My dream of Ryan unretiring and winning a ring with the Falcons this season remains intact (kidding, but also kinda not!) The energy was high today. Practice wasn’t full contact, but guys were playing fast and physical (lol sorry, I know many of you hate that phrasing by now, but it’s true). There was a bit of a battle for the ball between Avieon Terrell and Cash Jones that Jones talked with us about after practice, saying: “That’s our livelihood right there … the football. Any time you have a football, you don’t ever want to turn it over. We always — our goal is to give it back to the referee or the manager at any time possible, but (Aveion) is always working to get me better and all the other backs. So he tried to pop it up in the air, and we were trying to fight a little bit on the ground, but it was good work.” The DBs in particular were fun to watch on Friday. AJ Terrell prevented what would have been a gorgeous sideline catch by London by getting him out of bounds before he established possession. Cobee Bryant got flagged on one play with particularly sticky coverage (missed the WR’s jersey number). Drake London laid a massive block on Xavier Woods during 7-on-7s. After practice, Cash Jones spoke to the media. He says he doesn’t know much about this year’s UGA team, but he knows from his time in the program that they’re going to go in there, put their heads down, work hard, and have fun. On his former teammate at UGA, Zachariah Branch, he had high praise for his intelligence and versatility, saying, “He’s a super-smart kid.” Speaking of Zachariah Branch, I am once again calling bullshit on his “arrest” last spring. I know they dropped all of the charges, which was the right call, but there is zero chance he was “imposing” or intimidating enough to the cop(s) to justify arresting him in the first place. “Yeah, it’s fun to have a superhero back there,” Drake London said about Bijan Robinson’s hold-in ending and his return to practice. Tomorrow’s practice will be held under the Saturday Night Lights at Lanier High School. Full details can be found on the Falcons’ website . The Falcons will be in full pads, and based on the physicality we saw today, I think it’ll really be something. I’ll be there (and I’m hopeful Adnan will too!) and will have all of the coverage for you right here on The Falcoholic.

title: Falcons cut LB Troy Andersen, sign WR Kristian Wilkerson
summary: Troy Andersen arrived in the NFL with sky-high potential and many questions about whether he’d live up to it. We saw brief, tantalizing glimpses of the kind of player he could be, but injuries ultimately derailed his career as a Falcon. Now his time with Atlanta is over. Per Will McFadden with the Falcons, Andersen […]
full_text: ATLANTA, GEORGIA - SEPTEMBER 29: Troy Andersen (44) of the Atlanta Falcons reacts after an interception run back for a touchdown against the New Orleans Saints during the second quarter at Mercedes-Benz Stadium on September 29, 2024 in Atlanta, Georgia. (Photo by Todd Kirkland/Getty Images) | Getty Images Troy Andersen arrived in the NFL with sky-high potential and many questions about whether he’d live up to it. We saw brief, tantalizing glimpses of the kind of player he could be, but injuries ultimately derailed his career as a Falcon. Now his time with Atlanta is over. Per Will McFadden with the Falcons, Andersen has been cut . The Falcons signed former Raiders wide receiver Kristian Wilkerson in a corresponding move. It was a move that felt inevitable, but it’s still a gloomy day. Andersen had moments in his rookie season back in 2022 after the team made him a second round pick out of Montana State, forcing a fumble, piling up three quarterback hits, and showing intriguing coverage potential in five starts over 17 games. His 2023 season was almost entirely wiped out by injury, but he returned to a major role in 2024 and started to put it all together with 12 tackles against the Chiefs and a dazzling 17 tackle effort against the Saints with an interception returned for a touchdown. Injury reared its ugly head again, however, and Andersen appeared in just three games the rest of the way, looking like a shell of the linebacker he briefly was. Andersen would never suit up for another regular season game after that for the Falcons. Injury is the entire story here; Andersen may never have fully lived up to the potential his athleticism suggested, but his coverage skills alone would have bought him some kind of long-term role with this Falcons corps. Instead, his NFL career is now very much in question after he appeared in just nine games over the past four seasons and was on the physically unable to perform (PUP) list once again in training camp. Atlanta wanted to make it work and Andersen no doubt very badly wanted to get back out there, but it was evidently not going to happen. The Falcons will move forward with Divine Deablo, Christian Harris, Kendal Daniels, Harold Perkins Jr., and whoever wins the rock fight for a reserve/special teams role behind them. Wilkerson, meanwhile, will join a receiving corps still trying to figure out its depth options. The ex-Patriot, Bill, and Raider has appeared in nine NFL games, catching six passes on 11 targets for 60 yards and three touchdowns. Wilkerson has some special teams value and was a camp standout for the Bills last summer, so perhaps he can make some noise in the weeks ahead. We wish Andersen well wherever he ends up next and hope he can continue a once-promising NFL career wherever he lands.

title: No more excuses: How the Falcons’ spending spree shows they still don’t get it
summary: The Atlanta Falcons sport the second-longest active playoff drought despite being within one or two games of a playoff berth for several years in a row. It’s become second nature for people to blame those shortcomings on the handful of things that seem to go wrong each year and cost them one or two games. […]
full_text: Feb 24, 2026; Indianapolis, IN, USA; Atlanta Falcons general manager Ian Cunningham speaks at the NFL Scouting Combine at the Indiana Convention Center. Mandatory Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Atlanta Falcons sport the second-longest active playoff drought despite being within one or two games of a playoff berth for several years in a row. It’s become second nature for people to blame those shortcomings on the handful of things that seem to go wrong each year and cost them one or two games. Whether it’s quarterback injuries , questionable play-calling , or missed field goals , the margins are always razor thin in the NFL. However, the fact that something new and different comes up every year that costs the Falcons in their postseason bid suggests there are deeper issues beyond the easy scapegoats. That deeper issue is the Falcons’ organizational blind spot to their own shortcomings . Rather than a team that has missed the playoffs for a better part of a decade, Atlanta operates like an organization that has earned the benefit of the doubt. With new decision-makers at the top of the organization, it’s paramount that they regain that trust by breaking that playoff drought this season. Because unfortunately, the contracts the new top brass handed out over the past six weeks to tight end Kyle Pitts and guard Matthew Bergeron appear to be more exercises in that lack of self-awareness. Not because Pitts or Bergeron didn’t deserve to get paid, but mostly because both players had a lot to prove in 2026 before earning such expensive contracts. But the Falcons decided to pay both players preemptively, which embodies the team’s inability to see their own imperfections. Kyle Pitts and the illusion of All-Pro potential Starting with Pitts, who in June inked a contract averaging $18 million annually , making him the third-highest-paid TE in football. It also makes him paid higher than a large number of No. 2 wide receivers, as Michael Pittman, Romeo Doubs, and Wan’Dale Robinson all signed deals in the $17 million-per-year range this offseason to be the secondary targets for their respective teams. It’s easy to see why Atlanta paid up after Pitts earned second-team All-Pro honors , until you actually scrutinize why he saw an uptick in 2025. One thing that certainly helped Pitts’ All-Pro bid was that several of the league’s top tight ends in Brock Bowers, Tucker Kraft, George Kittle, and Sam LaPorta all had injury-plagued 2025 seasons. It also helped that Pitts was sharing the field with a Falcons wide receiver corps that was also ravaged by injuries , inconsistency, and absence . It’s no coincidence that Pitts’ best seasons were 2021 and 2025. The former was a season when he didn’t have to share the field with Drake London, and the latter was the season when London was most limited by a knee injury that basically wiped him out for the final seven games. Pitts’ production is tied to empty receiver rooms In 2021, with Calvin Ridley stepping away from the team after five games, Russell Gage had to step into the role as the team’s top wideout and didn’t really start living up to that billing until after Thanksgiving. That left a lesser version of Olamide Zaccheaus and Tajae Sharpe as the receivers that Pitts was sharing the field with. While people like to attribute Pitts’ rookie-season success to the steady presence of veteran quarterback Matt Ryan, it becomes clearer in hindsight that the lack of viable alternate pass-catching options at wide receiver led Ryan to force the ball to Pitts more. History repeated itself in 2025. When London missed half the year, secondary options like Darnell Mooney, Ray-Ray McCloud, and KhaDarel Hodge vanished as well. Pitts wasn’t competing for targets in an elite passing attack, but rather monopolizing targets playing across practice-squad-level options like David Sills and Casey Washington. This led to a spike in production when he averaged 2.28 yards per route run per PFF after London’s knee flared up. That figure exceeded the 2.23 yards per route run by Ja’Marr Chase last year, exemplifying high-end No. 1 receiver production. However, in the 10 games that Pitts played alongside a relatively healthy London before the latter’s knee injury, his yards per route run were 1.36, marginally better than his 1.33 figure from 2024. Comparatively, that figure matches the production of Noah Fant from 2025, who signed a deal averaging about $4.4 million per year this offseason. Pitts’ production in the front half of 2025 was marginally better than McCloud’s in 2024, who averaged 1.25 yards per route run, far from deserving of being paid like a premier tight end or No. 2 wideout. The larger point is Pitts needed to show in 2026 whether he was worth such a high premium by again producing at a high level while sharing the field with London and, hopefully, not the dregs of the wide receiver position. Yet, the Falcons just handed out that massive contract, assuming Pitts will live up to the hype. It’s no different from how every year we hope the Falcons will bounce back and make the playoffs, yet they fail to deliver. Bergeron got rewarded before even taking the test With Bergeron, I don’t need a bunch of fancy stats to illustrate the team’s decision to jump the gun, beyond the fact that Bergeron has never graded out as a top-20 guard according to PFF. Yet, the Falcons felt it necessary to give him a contract that pays him like he’s the best guard in football. The price of guards has been inflated in recent years, with high-end contracts handed out to other mid-tier starters like Robert Hunt, Aaron Banks, and Zion Johnson, so perhaps a market markup was inevitable whenever Bergeron’s extension came due. But the Falcons still had an entire season to evaluate him under offensive line coach Bill Callahan. They could have tested his fit in Kevin Stefanski’s new scheme before writing the check. Assuming he passed both tests, the team would have received far less pushback from paying a premium for the only starting lineman entering the prime of his career. But instead, the Falcons rewarded him with an “A” before he even sat down to take the exam. Bergeron is a solid guard, but he hasn’t proven he’s one of the best guards in football. He needs to show that first before it’s just accepted. Just like the Falcons are a capable team that has missed the playoffs for eight years and needs to show it can break that streak before it re-earns the benefit of the doubt. New names, same delusions: Why trust must be earned It’s easy for many to dismiss these complaints and trust that the decision-makers in general manager Ian Cunningham, head coach Kevin Stefanski, and El Presidente Matt Ryan know what they’re doing. But I ask why? None of these people have established they can build a winner. Both Cunningham and Ryan are first-timers in their respective roles, and Stefanski’s recent body of work in Cleveland strongly hints that he lost all the mojo that earned him NFL Coach of the Year honors twice in six years. The man hasn’t produced a quality offense in four seasons, and twice had to strip himself of play-calling duties because he wasn’t capable of making it work. From top to bottom, 2026 is meant to be a “prove-it” year for everybody in the organization, whether it’s the front office, the coaching staff, the quarterbacks , Pitts, or Bergeron. But the Falcons keep handing out top-of-market deals to unproven entities, and their only response is, “Trust me, bro. “ This organization has squandered any trust by its inability to get over the hump the last eight years. While we hope that Pitts and Bergeron, now fueled and inspired by their paydays, play the best we’ve seen from them to date, the new decision-makers seem to be falling right in line with those same delusions of grandeur that doomed their predecessors. Cunningham, Stefanski, and Ryan are not to blame for the past eight years, but they blew a golden opportunity to…

The Ravens had worked out three total linebackers during the week before adding Johnson. Ravens are signing LB Jamon Johnson, per source. — Jeff Zrebiec (@jeffzrebiec) August 7, 2026 Johnson, 24, is a Maryland native who attended high school in Baltimore. Johnson was a defensive contributor on Georgia’s back-to-back national title teams in 2021 and 2022. He later transferred to Kentucky for his senior campaign. Johnson went undrafted last year and signed with the Packers in April. He started one game and recorded 10 tackles with a pass breakup in 67 total defensive snaps. For the Ravens, Johnson will help bolster their depth chart at the linebacker spot. Teddye Buchanan has yet to return to on-field action as he recovers from a torn ACL and Roquan Smith is unlikely to see much if any playing time in the preseason. The rest of the group consists of Trenton Simpson, Carl Jones and Jay Higgins IV, who made the roster last year as an undrafted free agent. As a prospect, Johnson profiled as a strong run defender with good defensive instincts. His best chance to stick around long-term for the Ravens would be to stand out on special teams and carve out a role for himself there.

title: How have Buffalo Bills homegrown contract extensions fared in Brandon Beane era?
summary: The Buffalo Bills extending right guard O’Cyrus Torrence as they finished training camp at St. John Fisher University got me thinking… how have Brandon Beane’s draft-and-develop contract extensions fared in his tenure as the team’s GM? In 2025, Beane signed Greg Rousseau, Khalil Shakir, Christian Benford, Terrel Bernard, and James Cook to second contracts, and […]
full_text: ROCHESTER, NEW YORK - JULY 29: General manager Brandon Beane of the Buffalo Bills addresses the media following practice during training camp at St. John Fisher University on July 29, 2026 in Rochester, New York. (Photo by Joe Hrycych/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Buffalo Bills extending right guard O’Cyrus Torrence as they finished training camp at St. John Fisher University got me thinking… how have Brandon Beane’s draft-and-develop contract extensions fared in his tenure as the team’s GM? In 2025, Beane signed Greg Rousseau, Khalil Shakir, Christian Benford, Terrel Bernard, and James Cook to second contracts, and now Torrence enters that growing list of homegrown talents secured long term by the organization. Let’s take a full scale look at how the deals have ultimately fared to create a barometer of sorts for Beane and Co. on these financial decisions. Due to my love of the NFL Draft, I’ll run through each player based on draft year. And I’ll label each outcome as “successful, OK, and bad.” Josh Allen No lengthy description needed, and he’s gotten multiple long-term deals in Buffalo. He’s worth every penny. And then some. Verdict: Successful Taron Johnson Johnson’s initial extension in Buffalo was a three-year, $24 million pact in October 2021, and the super pesky nickel corner rewarded the Bills with durable play that culminated in a second-team All-Pro distinction in 2023. The more recent three-year, $30M extension with $17.8M guaranteed wasn’t nearly as fruitful, but Beane’s original decision to lock up Johnson in 2021 was very prudent. Verdict: Successful Ed Oliver Because Oliver was a first-round pick, the Bills had time to take a little longer with this decision thanks to the fifth-year option being secured the year before. However, after his fourth NFL season, the defensive tackle signed a four-year, $68M with $45M in total guarantees, a deal on which he’s still playing. When healthy, Oliver has become one of the Bills best defensive players, even if he’s never reached true routine game-wrecker status. It’s not a slam dunk of a verdict here, but I’m going with this as a successful extension, as the $24.5M guaranteed at signing in Oliver’s extension now ranks as the 22nd-most among defensive tackles. Verdict: Successful Dawson Knox Knox signed a four-year, $53.6M extension in early September 2022 after a nine-touchdown third season with the Bills. His 49 receptions during the regular season in 2021 remain a career high. While Knox has become a consummate three-down pro at tight end, a fantastic mentor for Dalton Kincaid, and one of the key camaraderie pieces on the team, the $31M in total guarantees he received in the initial extension would’ve ranked fifth among all tight ends today (!)… had he not agreed to renegotiate his deal after 2024. The three year, $20M extension Knox signed in 2026 is more commensurate with his production. Verdict: OK / Bad Greg Rousseau While the $80M total price tag on the four-year Rousseau extension may have seemed lofty, one year later his $38.7M fully-guaranteed-at-signing figure is now the 13th-highest among edge rushers. Rousseau has been developed very well — albeit not unbelievably — by the Bills since he was the club’s first-round pick in 2021 after opting out of his final season at the University of Miami due to COVID and entering the league at 21 years old. Has he regularly been a menace? Not really. He’s another consummate three-down player from the McDermott era who’s absolutely a good player and at times a great player but has yet to become a genuine star or superstar. Verdict: Successful / OK Spencer Brown Brown signed his September 2024 contract worth a grand total of $72M across four new years. And while that $72M is still the sixth-most among right tackles, the $19.8M guaranteed at signing is 17th-highest at the position. Brown has become one of the best young right tackles in the NFL and core piece of Buffalo’s sturdy offensive line. This is an extension Beane is likely thrilled he got ahead of. Verdict: Success James Cook Speaking of that, given what we’ve seen recently with new money for Bijan Robinson, Jonathan Taylor, and Jahmyr Gibbs, the Bills front office probably can’t be more relieved the Cook extension got done when it did, in August 2025. The $15.2M Cook received in his four-year, $46M deal is now the 17th-highest among running backs. Robinson and Taylor got $37.5M and $19.3M fully guaranteed at signing respectively. Still waiting on the full guarantees in Gibbs’ deal. Oh yeah, and Cook led the NFL in rushing in 2026 and has yet to reached 1,000 career touches in the NFL. Verdict: Success Terrel Bernard I’ll keep this one short because, when healthy, Bernard has been a quarterback of the defense and one of the better, splash-play creating coverage linebackers in football. His 2025 was plagued by injury, as has sizable chunks of the past few seasons. It’s not necessarily fair to Beane nor Bernard, but that is the nature of the beast in the NFL. The four-year, $42M deal Bernard signed in 2025 featured $14.1M guaranteed at signing, which is the 24th-most at the position. It’s hardly an expensive deal, relatively speaking. If Bernard can stay healthy in 2026, this verdict could jump all the way to the successful label. Verdict: Bad Khalil Shakir I’ve loved Shakir since his time as a prospect coming out of Boise State, and he’s developed into an elite-level YAC receiver with reliable hands as a professional. Shakir’s four-year, $60.2M extension seems sizable, yet the $18.1M guaranteed at signing is now the 43rd-highest (!) among all receivers. Massive win here. Verdict: Successful Christian Benford Benford deserves more love as one of the better outside cornerbacks in football, and Beane likely loves he got ahead of the eruption at the cornerback market. Benford’s four-year, $69M deal includes a mere $18.8M fully guaranteed, which is now the 31st-most at the cornerback spot. Crazy, right? And Benford will only turn 26 in September. He’s not nearly as flashy as other top corners, doesn’t have an early-round draft pedigree, and didn’t play at a Power 4 school. But he has seven interceptions and 29 pass breakups in the regular season in his first four years in the NFL and is a tackling machine on the outside. Verdict: Successful Total Tally Succesful: 7 Succesful / OK: 1 OK / Bad: 1 Bad: 1 What do you think about Beane’s track record of contract extensions?

title: Who is the next Buffalo Bills contract extension?
summary: The Buffalo Bills have locked up O’Cyrus Torrence with a massive four-year extension just a few months after extending Connor McGovern. In 2025, it was James Cook and Christian Benford and Josh Allen and Greg Rousseau and Terrel Bernard and Khalil Shakir. So that begs the question: Who is next for a Buffalo Bills contract […]
full_text: ORCHARD PARK, NEW YORK - JANUARY 04: Alec Anderson #70 of the Buffalo Bills poses with the crowd after defeating the New York Jets at Highmark Stadium on January 04, 2026 in Orchard Park, New York. (Photo by Jason Miller/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Buffalo Bills have locked up O’Cyrus Torrence with a massive four-year extension just a few months after extending Connor McGovern. In 2025, it was James Cook and Christian Benford and Josh Allen and Greg Rousseau and Terrel Bernard and Khalil Shakir. So that begs the question: Who is next for a Buffalo Bills contract extension? Here’s my list in order of likelihood. I don’t anticipate any of these happening before the season starts, but a midseason extension could be possible for one or two of these guys. I only went with contracts above a couple million bucks, so sorry to the likes of Ty Johnson. DT Ed Oliver Free agent in 2028 Ed Oliver is a game-changer on a team without many of them. He has one more year left on his deal in 2027 but his cap hit jumps from $13.7 to $28.3 million next year because of the pushed out cap hits catching up to the Bills. Oliver will only be 29 this December. I think this is a no-brainer and could be done before the season starts. Buffalo doesn’t usually extend guys with two years left on their deal, so expect it to be a modest in time frame with one or two years. OL Alec Anderson Free agent in 2027 I think they could extend him during the season if he wins the left guard job. Here’s the scenario. David Edwards was the sixth offensive lineman, then the starter at left guard when he earned a two-year, $6 million contract. If Anderson wins the job and signs that type of short extension, it’s an absolute win. S C.J. Gardner-Johnson Free agent in 2027 Currently the starter at safety, if he makes an early season impact, you can see a scenario where the Bills offer him a two-year extension. CJGJ has bounced around the last few years and finding an organization that “gets him” has to be something he would embrace. TE Dalton Kincaid Free agent in 2028 Kincaid needs to prove he’s healthy, but if he does this is a priority for next offseason. His 2027 cap hit is $8.1 million so they can lower than with a midsize extension. A Cole Kmet/Jake Ferguson four-year, $50 million contract would place him seventh in the NFL, so it’s probably going to be a touch higher than that. LB Dorian Williams Free agent in 2027 The fact that Kincaid is higher than Williams despite the linebacker being a free agent after 2026 should tell you something. The Bills drafted Kaleb Elarms-Orr this offseason and he has looked stellar early while Williams was out with an offseason injury. Williams would have been much higher on this list a couple months ago. S Cole Bishop Free agent in 2028 If Bishop adjusts to the Jim Leonhard defense as well as I think he is going to, Buffalo may lock him up as early as February 2027. He is already setting himself up as one of the leaders on the defense. ED Michael Hoecht Free agent in 2028 I think he needs to play a full season healthy, but if he’s a man on fire and approaches double-digit sacks, he could be a 2027 offseason priority. OL Lloyd Cushenberry Free agent in 2027 If he wins the left guard job, the same scenario could play out with him that I described with Alec Anderson. They could even put the two of them in a room with one contract and do a reverse auction. Which one is willing to go lower as our left guard. Since he’s clearly behind Anderson in camp, I’ll add him last on the list. Bills players who just missed the list WR Josh Palmer If Palmer plays a big role this year and Keon Coleman busts, there is a scenario where the Bills pop two more years on the Palmer deal. K Tyler Bass He is a free agent after 2027 and already 8th in average salary. If he has a good season, they will tack on a couple years and some cash. WR Keon Coleman If I am the Bills, I don’t pay Coleman even after one really good season, so he seems more like an August 2027 extension to me at the earliest. LB Joe Andreesen Andreesen is going to be a restricted free agent next year. The right of first refusal is $3.8 million, so they won’t tag him with that. I can see him signing a three-year deal or something as a special teams stalwart. RB Ty Johnson I don’t think he’s going to sign a big enough contract to warrant being on the list, but he’s a free agent after the season. Tell me how I’m wrong. Tell me how I’m right. I’d love to chat with you in the comments about why Ed Oliver is the right answer here. Join the conversation! title: O’Cyrus Torrence extension makes it hard for Bills to keep Dion Dawkins in 2027
summary: In every budget, when you pay for one thing you are making a value assessment on another. In the case of the Buffalo Bills, an O’Cyrus Torrence extension likely means saying goodbye to another member of their expensive offensive line. Yes, general manager Brandon Beane has said he values protecting Josh Allen. That doesn’t mean […]
full_text: BUFFALO, NEW YORK - NOVEMBER 8: Buffalo Bills players Dion Dawkins and O'Cyrus Torrence watch in the audience during Friday night Smackdown at KeyBank Center on November 8, 2024 in Buffalo, New York. (Photo by WWE/Getty Images) | WWE via Getty Images In every budget, when you pay for one thing you are making a value assessment on another. In the case of the Buffalo Bills, an O’Cyrus Torrence extension likely means saying goodbye to another member of their expensive offensive line. Yes, general manager Brandon Beane has said he values protecting Josh Allen. That doesn’t mean he’s willing to sacrifice his defensive rebuild for it. Buffalo Bills salary cap in 2027 is tight According to Spotrac, the Bills have the second-most cap space already accounted for in 2027 and are a staggering $54 million over the projected cap. They’ll be able to manipulate that number with salary conversions, so it’s not as dire as you might think, but four of the players at the top of the cap hits are 30 or older next year; Josh Allen, DJ Moore, Ed Oliver, and Dion Dawkins. The Bills have been pushing out cap hits on Allen and other players for several years now, and that starts to catch up eventually. Every dollar that is paid eventually gets accounted for. The recent mid-to-high-money deal for players like Terrel Bernard, James Cook, Khalil Shakir, Christian Benford, Spencer Brown, and Greg Rousseau are extending past their initial low cap hits into maturity with the prorated monies from three seasons now hitting the cap at the same time. Buffalo Bills offensive line spending is pricey The Torrence extension means the Bills have four big offensive line salaries on their roster. Here is the list in terms of annual value: Dion Dawkins ($20 million/season) O’Cyrus Torrence ($19.5 million/season) Spencer Brown ($18 million/season) Connor McGovern ($13 million/season) How many teams have four players with more than a $13 million average annual salary on their offensive line? The numbers are low. The Philadelphia Eagles have four players making more than $17 million per season on their current deals. The Kansas City Chiefs have three over $15 million per year. Carolina Panthers have three over $13 million. Why Dion Dawkins is the most likely cap casualty Before we get started here, I like Dion Dawkins. I’ve interviewed him. We’ve seen him on Hard Knocks and at NFL Honors. He’s a good dude and we like him. Let’s admit all that right up front. Dawkins is currently set to make just under $20 million in cash in 2027. Neat season is the final year of his deal and he’s going to be 33 heading into the season. If they are looking to reload the offensive line with younger players, Dawkins clearly sticks out for his age — he is three years older than any other player on the OL. Why the Bills would release Dion Dawkins after 2026 Keeping four players on big contracts at one position is not something Brandon Beane has done in the past, specifically on the offensive line. (He also never paid a guard before, so there is a first time for everything.) If Dawkins begins to fall off in 2026 and the 2027 salary doesn’t make sense any more, they can release him and save $11 million in 2027 cap space. That’s a sizable chunk of space for the Bills to go out and sign or draft his replacement. They could think about popping Spencer Brown over to left tackle or promoting one of the options on their roster currently. They drafted Jude Bowry in the fourth round in 2026, Chase Lundt in the fifth round in 2025, and Tylan Grable in the sixth round in 2024. Ryan Van Demark stepped in for Dawkins last year and played well and will be a free agent after the season with the Vikings. Why the Bills would keep Dion Dawkins after 2026 If Dawkins continues his solid play in 2026, they could keep him in 2027 for just under $20 million. Yes they would have a very expensive offensive line. But that left tackle number would be 16th in the NFL in terms of left tackle spending, meaning they might not be able to sign a better option for a cheaper contract. That would continue to protect Josh Allen in his low 30s with James Cook and DJ Moore before that trio ages up a bit more and would allow the Bills to continue stacking defensive talent with draft picks. Keep the offensive players in their prime protected and build the other spots. The fifth starter on the Bills OL will also likely be a free agent after 2026 — Alec Anderson, Lloyd Cushenberry, and Austin Corbett are all on one-year deal currently — so having a potentially brand new blind side for Josh Allen in 2027 isn’t really appealing. Leave your thoughts and questions in the comments section below and I’ll happily come back and debate or answer questions. Positional spending and budgets is something folks don’t often think about over thw course of multiple seasons, so it’s a good thought exercise.

title: O’Cyrus Torrence contract extension: What does it mean for the Bills and the offensive line?
summary: The Buffalo Bills have locked up another major piece of their offensive line, agreeing to a four-year, $78.4 million contract extension with right guard O’Cyrus Torrence. The extension carries an new money average annual value of $19.5 million and includes $46 million in total guarantees as first reported by Adam Schefter. He’s now the seventh-highest […]
full_text: PITTSBURGH, PENNSYLVANIA - NOVEMBER 30: O'Cyrus Torrence #64 of the Buffalo Bills warms up before a game against the Pittsburgh Steelers at Acrisure Stadium on November 30, 2025 in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Justin K. Aller/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Buffalo Bills have locked up another major piece of their offensive line, agreeing to a four-year, $78.4 million contract extension with right guard O’Cyrus Torrence. The extension carries an new money average annual value of $19.5 million and includes $46 million in total guarantees as first reported by Adam Schefter. He’s now the seventh-highest paid guard in the NFL in new money average. But there is another way to look at the deal from Buffalo’s perspective. Torrence still had the final year of his rookie contract remaining in 2026. Add that to the new extension and the Bills now effectively have their 26 year-old starting right guard under contract for the next five seasons for approximately $82 million. That works out to roughly $16.4 million per season across the entire five-year window. And for a player who simply hasn’t missed games, there is plenty of value in that security. Why the Bills extended O’Cyrus Torrence Torrence has played all 51 regular-season games since Buffalo selected him 59th overall in the second round of the 2023 NFL Draft, in addition to every Bills playoff game during that span. His availability goes well beyond simply dressing on Sundays. Torrence played 100% of Buffalo’s offensive snaps as a rookie in 2023, followed by 93.1% in 2024 and 99.7% last season. For three years, he has essentially been a permanent fixture at right guard. Now he’s being paid like one. How does the O’Cyrus Torrence deal compare with the rest of NFL guards? The $19.5 million annual value comes in considerably higher than earlier market projections that placed Torrence around $13.1 million per season. The guard market continued moving this offseason, however, including Joe Tippmann’s four-year, $66.4 million extension with the New York Jets. Torrence’s deal blew past that number. O’Cyrus Torrence’s new deal makes an expensive Bills offensive line Buffalo is now paying significant money across its offensive line. Left tackle Dion Dawkins received a three-year, $60.6 million extension in 2024, while right tackle Spencer Brown signed a four-year, $72 million extension later that year. This past March they also secured center Connor McGovern to a four-year, $52 million extension. But if there is one place the Bills should be comfortable investing, it is in front of Josh Allen. How is the O’Cyrus Torrence deal structured? The next piece of the Torrence contract will be particularly interesting. The four-year, $78.4 million headline tells us what the extension is worth, but the structure will tell us much more about Buffalo’s actual commitment. With $46 million guaranteed, how much is fully guaranteed at signing? How much cash will Torrence receive over the first three years? And does the fourth year contain a large non-guaranteed salary that gives Buffalo an eventual exit point? It also provides context for the future of left tackle Dion Dawkins depending on where the cap numbers start to pick up. Those details will determine whether this is truly a four-year commitment or another contract structured to give the Bills flexibility on the back end. For now, we know this much: Buffalo didn’t wait for Torrence to reach free agency and let the rest of the NFL determine his value. Does the O’Cyrus Torrence deal make sense for the Bills? I’ll admit, I did not anticipate Torrence coming in this far north of Joe Tippmann’s deal. At $19.5 million per year, the AAV is a bit surprising and certainly higher than where I expected this contract to land. But if I’ve learned anything from covering Bills contracts, it’s to wait until all of the numbers come out before making a final judgment. The headline numbers only tell part of the story. Once we see the guarantees, bonuses, cash flow and year-by-year cap hits, we’ll get a much better idea of what Buffalo actually committed to Torrence. There is a beautiful art to contract structuring, and the Bills have become pretty good at making a big number on paper look much different once you get underneath it. O’Cyrus Torrence is now locked in for the next five years, hopefully through the prime of his career. And the Bills have made it very clear what they believe that stability is worth it.
author: Sara Larson

title: Buffalo Bills 2026 scouting report: cornerback D.J. Miller
summary: The Buffalo Bills shuffled the deck in their defensive backfield a bit last week, releasing a player I was high on entering this offseason in Wande Owens. Moves on the fringes don’t often draw big headlines, but in the summertime, it’s often those moves that coaches sweat the most. How can they find players who […]
full_text: KANSAS CITY, MO - MAY 30: Kansas City Chiefs cornerback D.J. Miller (38) catches a ball during OTA's on May 30, 2024 at the Chiefs practice facility in Kansas City, MO. (Photo by Scott Winters/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Buffalo Bills shuffled the deck in their defensive backfield a bit last week, releasing a player I was high on entering this offseason in Wande Owens. Moves on the fringes don’t often draw big headlines, but in the summertime, it’s often those moves that coaches sweat the most. How can they find players who fit their system that, perhaps, other teams have overlooked? In today’s installment of “91 players in 91 days,” we discuss a cornerback who views himself as more of a Swiss Army knife than a mere corner. _____________________________________________________________________________ Name: D.J. Miller Number: 46 Position: CB Height/Weight: 5’10” 193 lbs. Age: 25 (26 on 8/11/2026) Experience/Draft: 1; signed with the Kansas City Chiefs following the 2024 NFL Draft College: Kent State Acquired: Signed with Buffalo on 7/31/2026 Financial situation (per Spotrac): Miller’s one-year contract is worth $885,000 overall. That number also represents his cap hit if he makes the 53-man roster. Buffalo will not carry any dead cap charge if they release him. 2025 Recap: Miller spent the 2025 season in two places, starting out in the UFL with the Michigan Panthers before spending training camp with the NFL’s Detroit Lions. While with Michigan, he totaled 29 tackles, two interceptions, and eight pass breakups. Michigan made the UFL Playoffs, and in two postseason games, Miller totaled nine tackles and three pass breakups as the Panthers lost the UFL Championship Game to the DC Defenders. In the preseason with the Lions, Miller was around the ball often, just as he had been while playing in the UFL. In two NFL exhibition games, Miller had 10 tackles, one tackle for loss, and two pass breakups. He did not make Detroit’s roster, and he was not signed to any team’s practice squad following final cuts in August. Positional outlook: Miller is one of six players listed at cornerback on Buffalo’s current roster. Toriano Pride Jr., Dee Alford, Christian Benford, Maxwell Hairston, and Davison Igbinosun are the others. Te’Cory Couch, Kani Walker, Jordan Hancock, and Jordan Dunbar are all listed at defensive back but play corner. 2026 Offseason: Miller returned to the UFL in the spring, playing for the Colombus Aviators. He once again played well, totaling three interceptions, one of which he returned for a touchdown, nine pass breakups, and 24 tackles (one tackle for loss) in the spring league. 2026 Season outlook: Miller has a long road to making the roster, but he does a lot of things that coaches love. He can play multiple spots in the secondary, something highlighted in the team’s bio that they posted when they signed him. He has a great work ethic—something that was also highlighted in his bio—and he has produced at multiple stops throughout his time playing football. He views himself as a defensive back, not a particular positional player, and that desire to be a good football player at any spot in the defensive secondary could significantly benefit him this summer. Miller is only 5’10”, but his wingspan is 74”. He ran a 4.56-second forty-yard dash at Kent State’s pro day back in 2024, a solid but unspectacular time, but he also completed the three-cone drill in an excellent 6.65 seconds. His vertical was measured at 38.5”, as well. All of these numbers indicate that Miller is a player who, athletically at least, could help Buffalo as it transitions to a more attack-oriented defense. Can he showcase enough ability to unseat someone else who likely is in front of him at the moment? That last question is the big one, and I’m not sure that Miller is going to be able to do it. With Benford, Hairston, Igbinosun, and Alford all written in Sharpie on the 53-man roster, that doesn’t leave much space for other corners. Miller’s versatility helps, but he’d have to be better than Hancock, who projects as a reserve and special teams player already, as well as someone like Pride Jr. or veteran safeties like Damar Hamlin or Geno Stone. D.J. Miller has an outside chance at making the 53-man roster, but ultimately, I think he’s auditioning for a spot on the practice squad over these next few weeks.

title: 2026 Season Opener Countdown: 37 Days Remaining
summary: Here at Cat Scratch Reader we have counted down the final 100 days leading up to the Carolina Panthers season opener by for at least the past ten years. We’ve always done this by highlighting the current player on the roster whose jersey number matches the day on the countdown. This year, we decided to […]
full_text: HOUSTON, TX - SEPTEMBER 29: Head Coach Ron Rivera of the Carolina Panthers walks around the field before a game against the Houston Texans at NRG Stadium on September 29, 2019 in Houston, Texas. The Panthers defeated the Texans 16-10. (Photo by Wesley Hitt/Getty Images) | Getty Images Here at Cat Scratch Reader we have counted down the final 100 days leading up to the Carolina Panthers season opener by for at least the past ten years. We’ve always done this by highlighting the current player on the roster whose jersey number matches the day on the countdown. This year, we decided to change that up a bit by counting down our own list of the Top 100 Panthers of all time. This does not correspond to jersey number, does not need to be somebody who wore a jersey, and will in no way be controversial. #37. Ron Rivera The Panthers haven’t had a lot of coaches in their relatively brief existence in the NFL, but two in particular stand out head and shoulders above the rest. The first was John Fox , who came in at number 45 on our countdown. The second was the coach that followed right after him and ended up being almost a carbon copy—Ron Rivera. Rivera’s start in the NFL came as a rotational linebacker for the Bears in the 80s and 90s, including on the infamous 1985 team that won the Super Bowl. He briefly went in to the media after his playing career before rejoining the Bears as a defensive assistant in 1997. He again left for a short time to join Andy Reid’s staff on the Eagles as linebackers coach before again returning to the Bears, this time as defensive coordinator. He departed after three years to join the Chargers, where he started as linebackers coach before being promoted to defensive coordinator. He was hired as head coach in Carolina in 2011 after the firing of John Fox. Rivera had long been a hot name in coaching circles, so his hiring was seen as a win for the Panthers and a long overdue promotion. While the Panthers had a significant bounce back from the wayward ending of Fox’s tenure, the team struggled to win close games with Rivera’s uber conservative decision making a common scapegoat. In his third season, with the Panthers floundering and his seat heating up, Rivera flipped his decision making and started leaving the offense on the field for more fourth downs. The Panthers went on a franchise best winning streak in response, and the Riverboat Ron nickname was born. The Panthers ended up making the playoffs that season with a 12-4 record. The following season didn’t go as well, but Rivera still got the team into the playoffs with a 7-8-1 record by leading them to four straight wins to close the season. That proved to be a bridge to what would be the best Panthers season of all time. Led by MVP Cam Newton and an opportunistic defense, Rivera’s Panthers won their first 14 games of the season en route to a 15-1 record. They carried that momentum into the playoffs, where dominant wins over the Seahawks and Cardinals took the team to the Super Bowl. There, they were taken down by the Broncos’ dominant defense. The Panthers struggled to recapture that form in the following years. They did rebound in 2017 to go 11-5 but were unceremoniously bounced from the playoffs by the Saints. Both of the following seasons ended with losing records, and Rivera wouldn’t even see out the end of the second of those. He was fired in 2019 after the team started losing games again after the magic of the Kyle Allen experience had worn off. The Ron Rivera era is kind of hard to accurately describe. On one hand, he’s been inarguably the most successful Panthers coach in history with the most wins in franchise history along with three division titles and four playoff appearances. On the other hand, he had six losing seasons compared to just three winning seasons and never seemed to consistently get the team over the hump despite some very talented rosters in some respects. It’s the best we’ve ever had it, but it also feels like we could have maybe even had more. However you slice it, Rivera was the best coach the Panthers have ever had, and he’s a great human being. That slots him in at number 37 on the top 100 Panthers of all time.

title: Bears sign veteran SAF Xavier Woods
summary: The Bears have signed veteran safety Xavier Woods, the team announced on Friday. As a corresponding move, they have given defensive back Dallas Flowers an injured/reserve designation. Woods, who turned 31 in July, is entering his tenth season in the NFL. Not to be confused with the wrestler of the same name, Woods has been […]
full_text: LAS VEGAS, NEVADA - OCTOBER 12: Xavier Woods #25 of the Tennessee Titans stands on the field during the first half of an NFL football game against the Las Vegas Raiders at Allegiant Stadium on October 12, 2025 in Las Vegas, Nevada. (Photo by Brooke Sutton/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Bears have signed veteran safety Xavier Woods, the team announced on Friday . As a corresponding move, they have given defensive back Dallas Flowers an injured/reserve designation. Woods, who turned 31 in July, is entering his tenth season in the NFL. Not to be confused with the wrestler of the same name , Woods has been a starter at safety for a majority of those seasons, having started in 121 of the 134 games he’s played. He began his career as a sixth-round pick from Louisiana Tech by the Cowboys, for whom he played four seasons. He overlapped for one season with Bears defensive backs coach Al Harris in Dallas, who was his defensive backs coach in 2020. After his rookie deal expired after the 2020 season, he bounced around the league for a bit, having stints with the Vikings, Panthers, and Titans. In his 2025 season with the Titans, Woods ended the year with 39 tackles, two interceptions, three pass deflections, and a sack. He played in 11 games for Tennessee, starting in ten of them. His 75.9 PFN Safety Impact Score ranked No. 42 among 85 qualified safeties, generally placing him as an average starting option. Notable safeties he ended the year with a higher score than include Budda Baker, Malaki Starks, Jaquan Brisker, and Javon Bullard. The Bears’ decision to sign Woods makes sense, given the recent injury that Coby Bryant suffered . He’s anticipated to miss the first few weeks of the regular season with a hyperextended knee, bone bruise, and small fracture. It’s worth noting that Elijah Hicks, who has been on Chicago’s active roster each of the last four seasons, is also currently on the PUP list with a shin injury. Woods figures to compete with Cam Lewis for a starting safety spot alongside Dillon Thieneman while Bryant recovers. Once Bryant returns, Woods could still serve as a valuable backup with the versatility that Bears defensive coordinator Dennis Allen likes in his safeties; he took 27.3% of his defensive snaps in the box in 2025, as well as 14.9% in the slot. New #Bears safety Xavier Woods had a 75.9 PFN Safety Impact Score in 2025 That’s a higher score than several notable names like Budda Baker, Malaki Starks, Jaquan Brisker, and Javon Bullard pic.twitter.com/gyFtmXHHd6 — Jacob Infante (@jacobinfante24) August 7, 2026
