title: Is Dennis Allen Responsible for Defensive Injuries?
summary: Chicago media personality Dan Bernstein recently made a claim that Dennis Allen’s coaching style makes his players more injury prone, citing that many around the Saints felt Allen was the cause of their injury-plagued 2024 season. He also claims that something in his coaching approach has caused the rash of injuries to Chicago’s defense since […]
full_text: Chicago media personality Dan Bernstein recently made a claim that Dennis Allen’s coaching style makes his players more injury prone , citing that many around the Saints felt Allen was the cause of their injury-plagued 2024 season. He also claims that something in his coaching approach has caused the rash of injuries to Chicago’s defense since Allen showed up in January 2025. Today, I want to look at the evidence to see if the numbers back up the claim that Allen’s teams are consistently injured. Correlation alone doesn’t prove causation, but we don’t need to worry about why injuries follow Allen around unless we see whether they actually do. The Setup The metric I’m going to use is Adjusted Games Lost, which is published by FTN Fantasy . Here is their explanation of their system: “Adjusted games lost doesn’t just add up total injuries. It accounts for both absent players and those playing at less than 100%, and it specifically measures injuries to expected starters and important situational players rather than little-used backups.” In short, Adjusted Games Lost (AGL) tries to measure the total impact injuries have on a team. It has been widely used to evaluate injuries for well over a decade now, but unfortunately, all of their data before 2023 was on Football Outsiders, which no longer exists. I was able to use a combination of links from old Tweets and the Internet Archive to get data going back to 2018, which gives us 8 years’ worth of data ( 2018 , 2019 , 2020 , 2021 , 2022 , 2023 , 2024 , 2025 ). Data Over those 8 seasons, Allen had 3 different roles: New Orleans Defensive Coordinator: 2018-21 New Orleans Head Coach: 2022-24 Chicago Defensive Coordinator: 2025 The list below shows how his teams ranked in AGL, with a lower ranking being better (1 = healthiest, 32 = most injured). For the seasons where he was a head coach, I looked at the health of the offense, defense, and overall roster, while I just showed the defense for the seasons where he was the defensive coordinator. 2018: 8th 2019: 17th 2020: 3rd 2021: 10th 2022: offense 26th, defense 14th, overall 23rd 2023: offense 16th, defense 5th, overall 7th 2024: offense 32nd, defense 10th, overall 29th 2025: 26th Analysis There is nothing here to suggest that injuries follow Allen. Averaging the overall rankings from his years as head coach with the defensive rankings from his years as defensive coordinator gives a value of 15.4, which is right around average for a 32-team league. Sure, he’s had years where the injuries hit hard, but he’s also had years where his teams and/or units were healthier than average. If you only look at recent history, it’s easy to say Allen has a problem with injuries. The Bears’ defense was one of the most injured units in the NFL in 2025, and his Saints team was demolished by injuries in 2024. His 2022 Saints team was also among the 10 most injured, meaning his units have been plagued by injuries for 3 of the last 4 seasons. But unless Allen changed something in his approach that exposed players to greater injury risk, that is just bad luck. It only looks like an Allen problem if you zoom in on a small sample and ignore the larger picture. I could just as easily have said after 2023 that Allen’s teams had been among the 10 healthiest in the league 3 of the last 4 years, so he was doing something right to help his players stay healthy. Conclusion In order to claim that Dennis Allen is responsible for the injury problem on Chicago’s defense, as Dan Bernstein recently did, we would first have to find that Allen’s teams have a track record of higher than normal injury rates. A closer examination of the evidence suggests that is not the case. While individual seasons have featured high injury attrition, the units under Allen’s care have had average injury luck over the last 8 seasons. Injuries happen in football, and staying healthy is often as much a matter of luck as anything else. Allen’s teams have had poor injury luck the last 2 years, but there is nothing to suggest that it is his fault. Most importantly for Bears fans, that means there’s no reason we should expect the high injury rate of 2025 to continue.

title: Cash, Stash, or Slash: D’Andre Swift
summary: One of the more interesting names to discuss when looking at futures with the Chicago Bears is running back D’Andre Swift. Swift was brought in by Ryan Poles before the 2024 season and had a subpar year, failing to reach 1,000 yards and averaging less than 4 yards per carry (3.8). Many thought (myself included) […]
full_text: LAS VEGAS, NEVADA - SEPTEMBER 28: Luther Burden III #10 and D'Andre Swift #4 of the Chicago Bears celebrate after Swift's receiving touchdown against the Las Vegas Raiders in the fourth quarter of a NFL 2025 game at Allegiant Stadium on September 28, 2025 in Las Vegas, Nevada. (Photo by Ian Maule/Getty Images) | Getty Images One of the more interesting names to discuss when looking at futures with the Chicago Bears is running back D’Andre Swift. Swift was brought in by Ryan Poles before the 2024 season and had a subpar year, failing to reach 1,000 yards and averaging less than 4 yards per carry (3.8). Many thought (myself included) that Ben Johnson would want to move off Swift as quickly as possible. When Johnson was a play-caller in Detroit with Swift, he first reduced his role, and Swift was sent to Philadelphia not long after. There was an assumption that Johnson didn’t particularly care for Swift’s play in Detroit, and while it’s possible that was true then, it doesn’t appear to be true now. Swift had an excellent season last year, increasing his touchdown total by 50% and raising his yards-per-carry average by 1.1 yards. He ran downhill; he played hard; he did everything Ben Johnson asked of him. Swift definitely outplayed his $8m per year salary. Swift enters the final year of his contract, and it’s a pretty safe assumption that the Bears aren’t going to extend him this offseason. But what should the plan be for 2027? Is it worth extending him before the new league year begins this upcoming March? D’Andre Swift: Stash At this point, it’s just too difficult to determine what the Bears should do with Swift. Swift is currently the 18th-highest-paid running back, and if he is interested in returning to Chicago for similar money or a slight raise, it would make sense to give him another contract. But if Swift has a similar season to what he had in 2025, he may be looking for a hefty pay raise. If Swift is looking to become one of the 10 highest-paid running backs in the NFL and looking for a salary around $15 million, that’s just not something the Bears should be interested in doing. The Bears are going to have a lot of work to do on the 2027 roster. Sure, the offense is largely stabilized, but the defense is going to need a ton of players, both in free agency and through the draft, infused into that unit to make it more functional. The Bears are going to have to allocate their financial resources to a Caleb Williams extension and to multiple pieces on the defense. With that in mind, that may make them restrained with what they can do at running back. If Swift wants a big raise, that probably can’t happen, but if Swift is gone, using a high draft pick on a running back when the defense needs multiple young pieces added to it with day 1 and day 2 picks also may not be something that makes a lot of sense for Chicago to do either. Kyle Monangai was a great story as a seventh-round rookie, but I also think most fans can look at Monangai and realize he’s in a great role right now as a complementary back. He probably doesn’t have the shiftiness and explosiveness you need out of your primary back, so letting Swift walk and letting Kyle become the workhorse also isn’t the best plan. With all these moving parts and multiple things up in the air, it makes a lot of sense for the Bears to see how Swift looks in year two of the Ben Johnson offense, make sure he is still running with the same determination he showed in 2025, and if he looks good and his salary demands are reasonable, you can make a decision late in the season or before the new league year to give him a new contract and keep him around. The Bears’ running back room is thin. There really isn’t anything developing right now behind Swift and Monangai so it’s probably best to see if they can play this out this year, keep Swift on an affordable deal, and start figuring out the Bears RB room 2.0 in 2027.

title: Ryan Poles and the NFL Draft: (Ryan Pace addenum) Part 3
summary: In the last two parts of this series, the focus was on Ryan Poles and his efforts at building the Chicago Bears through the draft. This article is instead focused on his immediate predecessor, Ryan Pace. There are some who will be tired of discussing the 7-year GM of the Bears, and that’s fair. This […]
full_text: In the last two parts of this series , the focus was on Ryan Poles and his efforts at building the Chicago Bears through the draft. This article is instead focused on his immediate predecessor, Ryan Pace. There are some who will be tired of discussing the 7-year GM of the Bears, and that’s fair. This article is not for them. Instead, this article is for those who are either curious about one series of objective measures of Pace or for those who believe it is possible to learn about implications from this general manager’s career for others in the same profession–what can we learn about Ryan Poles’ challenges by studying those of Ryan Pace? The Quarterbacks in the Room It needs to be acknowledged that anything Pace might have done well was completely undermined by his selections at quarterback. He traded up both times and spent a pair of top-11 picks in different drafts selecting a pair of quarterbacks who ended up being unable to reach a second contract with the team. By cost, the picks sacrificed to get those two passers would be valued at #2 (Trubisky) or #9 (Fields). Officially, they took place at #2 and #9. By draft position, they ranked in the 27th and 21st percentile for QBs taken in their draft tier, as well. Therefore, when considering Pace’s drafting as a whole, this article will frequently exclude the value of these two high-cost, high-impact mistakes. Offense vs Defense Even once quarterbacks are excluded from the equation, Pace struggled when it came to drafting offensive players compared to his ability to draft defensive players, at least until the end of his time in Chicago. His QB-exclusive offensive drafting places him the 48th percentile, but his defensive drafting in in the 70th percentile. Pace was able to find at least two players in the upper third at all three levels of defense and they are spread evenly throughout position, but four of his nine “upper tier” offensive draft picks were running backs. Compared to Ryan Poles, he was far less balanced as a GM, but he had at least one “top tier” defense draft each season, even in cases where it was simply a 7th-round pick that stayed in the league longer than expected. Here is how on a per-draft basis he compares to Ryan Poles, once quarterbacks are excluded from the picture. It’s worth noting the volumetric advantage that Ryan Poles has, in that he made 1.5 more selections per year in his first three years than Poles did in his seven. However, despite making fewer total selections, Pace found more (non-QB) top-third offensive players in each draft; he also had more mistakes. Pace and Poles alike had very few true misses on defense, as well. However, Pace trailed in mediocre picks. On that note, Poles has only one defensive players in the 90th percentile or better, while Pace has five. Even when controlled for number of years in position, Pace found exceptional defenders at twice the rate of Poles. On the other side of the ball, Pace found roughly one 90th-percentile offensive player every other year; Poles has not yet done this (though 2025 might change that). Pace was always explicit in his desire to find “playmakers” in the draft, and it seems like he did so even if the cost was proportionately higher misses. Poles, on the other hand, seems substantially more conservative. Year-to-Year Change Ryan Pace, more or less, improved over time. He learned on the job. Sort of. In year three, his two most valuable selections were spent on Mitch Trubisky and Adam Shaheen. In year seven, he drafted Teven Jenkins and Dazz Newsome (and Justin Fields). In fact, just as Jenkins represented a known risk with his prior back injury, some of his biggest successes (like Eddie Jackson) also represented risks. Thus, while it seems fair to say that Pace did improve with his job over time, his fundamental draft tendencies remained the same. He took risks, he traded away selections, and he drafted well when it came to defense and running backs. He struggled to identify quarterbacks and other high-leverage offensive players. If Poles extends on the same growth pattern as Pace but does not suffer the same drop-off, or even if his drop-offs are smaller, the Bears could very well see their fortunes as a franchise improve reliably. No Void Over the course of seven drafts, Ryan Pace made only five selections in Round 3 and Round 4 put together. So instead of a pair of peaks with a notable valley in the middle, Pace’s draft profile was fairly steady once quarterbacks are excluded. Pace struggled in the first round, even independent of quarterback selection. Leonard Floyd was almost perfectly a middle-of-the-pack selection with a high value pick, Kevin White was a clear miss, and only Roquan Smith stood out as a special selection. In the second round, he also made a number of questionable selections. However, the general drafting trend besides that is strong. In fact, after the first two rounds, Pace’s 7-year run drafting as general manager was notably superior to Poles’ first 3-year span with Eberflus. Ideally, a GM would be able to combine the “safety” of Ryan Poles in the first two rounds while adding the potential for dramatic successes like Ryan Pace. However, it is also worth noting that Pace did hit on an interesting approach to avoid the potential mediocrity of Round 3 and Round 4–he simply made very few of those selections, leveraging those picks instead for different opportunities. This is a potential avenue worthy of consideration for Poles as well, in that he needs playmakers as much as he needs role players. Conclusions Ryan Pace did not simply struggle because he failed to draft the right quarterbacks, and to claim oversimplifies the job ahead of Ryan Poles. Instead, Pace was unable to stabilize his success rate given the risky nature of his approach to the draft. Meanwhile, Poles might have managed to find a franchise quarterback, but his conservative approach is limiting Chicago’s chances to find impact players. Finding talent in the “middle third” of each round of the draft is not a path to regular victory, and more than trading away too many picks and missing repeated high-value selections might be.

full_text: FOXBOROUGH, MASSACHUSETTS - DECEMBER 1: Dexter Lawrence II #97 of the New York Giants runs prior to an NFL football game against the New England Patriots at Gillette Stadium on December 01, 2025 in Foxborough, Massachusetts. (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Cincinnati Bengals shocked the NFL world this offseason by trading the 10th overall pick to the New York Giants in exchange for superstar defensive tackle Dexter Lawrence. Lawrence, also known as ‘Sexy Dexy,’ has been one of the best defensive tackles in the NFL for years and was ready for a change of scenery going into 2026. The Bengals were in desperate need of defensive help, and obtaining Lawrence has already paid off throughout training camp. The offense has struggled more than usual because of his presence in the middle, and Sexy Dexy has added significant value to the defensive line as the anchor. Head coach Zac Taylor recently shared his thoughts on Lawrence and a specific play he made that caught the eye of everyone online. “A relentlessness to him,” Taylor told Geoff Hobson of Bengals.com . “Ted (Karras) has his hands full, and it’s making Ted better. Whatever year Ted’s in (11). I think it’s certainly a grind for both those guys. They’re two smart guys that are doing everything they can to win the rep and help their unit, but he’s tough. “We ran a counter play that was really good the other day, and he just reached around and grabbed Chase Brown. And there’s nothing I would have told (right guard) Dalton (Risner) to do differently. Dalton did a great job 99% of the time against 99 of 100 tackles. That’s going to be a great block. And Dexter just made that play. That’s a rare play for a guy to make.” It is no surprise that Lawrence was going to be a massive piece moving forward, but his impact already is incredible to see.

full_text: Cincinnati Bengals defensive end Cashius Howell (55) during minicamp, Tuesday, June 16, 2026, at Kettering Health Practice Fields in downtown Cincinnati. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co A very serious question is about to be discussed over this preseason, and it is whether Andrei Iosivas is the third best wide receiver on this team? Last season Iosivas had some nice moments, but he also had some serious reliability issues with some key drops over quite a few games. You could also argue that he hasn’t really done enough with the opportunity afforded to him by coverages being far more lax with while being more concerned with Ja’Marr Chase and Tee Higgins. Having a more dynamic athlete could open up the offense even more. That is where Colbie Young, the rookie fourth round pick out of Georgia comes in. Young has a bit more to him athletically than Iosivas, and so far in training camp, he has been making some show stopping plays. Whether it is making catches at the highest point or making catches between defenders over the middle, he has done it all. Colbie Young keeps making more highlights at Bengals training camp The Bengals had a question mark at third wideout this offseason after a rough go from Andrei Iosivas last year. Young is here now to compete for the job when the snaps don’t go to tight end Mike Gesicki and others. Bengals rookie Cashius Howell earning high praise as ‘real deal’ “He’s the real deal,” veteran defensive tackle Jonathan Allen said. “Everything you’ve seen on tape; you see him do it at the NFL level. He’s gonna be in the league a long time. He’s a dog.” Howell is being afforded some extra reps as Shemar Stewart is out with a hyperextension. Easy to say he is doing the most with it. Thursday was one of his first opportunities to get some run with the starters, and he literally put Orlando Brown Jr. on his back with a power move. That isn’t exactly how pass rushers beat Brown, and it certainly isn’t how you’d expect Howell to have done it when the team took him in the second round of the draft this year. He is showing that deep bag of pass rush tricks is not just an over used talking point for him during the draft cycle. Allen’s quote about him just adds more credibility to the idea that Cincinnati got a very good pass rusher. Five Observations from Day 7 of Bengals Training Camp “I’ve been really pleased with some of the stuff we’ve been able to do in the run game,” OC Dan Pitcher said. “I know that’s sometimes a hard thing to evaluate when you’re not tackling ball carriers and bringing them to the ground and really getting a sense for what’s a good run and what isn’t. We’ve had several explosive runs.” Some really interesting things gathered by Dan Hoard. This in particular about the running game is interesting. It is tough to tell, but if it can transfer over to actual games then that is a huge thing this team has been missing for a few years now. Bengals’ Zac Taylor reveals plan for starters in first preseason game Speaking with reporters around Thursday’s training camp practice, Taylor said that his starters will see some action during next Thursday’s opener against the Detroit Lions in Cincinnati. Even without the “the Bengals have had slow starts for X amount of years” talking point Taylor is prepared to send in his starters during the preseason. It isn’t inherently a bad idea by any means, but we all saw last year that just because you start 2-0 doesn’t really mean anything. It is definitely a delicate balance that each coach and players will feel differently about. The risk could be very big, though. And when it is for the sake of some live reps in a meaningless game, it does become one that will have plenty of people looking back on it unkindly if something does happen. How do you feel about the starters playing in Week 1 of the preseason?

title: Bengals working on tackling issues during training camp
summary: It’s no secret the Cincinnati Bengals have been among the worst tackling defenses in all of football over the last few seasons. On Thursday, the team began working on drills to try to improve their tackling issues. Zac Taylor said the Bengals would not be doing live tackling in practice, so the reps will come […]
full_text: Cincinnati Bengals safety Jordan Battle (27) chats with young fans during practice at the Paycor Stadium practice facility in downtown Cincinnati on Monday, Aug. 3, 2026. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co It’s no secret the Cincinnati Bengals have been among the worst tackling defenses in all of football over the last few seasons. On Thursday, the team began working on drills to try to improve their tackling issues. Zac Taylor said the Bengals would not be doing live tackling in practice, so the reps will come in drills over the next few practices to get ready for the Thursday preseason game against Detroit. This comes after defensive coordinator Al Golden said Tuesday that the Bengals would hold multiple live tackling drills in each of the next three practices starting Thursday morning. Demetrius Knight driving the pad into the ground and then some on tackling drills. #Bengals @FOX19 pic.twitter.com/ToBFEkYcC3 — Jeremy Rauch (@FOX19Jeremy) August 6, 2026 The improvement starts with the second-year linebackers. Demetrius Knight Jr. and Barrett Carter each finished in the top 15 of missed tackles on the season in 2025. Knight had a 15.0% missed tackle rate, with Carter closely behind that with a 14.8% missed tackle rate. Those numbers will have to improve for this Bengals defense to finish as a top half of the league unit in 2026. The additions of Dexter Lawrence and Jonathan Allen should free the young linebackers up to be in position to make plays this year. Now it is up to them to go out there and get the job done. Another position that will need improved tackling is at the safety position. Going from Geno Stone to Bryan Cook should immediately help at one of those spots. Stone finished the season with an abysmal 18,7% missed tackle rate, often looking like he didn’t want to get physical against the run or after a catch in the open field. Meanwhile, Bryan Cook was one of the better tacklers for a safety in the NFL, finishing the season with just a 5,7% missed tackle rate. The best in the NFL at the position was 4,1% for a player that played in at least 50% of the snaps on the season. At the other safety spot is the returning Jordan Battle. Battle will need to improve on his 13.7% missed tackle rate from 2025. Entering a contract season, it is a make-or-break year for Battle. He has flashed physicality at times against the run, but also has left people scratching their heads with pursuit angles and letting up after a catch near him at times in 2025.

full_text: BEREA, OHIO - JUNE 09: Dillon Gabriel #6 of the Cleveland Browns delivers a play call to the offense during the Cleveland Browns Mandatory Minicamp at CrossCountry Mortgage Campus on June 09, 2026 in Berea, Ohio. (Photo by Nick Cammett/Diamond Images via Getty Images) | Diamond Images/Getty Images The Cleveland Browns are two weeks into training camp, and installation periods are finished. Head coach Todd Monken has maintained all along that he will likely name a starter between QB Deshaun Watson and QB Shedeur Sanders later in training camp, after both players have been evaluated through rotating days of reps. Unfortunately, the results have been less-than-desirable in camp thus far. Watson still looks lost or wild most days, with a few good throws mixed in between. Sanders shows that same promise as he did a year ago, but the speed might not be quite there yet. That opened the door for our Reacts poll this week, which asked whether QB Dillon Gabriel should be included in the team’s quarterback competition. An overwhelming 68% of fans said “yes,” which is a very high amount, given the fact that fans lost faith in him last year due to his issues with getting the ball down the field. While the media has been pumping him up a bit, I’ve remained skeptical, due to my doubts on whether he’s improved upon his inability to get the ball downfield a year ago. Lane Adkins of The OBR sees that as a positive change to his game this offseason, though: Big difference in Dillon Gabriel this summer is, he keeps his eyes downfield consistently and you can see where/when he checks out/down. He's throwing the ball well, has been consistent throughout process — LA (@TheRealLA__) August 6, 2026 The Browns are still heavy underdogs to make the postseason, at 64/1 compared to the other teams, according to FanDuel Sportsbook .

Both quarterbacks. A timeout just had to be called because of how bad it was.” And then, you have QB Shedeur Sanders overthrowing a downfield pass for an interception by S Emmanuel McNeil-Warren : 3. Jenkins played three years at Tulane with 13 career sacks, 107 tackles, and 27 tackles for loss. Jenkins played in the UFL this spring, with six tackles for loss, 1.5 sacks, and 10 tackles.

Of almost equal importance, the Browns still have […]
full_text: BEREA, OHIO - JUNE 11: Spencer Fano #55 of the Cleveland Browns runs a drill during the Cleveland Browns Mandatory Minicamp at CrossCountry Mortgage Campus on June 11, 2026 in Berea, Ohio. (Photo by Nick Cammett/Diamond Images via Getty Images) | Diamond Images/Getty Images The entire focus from the outside looking in with the Cleveland Browns has been about the quarterback position . At practice on Friday, HC Todd Monken reiterated that Shedeur Sanders and Deshaun Watson have not separated from each other, despite a noted difference in some snaps on Thursday . Of almost equal importance, the Browns still have big decisions to make on their offensive line. At this point, only Zion Johnson seems locked into his position and that he will be starting. So with left guard locked in place, who will fill the rest of the starters? Most believe that first-round pick Spencer Fano has the left tackle job as his to lose, but he’s been alternating starting with veteran Dawand Jones during training camp. Tytus Howard received a contract extension after Cleveland traded for him, but he could slide inside to right guard or stay at right tackle. Elgton Jenkins has been dinged up, as has Parker Brailsford, so the center position is very much up in the air. When I asked Monken about how important talent versus fit were on the offensive line, the coach led with the idea that the talent has to be present: After discussions around the facility on Friday, it is very clear that Johnson is highly likely to stick at left guard and Fano is likely to start at some position. After that, the Browns starting offensive line could be decided by a combination of health and talent, even if players are lined up at positions that are somewhat unexpected. full_text: BEREA, OHIO - APRIL 21: Head coach Todd Monken and Deshaun Watson #4 of the Cleveland Browns watch a drill during a voluntary veteran minicamp at CrossCountry Mortgage Campus on April 21, 2026 in Berea, Ohio. (Photo by Nick Cammett/Diamond Images via Getty Images) | Diamond Images/Getty Images At this point in time, the Cleveland Browns quarterback competition is up in the air until HC Todd Monken says it isn’t. Deshaun Watson may have come in with a leg up , but Shedeur Sanders has reportedly made strides. Neither has seemed to distance themselves in the competition so far, almost two weeks into training , with Monken noting that finishing installs was a priority in the process . What is best for the Browns may not be either quarterback, as Dillon Gabriel has shown some nice play so far in training camp . In the end, everyone is trying to figure out what Monken is thinking and might prioritize. As an experienced coach, despite this being his first time as an NFL head coach, Cleveland fans are unlikely to get a straight answer until he wants the information out there. That leads everyone to try to look for clues. Mary Kay Cabot believes she may have seen one on Thursday that indicates that Watson has taken the first lead as “QB1” in the Browns QB competition : The significant part about this practice is that Watson went first in two 7-on-7 periods and Sanders went second. Up until Day 8, the QB who’s serving as QB1 for the day has gone first in almost all of the 7-on-7s and 11-on-11s. The fact that Watson got those extra first-team reps could signal that he’s about to unofficially move into the QB1 role and get the bulk of the starting snaps. Monken noted on Wednesday that by Monday it should become evident who they’re planning to start at most of the key positions. Cleveland’s head coach may enjoy watching media and fans argue over what is “evident” or not over the next few days of practice. Whether that means he will address it with the media on Friday or Saturday, we will find out. title: Browns current roster: ‘Future Hall of Famers’ are mostly young
summary: As late as the end of the 2025 NFL season, the next future Hall of Famer for the Cleveland Browns was clearly DE Myles Garrett. Technically, Garrett landed in the Hall for his amazing single-season sack record in 2025. After OT Joe Thomas was inducted a few years ago, something he talked about in an […]
full_text: BEREA, OHIO - JUNE 11: Jared Verse #8 of the Cleveland Browns looks on during the Cleveland Browns Mandatory Minicamp at CrossCountry Mortgage Campus on June 11, 2026 in Berea, Ohio. (Photo by Nick Cammett/Diamond Images via Getty Images) | Diamond Images/Getty Images As late as the end of the 2025 NFL season, the next future Hall of Famer for the Cleveland Browns was clearly DE Myles Garrett . Technically, Garrett landed in the Hall for his amazing single-season sack record in 2025. After OT Joe Thomas was inducted a few years ago , something he talked about in an exclusive interview with DBN’s Barry Shuck , the next Hall of Famer to go in wearing orange and brown was Garrett, and a lot of question marks. Several former Browns have made it to different rounds of Hall of Fame voting recently , with CB Joe Haden and OL Alex Mack becoming eligible for the honor this year. OL Joel Bitonio’s candidacy will be an interesting one, now that he is retired, as very few guards are actually enshrined in Canton. With the Hall of Fame game Thursday night and the newest inductions coming on Saturday, a piece on ESPN looked at every team’s roster and who on it could be the team’s next inductions from their current roster. For Cleveland, it is a couple of very young players and CB Denzel Ward: Work to do: LB Carson Schwesinger, Edge Jared Verse, CB Denzel Ward While Myles Garrett has already done enough to earn enshrinement, Verse — who came to Cleveland in the Garrett trade this summer — is years of high play and a leveling up away from matching that. Starting his career with two Pro Bowl appearances and a Defensive Rookie of the Year award is of course good for his case. Schwesinger succeeded Verse as Defensive Rookie of the Year, and while off-ball linebackers can struggle to rack up the sort of stats that draw attention from voters, the 2025 second-rounder managed 2.5 sacks and 11 tackles for loss in his debut season. With the Hall generally inducting just a handful of players each year, there will be great players who do not make the cut. Ward will need a long career and the Browns to have some success to push him into that elite category, while Verse (going into Year 3) and Schwesinger (going into Year 2) are just getting started. full_text: Out of all the players participating in Cleveland Browns training camp this offseason, Denzel Boston has certainly received the most excitement from both local and national media members. Between his physical tools and playmaking abilities, expectations are soaring for him going into the 2026 season. But is the conversation surrounding him warranted? Already in camp, he has shown he excels at winning contested catches and creating mismatches against the defensive backs. Media members who have watched him every day at training camp have been astonished by how hard it has been for the defense to cover him. A quick smattering of the hype surrounding Boston, via social media: Friend at Browns practice today said watching Denzel Boston was a religious experience — Ian Hartitz (@Ihartitz) August 5, 2026 Cleveland takeaways: 🔸Denzel Boston 🔸Rookie WR Denzel Boston 🔸Browns’ second-round draft pick Denzel Boston 🔸No. 12 for the Browns, the wideout 🔸Boston, the kid from Washington 🔸that big rookie receiver, Boston 🔸Denzel Boston — Benjamin Solak (@BenjaminSolak) August 5, 2026 If there’s any Denzel Boston stock left to buy, you should consider buying some. — Zac Jackson (@AkronJackson) August 5, 2026 Best player at Browns practice today? Denzel Boston. Three Touchdowns already. Just too big to cover — Max Loeb (@loebsleads) August 5, 2026 The Denzel Boston hype is real.. Been DOMINANT in.. OTAs ✅ Minicamp ✅ Training camp ✅ Legit threat in the RZ, tremendous hands & a fluid mover for a 6'4 behemoth Grab a share or 2 He & KC Concepcion should be 1A & 1B for years 🚀 https://t.co/MnF6qaHp03 pic.twitter.com/J3itB6H9l2 — Gridiron Nerd (@GridironNerd) August 5, 2026 Needless to say, Boston is the talk of Cleveland. The uncertainty at quarterback and with the offensive line will have a significant impact on the offense as a whole, including the level of production Boston is ultimately able to generate. title: Deshaun Watson, Shedeur Sanders: Browns QB competition lingers on
summary: At Cleveland Browns training camp, installs are coming to an end– an important step, but where do things stand after almost two weeks of practices? New coach. New offensive system. Same questions. Evaluating the Browns quarterback room as constructed was an easy task last season and the year prior. Lack of talent, low ceiling, and […]
full_text: BEREA, OHIO - JUNE 11: Shedeur Sanders #2 of the Cleveland Browns laughs with Deshaun Watson #4 during the Cleveland Browns Mandatory Minicamp at CrossCountry Mortgage Campus on June 11, 2026 in Berea, Ohio. (Photo by Nick Cammett/Diamond Images via Getty Images) | Diamond Images/Getty Images At Cleveland Browns training camp, installs are coming to an end – an important step, but where do things stand after almost two weeks of practices? New coach. New offensive system. Same questions. Evaluating the Browns quarterback room as constructed was an easy task last season and the year prior. Lack of talent, low ceiling, and uncertainty surrounded the entire room. Deshaun Watson, who is trying to salvage his career, is the only veteran in the room, but he hasn’t played since 2024. Shedeur Sanders and Dillon Gabriel were rookies last year, with Gabriel getting the first opportunity before Sanders last training camp. Sanders eventually took over, but neither him nor Gabriel did enough to prove they could be the starter in the future. Fast forward to today, the QB battle between Watson and Sanders is ongoing. As of now, neither Sanders nor Watson has taken the lead for the starting job. The more things change, the more they stay the same? It’s easy to formulate opinions about the current QB competition when you use a “QB tracker” that is lacking context when it comes to stats. However, as camp goes on, the reports coming out of camp regarding the competition have been back and forth. One day, Sanders is leading the competition, or Watson is leading the competition. At the same time, others are saying no one has stood out so far throughout the competition. Granted, the quarterbacks are learning a new offense, and they are currently going through the install period, but the little things when it comes to playing the quarterback position matter. Browns GM Andrew Berry to @bykevinclark on what he wants to see from whoever wins the QB competition: "Operating and decision-making … there's a set of at least 60 decisions that that player's going to make. And they're not going to be right in all of them. But if they can do… pic.twitter.com/yWbE1wun2h — Daniel Oyefusi (@DanielOyefusi) August 6, 2026 Browns coach Todd Monken on two attributes that are vital for a quarterback to have: mental toughness and accuracy. pic.twitter.com/oZBispXh2C — Daniel Oyefusi (@DanielOyefusi) August 5, 2026 However, the one that stands out as important is the pre-snap process. I was most impressed by the pre-snap operation today. It wasn’t perfect (Todd Monken ripped into a receiver one play) but on a day when Cleveland missed its top two centers, the offense won the cadence battle a couple times. https://t.co/cYEyJ6DWnV — Daniel Oyefusi (@DanielOyefusi) August 5, 2026 It’s clear that head coach Todd Monken is emphasizing the mental side of the quarterback position ahead of the physical. Monken is responsible for evolving Baltimore Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson and his passing ability, so it’s clear why he is putting a ton of emphasis on that. In terms of the quarterbacks, both Watson and Sanders have had their share of good and bad days, but neither has strung together consistent days. Sanders has talent, but his ceiling is uncertain. Due to his lackluster tape from last season, he’s in a battle with Watson instead of having solidified his position as an NFL starter. There is a case to be made that if Sanders put together quality tape last season, he’s unequivocally the starter. It’s a reason why this is a QB battle, and it’s not because of Watson’s contract. The QB battle between Watson and Sanders will likely take the entire preseason and could come down to the preseason finale against the New England Patriots. However, the battle should be settled after the joint practices and second preseason game. It’s a possibility that the Browns are quietly shopping Sanders, in case he doesn’t win the starting job, due to the overcrowded room. Does that mean Sanders is likely to be traded? Probably not, and Cleveland is hoping it doesn’t come to that. Watson is likely going to play out his contract and move on after the season. Who knows, Gabriel, who many people have written off, could sneak into the competition and win the job, but that is still more of a long shot. The QB battle has no clear leader, and it might be a while before the team finds the answer before the end of the preseason. Where do you think the QB competition stands at this point in the process? title: This week made the Cowboys front office look smart
summary: Javonte Williams is not Bijan Robinson or Jahmyr Gibbs. Let me reiterate: Javonte Williams is not either of Bijan Robinson or Jahmyr Gibbs. Got it? Got it. It is true that the Dallas Cowboys do not employ one of the very best running backs in the NFL, but they certainly employ one of legitimate and […]
full_text: OXNARD, CALIFORNIA - AUGUST 4: Javonte Williams #33 of the Dallas Cowboys runs with the ball during training camp at River Ridge Playing Fields on August 4, 2026 in Oxnard, California. (Photo by Ric Tapia/Getty Images) | Getty Images Javonte Williams is not Bijan Robinson or Jahmyr Gibbs. Let me reiterate: Javonte Williams is not either of Bijan Robinson or Jahmyr Gibbs. Got it? Got it. It is true that the Dallas Cowboys do not employ one of the very best running backs in the NFL, but they certainly employ one of legitimate and capable talent. Last season showed that. Williams finished last season with over 1,200 rushing yards (1,201 specifically so just barely, still counts) and found the endzone 11 times. He was a key part of what made the Cowboys’ offense such a threat and particularly what made it such a dynamic one. This week made the Cowboys front office look brilliant If you haven’t been following news across the NFL this week then you may have missed the way that the running back market ballooned. Bijan Robinson got the party started with a record-breaking extension. His deal with the Atlanta Falcons was a three-year extension worth up to $75M which made him the highest-paid running back in NFL history. Then came Jonathan Taylor and the Indianapolis Colts. Indy extended their star to the tune of a two-year, $44M deal. On Friday the Detroit Lions joined the fold as they extended Jahmyr Gibbs to a three-year deal worth up to $75.75M ($51.5M guaranteed) so Robinson’s spot at the top of the market ended rather quickly. All three of these running backs finished ahead of Williams last season, but only five others did as well. Williams was a top-10 back last year by rushing yards, and while not the only way of measuring a running back’s worth, the Cowboys have him for pennies on the proverbial dollar. Dallas actually struck a deal with Williams all the way back in February. It was a three-year, $24M that helped keep him in tow, stopped him from hitting free agency outright, and most importantly got done before the deals listed above and others that came this offseason like Breece Hall and De’Von Achane. Simply put, the Cowboys have a good thing going right now with Javonte Williams and they clearly knew it. We talk all the time about how getting ahead of things generally makes you look smart from a financial perspective, and that this deal is so far in the rearview mirror certainly corroborates that. Even if you would prefer any of the other backs listed in this overall discussion, would you really prefer them for their price tags? Relative to the context of the Cowboys’ current roster? We haven’t had a chance to say this a lot in recent seasons, but good for the Cowboys in taking care of business (literally) when and how they did here. More of it! Please.

title: Cowboys countdown to kickoff: Top 100 iconic games – Day 37
summary: It is Day 37 of our 100-day countdown to kickoff. We are looking back at the 100 most iconic games in Dallas Cowboys history. The countdown will leads us right up to the opening game of 2026. Our look back doesn’t depend on just one criteria for our rankings. We take into consideration things like […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA--SEPTEMBER 30: Cornerback Deion Sanders #21 of the Dallas Cowboys follows the actions in the game between the Dallas Cowboys vs the Philadelphia Eagles on September 30, 1996 at Veterans Stadium in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Al Pereira/Michael Ochs Archives/Getty Images) | Getty Images It is Day 37 of our 100-day countdown to kickoff. We are looking back at the 100 most iconic games in Dallas Cowboys history. The countdown will leads us right up to the opening game of 2026. Our look back doesn’t depend on just one criteria for our rankings. We take into consideration things like how big the game was for the organization, how memorable the game was, games that had unusual events take place, games that are a part of NFL lore, Cowboys firsts, and games where the Cowboys just plain dominated. Variety is the spice of life and we have all different kind of Cowboys games to review. At the bottom, we’ll link each day of the countdown so you can go back and check out any you missed. We’re now on Day 37 of our 100-day countdown to kickoff, when we revisit a gritty rivalry win from the Cowboys’ last Lombardi Trophy run. Dallas entered the divisional round at 12-4, while Philadelphia arrived at 10-6 after scoring 58 points in its Wild Card win over Detroit. The Eagles had also beaten Dallas late in the regular season, but the Cowboys controlled the rematch. Sunday, January 7, 1996 — 12:30 p.m. ET Texas Stadium, Irving, Texas Final Score: Dallas Cowboys 30, Philadelphia Eagles 11 Philadelphia had beaten Dallas 20-17 after stopping Emmitt Smith on consecutive fourth-and-one plays in the infamous “Load Left” game. The defeat raised questions about whether the Cowboys had become too predictable and whether the Eagles’ physical defense could disrupt them again in January. But the Cowboys opened the scoring on their second possession which gave the team optimism. Troy Aikman moved the offense into Philadelphia territory before Chris Boniol made a 24-yard field goal, giving Dallas a 3-0 lead. The Eagles’ defense then produced its first major play when Mark McMillian intercepted Aikman and returned the ball 34 yards to the Dallas 43. Philadelphia turned that interception into points, but the drive came at a cost. Starting quarterback Rodney Peete suffered a concussion after Darren Woodson stopped him one yard short of a first down near the Dallas goal line. Gary Anderson made a 26-yard field goal tying the game at 3-3, but Randall Cunningham was forced to take over at quarterback. Dallas responded with the game’s signature drive. Smith carried four times for 25 yards and caught a 22-yard pass, helping the Cowboys move 70 yards downfield. Barry Switzer then put Deion Sanders into the offense and called an end-around. Sanders took the handoff, accelerated around the edge, and raced 21 yards for the first touchdown of the afternoon. This play gave Dallas a 10-3 lead and demonstrated why Sanders was added to an already loaded championship roster. Before halftime, the Cowboys added another touchdown. They marched 79 yards and relied on Smith to score from one yard out, making it 17-3. Boniol’s extra point completed a 14-point second quarter and put Philadelphia in a difficult position against a defense that was already controlling the line of scrimmage. While the third quarter wasn’t spectacular, it was precisely what Dallas needed. The Cowboys maintained control of the ball, forcing punts and capitalizing on Philadelphia’s field position whenever they could. Boniol kicked an 18-yard field goal before drilling another from 51 yards, extending the lead to 23-3. Entering the fourth quarter, the Eagles had scored only once in the previous three periods. Philadelphia’s coverage strategy focused heavily on Michael Irvin, effectively preventing him from catching a reception throughout the game. This strategy, however, created opportunities for other players. Kevin Williams had one of the best games of his career, repeatedly exploiting weaknesses in the Eagles’ secondary and providing Aikman with a reliable target in the passing game. Irvin eventually got his moment. With Dallas already comfortably ahead in the fourth quarter, Aikman found him for a nine-yard touchdown. It was Irvin’s only catch of the afternoon, but it pushed the score to 30-3 and officially turned a physical playoff game into a decisive rivalry victory. This game belongs on the countdown because it was a necessary step in the final championship run of the Cowboys’ 1990s dynasty. Dallas had been embarrassed in Philadelphia only weeks earlier and faced a rival that believed it had discovered a formula for stopping Smith and disrupting the Cowboys’ offense. Instead, Dallas won by 19 points, controlled both lines of scrimmage and showed that its roster was deep enough to win even when Irvin was removed from most of the game. #Cowboys vs #Eagles 1996 Divisional Round Final Score: Dallas Cowboys 30, Philadelphia Eagles 11 #DallasCowboys #NFL (📽️: @nfl ) pic.twitter.com/QioJOLLMHV — Mike Poland (@kenfigkowboy) August 7, 2026 Interesting Facts About the Game Deion Sanders affected the game in nearly every possible way. He scored on a 21-yard end-around, intercepted Cunningham, caught a 13-yard pass and returned two punts for 21 yards. title: Cowboys former 2nd-round pick getting pushed off roster by UDFAs
summary: Luke Schoonmaker’s time may finally be running out for the Dallas Cowboys. The second-round pick in the 2023 NFL Draft never really challenged Jake Ferguson for the starting tight end job as was hoped, nor has he shown much improvement thus far in his career. As a result, his time in Dallas may expire before […]
full_text: Luke Schoonmaker’s time may finally be running out for the Dallas Cowboys. The second-round pick in the 2023 NFL Draft never really challenged Jake Ferguson for the starting tight end job as was hoped, nor has he shown much improvement thus far in his career. As a result, his time in Dallas may expire before his rookie contract does. Schoonmaker is entering a contract year this season and currently finds himself on the roster bubble nearly two weeks into training camp. No. 86 has enjoyed the relative safety a player of his draft status generally gets throughout his first three seasons with the Cowboys, but that security seems to be running out. He may have to fight tooth and nail to even make the roster. Although Schoonmaker was technically Dallas’ TE2 based on the number of offensive snaps he played last season (391), many would agree Brevyn Spann-Ford ended up surpassing him on the depth chart despite playing 91 less snaps (300). Spann-Ford has shown continued development after going undrafted in 2024 and is now considered by many the primary backup. Where Schoonmaker has shown very little improvement/development since entering the league, Spann-Ford has grown by leaps and bounds as both a blocker and receiver since joining the Cowboys. The former UFDA is currently having a strong training camp, further cementing himself as Dallas’ TE2 heading into the 2026 NFL season. With Spann-Ford surpassing him on the depth chart, at best, Schoonmaker currently finds himself third on the TE depth chart right now. His slide might not stop there though with the way Michael Trigg has started to shine in multiple practices now, catching the eye those in attendance and making a name for himself. Couple of days in a row where Trigg has made a play in team drills. Also, shoutout to @NickHarrisFWST for the fantastic footage and coverage this week. https://t.co/OQOda5yZ9z — Locked on Cowboys (@lockedoncowboys) August 6, 2026 Michael Trigg signed with the Cowboys after the completion of the 2026 NFL Draft as an undrafted free agent. Many believed him to be a mid-round draft prospect, but for whatever reason he never heard his name called. Despite going undrafted, he’s been one of the more hyped up of Dallas’ rookies and so far hasn’t disappointed at training camp. This could have Schoonmaker looking over his shoulder once again. If Trigg continues to improve and earn the trust of the coaching staff and his teammates alike, he could very well push No. 86 right off the roster seeing as how the Cowboys typically only carry three TEs on the depth chart. This is an interesting situation to keep a close watchful eye on out the rest of training camp and preseason. It could end up being one of those cautious tales about how production speaks louder than words, whether you are ultimately drafted or not. What’s your take BYB? Will Schoonmaker make the roster this season?

title: Ryan Flournoy continues great start to training camp on Thursday
summary: Ryan Flournoy got to play in 16 games with four starts in 2025. He delivered 40 receptions for 475 yards and scored four touchdowns, with 29 of his catches being for first downs. Undoubtedly, Flournoy established himself as the WR3 for the Dallas Cowboys behind CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens. In the NFL, you can’t […]
full_text: OXNARD, CALIFORNIA - AUGUST 4: Ryan Flournoy #19 of the Dallas Cowboys runs after the catch during training camp at River Ridge Playing Fields on August 4, 2026 in Oxnard, California. (Photo by Ric Tapia/Getty Images) | Getty Images Ryan Flournoy got to play in 16 games with four starts in 2025. He delivered 40 receptions for 475 yards and scored four touchdowns, with 29 of his catches being for first downs. Undoubtedly, Flournoy established himself as the WR3 for the Dallas Cowboys behind CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens. In the NFL, you can’t just ball out once. There has to be consistency. So, it was important that once the Cowboys got to Oxnard for training camp that Flournoy continued to show progression, especially with a bigger role in the offense on the horizon. He’s gotten off to a very good start during the first week, but Thursday he stood out. Rookie safety Caleb Downs has looked every bit like a first-round pick as he’s been all over the field. However, being it’s his first camp, growing pains are expected, and Flournoy gave him just that in one-on-one drills. He did a great job luring Downs to sleep to get the proper release before catching a quick out route. Caleb Downs vs. Ryan Flournoy. 🔥 #Cowboys pic.twitter.com/JH4V2d2saU — Patrik [No C] Walker (@VoiceOfTheStar) August 6, 2026 The highlight play for Flournoy came during the team period. Dak Prescott rolled out to his right and threw on the run, and Flournoy made a nice grab while sliding on the ground. This showed great body control and concentration on his part, and also trust from Prescott that he doesn’t have to throw a perfect pass for Flournoy to make plays (the throw was still a good one). Flournoy was also seen making plays on crossing routes during the team period, and he took some reps returning punts along with Downs and KaVontae Turpin. Dak to Ryan Flournoy pic.twitter.com/lPQthueBfA — Jon Machota (@jonmachota) August 6, 2026 What we’ve seen from Flournoy is continued growth from his performance a year ago. Now, he has expectations to be an even bigger contributor, and from the looks of things, he is poised for a breakout season, which will elevate an already potent offensive attack in Dallas. With Lamb and Pickens doing their thing, it puts a ton of stress on the opposing defense, which gives Flournoy plenty of opportunities to produce in one-on-one situations. Plus, at 6’1″ and around 205-210 pounds, he can be a power slot receiver that can make it difficult for nickel corners to cover him with his size and athleticism. The thing now is for Flournoy to keep stacking good days in camp and get to the regular season healthy. Is Flournoy the best candidate for a Cowboys breakout season? Or do you have another player in mind?

title: Core traits defining the Cowboys new Leadership Council
summary: The coaching staff of the Dallas Cowboys selected their 11-player Leadership Council, and it features a wide variety of players, and some may not be who you expected. Rather than just a collection of the team’s most popular stars, this group features players possessing positive locker room influence, strong communication, and elite professional standards. What’s […]
full_text: OXNARD, CALIFORNIA - JULY 30: Head coach Brian Schottenheimer of the Dallas Cowboys speaks with members of the media during training camp at River Ridge Playing Fields on July 30, 2026 in Oxnard, California. (Photo by Ric Tapia/Getty Images) | Getty Images The coaching staff of the Dallas Cowboys selected their 11-player Leadership Council, and it features a wide variety of players, and some may not be who you expected. Rather than just a collection of the team’s most popular stars, this group features players possessing positive locker room influence, strong communication, and elite professional standards. What’s so special about the players chosen? Today, we’ll run through each player and explain why each of them make a great choice for this honor. Dak Prescott – Resilience As the longest-tenured Cowboys player and the face of the franchise, Prescott is the epitome of a team leader. He embodies all the council’s core traits. His career is defined by immense resilience, battling one moment of adversity after another. His ultimate high-character moment came when he won the 2022 Walter Payton NFL Man of the Year Award for his extensive Faith Fight Finish Foundation work and openness about mental health, establishing him as an elite locker room anchor and one of the NFL’s all-around great guys. CeeDee Lamb – Influence Despite all the glitter and glam that comes with the 88-star receiver gig, Lamb has provided some underrated influence in the locker room. A key moment came early in the 2023 season when a frustrating loss to San Francisco appeared to fracture the team. Instead of fracturing, Lamb took accountability and actively got in sync with Prescott, completely reshaping the Cowboys’ offense for a historical turnaround down the stretch. And he demonstrated he wasn’t afraid to get his hands dirty, aggressively blocking and leading by example with immense work ethic. Javonte Williams – Grit Nothing demonstrates perseverance more than returning from a devastating multi-ligament knee injury to prove you’re not damaged goods. The Cowboys bet on Williams in free agency last year, and he rewarded them with a 1,200-yard, 11-TD season. They, in turn, rewarded him with a pay raise. He doesn’t say much and lets his max-effort play do the talking. He exemplifies what toughness is, both mentally and physically. Jake Ferguson – Heart Ferguson is a player you probably wouldn’t like if he’s not on your team. He’s pesky, he’s brash, and he plays with a lot of swagger. His emotion is what gives him his edge, as he’s intense. He’ll run through defenders, hurdle them, and then point and snicker about it later. He’s a refuse-to-quit kind of guy and represents the competitive fire needed in the locker room and offers no apologies for it. Tyler Smith – Selflessness It’s so weird to see this once raw draft “reach” evolve into one of the most mature individuals on the team. From the onset, he was bounced around between positions and has answered every call. Now, as one of the game’s most physical interior blockers, he’s the staple of this offensive line. He’s a leader, helping his younger teammates with nutrition and conditioning, but he’s also a young guy himself who is still growing. He doesn’t look ahead or buy into any hype, and with each day he serves as the stabilizing force for this team’s culture. Tyler Booker – Fearlessness While the council is laced with experienced veterans, Booker stands as the pup of the group, entering just his second year in the league. He’s used to the leader role, holding the captain honor under Nick Saban at Alabama for three years, so his making the cut was a “no-brainer” choice for Schottenheimer. Not one to be shy, Booker is vocal in team meetings, willingly speaking his mind and doing so with conviction. From the moment he shared he wanted to make his opponents rethink their career choices, it was evident he was a fearless competitor, and his making this group at just 22 years old is just a continuation of the high standard he’s already set for himself. Quinnen Williams – Determination Williams is motivated by an unselfish desire to win. He’s not interested in the slightest in talking about his stats or personal goals. His focus is on being better and making the team better. As an elite talent formerly stuck in purgatory on a New York Jets team, he has gained a clear understanding that complacency is a killer, and he demands perfection from others, which is something you can get away from if you bring All-Pro effort on every snap. Kenny Clark – Wisdom Often viewed as a “throw-in” to the Micah Parsons trade, Clark’s importance to the team has always been highly underrated. And at age 30, some question how good he still is because it’s easy to forget that he’s made a career out of using his raw power and mastering fundamentals. Schottenheimer has praised the veteran recently for his precision hand placement and body leverage, making him still one of the best block-shedding defensive tackles in the game. Clark just has an elite understanding of what he’s supposed to do. His chemistry with Williams continues to grow, and these two are exceptional leaders in the trenches for guys on both sides of the ball. Rashan Gary – Accountability Despite being a veteran, Gary is new to the Cowboys, so making this list is a testament to what he’s done over his career. He’s a hard worker and sets an example for others, showing a strong level of commitment to his job approach. He shows up early, mentors younger players, and ensures no one is slacking. New guy or not, he’s already commanding the attention of the locker room and holding teammates accountable. Jalen Thompson – Versatility Thompson is another first-time Cowboy to make this group. He’s the team’s top free agent signing of the spring, lauded for his sharp communication skills. His football smarts make him one of the new tactical brains of Christian Parker’s secondary. His understanding of the safety position allows him to be a versatile piece to this defense. His willingness to do anything sets a great precedent and shows younger players that there are no bounds to their learning. Bryan Anger – Consistency When Anger joined the Cowboys, he was already an “old” veteran at 33, with nine years of experience, playing multiple years across three different teams. If he could just hang on for a couple of years, that would be great. Little did we know, he was just getting started. He’s now spent five years with the Cowboys, his new longest-tenured team. And he now has two All-Pro seasons, something he never had before coming to Dallas. He’s a quiet professional who has been a model of consistency over his 14 years in the league. Each player shares traits deeply trusted by the coaching staff. Maturity and self-discipline are critical, but having a variety of culture also matters. They want these players to impact the locker room the right way and be guys others want to emulate. Seeing things objectively and communicating their concerns is important to the coaches, and they feel they have chosen the right guys for this role. What do you think? Who do you feel was left off this list?

title: Cowboys news: Dallas gets “good news” on two key injuries
summary: Thursday’s practice for the Dallas Cowboys gave all of us some scares on the injury front. After rookie linebacker Jaishawn Barham and defensive lineman Otito Ogbonnia exited practice with injuries, we now have updates on what happened and early reports on the severity. We also have reports from training camp, including a great day of […]
full_text: Thursday’s practice for the Dallas Cowboys gave all of us some scares on the injury front. After rookie linebacker Jaishawn Barham and defensive lineman Otito Ogbonnia exited practice with injuries, we now have updates on what happened and early reports on the severity. We also have reports from training camp, including a great day of practice for Brevyn Spann-Ford, and the addition of a new tight end. Practice Points: LB Jaishawn Barham exits with injury – DallasCowboys.com Jaishawn Barham has had an incredible start to training camp, but he gave us all a scare in Thursday’s practice. Early reports sound like he’ll be just fine. It doesn’t appear as if the injury is serious and the Cowboys will likely just monitor Barham’s progress in the next few days. The third-round pick from Michigan has been getting some first-team reps at linebacker, alongside Dee Winters. Barham has been overly impressive with his quickness to the ball and his physicality, which was also on display earlier in practice when he mixed it up with running back Israel Abanikanda on a 1-on-1 drills. Dallas Cowboys Injury Updates Following Third Padded Practice of Training Camp – Mike Moraitis, SI.com Otito Ogbonnia exited Thursday’s practice, but he did return to the field and finish practice. Ogbonnia has had a strong training camp and expects to play a big role in 2026. According to Joseph Hoyt of the Dallas Morning News , defensive lineman Otito Ogbonnia briefly exited to the medical tent during practice before eventually returning. Cowboys claim TE Zack Kuntz off waivers – Matthew Lenix, Blogging the Boys The Cowboys lost TE Princeton Fant for the season earlier this week to a torn ACL. Former Las Vegas Raider Zack Kuntz will take his place on the roster. The Dallas Cowboys lost tight end Princeton Fant to a torn ACL on Monday. In a move to replace him, they have claimed Zack Kuntz off waivers from the Las Vegas Raiders per Nick Harris of the Fort Worth Star-Telegram. Kuntz is a former seventh-round pick of the New York Jets in 2023. In two seasons with the team, Kuntz only appeared in two games an didn’t log any stats. Cowboys fan gifts Dak hat with photo of his late brother, Jace, on it – Paul Livengood, Mike Leslie, WFAA Dak Prescott was gifted a pretty cool gift from a fan after Thursday’s practice. This is what it’s all about. Dallas Cowboys quarterback Dak Prescott has made it a habit to give back to the fans and the community, even on his own birthday . But this time, the kind gesture of a Cowboys fan touched the heart of Prescott. A fan gave Dak a hat at Cowboys training camp practice on Thursday, but no ordinary hat. No. This hat was special: with a photo of Dak’s late brother, Jace, on the side of it. Cowboys Training Camp Recap: Brevyn Spann-Ford shows exactly what he needed to in practice No. 6, new roster lock emerges – Mauricio Rodriguez, A to Z Sports Thursday’s practice gave a nice look into a few players trying to breakout in 2026. Brevyn Spann-Ford is looking to do that and more. Spann-Ford had what I’d call the best individual practice of the day and his best in camp yet. He made a spectacular diving catch over the middle of the field with safety Markquese Bell in coverage. Bell did not stand a chance. Then came the run game. Running back Javonte Williams ripped off a big gain, and there was Spann-Ford as a pulling blocker, completely swallowing up linebacker DeMarvion Overshown and opening up the lane. Cowboys rookie defensive back Caleb Downs is living up to expectations while learning two spots – Dan Greenspan, AP News We already knew Caleb Downs was smart. But we’re now seeing why his intelligence is so highly regarded in the football world. Parker has been pleased with Downs’ willingness to learn, particularly as he navigates different positions. It stood out to the 34-year-old Parker, who had success helping young defensive backs thrive in his previous role with the Philadelphia Eagles, during the pre-draft process. “Curiosity is one thing for young players that you really look for,” Parker said. “They want to know the why behind everything.” Daily discussion question: Who is the MVP of camp so far?

title: The Super Bowl 50 trophies nobody talks about
summary: As fans gear up for what everyone in Broncos Country hopes will be another historic Super Bowl run, I got to thinking about the additional hardware that the Broncos picked up following their Super Bowl 50 run. What I am talking about are the gold 5 and 0 that accompany the Lombardi trophy from that […]
full_text: SAN FRANCISCO, CA - FEBRUARY 08: The Super Bowl trophy and the Super Bowl 50 MVP trophy was on display during the presentation for the MVP at the Moscone Center West on February 8, 2016 in San Francisco, California. Von Miller #58 of the Broncos was the games MVP. (Photo by Thearon W. Henderson/Getty Images) | Getty Images As fans gear up for what everyone in Broncos Country hopes will be another historic Super Bowl run, I got to thinking about the additional hardware that the Broncos picked up following their Super Bowl 50 run. What I am talking about are the gold 5 and 0 that accompany the Lombardi trophy from that Super Bowl in just about every picture since the win. Plenty of teams win Super Bowls. Only the Broncos got multiple trophies for doing so. #SB50 pic.twitter.com/nOIpfQr9DD — Andrew Mason (@MaseDenver) April 28, 2016 Sure, leading up to Super Bowl 50, everyone saw these gold numerals with the Lombardi at various press conferences and whatnot, arranged proportionally to match the logo from that Super Bowl. There was never any indication they would be awarded alongside the Lombardi and, during the trophy presentation, the numbers were not part of the ceremony. So what, exactly, are they? Wikipedia says : In addition to the Vince Lombardi Trophy that all Super Bowl champions receive, the Broncos also received a large, 18-karat gold-plated “50”. Each digit weighs 33 lb (15 kg) for a total of 66 lb (30 kg). Like the Lombardi Trophy, the “50” was designed by Tiffany & Co. So how did they go from press conference display pieces to prominent components of the Broncos trophy display case? Well, that’s a great question, because internet research and AI assistance don’t provide a clear answer. Like I said, they weren’t a part of the postgame presentation and they don’t appear in any of the clips online during the parade or rally. In fact, the first time (that I can find) that they were seen, not in a promotional context and with the Broncos organization, was during the end-of-year press conference with legendary Broncos Gary Kubiak and John Elway. They are currently behind glass in the Broncos trophy case labeled “Super Bowl Trophy and Lombardi Trophy.” Probably the only time in the history of football, past or future, that the Lombardi trophy gets second billing. These bonus trophies clearly were handed off sometime between the end of the trophy presentation and that press conference. One wonders if someone with the NFL saw them and wondered, “What am I going to do with these?” and sent them to Denver. It’s also entirely possible there was more than one set made since the NFL’s golden anniversary was such a big deal. If so, where are those? The Hall of Fame in Canton, Ohio seems like a logical choice, but research and AI are unable to confirm or disconfirm. So, Broncos Country, that Super Bowl 50 win got us not only a Lombardi, but two bonus trophies that are pretty awesome in their own right. No other team has ever received bonus trophies for winning a Super Bowl and so, if you ask me, that is just another reason why the Denver Broncos are the best team in the NFL… bur do we need any more reasons? If you know anything about these bonus trophies, please share in the comments!

title: Broncos DL Matt Henningsen suffered a torn Achilles
summary: One year ago, on August 7th of 2025, Denver Broncos defensive lineman Matt Henningsen suffered a season-ending Achilles injury. A brutal injury that can end the careers of some players. Henningsen rehabbed, was re-signed by the Broncos, and was able to get back on the practice field and be ready for training camp. Not only […]
full_text: ORCHARD PARK, NY - NOVEMBER 13: Matt Henningsen #91 of the Denver Broncos looks on from the field during an NFL football game against the Buffalo Bills at Highmark Stadium on November 13, 2023 in Orchard Park, New York. (Photo by Perry Knotts/Getty Images) | Getty Images One year ago, on August 7th of 2025, Denver Broncos defensive lineman Matt Henningsen suffered a season-ending Achilles injury. A brutal injury that can end the careers of some players. Henningsen rehabbed, was re-signed by the Broncos, and was able to get back on the practice field and be ready for training camp. Not only did he return to the field, but he has been a standout player for the Broncos’ second- and third-team defensive line and was making a case for a 53-man roster spot. Unfortunately, the universe just has it out for Henningsen because exactly one year from his previous Achilles injury, Matt Henningsen went down early in practice and had to be carted off the field. The injury did not look good, and a few moments ago, 9NEWS Denver’s Mike Klis confirmed those fears when he reported that Henningsen suffered an Achilles injury. Devastating news: #Broncos DL Matt Henningsen suffered a torn Achilles today per source. It occurred one year after he tore his other Achilles during joint practice with 49ers in Santa Clara. All that rehab. All that work to come back. And Henningsen was having a good camp. — MikeKlis9NEWS (@mikeklis9news) August 7, 2026 Henningsen was a 6th-round selection for the Denver Broncos back in the 2022 NFL Draft and became an instant contributor for them in the middle of their defense. He would appear in 34 games for the Broncos between 2022 and 2023 before spending the 2024 season on the team’s practice squad. He looked like a strong candidate for a practice squad spot last year before the Achilles injury and was once again making a case for a spot on the team this year, but unfortunately, the Achilles injury got him again. It’s tough to ignore the coincidences here. The same injury, to the same player, exactly one year apart. Absolutely devastating for Henningsen. This will unfortunately put his NFL future in limbo moving forward as well. He re-signed with the team on a one-year deal this offseason, so we’ll see if the team will bring him back again or not. This is also a hit to the Broncos’ defensive line depth. Henningsen was one of their top reserve/depth players, and now he is done for the year for a second straight season. I would look for the Broncos to bring in some depth, especially before their preseason opener next week, since veterans like DJ Jones, Zach Allen, and Malcolm Roach are not expected to play much, if at all. The injury bug has bitten the Broncos early in training camp, but thankfully they have been mostly minor thus far. Henningsen’s injury changes that, and hopefully Marvin Mims and Nate Adkins, who both left practice as well, only suffered minor injuries. Stay tuned to Mile High Report as we keep you updated on all things happening at Broncos Training Camp.

The scenario was 1:21 left in the game, the offense is down 20-24, and the ball is on their own 39-yard line, and they do not have timeouts. They need a touchdown to win the game. This is a pretty tough scenario for most quarterbacks, but it is where Bo Nix shines, and he would lead yet another late 4th-quarter comeback to get the win for the Broncos offense. Practice ended with a situation period: 1:21 left in the game. Offense down 20-24, ball on own 39. No timeouts. GREAT… — Zac Stevens (@ZacStevens) August 7, 2026 The first play of the drive did not go well. Broncos walk it off, and the offense gets a big win to end practice. Both sides were down some key players, but a win is a win Broncos run game was working today It has been rough sledding for the Broncos’ run game thus far, but today they finally broke through, and all three of their main backs had good gains on the ground. The two main winners of the day, however, were starter JK Dobbins and rookie Jonah Coleman, who, according to some reports, had the best run of camp thus far. Couple of big runs for JK Dobbins with the 1s and now Jonah Coleman with the 2s. One could argue they are the biggest runs of camp so far — Ryan Edwards (@redwardsradio) August 7, 2026 It should be noted that Malcolm Roach, DJ Jones, and Alex Singleton, the middle of the Broncos’ run defense, all received vet days today. So, their absences likely impacted this, but still, it was great to see the Broncos’ run game get going a little bit today. The most noteworthy thing I am taking away from this is Jonah Coleman looking good. Head Coach Sean Payton singled Coleman out as the “pleasant surprise” of camp thus far, so it’s good to see he’s making a positive impression. We won’t see Coleman’s biggest impact until the preseason when the run game can actually be unleashed and tested. Until then, we won’t learn too much about the Broncos’ run game. More injuries – including WR Marvin Mims Jr. Unfortunately, the injury bug bit and bit hard today. It all started early in practice when defensive lineman Matt Henningsen went down during a drill, in what ended up being a dreaded non-contact drill. He was clearly in pain and was carted off the field. It looked bad, and unfortunately for Henningsen, it ended up being bad. 9NEWS Denver’s Mike Klis is reporting that Matt Henningsen suffered a torn Achilles, one year to the date of him suffering the same injury last year. He rehabbed and got back into football shape and was having a good camp, according to reports, just to suffer the same season-ending injury exactly one year later. Tough break for Henningsen and the Broncos. Devastating news: #Broncos DL Matt Henningsen suffered a torn Achilles today per source. Head Coach Sean Payton will be away from the team until Sunday, so we’ll hear from DC Vance Joseph tomorrow, who will hopefully provide some updates. The Broncos will likely need to address the defensive line and wide receiver positions in the coming days.
