title: Nik Bonitto ranked 32nd in NFL’s Top 100
summary: Another player on the Denver Broncos has earned a spot in the NFL’s Top Players of 2026 list. Fifth-year edge rusher Nik Bonitto comes in at 32nd this year. That’s a six-spot leap from last year’s rankings. Other Broncos that have made the list thus far are left tackle Garett Bolles (42nd), quarterback Bo Nix […]
full_text: DENVER, COLORADO - NOVEMBER 06: Nik Bonitto #15 of the Denver Broncos stands on the field during the second half of an NFL football game against the Las Vegas Raiders at Empower Field At Mile High on November 06, 2025 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Brooke Sutton/Getty Images) | Getty Images Another player on the Denver Broncos has earned a spot in the NFL’s Top Players of 2026 list. Fifth-year edge rusher Nik Bonitto comes in at 32nd this year. That’s a six-spot leap from last year’s rankings. Other Broncos that have made the list thus far are left tackle Garett Bolles (42nd), quarterback Bo Nix (59th), wide receiver Courtland Sutton (68th), and defensive lineman Zach Allen (73rd). Two other players who have not been ranked but certainly will are offensive guard Quinn Meinerz and shutdown cornerback Patrick Surtain II. After a quiet start to his NFL career, the fifth-year pro has made monumental strides the past three seasons. In 2025, Bonitto had a career high 14 sacks. Additionally, he posted 14 tackles for loss and 28 quarterback hits. With that type of production, there is no doubt he is one of the best pass rushers in football. No. 32 on the NFL Top 100 Players of 2026… @Broncos LB Nik Bonitto! @NFLFilms pic.twitter.com/oK4OPMv4Is — NFL (@NFL) August 7, 2026 According to SIS Data Hub , Bonitto had an impressive 74 quarterback pressures last season. That’s 26 more than his previous career high of 48 in 2024. Additionally, Bonitto’s 20.5-percent pressure rate ranked second in the NFL. A second-round draft pick out of Oklahoma in the 2022 NFL Draft; he has developed into one of the league’s most dominant defenders. Last September, the Broncos rewarded him with a four-year extension worth $106 million dollars with just shy of $39 million guaranteed. With a flurry of edge defenders recently receiving new contracts since then, Bonitto’s extension looks like a bargain. As of now, his contract ranks fifteenth amongst all edge defenders in average annual value, and his total guarantees are essentially half of those ahead of him. Through four seasons, Bonitto has amassed 138 tackles, 44 tackles for loss, and 37 sacks. He also has a pick-six and six forced fumbles. His ascent is key reason why the Broncos have led the league in sacks the past two seasons and become one of the NFL’s top defenses. Denver will need him to play at a high level again in 2026 to make their Super Bowl aspirations come true.

title: Riley Moss vows to stay aggressive and create more turnovers
summary: Cornerback Riley Moss has one of the hardest jobs in the National Football League. Trying to shutdown high-end wide receivers on a weekly basis is already tough enough. That task becomes a lot harder playing across from a Hall of Fame caliber player like Patrick Surtain II. Appearing in eight games as a rookie, Moss […]
full_text: HOUSTON, TX - NOVEMBER 02: Riley Moss #21 of the Denver Broncos celebrates during an NFL football game against the Houston Texans at NRG Stadium on November 2, 2025 in Houston, Texas. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images Cornerback Riley Moss has one of the hardest jobs in the National Football League. Trying to shutdown high-end wide receivers on a weekly basis is already tough enough. That task becomes a lot harder playing across from a Hall of Fame caliber player like Patrick Surtain II. Appearing in eight games as a rookie, Moss had just one pass thrown against him. Since then? It has been trial by fire for the former Iowa Hawkeyes standout. Pending the source, Moss was targeted at least 100 times the past two seasons. That volume placing him as one of NFL’s most targeted corners. With quarterbacks going in your direction that often, an occasional big play given up or a penalty against you is bound to happen. It’s just a part of the game. Even so, Moss has never shied away from a challenge. In fact, he has embraced it. Yesterday after practice, Head Coach Sean Payton took a moment to praise the fourth-year cornerback’s approach to the position. “A little grit and toughness. He can bury the last play. He knows he’s going to get a lot of traffic and attention. Yes, I like his toughness,” stated Payton. “I think it’s a tough position to play, and he doesn’t back down at all from that, his confidence doesn’t wane. That’s a really good trait.” Last season, Moss led the league in passes defended with 19 last seasons. Additionally, he allowed only a 53.4 completion percentage which was 11th best for boundary cornerbacks. That’s quite impressive, especially how often he is challenged every week. Unfortunately, Moss was on the wrong end of the scale in one respect—penalties. He was worst in the league in that respect drawing 11 throughout the course of the 2025 season. Entering his fourth season with the franchise, a contract year, Moss vowed to stay aggressive in his approach on gamedays despite the high number of flags going his direction. “My parents have always told me this, I like to learn the hard way. It actually helps me out in those situations because yes, they’re going to throw the flag because I’m being too aggressive. But even ‘VJ’ will tell me, ‘Keep going out there. Keep playing aggressive.’ It happens,” stated Moss. “I know I need to do better as a whole this season, and I have been. It’s been a big focus of this camp. I’m still going to play aggressive and not shy away from it.” In addition to playing aggressive, Moss mentioned one area he is hoping to get much better at—creating turnovers. Despite an eye-popping 27 passes defended combined the last two seasons, Moss has just two interceptions in his career to date. Finding a way to turn some of those into game-changing plays would certainly help the Broncos in their quest for a fourth Lombardi Trophy. This offseason and through training camp, Moss and the entire defense has been working diligently to make that improvement. After practice, he reflected on last season and how he plans to reel in more interceptions in 2026. “I was in great position for the most part the entire year last year. Now it’s turning my head and trusting my ability to go and play the ball because the receiver is also playing the ball. It’s just getting out of that habit of that man-to-man instead of just going out there and looking for the ball. It’s a hard habit to break, I won’t lie to you, but that’s why we’re out here practicing. It’s been a big point of emphasis for me.”

title: Sean Payton reflects on Mike Shanahan’s legacy, Hall of Fame case
summary: Good morning, Broncos Country! Mike Shanahan is a Hall of Famer. He’s one of the best coaches in the history of the NFL. Whether the former Denver Broncos head coach and member of the Broncos Ring of Fame gets the nod when the committe votes this year for induction next year remains to be seen. […]
full_text: DENVER, CO - OCTOBER 31: Former Head Coach for the Denver Broncos Mike Shanahan stands on the field during halftime against the Washington Football Team at Empower Field at Mile High on October 31, 2021 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Justin Edmonds/Getty Images) | Getty Images Good morning, Broncos Country! Mike Shanahan is a Hall of Famer. He’s one of the best coaches in the history of the NFL. Whether the former Denver Broncos head coach and member of the Broncos Ring of Fame gets the nod when the committe votes this year for induction next year remains to be seen. As current Broncos head coach Sean Payton said on Thursday after training camp practice (Shanahan was in attendance) in regards to Shanahan and his Hall of Fame candidacy: “Yes. He’s going to be there … Mike’s going to be there. It’s not if; it’s just what year.” Shanahan’s resume speaks for itself. He’s the winningest coach in Broncos’ history, one of the most successful franchises in the history of the NFL. Shanahan is one of seven coaches to win back-to-back Super Bowls (Chuck Knoll did it twice with the Pittsburgh Steelers). Of those seven, four are in the Hall of Fame, with two as locks when the time comes for Bill Belichick (maybe?) and Andy Reid. From 1996-98, Shanahan oversaw one of the most successful periods in NFL history. Denver won 46 games and two Super Bowls. The Shanahan coaching tree and his offensive mind continue to influence the league in major ways. His time as offensive coordinator with the San Francisco 49ers helping Steve Young win his first Super Bowl as a starting quarterback. If that wasn’t enough, here’s some more tidbits to prove how incredible Shanahan was, especially in Denver. The Broncos led the league in both 1,000-yard rushing seasons (11) and 1,000-yard receiving seasons (18) during Shanahan’s 14 years as Denver’s head coach. “I think, and this is with respect to Mike, there was only one Shanahan offense, and then there were these offshoots and very good offshoots,” Payton said to the media on Thursday. “I think that it really depends on … Each coach has taken his maybe spin on it. The one thing I would say is the commitment to running the ball well. You always felt that with Mike’s teams. A strong commitment to running the ball well, and the boots and the play-actions that come off of it. “Those are the first things that hit my mind. Then obviously the route combinations can vary, but that would be the first thing that I think they did better than anyone. They ran the stretch series, the play-action off of it. It really became problematic for defenses.” Of course when anyone discusses a candidate for the Hall of Fame, it comes back to the impact they had on the NFL. The old, “Can you write the story of the NFL without Mike Shanahan?” For Shanahan, he continues to leave his mark even after long being retired. As Payton said on Thursday: “My first year in the league in 1997 with Philadelphia, Jon Gruden had me, we had Beta then, had me cutting up four offensive teams, one being Denver. There was a game, you guys were too young, but they played Dallas and Mike started getting into these, the (wide receiver) outside Rod Smith to get man-zone reads. It was an empty package. It was like Denver really had a good offensive game that day … it was must-watch. You had to get that game tape. “So Mike, and then the coaching tree, and then the Super Bowls, every element of it fits just like the Broncos and Elway and the many members of that team. There’s a chapter, a number of chapters, that are attributed to that timeframe. So I’m looking at it really more in a microscope relative to what he was doing before anyone else was doing it. “So there are elements to him being the head coach, but then him being a heck of an offensive play caller and a forward thinker relative to how he utilized his personnel, the success they had with the wide-zone scheme, all of the play-action mechanics with. So yes, a very important part of our history.”

title: Lions training camp scrimmage notes: UDFA shines among strong LB performance
summary: The Detroit Lions held a scrimmage-like practice on Friday, their fourth straight day in pads. One of the neat things about these scrimmages is that they’ll often have the first-team offense go against the second-team defense, giving some depth players an opportunity to go against starting-level talent. It’s a huge opportunity for some players further […]
full_text: Detroit Lions linebacker Erick Hunter (48) practices during training camp at Meijer Performance Center in Allen Park on Friday, July 31, 2026. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co The Detroit Lions held a scrimmage-like practice on Friday, their fourth straight day in pads. One of the neat things about these scrimmages is that they’ll often have the first-team offense go against the second-team defense, giving some depth players an opportunity to go against starting-level talent. It’s a huge opportunity for some players further on the depth chart, and undrafted rookie linebacker Erick Hunter was one of a few on Friday who took full advantage. I’ll break down each of the 12 drives from practice below, along with the key plays and notable performances along the way Drive 1 — First-team offense vs. second-team defense The scrimmage kicked off with a play-action pass to Amon-Ra St. Brown for an easy 8 yards with Christian Izien in coverage. With no Jahmyr Gibbs, Isiah Pacheco, or Sione Vaki, the run game wasn’t very effective all day. Facing a third-and-8, Jared Goff found Jameson Williams on a dig route that he turned upfield for a huge 30-yard gain. Chris Smith and Joe Bachie shared a sack. Isaac TeSlaa helped Detroit convert a second third-and-long on another crossing route. Now in the red zone, the Lions offense couldn’t convert a third-straight third down, with Goff forcing a pass to Amon-Ra St. Brown that was intercepted by the aforementioned Hunter. Drive 2 — Second-team offense vs. first-team defense It was a three-and-out for the second-team offense. Good plays by Chuck Clark shutting down a Greg Dortch slant reception attempt, and Rock Ya-Sin making an open-field tackle on Jackson Meeks well short of the line to gain on third down. Drive 3 — Second-team offense vs. first-team defense Fantastic drive from Derrick Barnes, who immediately forced a throwaway on a play-action boot by not losing contain and pressuring Luke Altmyer. A few plays later, he blew up a screen pass to Kye Robichaux. Devin White—who replaced injured Malcolm Rodriguez in the starting lineup—also had a strong day, chasing down Robichaux on a toss play behind the line of scrimmage. Jack Campbell ended the linebacker-dominant drive with an easy tackle on a third-down dump-off. Special teams break The Lions worked on a drill in which two players begin engaged together, and one tried to disengage and get downfield. Erick Hunter won both of his reps decisively, both as a blocker and a pursuer—continuing his strong day. It’s worth noting that Hunter got a shout-out from special teams coordinator Dave Fipp Drive 4 — First-team offense vs. first-team defense — Starting at 50-yard line Tough start to the drill by running back Jabari Small. He was stuffed on first down for a two-yard gain, then couldn’t hold onto a swing pass that could’ve been a big gain. An illegal contact penalty bailed out the offense early, but it wouldn’t last long… Aidan Hutchinson picked up a sack against the right side of the offensive line. Detroit worked into a fourth-and-manageable with two completions to St. Brown (9, 5 yards). But on fourth-and-2, Chuck Clark—who had a strong overall day—broke up a pass to Jameson Williams. Drive 5 — Third-team offense vs. second-team defense — Starting at 50-yard line Not much success from the second-team offense, either. Cedrick Wilson gave them some optimism with a deep curl (against Roger McCreary) for 14 yards. But Anthony Lucas and Ahmed Hassanein combined for pressure, forcing an intentional grounding Altmyer missed on a deep shot to Tay Martin, who had beaten Khalil Dorsey on third down. Jake Bates drilled a 54-yard FG. Drive 6 — First-team offense vs. first-team defense — Starting at opponent’s 25-yard line Two strong defensive plays kicked off the drive: White stopping a St. Brown crosser for just 3 yards. Then Chuck Clark crashing down on a run stop for a 4-yard gain. But on third-and-short, Goff did an amazing job splitting pressure from both Alim McNeill and Tyleik Williams for a needled pass to Jameson Williams on a crossing route for an 18-yard touchdown—and the offense’s first true win of the day. Drive 7 — Second-team offense vs. second-team defense — Starting at opponent’s 25-yard line After an initial first down, the second-team offense failed to move the ball. Ahmed Hassanein nearly picked up a TFL, but was a little out of control in the backfield. He still slowed down the play enough to help force just a 4-yard gain. Altmyer missed an open Meeks. Loren Strickland with a nice tackle well short of the sticks on a fourth-and-5 pass to Malik Cunningham. 49-yard FG GOOD. Drive 8 — First-team offense vs. first-team defense — Starting on opponent’s 25-yard line White continued his relentless pursuit of St. Brown, popping him at the sidelines for just a 4-yard gain. Perhaps the best run of the day: A counter to Saylors with good lead blocks by Christian Mahogany and Tate Ratledge for 7 yards. White times a blitz perfectly, giving Alim McNeill an opportunity to win a 1-on-1—and he does for a 5-yard loss on a run stop. Jamo with a big third-down conversion on a comeback route opposite Rock Ya-Sin. White continues his strong day with back-to-back run stuffs. Isaac TeSlaa has a one-handed attempt, but Nick Whiteside had too good of coverage. On fourth-and-goal, Goff found St. Brown for a 3-yard touchdown—then followed it up with a corner route to St. Brown for the two-point conversion. I’m still not entirely sure how the ball got through Thomas Harper’s blanket coverage. For good measure, Jake Bates attempted a 55-yard FG and drilled it. Drive 9 — Third-team offense vs. third-team defense — Starting on own 1-yard line Practicing being backed up against their own end zone, it was a disaster drill for the following offensive line (left to right): Devin Cochran, Melvin Priestly, Michael Niese, Mason Miller, Larry Borom. The drive: false start, false start, run for 0 yards, drop by Greg Dortch, potential sack from Eric O’Neill. Drive 10 — First-team offense vs. first-team defense — Starting on own 1-yard line Much better results for the first-team offense on the same drill. Short passes to St. Brown (Ya-Sin in coverage) and TeSlaa (Rakestraw) earned some breathing room and a first down. But Hutchinson shut down the next run for 0 yards. Then it was two straight “successful” bombs to Jameson Williams — an 87-yard touchdown and a 94-yard touchdown. However, the first was called back after a very obvious push-off from Williams on Rakestraw. The second probably didn’t ever really happen, because Hutchinson had cleanly beaten Penei Sewell for the sack/safety. Drive 11 — Second-team offense vs. first-team defense — Situational: Tied 24-24, 3:45 left, starting on opponents’ 44-yard line with three timeouts Aidan Hutchinson vs. the second (maybe third)-team offensive line is not fair. He immediately beat Colby Sorsdal for a sack. The next drive, there were multiple extra bodies on Hutchinson for help. Barned shut down a run from Robichaux, and Maddox and Ya-Sin shut down a Kennedy slant route well short of the sticks. Three-and-out. 58-yard FG GOOD. Drive 12 — First-team offense vs. second-team defense — Situational: Down 3 points, 1:32 left, 3 timeouts, starting on own 31-yard line The offense would end up winning this drill, but they got bailed out twice. The first bail out came after a very strong third-and-10 pass breakup from Nick Whiteside on Jameson Williams. Unfortunately for Whiteside, he shoved Williams after the play and earned a personal foul penalty. Whiteside rode the bench the rest of the drive after the costly penalty. The offense got bailed out again on third-and-3 when a 15-yard facemask penalty negated an incomplete pass. St. Brown would make them pay. Goff laid a perfect turkey-hole shot between Izien and Abney for 15 yards. Then, in the red zone, St. Brown took an inside route, shook a tackle attempt from Damone Clark, juked Dorsey out of his shoes, and…

title: Lions RB Jahmyr Gibbs: Contract talks were ‘extremely stressful’
summary: Jahmyr Gibbs was all smiles when stepping in front of the lectern at Allen Park Friday afternoon. With his deal now signed through the 2030 season, Gibbs can focus on what he’s wanted to the entire time: football. But he admitted in his press conference that the last few weeks have been hard. “This process […]
full_text: Jahmyr Gibbs was all smiles when stepping in front of the lectern at Allen Park Friday afternoon. With his deal now signed through the 2030 season, Gibbs can focus on what he’s wanted to the entire time: football. But he admitted in his press conference that the last few weeks have been hard. “This process was extremely stressful, because I just wanted to play ball,” Gibbs said. “I missed being out there with my teammates and coaches. It’s just fun being out there right now with my pads and stuff on. It just feels a lot better.” Gibbs’ hold-in lasted a week into training camp, forcing him to miss the first six practices of the summer. For someone as relatively soft-spoken as Gibbs, it may have come as a surprise to some. And while it was clear the Lions running back wasn’t super comfortable with the media circus chasing him around for a week, he believed it was a necessary part of the process. “It was really hard, but it’s a business,” Gibbs said. “Stuff has just got to get done, but, yeah, it was really hard.” In the end, Gibbs clearly got what he was seeking: a three-year extension that makes him the highest-paid running back in NFL history. His reported $22.5 million per year average value is a record-high for a running back and his $51.5 million guaranteed is only second to rookie running back Jeremiyah Love (whose rookie contract comes fully-guaranteed as the third overall pick). It’s been a rare offseason in which several running backs have exploded the market, years after there appeared to be a general consensus around the league that backs don’t deserve big paydays. Gibbs said it was important for him to continue to push the running back market for the younger generation of backs, showing that becoming a full well-rounded back can result in big paydays. He got calls from several high-profile running backs throughout the process giving him encouragement, including Derrick Henry, Christian McCaffrey, Jonathan Taylor, James Cook, and DeVon Achane. “They all reached out, showed some love. As always, we’re all in this together,” Gibbs said. So Gibbs is paid. He’s back on the field. He’s earned a few Pro Bowls and set a handful of records along the way. What’s next for the 24-year-old back? “Ultimately, I just want to win a Super Bowl with this team, and do anything it takes to get that.”

Reed (undisclosed) S Kerby Joseph (PUP, knee) S Brian Branch (PUP, Achilles) We’ve got a lot of injuries questions saved for Dan Campbell’s next press conference (Sunday morning). Bridgewater, Pacheco, Scruggs, and Reed all missed Thursday’s practice, and their absence on Friday suggests it may have been more than rest or heat-related issues. Hopefully, we get some good news from the Lions head coach Sunday, but at this moment, there is no news on their absences. summary: According to Adam Schefter, the Detroit Lions are signing free agent defensive tackle Ben Stille. He was first taken in as an undrafted free agent by the Miami Dolphins and made seven game appearances his rookie season. From […]
full_text: Aug 10, 2024; Glendale, Arizona, USA; Arizona Cardinals defensive end Ben Stille (90) against the New Orleans Saints during a preseason NFL game at State Farm Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Mark J. Rebilas-USA TODAY Sports | USA TODAY Sports via Reuters Con According to Adam Schefter, the Detroit Lions are signing free agent defensive tackle Ben Stille. Stille is a former Nebraska Cornhusker who has spent the past four years bouncing around NFL rosters. He was first taken in as an undrafted free agent by the Miami Dolphins and made seven game appearances his rookie season. From there he bounced between the Browns, Cardinals, Buccaneers, back to the Cardinals and back to the Dolphins before his most recent stint on the Atlanta Falcons’ practice squad for the last couple months of the 2025 season. In total, Stille has made 18 game appearances, one start, and produced 2.0 career sacks. At 6-foot-4, 296 pounds, Stille is more in the three-tech kind of build, but has some experience kicking all the way out to the edge. While it’s unclear if the signing is related, Lions defensive tackle Mekhi Wingo did leave Thursday’s practice with a groin injury. Tyler Lacy also left practice early, but Detroit did not provide an update on his condition.

Gibbs’ three-year, $67.5 million contract is a record-setter for any […]
full_text: DETROIT, MICHIGAN - DECEMBER 4: David Montgomery #5 of the Detroit Lions and Jahmyr Gibbs #0 of the Detroit Lions react as they run off the field following an NFL football game against the Dallas Cowboys at Ford Field on December 04, 2025 in Detroit, Michigan. So it should come as no surprise that when Gibbs received his three-year extension on Thursday evening, there was an outpouring of love from Gibbs’ teammates, both past and present. Gibbs’ three-year, $67.5 million contract is a record-setter for any NFL running back in history. So, of course, it was a cause for celebration. Let’s look at some of Gibbs’ peers and their reactions to the news. Let’s start out with a player that may have the closest relationship with Gibbs than any other player in the league: former Lions running back David Montgomery. The “Knuckles” to Gibbs’ “Sonic,” Montgomery now plays for the Houston Texans after being traded this offseason. But he still wanted to offer up some love for Gibbs on his Instagram page Thursday night. “Proud of you my dawg,” Montgomery captioned his story. Another player who is extremely close to Gibbs is star receiver Amon-Ra St. Brown. He opted to just go the emoji route for his reaction. Then there are a few old Lions running backs who previously had shared a room with Gibbs. Craig Reynolds meme’d up a photo of Gibbs in a perfect way… While former Lions running back Jermar Jefferson shared his pride in Gibbs. One of the players who paved the way for Gibbs—both as a blocker and as a young core player who already got paid—Penei Sewell, offered his congratulations online. And, finally, old friend Frank Ragnow chimed in about Gibbs. Not only congratulating the Lions running back, but offering a comment on his character: “Nice guy too,” he wrote.

title: Detroit Lions roster 2026: Rock Ya-Sin, Greg Dortch, Keith Abney are underrated
summary: “I told those guys, this may have been our only shot. Do I think that? No. Do I believe that? No. However, I know how hard it is to get here. I’m well aware. And it’s gonna be twice as hard to get back to this point next year than it was this year. That’s […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PA - NOVEMBER 16: Detroit Lions cornerback Rock Ya-Sin (23) warms up before the game between the Detroit Lions and Philadelphia Eagles on November 16, 2025 at Lincoln Financial Field in Philadelphia, PA. (Photo by Kyle Ross/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images “I told those guys, this may have been our only shot. Do I think that? No. Do I believe that? No. However, I know how hard it is to get here. I’m well aware. And it’s gonna be twice as hard to get back to this point next year than it was this year. That’s the reality. And if we don’t have the same hunger and the same work — which is a whole ‘nother thing once we get to the offseason — then we’ve got no shot of getting back here. “I don’t care how much better we get, or what we add, or [who] we draft. It’s irrelevant. It’s gonna be tough. Everybody in our division’s gonna be loaded back up. And, you know, you’re not hiding from anybody anymore. Everybody’s gonna want a piece of you. Which is fine, you know. “So it’s hard. You wanna make the most of every opportunity. We had an opportunity and we couldn’t close it out.” That’s what Lions head coach Dan Campbell told the media after his team blew a 24-7 first half lead to the San Francisco 49ers in the 2023 NFC Championship game. That 34-31 loss was followed by the Lions’ 15-2 regular-season record in 2024, and their subsequent 45-31 wild-card round bollixing at the hands of Jayden Daniels and the Washington Commanders. After last season’s 9-8 record and postseason miss, Campbell’s words resonated more clearly than ever. Certainly, injuries had a lot to do with the dropoff … …but as the Lions head into the 2026 season, what is expected of them? They have the quarterback in Jared Goff. Jahmyr Gibbs is one of the NFL’s most consistently explosive running backs. There’s a receiver trio in Amon-Ra St. Brown, Jameson Williams, and Isaac TeSlaa that is capable of shredding any defense, and tight end Sam LaPorta is no slouch, either. The offensive line should be good enough. Things are a bit dodgier on defense, as the injury data tells us, but Campbell and his coaches are suddenly dealing with a franchise on the precipice of a “competitive window” discussion sooner than a lot of people imagined. If these Lions are to transcend the doubts, they’ll need the level best from everybody on the roster — superstars and lesser-known players alike. To that end, I’ve identified three Hidden Gems for the 2026 Lions — one underrated veteran, one underrated free agent. and one underrated draft pick. Underrated veteran: CB Rock Ya-Sin A Lions secondary that looked like the class of the NFL not too long ago has all kinds of question marks around it now. Brian Branch’s and Kerby Joseph’s injuries of late have been their own issues , and those issues are not yet resolved. What cornerback Terrion Arnold did to get himself released from the team on June 29 was an entirely different level of problematic; when one’s off-field life intervenes to the tune of four counts of kidnapping and four counts of armed robbery, football really isn’t the point anymore. Still, defensive coordinator Kelvin Sheppard has to put a defensive backfield out there, which is where veteran cornerback Rock Ya-Sin comes in as he did last season. Arnold missed nine games in 2025 to concussion and shoulder issues, and fellow cornerback D.J. Reed missed six games with a hamstring injury. The Lions had signed Ya-Sin to a $1.17 million contract before the season, and it wasn’t a big deal in the public eye. It was also Ya-Sin’s fifth team in the last five seasons — the 2019 second-round pick of the Indianapolis Colts out of Temple had drifted from Indy to Las Vegas to Baltimore to San Francisco to Detroit since 2021. But with Arnold and Reed unable to take the field, it was the journeyman Ya-Sin’s time to shine, and he did for the most part, In Weeks 1-9, Ya-Sin had just 98 coverage snaps, and he allowed 10 catches on 19 targets for 94 yards, 10 yards after the catch, four pass breakups, and an opponent passer rating of 84.1. Especially with Arnold out, Ya-Sin’s participation increased dramatically. In Weeks 10-18, he had 284 coverage snaps (only Amik Robertson had more among Detroit’s cornerbacks with 287), and Ya-Sin gave up 17 catches on 31 targets for 193 yards, 70 yards after the catch, five pass breakups, and an opponent passer rating of 73.7. Ya-Sin didn’t have an interception last season, but he also allowed only one touchdown on all those targets. Rock Ya-Sin: A name @Lions fans will want to remember in 2026. pic.twitter.com/k63IXOKuZ9 — Doug Farrar ✍ (@NFL_DougFarrar) June 26, 2026 “I want to take the ball away more this season,” Ya-Sin said in March regarding his plans for 2026 . “I really thought I left some [plays] on the field last year — some interceptions, some forced fumbles. I want to do a better job of that this year. I want to take the ball away. “Last year, I was proud that I stepped up when I got the opportunity. I got to do a lot of cool things last year. Match up against a lot of really good receivers, and do things in my career up to that point I hadn’t done yet. That was really cool stepping up when guys got hurt, and [we didn’t take] a step back, or [miss] a beat. I was proud of that.” It helps that Ya-Sin is a natural press cornerback. Last season, the Lions had at least one cornerback in press coverage on 70% of their snaps, the sixth-highest rate in the NFL. Sheppard had two cornerbacks in press 28% of the time, the league’s fourth-highest rate, and the Lions tied with the Buffalo Bills and the Chicago Bears for the NFL’s highest rate of three cornerbacks in press on a play at 11%. It’s why Ya-Sin wanted to return. He did so on a one-year, $3.2 million contract, with $1 million guaranteed. “I was ready to go from those four or five teams I had been on,” he said in March. “Like, when it was time to go, I was happy to go. But this was the first time I really wanted to come back, and I let my agent know that before the season had ended. I’m just glad to be back. “Certain guys fit better with certain teams, and I feel like I fit better here than I fit with those previous teams.” Is Ya-Sin the ideal No. 1 cornerback for any NFL defense ? Probably not, but beggars can’t be choosers, as they say, and with a secondary in so much doubt, it’s nice to have somebody who has excelled of late in Sheppard’s defense. Underrated free agent: WR Greg Dortch The Lions dropped from third in Offensive DVOA under Ben Johnson in 2023 to seventh in 2025 under John Morton, and in 2026, former Arizona Cardinals OC Drew Petzing will be in charge of Detroit’s offense. The one guy Petzing clearly wanted from his Arizona days was receiver/returner Greg Dortch, who signed a $1,402,500 contract to play in the Motor City. “It was a big reason,” Dortch said of his familiarity with Petzing . “Obviously, just the comfort factor. The trust and the success that I’ve had with him being my OC the three years together. Drew is very smart, and knows exactly how to get people the ball.” Last season, for the Cardinals, Petzing got the 5-foot-7, 175-pound Dortch the ball for 29 catches on 33 targets for 206 yards and three touchdowns, 15 yards and a touchdown on seven rushing attempts, and Dortch himself took the ball on 30 kick returns for 796 yards (26.5 yards per return), and 16 punt returns for 185 yards (11.6 yards per return). The return game is where Dortch’s addition could pay off the most. Greg Dortch could make the @Lions ' return game rather fun in 2026. pic.twitter.com/VgxJ11Ybk1 — Doug Farrar ✍ (@NFL_DougFarrar) August 5, 2026 “Did you see some of those returns yesterday?” Campbell asked a reporter on July 31 when queried about how Dortch will help the Lions. “Those drills we had, I love [Lions Special Teams Coordinator Dave] Fipp’s. Man, his return ability really showed up. Certainly, we know what he’s able to do from afar just on tape. “And so, for him, it’s,…

title: Packers Family Night Recap: Trey Smack nearly perfect at Lambeau Field
summary: The Green Bay Packers’ rookies made their Lambeau Field debut on Friday night when the team hosted their Family Night practice in front of over 60,000 fans. If you weren’t able to attend Packers training camp this summer, this was your first opportunity to get a look at Green Bay in team drills — which […]
full_text: ASHWAUBENON, WISCONSIN - JULY 31: Trey Smack #28 of the Green Bay Packers looks on during the Green Bay Packers training camp at Ray Nitschke Field on July 31, 2026 in Ashwaubenon, Wisconsin. (Photo by Patrick McDermott/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Green Bay Packers’ rookies made their Lambeau Field debut on Friday night when the team hosted their Family Night practice in front of over 60,000 fans. If you weren’t able to attend Packers training camp this summer, this was your first opportunity to get a look at Green Bay in team drills — which are barred from being recorded at Packers practices. Here are all the news and notes, from the offense, defense and special teams, including injury updates, for those of you who weren’t able to watch the practice in person, via the Packers TV Network or on Packers.com. Injuries RB Josh Jacobs (groin) RB Chris Brooks (hamstring, NFI) TE Tucker Kraft (knee) TE Luke Musgrave (neck, PUP) LG Aaron Banks (knee) RT Zach Bako-Bewele (knee) DL Devonte Wyatt (knee) DL Javon Hargrave (knee, PUP) DL Jordon Riley (ankle, PUP) EDGE Micah Parsons (knee, PUP) CB Carrington Valentine (hamstring) CB Kamal Hadden (ankle/finger) CB Domani Jackson (undisclosed) S Jonathan Baldwin (knee) LS Matt Orzech (calf, PUP) The Packers were hyper-conservative on the injury front at Lambeau Field tonight. Previously in training camp, players like Kraft, Banks, Bako-Bewele, Wyatt and Hadden had at least participated in individual drills with the team. On Friday, they were dressed down and held out of practice completely. So far, the only injuries that seem to have the potential to bleed into the regular season, at least based on the comments of the coaching staff, are Parsons, Riley (who will start on the PUP list after suffering season-ending injuries in 2025) and potentially Musgrave, who is dealing with a neck issue. Offense Jordan Love shoots and scores. Tucker Kraft joins the celebration. #Packers pic.twitter.com/DjIYYdlYDN — Dominique Yates (@RealDYates) August 8, 2026 Starters Love Golden – Watson Lloyd Dabney – Whyle Morgan – Burton – Rhyan – Monk – Belton LVN – Brooks – Stackhouse – Brinson – Sorrell Coop – Zaire Cisse – Nixon Willaims – X — Andy Herman (@AndyHermanNFL) August 8, 2026 With Banks and Bako-Bewele out, the Packers used a “starting” offensive line of Jordan Morgan, Jager, Burton, Sean Rhyan, Jacob Monk and Anthony Belton. Generally, in training camp, Green Bay has played Darian Kinnard at right tackle as Bako-Bewele’s injury sub and kept Belton at right guard, but since Burton has recovered from his hamstring injury, Burton has been getting in the mix more — forcing Belton to tackle. Donovan Jennings, who snapped today for the second-team unit, also got looks with the first-team offense at guard. If that’s the pecking order on the offensive line, then the 10th offensive line spot, and potentially the final one on the 53-man roster, will probably come down to John Williams (who has been playing every position in camp) and Travis Glover. Beyond the offensive line, there wasn’t too much interesting going on with the first-team lineup, in terms of the rotation. Maybe the next most notable piece of news was that Pierre Strong Jr. does seem to be ahead of running backs Damien Martinez and Jaden Nixon behind MarShawn Lloyd, Jacobs and Brooks (the latter two of which weren’t participants in practice today). Jordan Love with a 50-plus-yard touchdown to Matthew Golden. Get used to this. pic.twitter.com/9adoadDosG — Zach Jacobson (@zacobson) August 8, 2026 The play of the night was made when quarterback Jordan Love connected with second-year receiver Matthew Golden on a 52-yard touchdown pass when Golden was matched up with safety Javon Bullard. Golden had a good day overall, as did Love, who has only thrown two interceptions in camp — one being a screen that was run the wrong way, per head coach Matt LaFleur. Savion Williams with a contested slot fade TD from Tyrod Taylor!!! pic.twitter.com/tXknkPgJrd — Alexander Basara (@Basaraski) August 8, 2026 Another receiver who had a nice catch was Savion Williams, who high-pointed a ball against safety Kitan Oladapo, who has a 6’5” wingspan. Williams appears to be the first man up off the bench in the Packers’ receiver rotation, behind Christian Watson, Golden and slot receiver Jayden Reed. Defense Anthony Campbell with a very quick pressure that leads to a near pick, but dropped by St-Juste. Nice little run by Nixon inside. (Jaden) — Andy Herman (@AndyHermanNFL) August 8, 2026 Interior defensive lineman Anthony Campbell just continues to rack up pass breakups throughout camp and is up to five. Campbell, who was signed to the Packers’ practice squad just days before Green Bay faced off against the Chicago Bears in the playoffs last season, has been the “out of nowhere” riser so far. It’s possible that he could push for a roster spot, which could be bad news for either Karl Brooks or Nazir Stackhouse, the two linemen among the Packers’ top-six at the position who are easiest to part ways with. Another good rep against the run for Barryn Sorrell. Beat Jordan Morgan and probably would have stopped Lloyd there — Zach Kruse (@zachkruse2) August 8, 2026 Over and over again, edge defender Barryn Sorrell, who has been stepping up as the replacement “starter” in practice opposite Lukas Van Ness while Micah Parsons is sidelined, made plays in the run game on Friday night. Interior defensive lineman Warren Brinson also flashed with the first-team unit. Christian Watson and Brandon Cisse had a couple competitive reps in 1-on-1s. Here are the first and third. Cisse had a nice PBU on a slant on the second and got a dap from Watson after. pic.twitter.com/rUd2dVth2N — Matt Schneidman (@mattschneidman) August 8, 2026 For those of you who want video of rookie second-round pick cornerback Brandon Cisse, here are some reps that he got against Christian Watson. Cisse was pushed into the “starting” role tonight as Carrington Valentine is out with an injury. Generally, the Packers’ pecking order at the cornerback position has been: Keisean Nixon, Valentine, Cisse and Benjamin St-Juste, when the unit has been healthy. Cisse cramped up late in practice and missed Green Bay’s two-minute period, which pushed St-Juste into the starting lineup opposite Nixon. Special Teams Lousy camera work but here’s Smack from 61 to end his warmup. pic.twitter.com/BHjY2UVwMx — Bill Huber (@BillHuberNFL) August 7, 2026 Rookie kicker Trey Smack went six of seven at Lambeau Field tonight, with his only miss being a 51-yarder that he hooked. Leg strength isn’t an issue for Smack, who is probably good for a 65-yard attempt, based on what he flashed in the practice warmup. Smack responded to his miss by hitting a 47-yarder in the two-minute drill, even after the kicking team was set back five yards for a false start. Overall? Pretty good night. Kickoff unit: Cisse – Bullard – Mosby – Melton – McDuffie – Niemann – St-Juste – Perry – Williams – Hopper (not in any specific order). — Andy Herman (@AndyHermanNFL) August 8, 2026 If you want to know who is going to make the end of the Packers’ roster, pay attention to their special teams units. For the most part, Green Bay’s kickoff team wasn’t too surprising. The two players here who probably won’t make the initial 53-man roster are edge defender Arron Mosby and safety Mark Perry. Mosby is pretty much a special teams-only player, and it’s tough to find room for him when Green Bay has Lukas Van Ness, Barryn Sorrell, Brenton Cox Jr., Dani Dennis-Sutton and Collin Oliver ahead of him on the defensive depth chart, and that’s before Micah Parsons returns to the team. I assume that Mosby will be on the Packers’ practice squad until the team suffers a couple of injuries and he’s called up, which is how Mosby’s situation with Green Bay has played out the previous two seasons. On the Perry front, I think he’s essentially a placeholder for another safety, be it Xavier McKinney (who generally…

title: Fans grade Packers position groups going into the 2026 season
summary: Earlier this offseason, we asked Green Bay Packers fans in The Feed to give each position group on the roster a letter grade heading into training camp. Now that all of the votes have been cast, we can calculate these position groups’ “GPA” and show you which positions that fans are the most confident in […]
full_text: GREEN BAY, WISCONSIN - NOVEMBER 10: Xavier McKinney #29 of the Green Bay Packers in action against the Philadelphia Eagles at Lambeau Field on November 10, 2025 in Green Bay, Wisconsin. (Photo by Michael Reaves/Getty Images) | Getty Images Earlier this offseason, we asked Green Bay Packers fans in The Feed to give each position group on the roster a letter grade heading into training camp. Now that all of the votes have been cast, we can calculate these position groups’ “GPA” and show you which positions that fans are the most confident in and least confident in on the 2026 roster. Below are the full “GPA” rankings, including the top comment from each batch of voting. There were a couple of surprises to me, but not too many. Safety starts our list from the top. Safety: 3.89 Solid Snake: It’s literally the best safety room in the league Short and to the point. Quarterback: 3.26 TITLETOWN1TOLOVE: We have a franchise QB with a great year could win the MVP award and a quality experienced backup. We also have 2 young guys to battle for a PS berth and do that developing thing to see if one could be a Love backup QB next year. A all the way. I wish we had a better long-term answer coming off the bench than 37-year-old Tyrod Taylor, but not too many teams have a significantly better backup than Taylor, either. Receiver: 2.97 SpeckledFluffyFox: If they need to rely on any of these guys, it means Kraft is broken for good. This one is a little too harsh for me. I like the top three guys, and expect Christian Watson and Matthew Golden to take a step forward this year (Watson sort of already did in his half-season post-injury). My question here is really the depth when you get past those three. Tight End: 2.92 adeltoro24: Kraft is really pulling the rest of the boys up here. As Davante used to say, Kraft is a top 2 TE and he’s not #2. No one else on this list is exciting in any specific aspect or that well rounded. It’s only gotten worse for the Packers’ tight ends since we ran this poll, too, as Luke Musgrave is now dealing with a neck injury that has kept him completely out of practice for the first week of camp. It really is Kraft and everyone else right now. Linebacker: 2.82 eddiemathews: Oh. I thought you meant the actual room. I’d need a picture. Heyo! Edge Defender: 2.66 Lovetoski: Too many unknowns to rate as anything other than incomplete at this point. I’ll let you know in October. It’s a really young group right now, with Lukas Van Ness, Barryn Sorrell, Brenton Cox Jr., Dani Dennis-Sutton, and Collin Oliver likely to make the 53-man roster before Micah Parsons returns from the PUP list at some point in 2026. A perfectly fair take. Running Back: 2.39 PackofBrews88: D I’ve never liked Jacobs. In the last 3 years (1 Raiders, 2 Packers), he has 5 games over 100 rushing yards and 12 under 50 rushing yards. Rushing yards aren’t the be-all-end-all stat but the eye test also tells me he’s not a weapon. Depth is unknown. Now go rush for 4,000 yards as a team this year 🙂 I think my love for blocking back Chris Brooks would have pushed me into the B range here. I’m also excited to see MarShawn Lloyd contribute this regular season. [Knocks on several pieces of wood.] Specialists: 2.23 Bearmeat: The only sensible answer IMO is “incomplete.” Rookie kickers usually struggle. But Trey hasn’t had that chance yet. And the punter is awesome. so I put “C” but I don’t feel great about it. The punter is great. The kicker and long snappers are question marks, as Matt Orzech is currently dealing with a calf injury. The team brought a veteran in while he’s hurt. I get shrugging your shoulders at the unit. Defensive Line: 2.20 AJax8: This defensive line has a chance to be much better than most people seem to think, but it’s dependent on Javon Hargrave not being washed. If he’s still 80% of the pass rusher he was in Philly, he and Wyatt are a hell of a duo and are going to make the edge rushers seem a lot better than they are. I’m less worried about Javon Hargrave, who is still on the PUP list with what the Packers have described as a short-term injury, and more worried about who will play next to Hargrave and Devonte Wyatt in 3-4 base looks. Without Hargrave or Wyatt in team drills, it’s been tough to gauge who has the upper hand right now for that job. Offensive Line: 2.07 TITLETOWN1TOLOVE: It is an average line right now, and I think it is in the C category. We all want a lot of improvement from these guys yesterday. Without being 5 Star General Obvious, we need to stay healthy, we need to gel, and we need to be the best we can be this coming January. Then we can talk about an improvement over the C. I do think we have some young talent, it is up to the coaches to bring out the best in them. I know a lot of folks think poorly of the coaches we have and maybe that’s a problem also. I’m always a glass half full type so I hope we can toast to the line later this year. Honestly, I think they’re a below-average line based on how they played overall last year, but playing Jordan Morgan at left tackle, Sean Rhyan at center and Anthony Belton at right guard will help their running game. The big question to me is whether the guards will be a little more consistent this year, particularly in pass protection. Cornerback: 1.65 Coldworld: I gave it a C. Then again, I’m pretty optimistic that Cisse can help early, at least sufficiently to help make us at least decent. Marlon Jones turned up again in camp today with a pick 6 (Neyor was probably the offensive standout). If Jones from nowhere and Jackson can help too then we might even be better. One can hope. As it stands though, we are a C. Just okay, with or without Nixon. Is anyone surprised cornerback was voted to the bottom of this list? Join the conversation! title: Packers’ defensive leaders ready to climb all-time leaderboards
summary: After exploring the Packers’ potential statistical milestones on offense yesterday, let’s take a look at what they might be able to do on defense this year. Defense, in general, is much less statistically oriented than offense, but there are still a few numbers we can look at. Interceptions Bolstered by eight interceptions in 2024, Xavier […]
full_text: CHICAGO, IL - JANUARY 10: Xavier McKinney #29 of the Green Bay Packers lines up before the snap during an NFC Wild Card Playoff game against the Chicago Bears at Soldier Field on January 10, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images After exploring the Packers’ potential statistical milestones on offense yesterday , let’s take a look at what they might be able to do on defense this year. Defense, in general, is much less statistically oriented than offense, but there are still a few numbers we can look at. Interceptions Bolstered by eight interceptions in 2024, Xavier McKinney’s career total of 10 puts him in a 10-way tie for 48th in Packers history. I’ll spare you the whole list, but if he gets a single interception, he’ll move past Atari Bigby (can’t ever miss a chance to bring up his name), Rasul Douglas, Terrell Buckley, and Damarious Randall. He probably will never reach the upper echelons of Packers history, but just four picks would get him into a three-way tie with Al Harris (woo!) and Ha Ha Clinton-Dix (boo!) for 33rd all-time. No other active Packers player has more than four interceptions in his Green Bay tenure. Time to bump those numbers up! Sacks There is a similar lack of sacks among active players on the Packers’ roster. Micah Parsons has been here just one season and he’s already the lead dog with 12.5. Pro Football Reference made the unwise decision a couple of years ago to integrate unofficial pre-1982 sacks into their team leaderboards with no way to sort out the two eras, so it’s difficult to accurately say how high Parsons could climb this year. It’s safe to say that he probably won’t threaten Kenny Clark (35 career sacks) for 10th all-time, though. However, if he manages 13.5 sacks in the time he’s on the field this year, he’ll find himself in a multi-player tie for fifth most in a single season. That’s probably about the best we could hope for this year, especially if he’s only playing 10 or 11 games or so. Tackles Tackles are really the only other major defensive stat, and that gets a bit tricky, too. The NFL didn’t officially track tackles at a league level until the early 2000s, so we’re only dealing with about 25 years of official history when we talk about tackle totals. That said, Keisean Nixon stands to become the 36th player in Packers history to crack 200 solo tackles this season; he enters the year with 196, so that seems like a pretty safe bet. And with 120 solo tackles to his name, Edgerrin Cooper will probably become the 37th at some point this year. He’s recorded 87 and 118, respectively, in his first two seasons, so he’ll probably crack 200 career solo tackles some time in the second half of the year.
author: Jon Meerdink

title: Green Bay Packers News: MarShawn Lloyd on track to make fans flip with excitement
summary: Green Bay Packers fans will flip out if MarShawn Lloyd can stay healthy this season and provide a quality change of pace as a second running back. They probably won’t literally be doing flips, however, like Lloyd did in practice on Thursday after scoring a big touchdown. Lloyd’s backflip was the highlight of a closed […]
full_text: ASHWAUBENON, WISCONSIN - JULY 31: MarShawn Lloyd #32 of the Green Bay Packers works out during the Green Bay Packers training camp at Ray Nitschke Field on July 31, 2026 in Ashwaubenon, Wisconsin. (Photo by Patrick McDermott/Getty Images) | Getty Images Green Bay Packers fans will flip out if MarShawn Lloyd can stay healthy this season and provide a quality change of pace as a second running back. They probably won’t literally be doing flips, however, like Lloyd did in practice on Thursday after scoring a big touchdown. Lloyd’s backflip was the highlight of a closed practice on Thursday, when the Packers reportedly installed a number of concepts that they are keeping close to the vest. The team has appeared to be a bit more paranoid than usual with what they’re revealing in their open practices thus far, so Matt LaFleur and company were surely happy to have a private practice so they could work on some of the more nuanced and surprising plays they want to have in their arsenal this season. Don’t expect Lloyd to be celebrating like that again, however. He was clear when talking to the media on Thursday afternoon that LaFleur had told him to stop doing that. That’s okay, though — when he scores touchdowns at Lambeau Field instead of on the practice field, there’s a different jumping celebration that will be expected of him. Lloyd may well get a chance to do a Lambeau Leap this evening as well, with Family Night taking place under the lights . Check out the details for tonight’s practice here and keep it at APC for full training camp coverage leading up to the Packers’ preseason opener next Thursday night. Here’s Everything I Saw During Practice 7 of Packers Training Camp | SI.com Bill Huber didn’t get into too much detail because of the secretive nature of the practice, but the lineup notes are the big things to see here. A new #1 offensive line (featuring rookie Jager Burton) and Brandon Cisse continuing to take all of the starter’s reps at cornerback are the most notable items. Packers RB MarShawn Lloyd’s backflip shows he’s finally healthy | NFL.com It’s great that Lloyd is not just healthy but looking explosive and dynamic so far in camp. Given the uncertainty around Josh Jacobs’ long-term future, both due to his legal issues and his contract, it would be enormous if Lloyd can become a major contributor this year. Why Packers are connecting with DC Gannon’s ‘turnt up’ vibe | ESPN Several young Packers players have commented on Gannon’s “crazy” energy, which is a very different side of him than what he showed as a head coach in Arizona. Packers linebacker Zaire Franklin making life easier for safety Xavier McKinney | Packersnews.com ($) It certainly sounds like the Packers intend for Franklin to have the green dot all season long, and his ability to communicate the calls is earning praise. Kangaroo spotted in Swiss woodland | SWI.com Maybe he got confused, booked a trip to Austria, and decided to stay in the Alps? Packers discussion in the feed If you didn’t watch last night’s Hall of Fame Game, that’s entirely understandable. Still, this was a fun moment from before the game, when Packers coach Matt LaFleur called in to talk to his little brother before his coaching debut. title: Packers 2026 Family Night Details & Discussion
summary: One of the best events of the Green Bay Packers’ season is here! Tonight, Lambeau Field opens up for the first time in the football season as the team heads out under the lights for the annual Family Night event. As in past years, the team will hold a practice session as part of the […]
full_text: GREEN BAY, WI - AUGUST 03: Green Bay Packers quarterback Jordan Love (10) throws during the Green Bay Packers Family Night on August 3, 2024 at Lambeau Field in Green Bay, WI. (Photo by Larry Radloff/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images One of the best events of the Green Bay Packers’ season is here! Tonight, Lambeau Field opens up for the first time in the football season as the team heads out under the lights for the annual Family Night event. As in past years, the team will hold a practice session as part of the evening’s festivities. There will be limited live tackling tonight — only one session is expected to have full contact, and that largely will be reserved for young players — but it’s still a big change as the team gets exposure to a largely full stadium after working on the team’s practice field up to now. In good news for fans outside the main Packers TV Network area, the practice will be live-streamed on Packers.com. So click your browsers over there to follow along, and keep it here at APC to discuss in the comments section below! title: Colts CB Cam Taylor-Britt to serve one-game suspension
summary: Indianapolis Colts cornerback Cam Taylor-Britt, who was signed as a free agent from the Cincinnati Bengals, will serve a one-game suspension for violating the the NFL’s personal conduct policy earlier this offseason. He will miss the Colts regular season home opener against the Baltimore Ravens on September 13th, due to pleading guilty to reckless driving, […]
full_text: WESTFIELD, IN - JULY 29: Indianapolis Colts cornerback Cam Taylor-Britt (26) runs through a drill during the Indianapolis Colts training camp practice on July 29, 2026 at the Grand Park Sports Campus in Westfield, IN. (Photo by Zach Bolinger/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Indianapolis Colts cornerback Cam Taylor-Britt, who was signed as a free agent from the Cincinnati Bengals, will serve a one-game suspension for violating the the NFL’s personal conduct policy earlier this offseason. He will miss the Colts regular season home opener against the Baltimore Ravens on September 13th, due to pleading guilty to reckless driving, while also driving without a license. He previously served 5 days in jail after pleading guilty to the charges. Originally a 2022 2nd round pick of the Bengals, the 26-year-old cornerback is coming off a season for Cincinnati in which he recorded 21 tackles (12 solo), a tackle for loss, and 5 passes defensed during 8 games (2 starts) in 2025, before suffering a season-ending Lisfranc injury. This offseason, Taylor-Britt reunited with Colts veteran defensive coordinator Lou Anarumo, who he played under with the Bengals defensively from 2022-24. So far, the early returns have been encouraging. While it’s still relatively early in training camp, Taylor-Britt has currently been operating as the Colts’ CB4, and figures to be ‘the next man up’ on the outside if either Sauce Gardner or Charvarius Ward were to miss time due to an injury—which given the latter’s recent head injury history, could be an important distinction going forward. At any rate, his suspension does not come at an opportune time (although would it ever?), as the Colts secondary will be tasked with slowing down 2x NFL MVP Lamar Jackson come Week 1 at home—and attempt to get off on the right foot at 1-0 to begin the 2026 campaign.

title: The Colts made the right choice look easy
summary: Sometimes life’s easiest choices are made a lot more complicated. The obvious is right in front of us, but overthinking sets in. The Indianapolis Colts were faced with the decision of whether to keep their franchise rushing leader who carried the team at times and proved he has plenty left in the tank due to […]
full_text: Sometimes life’s easiest choices are made a lot more complicated. The obvious is right in front of us, but overthinking sets in. The Indianapolis Colts were faced with the decision of whether to keep their franchise rushing leader who carried the team at times and proved he has plenty left in the tank due to a stellar 2025 season. Seems easy, right? Well, the Colts didn’t overcomplicate things and kept this season trending in the right direction. Jonathan Taylor isn’t going anywhere. The freshly signed two-year extension worth $44 million means the Colts are going to get everything Taylor’s got. If he stays healthy, that could be a lot. After truly breaking out in 2021, it appeared Taylor might have lost his edge. Injuries started to pile up and missed games meant missed opportunities. Some players never recover from that type of dip. Fortunately, Taylor caught his second wind. With over 3,000 yards and 29 touchdowns over the last two seasons, to say Taylor is back, would be an understatement. He has already cemented himself as the franchise leader in rushing touchdowns and is establishing himself as one of the best players in the league. Strip away the allure of the quarterback and Taylor was in the upper echelons of the NFL last year. A full-strength Daniel Jones will be the key to unlocking his full potential. If Jones provides offensive balance, Taylor will shine yet again. At the end of the day, will Jonathan Taylor be worth every penny? How many professional athletes can you say that about when they sign a new deal? That’s impossible to know at this point, but what we can say is that he is worth it now. Historical performance dictated that contract. Here’s hoping the future backs it up.

title: BJ Green, Zach Durfee Headline Jaguars’ Mock Scrimmage
summary: The Jacksonville Jaguars held their annual Teal and White mock game at the Miller Electric Center on Friday morning, a two-and-a-half hour padded session that served as the most game-like look at this roster yet in the 2026 preseason. The day produced some significant individual performances, a handful of injury concerns, and a slightly clearer […]
full_text: Jacksonville Jaguars defensive end BJ Green II (95) walks off the field during the first day of minicamp at the Miller Electric Center, Tuesday, June 9, 2026, in Jacksonville, Fla. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co The Jacksonville Jaguars held their annual Teal and White mock game at the Miller Electric Center on Friday morning, a two-and-a-half hour padded session that served as the most game-like look at this roster yet in the 2026 preseason. The day produced some significant individual performances, a handful of injury concerns, and a slightly clearer picture of where a few roster battles stand heading into the team’s upcoming stretch of three joint practices. Injury Updates The injury and availability picture ended up being much more complicated than expected before the first snap was taken. Left tackle Cole Van Lanen and Garrett DiGiorgio remained on the Active/Physically Unable to Perform list. Head coach Liam Coen confirmed after practice that Josh Hines-Allen was limited with routine load management at this stage of camp rather than anything injury-related. Starting right guard Patrick Mekari, who has been brought along slowly throughout camp, did not participate in team periods, and rookie lineman Emmanuel Pregnon, who was reportedly hobbled during Thursday’s practice, also wasn’t seen early. Pass Rush Had A Day The most dominant individual performance of the entire scrimmage belonged to B.J. Green II, and it was not particularly close. Green opened the day with a tackle for a loss, then followed it immediately with a sack on the very next play. After Dennis Gardeck added a sack in between, Green came back and recorded a second on the following drive. By the time the padded sessions wrapped up, Green had four sacks and a tackle for a loss, primarily against Jimto Obidegwu. His performance on Day 8 was the most emphatic individual statement any player in camp has made about his role on this roster. Rookie edge Zach Durfee had a significant day as well, beating Walker Little off the edge for a would-be sack on the very first play of the mock game – the play that ended Little’s participation for the afternoon. He later added a second sack against Wyatt Milum on third down, giving him two on the day and continuing a camp-long trend of the seventh-round rookie from Washington making it impossible to overlook him in the pass rush rotation. Coen lauded both young rushers following the scrimmage: “They’ve continued to do that throughout the course of the last few practices, and Durf had a good rush the other day, backed up. It would’ve been a 99-yard touchdown; it ended up being probably a safety. So, he’s showing up. B.J.’s continued to show up in both the run and the pass. So, I’ve been pleased with those guys.” I also noted Dennis Gardeck with two sacks to round out the group, in a dominant day against the Jaguars’ offensive line group. OL Rotation Into Question The previously mentioned non-participation list grew even larger in Friday’s session, as Walker Little went down on the very first play of the mock game without returning. Chuma Edoga, who stepped in as the swing tackle, was hobbled following his own opening play, before eventually working his way back into the practice. Little’s departure on the opening play represents the latest complication in what has been an unsettled situation at tackle throughout camp. He had been working at right tackle while Anton Harrison occupied the left tackle spot, an arrangement that has drawn major attention over the past week. His availability moving forward, and the depth questions that follow on both the left and right side could become more pressing. Coen confirmed that Little would be evaluated following practice, while providing no new updates, from the practice fields. With Mekari, Pregnon, Little, and Edoga all either unavailable or limited on Friday, the Jaguars worked through multiple combinations along the front five. The primary look featured Anton Harrison at left tackle, Ezra Cleveland at left guard, and Robert Hainsey at center, with Jonah Monheim at right guard, and Wyatt Milum at right tackle. Monheim’s performance was an unexpectedly clean performance, with no clear sacks or pressures surrendered in pass protection, while Milum worked at both right tackle and right guard, experiencing a rough early stretch that included a false start and the Durfee sack before stabilizing and finishing the day on a considerably stronger note. The right guard competition between Milum and Mekari is one to watch closely over the coming stretch of joint practices. Milum has earned consistent first-team reps throughout camp in Mekari’s absence, and the experience he accumulates before Mekari returns to full participation will carry real weight in how that competition ultimately resolves. Lawrence Sharp When It Counted Lawrence had a quiet opening before finding his rhythm as the session developed. He connected with Parker Washington twice during the third drive and was consistently accurate in the intermediate range, the 15 to 25-yard window, throughout the day. The biggest blemish was an early end zone pass toward Brian Thomas Jr. that nearly resulted in an interception, with cornerback Keni H Lovely getting both hands on the ball before letting it fall incomplete. Jalen Huskey was also in the area on that play. Liam Coen addressed the sequence after practice, describing it as a communication and timing issue between Lawrence and Thomas: “This is the time to do it, is to challenge some of your concepts and timing. I think that he [QB Trevor Lawrence] probably wanted to getthere a little quicker when he did. So, it was one of those plays that B.T. can go to the postor he can go behind the defender and stay there. And I think it was just a little bit of amiscommunication, from that standpoint, from the leverage and technique that I think it was Keni [CB Keni-H Lovely] was playing at corner. I don’t love the long foul ball, just like toss it up and see what happens. And I don’t think that’s what it was. It was more of a miscommunication that those guys will get right.” The other miss was a late practice overthrow to Jakobi Meyers on a 40-yard deep ball inside the hashes. Lawrence bounced back on the same drive as the missed Meyers’ target, finishing it with a back-shoulder throw to Brian Thomas Jr. in the red zone for a touchdown, however. Parker’s Down There Somewhere Washington was easily the starting offense’s most consistent playmaker on Friday. Whenever the office needed a play it was Washington who got the team on track. A 35-yard catch and run provided the spark the first-team unit needed early, finding the spot within the zone. Let us know if you've seen this one before… Grab free tickets to Sunday's practice: https://t.co/fhVdfYSB9O @Dream_Finders | #DUUUVAL pic.twitter.com/56mDh6TI9u — Jacksonville Jaguars (@Jaguars) August 7, 2026 He later capped the drive with a two-yard contested touchdown catch over cornerback Jabbar Muhammad, after a 15-yard reception to enter the redzone. Washington continues to show himself as a key that opens up this offense. I think camp was received well today 😊 Grab free tickets to Sunday's practice: https://t.co/fhVdfYT8Zm @Dream_Finders | #DUUUVAL pic.twitter.com/Cm9ZLu80Ub — Jacksonville Jaguars (@Jaguars) August 7, 2026 Play of the Scrimmage The individual play of the day, however, went to cornerback Buster Brown. On a Nick Mullens throw intended for running back J’Mari Taylor deep down the field, Brown kept his eyes on the backup quarterback, then climbed the ladder in coverage, coming away with the athletic interception. title: Chiefs training camp notebook Day 9: Kahlil Benson plays right guard
summary: The ninth practice of Kansas City Chiefs training camp was back to full pads, with the team working plenty of run game and full-team work. It is the second-to-last practice before a rest day on Sunday. Arrowhead Pride analyst Caleb James and I watched practice together; I recommend scanning Caleb’s timelines on X for all […]
full_text: ST JOSEPH, MISSOURI - JULY 25: Josh Thompson #62, Pete Nygra #50 and Kahlil Benson #70 walk toward the practice field during Kansas City Chiefs Training Camp at Missouri Western State University on July 25, 2026 in St Joseph, Missouri. (Photo by Jamie Squire/Getty Images) | Getty Images The ninth practice of Kansas City Chiefs training camp was back to full pads, with the team working plenty of run game and full-team work. It is the second-to-last practice before a rest day on Sunday. Arrowhead Pride analyst Caleb James and I watched practice together; I recommend scanning Caleb’s timelines on X for all the observations and clips he got out of Friday’s practice. Here’s everything to know from the work done by the Chiefs on the field: Attendance report Head coach Andy Reid spoke to the media at the podium after practice. Check out our injury update on the site from earlier . Kahlil Benson moves inside to right guard Starting right guard Trey Smith was the most notable absence from camp on Friday, mainly because the hip injury was a surprise as the team took the field. When the starting offensive line took form, it still featured rookie Kahlil Benson. This time, he played in Smith’s place at right guard and veteran Jaylon Moore manned right tackle for quarterback Patrick Mahomes. After spending what seems to be the entirety of the offseason playing right tackle, Benson was back inside at right guard, a position he accumulated nearly 1,000 collegiate snaps at between his time at Indiana and Colorado, according to Pro Football Focus . That said, he hasn’t played the position since 2024, so settling back in featured a few lost reps to defensive tackles Chris Jones and rookie Peter Woods in strong, dominating fashion. Peter. Woods. pic.twitter.com/UBHgDKoorK — Ron Kopp Jr (@RonOnChiefs) August 7, 2026 On this rep against Woods, offensive line evaluator Brandon Thorn of Bleacher Report shared his thoughts on why Benson lost in a post on X . “70 a tick late off the ball and it was curtains. Snap timing in the trenches >>>” The note aligned with Reid’s thoughts on Benson’s day, sharing them with local media after practice. “I thought he did okay; there were a couple of hiccups in there,” Reid said at the podium. “Things move a little bit faster when you’re inside… everything jumps on you quickly.” With the Chiefs’ defensive line looking like a strong unit for defensive coordinator Steve Spagnuolo to deploy in creative ways, it becomes an even stronger challenge for Benson. “When you go against Spags, you’re going to get a lot of different flavors, and you have to be able to make those decisions right now in an area that’s faster than the tackle position,” Reid explained. “I thought he held his own physically, for sure, and there are a couple of things he has to pick up from there.” My thought on the move: The Chiefs could be signaling that Benson is one of the team’s best five offensive linemen. If Reid values having as many of his best on the field at a time, it makes sense that Benson shifts inside with a veteran offensive tackle in the wings to fill in on the edge instead of keeping Benson at right tackle and having an existing reserve inside step up. Patrick Mahomes working on his mobility On one particular play in a full-team period, the Chiefs’ starting defense blitzed Mahomes, but the playmaking quarterback broke contain to the right and looked to make a play with his legs past the line of scrimmage. Pat breaks containment on a blitz rolling right, starts trying to make a play and dodging defenders… We get it Pat, you’re feeling good, maybe just throw the ball please 😅 — Ron Kopp Jr (@RonOnChiefs) August 7, 2026 By the end of the play, Mahomes was on the ground, and my stomach had dropped, but he was ultimately fine. It speaks to the comfort Mahomes has in his knee, but he’s also actively working to gain comfort in one of the most important aspects of playing the quarterback position, according to Reid. “To play in a game, you have to have escapability,” Reid emphasized to reporters. “Or you can’t be in there; you can’t play that position and be a target; you have to have some mobility back there. So he works on that. If it’s not there down the field, he takes off and runs. Every time he does it, it builds a little bit more confidence in the leg.” Brashard Smith moving up the depth chart After being selected in the seventh round of last year’s draft, coached up by a staff that is no longer with the Chiefs after his rookie year, Smith has earned a good number of snaps with the starting offense in camp this year. It’s clear that the focus for Smith is on pass protection. Reid believes he has taken positive steps in that direction as camp has progressed. “Protection for the young guys is the big thing,” Reid began. “So we’ve been putting him in position there where you have to know the rules, you have to be able to step up physically and hold onto it; he has done a nice job with that. With that, he has gotten more reps. We know he can run the ball, we know he can catch the ball, but that other part is a big part. The more reps he gets at it, the better he has gotten.” At the 2025 NFL Scouting Combine, Smith weighed in at 194 pounds. It has likely been a point of emphasis for Smith to gain weight as he has begun his professional career. Reid sees good progress there, too. “He looks a little bit bigger; he was skinny last year,” Reid said. “But it looks like he has put some good weight on.” The Chiefs will be back on the practice field in pads on Saturday morning, starting at 9:15 a.m.

After its conclusion, head coach Andy Reid provided an injury update, one that is still lengthier than anyone in […]
full_text: ST JOSEPH, MISSOURI - JULY 26: Head coach Andy Reid participates during Kansas City Chiefs Training Camp alongside quarterbacks Chris Oladokun #19, Patrick Mahomes #15 and Justin Fields #6 at Missouri Western State University on July 25, 2026 in St Joseph, Missouri. (Photo by Jamie Squire/Getty Images) | Getty Images The ninth full-team practice of Kansas City Chiefs training camp took place on a sunny day in St. Joe. The team worked for a full two hours on the grass fields at Missouri Western State University. After its conclusion, head coach Andy Reid provided an injury update, one that is still lengthier than anyone in Chiefs Kingdom would like to see. “One positive about these injuries is there’s nothing that the guys aren’t coming back from,” Reid assured local media. “But we got some nicks and bruises.” Players that did not practice Linebacker Jeffrey Bassa (groin) Defensive end Ashton Gillotte (hamstring) Right guard Trey Smith (Hip) “His hip was bothering him,” Reid said of Smith, who missed his first practice of camp on Friday. “[We] sent him to a specialist just to have it checked out. Precautionary, he’s going to be okay.” Cornerback L’Jarius Sneed (Knee) “L’Jarius, just like we did when he was here before, we’re managing his knee,” Reid told reporters. “We know the problem, and we manage through that.” Linebacker Drue Tranquill (Back) “Like last year, he gets low-back tightness,” Reid described the veteran. “Some soreness so we’re just calming him down.” Wide receiver Xavier Worthy (shoulder) “Xavier’s making progress with the shoulder,” Reid shared. Players that partially participated in practice Cornerback Mansoor Delane (Shoulder) Wide receiver Rashee Rice (Knee) “Delane got good work today, Rashee got good work today,” Reid shared about two players working back towards 100%. Unlike Rice, Delane has been wearing a non-contact jersey and has not participated in live-contact drills. Rice has been making progress each day throughout camp from a physical standpoint. Wide receiver Cyrus Allen (Shin bruise) The rookie wideout took the field in pads for the first time since he left Monday’s practice due to injury. He was not seen in drills that went against a defense, avoiding contact in only his second practice of camp in pads. “Ease him back in,” Reid said of Allen. “He did a good job when he was back in there, so that’s a positive.” “He’s at all the meetings; he’s focused in, he wants to get out there, he doesn’t want to miss,” Reid continued. “He’s been working hard; we’ll just ease him back in like I said.” Patrick Mahomes likely not playing preseason Week 1 Coach Reid was asked about his thoughts on Mahomes starting in the team’s first preseason game against the Los Angeles Rams next Saturday, August 15th. “There’s a pretty good chance I don’t play him,” Reid said. “And percentages are leaning that way. I don’t know if I’ll play him the second or third game; I don’t know that, but percentages probably lean against doing that. “We got new people in those other positions behind him that need some work,” Reid elaborated. “So the more reps they get, the better.” The Chiefs will have one more padded practice on Saturday at 9:15 a.m. before a rest day on Sunday.
