title: Patriots 2026 scouting report for WR Romeo Doubs
summary: The New England Patriots passing offense enjoyed considerable success during the 2025 season, but the need for improvement became obvious during the playoffs. Going against some of the NFL’s top-tier offenses, the lack of top-tier talent became an issue that contributed to the unit’s postseason struggles. And so, the Patriots set out to fix the […]
full_text: FOXBOROUGH, MA - AUGUST 01: New England Patriots wide receiver Romeo Doubs (87) warms up during training camp on August 1, 2026, at Gillette Stadium in Foxborough, MA. (Photo by M. Anthony Nesmith/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The New England Patriots passing offense enjoyed considerable success during the 2025 season, but the need for improvement became obvious during the playoffs. Going against some of the NFL’s top-tier offenses, the lack of top-tier talent became an issue that contributed to the unit’s postseason struggles. And so, the Patriots set out to fix the problem. One of the first investments made to do so was signing ex-Packers wideout Romeo Doubs to a four-year contract in free agency — a deal that sets him up to be one of the team’s most important receivers in 2026 and beyond. Hard facts Name: Romeo Doubs Position: Wide receiver Jersey number: 87 Opening day age: 26 (4/13/2000) Measurements : 6’1 7/8”, 204 lbs, 10” hand size, 32 1/4” arm length, 77 3/8” wingspan, 13 bench press reps, N/A Relative Athletic Score Experience NFL: Green Bay Packers (2022-25), New England Patriots (2026-) | College: Nevada (2018-21) Productive in a multi-faceted role during his high school career at Jefferson in Los Angeles, Doubs was a fairly highly-regarded college recruit who ended up getting almost a dozen scholarship offers as a three-star prospect. He eventually opted for the University of Nevada, where he was a heavily-involved wide receiver from the get-go and in his 44 total games ended up catching 225 passes for 3,322 yards and 26 touchdowns. A first-team All-Mountain West selection as both a junior and senior, Doubs entered the NFL in 2022 and was selected 132nd overall in the fourth round by the Packers. Once at the pro level, he picked up right where he left off. Doubs caught 42 passes his rookie year, good enough for fourth on the team and second among its wide receivers. Since then, he only strengthened his position in the Packers offense, and by the end of his fourth season in Green Bay had a combined 63 regular season and playoff appearances as well as 222 total receptions for 2,795 yards and 23 touchdowns on his résumé. Doubs turned his Packers tenure into a four-year, $68 million free agency deal with the Patriots in 2026. Scouting report Strengths: Doubs lacks some of the athletic traits the NFL’s top-flight wide receivers possess, but he has developed into a dependable receiving target nonetheless. From the release through the stem of the route to the catch point he has become a lot more refined, while showing a good feel for leverage and defensive coverage — a mix of skills that has made him particularly effective working in the red zone. Additionally, he has been getting better as a hands catcher and in the blocking department. Doubs is more than capable of making an impact on all three downs and from all over the formation. He also is able to generate quick separation and work the underneath areas of the field against both man and zone. In short, he is as consistent a wide receiver as you will find and therefore somebody deserving of the “go-to guy” label. Weaknesses: Doubs is not the most imposing athlete both in terms of build and explosiveness. He has good length but lacks size overall, which in turn puts pressure on his technique to beat press-man coverage or win contested catches. He makes up for it with natural hands and good concentration, but he is not a 50/50 jump ball specialist you would trust in such situations on a regular basis. He also won’t consistently challenge teams deep, in part because he lacks high-end long speed and his game as a whole is more horizontal than vertical. 2025 review Stats : 17 games (16 starts) | 832 offensive snaps (74.2%), 38 special teams snaps (8.5%) | 94 targets, 63 catches (67.0%), 848 receiving yards (13.5/catch), 7 TDs, 4 drops | 15 punt returns, 94 yards (6.3/return) | 1 penalty (incl. 0 declined/offsetting) Season recap: Doubs’ 2024 season ended in disappointment when he had to leave his team’s playoff loss to Philadelphia with a concussion. He managed to bounce back strongly, however, and in the final year under his rookie contract played arguably the best football of his career. Fully establishing himself as quarterback Jordan Love’s favorite receiver and a core piece of the Packers offense, Doubs finished the regular season ranked first on the team in targets (83), receptions (55) and receiving yards (724), and was tied for the lead in touchdowns (6). His production fluctuated a bit through the year, but he shined repeatedly. Whether it was catching three touchdowns against the Cowboys, hauling in seven receptions for 91 yards versus the Panthers, or averaging 20.7 yards on three receptions versus Baltimore, Doubs combined a high volume of snaps and opportunities with big-play potential. Never became that more apparent than the postseason. Even though Green Bay ended up coming short again, Doubs was on fire in the playoffs. He caught eight passes on 11 targets for 124 yards and a touchdown in the Packers’ 31-27 wild card loss to the Bears. ROMEO DOUBS WITH ONE HAND 😳 GBvsCHI on Prime Video Also streaming on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/EyFBmRtXRf — NFL (@NFL) January 11, 2026 Doubs’ efforts in the game against the Bears ultimately were for naught, but the fourth-year receiver showed a national audience — and the rest of the NFL — what he is capable of. Less than two months later, he was cashing in because of, in part, his performance that day and throughout the 2025 campaign overall. 2026 preview Position: Z/X-receiver | Ability: Quality starter | Contract: Signed through 2029 (2030 UFA) What will be his role? As if his contract wasn’t already enough of an indication, training camp confirmed that Doubs will be a starting receiver in New England. With A.J. Brown the top option on the perimeter and DeMario Douglas holding down the fort in the slot, he projects as the primary Z-receiver but is flexible enough to move elsewhere in the formation if the personnel package or play selection call for it. Either way, he should end 2025 among the Patriots’ leaders in wide receiver snaps, targets and catches. What is his growth potential? Even though his statistical production may not suggest so, Doubs improved as a receiver every season since entering the NFL. In every facet of the game, he is a better player now than he was earlier in his career. The hope for the Patriots is that the arrow will continue pointing up in an offense led by an MVP runner-up quarterback and one of the best play-callers in football. Does he have positional versatility? Even though he is the top Z-receiver on paper, Doubs will not be confined to one particular role in the Patriots’ offense. He lines up at the Z, but is also capable of moving to X or even to the slot when the team goes to condensed looks. Naturally, catching the football is his main task but New England would not have brought him in if he couldn’t also help out as a blocker in the run game. He additionally offers some special teams experience: besides the 15 punt returns he had in 2025, he also ran back a pair of kickoffs as a rookie. What is his salary cap situation? As noted above, Doubs signed a four-year, $68 million contract with the Patriots in March. The deal comes with an $8.6 million cap figure for the 2026 season that can be broken down as follows: it consists of a base salary ($3M), signing bonus proration ($3.75M), roster bonus ($1.7M) and two workout bonus prorations ($75k + $75k) as well as incentives classified as not likely to be earned ($3M). With the logical exception of the incentives, all of those numbers are guaranteed. How safe is his roster spot? Doubs is a nailed-on lock to make the Patriots’ roster this season and play a major role in their offensive operation. The real question is just how effectively his chemistry with quarterback Drake Maye will develop, but there have been promising…

title: What signing Eric Butler, waiving David Blay Jr. means for the Patriots
summary: The New England Patriots closed the busiest week of this year’s training camp so far by making a change to the backend of their roster. In a rookie-for-rookie transaction, they signed safety Eric Butler and placed defensive tackle David Blay Jr. on waivers. Let’s assess what the moves mean for the team from a big-picture […]
full_text: FOXBOROUGH, MA - JUNE 09: David Blay Jr. #96 of the New England Patriots in warmups during New England Patriots Minicamp on June 9, 2026, at Gillette Stadium in Foxborough, Massachusetts. (Photo by Summer Lamont/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The New England Patriots closed the busiest week of this year’s training camp so far by making a change to the backend of their roster. In a rookie-for-rookie transaction , they signed safety Eric Butler and placed defensive tackle David Blay Jr. on waivers. Let’s assess what the moves mean for the team from a big-picture perspective. Added versatility Butler spent his entire four-year college career at San Diego State, appearing in 48 games with 23 starts. While not a particularly noteworthy athlete as evidenced by his 5.86 Relative Athletic Score , he managed to make a positive impact on the Aztecs’ defense throughout his tenure. That is in large part because of his versatility. He primarily lined up as a box safety/linebacker hybrid his first two season. While offering solid length at 6-foot-2, he didn’t have the bulk to necessarily flourish in that role and was moved around the formation from his sophomore campaign on: he added slot duties, and later also saw regular action as a free safety. Per Pro Football Focus , he eventually ended his stint at San Diego State with 648 slot snaps, 474 box snaps, 294 free safety snaps as well as 21 split out wide and 14 on the line of scrimmage. He also has five-units special teams experience, with most of his action coming on the punt return unit, where he mostly served as a rusher, as well as on kickoff coverage and field goal/extra point block. He blocked two punts during his college career and registered five tackles in the game’s third phase. Given his versatile skillset, it would not be a surprise if Butler was eventually used as a rotational safety and multi-unit special teamer in preseason. With Brenden Schooler remaining on the NFI list, that would give the club some extra depth in two areas. Improved safety depth Speaking of Brenden Schooler, he and Butler are now two of eight total safeties on New England’s roster. The full group looks as follows, per our regularly updated Patriots depth chart : Safety (8): Kevin Byard (31), Craig Woodson (4), Mike Brown (33), Dell Pettus (24), Brenden Schooler (41), John Saunders Jr. (23), Peter Manuma (34), Eric Butler (—) Out of those eight safeties, three are locks to make the team. Kevin Byard and Craig Woodson are the starting duo, with Schooler a team captain on special teams. According to head coach Mike Vrabel, he remains a “large part” of the team’s plans but there is no “reason to rush him back now until he’s as close to 100% as he possibly can be.” As for the other safeties on the roster, including Butler, they will compete for what realistically will be no more than two if not just one spot. Needless to say, the newest addition to the group is likely facing the longest odds. Unsurprising outcome To make room for Butler, the Patriots parted ways with fellow undrafted free agent David Blay Jr. Waiving the 23-year-old reduces the defensive tackle group to nine players, which is still sufficient depth considering that New England recently signed veteran free agent Casey Rogers. The Rogers addition already seemed to mark the end of Blay’s journey; the new signing was present at practice wearing the same jersey number while the youngster was nowhere to be seen. That eventually turned out not to be the case, and Blay was back at practice the next day. Still, given that he did not make any noticeable contributions in training camp so far, the writing very much remained on the wall. Blay will now get a chance to go through waivers and get claimed by another team. If not, he will become a free agent. Minor cap impact Butler’s three-year UDFA deal with the Patriots is unlikely to include a signing bonus, which means that his addition has no immediate impact on the Patriots’ current salary cap space. The same is not true for waiving Blay. Blay’s own rookie pact featured a $10,000 signing bonus prorated over three years. Its impact on the 2026 books remains the same regardless of his status: it was $3,333 before he was cut, and it remains $3,333 now, albeit in dead cap. The entire rest of that bonus, however, will now hit the 2027 books for a combined sum of $6,667. In addition, Blay’s $50,000 salary guarantee might also become relevant soon. If he goes unclaimed through the waiver wire, it too would hit the Patriots’ 2026 books as dead cap to increase his potential combined salary cap impact for this season to $53,333.

title: Patriots sign safety Eric Butler following workout, waive defensive tackle
summary: A recent visitor to Gillette Stadium has returned one week later. The New England Patriots announced the signing of safety Eric Butler on Friday. In a corresponding 91-man roster move, the organization waived defensive tackle David Blay Jr. Butler, 23, was in Foxborough for a workout during the initial days of training camp in July. […]
full_text: San Diego, California - November 15: Eric Butler #6 of the San Diego State Aztecs looks on during their game against the Boise State Broncos at Snapdragon Stadium on Saturday, Nov. 15, 2025 in San Diego, California. (Meg McLaughlin / The San Diego Union-Tribune via Getty Images) A recent visitor to Gillette Stadium has returned one week later. The New England Patriots announced the signing of safety Eric Butler on Friday. In a corresponding 91-man roster move, the organization waived defensive tackle David Blay Jr. Butler, 23, was in Foxborough for a workout during the initial days of training camp in July. Prior to then, the 6-foot-2, 195-pound defensive back went unselected in the 2026 NFL draft and earned invitations to rookie minicamp with the Las Vegas Raiders and New Orleans Saints. A San Diego State product, Butler appeared in 48 games, including 23 starts, during his Aztecs career. He totaled 119 tackles, one sack, one forced fumble, one fumble recovery, one interception returned a touchdown, as well as two blocked punts. Blay, 23, had agreed to terms with the reigning AFC champions as part of the club’s undrafted class in May. The 6-foot-2, 292-pound rookie defensive lineman began his collegiate career at West Chester before stints at Louisiana Tech and Miami. Blay checked into 46 games over that span. And from 2023 through 2025, he made 35 appearances while notching 90 tackles and 6.5 sacks between Conference USA and ACC play. The Patriots move further into August with eight safeties in the fold, including Kevin Byard, Craig Woodson, Mike Brown, Dell Pettus, John Saunders Jr., Peter Manuma and special teams captain Brenden Schooler, who remains on the non-football injury list . On the interior defensive line, New England’s depth chart now stands at nine, including Milton Williams, Christian Barmore, Cory Durden, Joshua Farmer, Leonard Taylor III, Eric Gregory, Jeremiah Pharms Jr., Isaiah Iton and recent addition Casey Rogers. The preseason opens next Thursday at Gillette Stadium with a 7:30 p.m. ET kickoff against the Indianapolis Colts.

title: 6 performances of note from the Patriots’ 12th training camp practice
summary: After four straight days of practice, the New England Patriots decided to change things up a bit. It was scrimmage time in Foxborough, with Drake Maye’s White Team taking on the Blue Team led by his backup Tommy DeVito. To recap the session, please head over to our Patriots training camp notebook. In the meantime, […]
full_text: FOXBOROUGH, MA - AUGUST 07: Tommy DeVito #16 of the New England Patriots warms up during New England Patriots training camp on August 6, 2026 at Gillette Stadium in Foxborough, Massachusetts. (Photo by Summer Lamont/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images After four straight days of practice, the New England Patriots decided to change things up a bit. It was scrimmage time in Foxborough, with Drake Maye’s White Team taking on the Blue Team led by his backup Tommy DeVito. To recap the session, please head over to our Patriots training camp notebook . In the meantime, here is who caught our eye from the session. Standout of the day WR DeMario Douglas: Who else did you think we were going to pick? His name is in the headline of today’s practice recap, for crying out loud! Working with backup quarterback Tommy DeVito’s team, the starting slot receiver hauled in six receptions including a pair of touchdowns: one on a slant and the other on a corner route. He also made a big play during a late-practice two-minute work, charging up the seam to haul in a 50-yard pass from DeVito that put the group into field goal range. Douglas was the top pass catcher of the day, and indeed the whole week. Other performances of note QB Tommy DeVito: DeVito celebrated his 28th birthday in style. The Patriots’ backup quarterback had a good day leading the Team Blue offense. With DeMario Douglas as his preferred target, he threw a pair of touchdowns while also showcasing his accuracy and arm strength on that aforementioned 50-yarder late during the session. He went a respectable 13-of-16 on the day and showed why he is clearly the No. 2 on the QB depth chart. ED Xavier Holmes and LB Khalil Jacobs: While tight end Tanner Arkin has received most of the attention among the undrafted rookies, and rightfully so, Holmes and Jacobs are also in the midst of putting together strong training camps. The latter has a more favorable roster outlook than the former, but both boosted their case on Friday: Holmes registered both a would-be sack and a pass breakup when he batted down a screen pass, while Jacobs forced a pair of throwaways and nearly had an interception against Behren Morton. CB Kindle Vildor: The race for the Patriots’ final cornerback spots continues to evolve, and on Friday Vildor was one of the more notable competitors. The free agency signing, who has had an up-and-down training camp so far, broke up two passes intended for A.J. Brown on the opening drive of the scrimmage. K Andy Borregales: New England’s kicker has looked very good throughout the summer, which is why Friday was an uncharacteristic down day. Borregales missed a field goal from around 50 yards out, and he later also shanked an extra point. Both misses came to his left. Coming off five straight practices, the Patriots will now head into a two-day weekend without any sessions scheduled. They will return to the fields behind Gillette Stadium on Monday, for a session closed to the public. The next opportunity to watch the team will come on Tuesday with the Colts in town for a joint practice ahead of the two clubs’ preseason opener.

title: Patriots training camp recap: DeMario Douglas shines in Friday scrimmage
summary: After four straight days of work, the New England Patriots put the pads on for a scrimmage on Friday. Teams were split into blue and white and drafted by a divided coaching staff. Here’s what went down throughout the session on the hot and humid fields behind Gillette Stadium. Attendance Absent: CB Carlton Davis III, […]
full_text: Jul 28, 2026; Foxborough, MA, USA; New England Patriots wide receiver DeMario Douglas (3) makes a catch during training camp at Gillette Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Eric Canha-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect After four straight days of work, the New England Patriots put the pads on for a scrimmage on Friday. Teams were split into blue and white and drafted by a divided coaching staff. Here’s what went down throughout the session on the hot and humid fields behind Gillette Stadium. Attendance Absent: CB Carlton Davis III, OT Will Campbell, DL Christian Barmore, CB Charles Woods, OG Caedan Wallace, WR Cameron Dorner, FB Reggie Gilliam Limited: WR A.J. Brown, OT Morgan Moses Injured: WR Kyle Dixon PUP/NFI: ED Harold Landry III, S Brenden Schooler Mike Vrabel provided updates on Carlton Davis and Will Campbell on Friday, saying the cornerback would be out through next week’s preseason game while the offensive tackle is expected back to start next week. The Patriots were without Christian Barmore and Charles Woods, who each left practice early on Thursday, while Reggie Gilliam continues to see his workload managed. UDFA wide receiver Kyle Dixon did depart the scrimmage early with a trainer. Rookie offensive tackle Caleb Lomu also briefly departed albeit due to an apparent equipment malfunction. Takeaways Teams: With the roster divided in half, head coaches Terrell Williams (Team White) and Tony Dews (Team Blue) were in charge of drafting the roster. The only two rules: Drake Maye and center Jared Wilson must be together, while best friends Mack Hollins and Efton Chism are also a duo. As for the rest of the rosters, Team Blue was led by A.J. Brown, Christian Gonzalez and Milton Williams — as an emphasis on skill positions also gave them DeMario Douglas, Hollins and Chism, Rhamondre Stevenson, Hunter Henry, Marcus Jones, Craig Woodson and Kevin Byard. Team White, meanwhile, had an emphasis in the trenches with Caleb Lomu, Andrew Rupcich, Jared Wilson, Mike Onwenu, and Morgan Moses protecting Drake Maye, who largely threw to Kayshon Boutte, Kyle Williams, TreVeyon Henderson, and Eli Raridon. Dre’Mont Jones and Gabe Jacas then anchored their pass rush. For the rest of the coaching staff, quarterbacks coach Ashton Grant and safeties coach Scott Booker coordinated Team White, while wide receivers coach Todd Downing and cornerbacks coach Justin Hamilton coordinated Team Blue. DeVito and Pop: Drake Maye’s squad found themselves in an early deficit, much to do with Tommy DeVito and DeMario Douglas’ connection Team Blue. DeVito’s second drive ended with a slant touchdown to Douglas and the duo later scored on a corner route when drives started inside the red area. Douglas was then on scene for one last big play in two-minute work, as the first play from scrimmage saw him streak up the seam and get behind the defense for a 50-plus yard gain to immediately put the team in field goal range. DeVito, who celebrated his 28th birthday on Friday, also had strong completions to A.J. Brown on a play-action slant, Mack Hollins on a downfield flea-flicker, and two in-rhythm passes to Efton Chism. Maye’s offense: It was a slow start to the day for Drake Maye, whose first two drives ended in “punts” with multiple throwaways. The quarterback then led an eight-play scoring drive, which featured a seam shot to Eli Raridon, fourth-down conversion to Nick DeGennaro, and a touchdown on a play-action crosser to Romeo Doubs. Maye then ended his day with successful red zone and two-minute periods. He needed just one pass in the red zone as he connected with TreVeyon Henderson for a touchdown on a corner route, before working into field goal range with 1:05 on the clock behind multiple check-downs and a chunk play to Kyle Williams — who received notable praise from Mike Vrabel before the session — over the middle of the field. Other notes: With Will Campbell sidelined, Caleb Lomu repped at left tackle for Team White with Morgan Moses on the right side. As the veteran was limited, James Hudson worked at right tackle. Team Blue’s offensive line: Marcus Bryant, Alijah Vera-Tucker, Ben Brown, JonDarius Morgan, Dametrious Crownover. Partnered with Drake Maye, rookie tight end Eli Raridon caught three passes — one explosive up the seam and two check downs to kick start the two-minute drive. Perhaps the play of the day: a pass to wide receiver Tejhaun Palmer that was bobbled and nabbed out of the air by running back Myles Montgomery, who then took it for a 40-ish yard gain. The explosive play by Montgomery helped Behren Morton’s first drive end in a field goal. The rookie QB’s second drive did not goes as well, as it ended with a bad snap, sack, and near interception but Khalil Jacobs. Working on Team White, Gabe Jacas continued to be noticeable along the edge recording an early pressure against fellow rookie Dametrious Crownover and at least half a sack later with Leonard Taylor III, who also had a batted pass. UDFA pass rusher Xavier Holmes also remains impressive along the edge with a sack and pass breakup. Another day, another strong showing for defensive lineman Joshua Farmer with two more run stuffs. Veteran cornerback Kindle Vildor has two early pass breakups in coverage on A.J. Brown. Brandon Crossley, Marcus Jones, and Channing Canada also recorded pass breakups in the secondary. In total, Andy Borregales went 4-of-5 on field goals — with a max distance appearing to be 54 yards — and connected on 1-of-2 extra points. The Patriots will be off this weekend before returning to work on Monday. Practice will start at 10:15 a.m. ET and be closed to the public before the Indianapolis Colts come to town on Tuesday.

title: Patriots WR Kyle Williams receives high praise from Mike Vrabel
summary: So far this offseason, the New England Patriots have had a clear pecking order at wide receiver. A.J. Brown, Romeo Doubs and DeMario Douglas are the starting trio at the top, with Kayshon Boutte a fourth option who has repeatedly shown his big play abilities and chemistry with quarterback Drake Maye. Behind them, Mack Hollins […]
full_text: FOXBOROUGH, MA - AUGUST 06: Kyle Williams #18 of the New England Patriots runs in a drill during New England Patriots training camp on August 6, 2026 at Gillette Stadium in Foxborough, Massachusetts. (Photo by Summer Lamont/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images So far this offseason, the New England Patriots have had a clear pecking order at wide receiver. A.J. Brown, Romeo Doubs and DeMario Douglas are the starting trio at the top, with Kayshon Boutte a fourth option who has repeatedly shown his big play abilities and chemistry with quarterback Drake Maye. Behind them, Mack Hollins continues to see prominent snaps all over the formation. Then, there are sophomores Efton Chism and Kyle Williams. The former has seen some action with the starters as well, particularly during Doubs’ recent non-injury-related absence . The latter, on the other hand, has only occasionally taken the field alongside Maye and the top offense. That could very well change in the future, at least if Mike Vrabel is to be believed. Speaking to reporters ahead of Friday’s scrimmage on the Gillette Stadium practice fields, the Patriots’ head coach spoke highly about the 2025 third-round draft choice. In fact, he predicted a prominent role within the operation. “He’ll continue to earn opportunities,” Vrabel said. “I really, really know that Kyle is going to help us. His speed is going to help us.” How exactly that help would look like or indeed manifest itself Vrabel did not explain. He did, however, say that Williams’ particular speed-based skillset would be the foundation of his role. “We’re going to find ways to get him the ball, and it may be outside of just the normal installation plays,” Vrabel said. “That’s my responsibility, that’s Josh [McDaniels]’s responsibility, that’s Todd [Downings]’s, responsibility to put him in those positions where we see the speed that showed up last year. “I know that he is going to be a large part of what we’re going to do, and those opportunities will continue to come. His release skills, his speed, his vertical speed, those are all things that we have to continue to take advantage of as we progress.” Williams’ abilities as a big play threat were on display throughout his college career and also during his rookie season. While primarily serving as a backup X-receiver behind Boutte — a role arguably not best suited for his skillset — he caught 12 passes on 27 targets 223 receiving yards and three touchdowns. His 18.6 yards per reception ranked fifth in the NFL among wide receivers with double-digit catches. However, getting on the same page with his quarterback proved to be a problem for Williams. The same was true for his consistency, both on offense and in the return game, where he average 26.0 yards on 12 runbacks. And yet, the Patriots are steadfast in their belief in the 23-year-old — to a point where they would consider keeping seven wideouts on their opening day roster. “All we have to do is figure out the best way to keep guys that are going to help us win, that have roles on this team and that help us win,” said Vrabel. “It’s a great room. It’s a good competitive room. And by competing and getting out there every single day, those will by nature increase his opportunities.”

full_text: WEST LAFAYETTE, INDIANA - SEPTEMBER 06: Jeremiah McClendon #8 of the Southern Illinois Salukis breaks up a pass intended for Arhmad Branch #6 of the Purdue Boilermakers in the first quarter at Ross-Ade Stadium on September 06, 2025 in West Lafayette, Indiana. (Photo by Justin Casterline/Getty Images) | Getty Images The New England Patriots’ cornerback group suffered some losses early in training camp . Starter Carlton Davis has been out since the first week, while his backup, Charles Woods, suffered an injury during Thursday’s practice. Perhaps as a consequence of those issues, the team has invited a rookie free agent for a workout. Jeremiah McClendon is in town on Friday to try out for the Patriots, as first reported by Aaron Wilson of KPRC 2 Houston. McClendon, 23, bounced around quite a bit even before his college career began. The three-star recruit initially committed and decommitted to both Western Kentucky and Florida Atlantic before joining Marshall before his 2021 freshman campaign. After one season and five games, he joined Charleston Southern for a one-year stint and 10 more contests. He spent the 2023 season as a redshirt at Florida International before one more transfer to Southern Illinois for his final two seasons of college football. In his two years with the Salukis, McClendon started 16 of his 20 games and posted some impressive numbers. Besides registering 84 tackles, he also had 18 pass breakups, three interceptions, a pair of sacks, two forced fumble, one recovery, and a blocked kick. Primarily an outside cornerback in the mold of the aforementioned Davis and Woods, the 5-foot-11, 187-pounder went unselected in this year’s NFL Draft. He joined the New Orleans Saints as a free agent but was released again in late May. The patriots currently have a full roster. They hosted another free agent , veteran offensive lineman Greg Van Roten, on Thursday

title: Patriots injury updates on Will Campbell, Brenden Schooler and others
summary: Coming off four straight days of practices, the New England Patriots are dealing with multiple injuries. Speaking to reporters ahead of Friday’s team scrimmage, head coach Mike Vrabel gave updates on some of them: wide receiver Romeo Doubs, offensive tackle Will Campbell, cornerback Carlton Davis and special teamer Brenden Schooler. Here’s the information that he […]
full_text: FOXBOROUGH, MA - AUGUST 06: Will Campbell #66 of the New England Patriots arrives to New England Patriots training camp on August 6, 2026 at Gillette Stadium in Foxborough, Massachusetts. (Photo by Summer Lamont/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Coming off four straight days of practices, the New England Patriots are dealing with multiple injuries. Speaking to reporters ahead of Friday’s team scrimmage, head coach Mike Vrabel gave updates on some of them: wide receiver Romeo Doubs, offensive tackle Will Campbell, cornerback Carlton Davis and special teamer Brenden Schooler. Here’s the information that he gave. Patriots injury updates: 8/7 WR Romeo Doubs: After missing back-to-back practices, Vrabel said that Doubs will be with the team again on Friday. His absence, he explained, was not injury related: “It was a personal thing, I don’t know if he wants to address it. It’s all very positive. But he’s back and ready to work.” OT Will Campbell: Vrabel said that the Patriots’ starting left tackle, who had been wearing a brace on his left arm the last two practices and was limited on Thursday, was not expected to participate in Friday’s scrimmage. However, he sounded optimistic that Campbell would be “ready to go” after the weekend. CB Carlton Davis III: Davis has been out since the first week of training camp, and it sounds like his absence will extend into next week. Vrabel said that he anticipates the starting cornerback to be out at least until the end of next week, and that he will neither participate in the upcoming joint practice with the Colts on Tuesday nor the opener against them two days later. S Brenden Schooler: Schooler remains on the non-football injury list, and Vrabel refrained from giving concrete updates. What he did say is that the Patriots want to be “very cautious” with the team captain and that there “is no real reason to push that or force that issue.” He remains a “large part” of the Patriots’ plans even though there would be no “reason to rush him back now until he’s as close to 100% as he possibly can be.” The Patriots will hold their 12th practice of the summer on 10:15 a.m. ET on Friday. They will subsequently have two off-days before returning on Monday.

Jones is an LSU product who was born and raised in New Orleans but spent his best years in the NFL with the Atlanta Falcons. He made 100+ tackles in every full season he played and was also named to the Pro Bowl in 2017. During his rookie year, Jones helped the Falcons reach the Super Bowl and recorded nine tackles and a forced fumble in the game. The Falcons would ultimately blow a 28-3 lead in the second half and fall short of their first championship. Jones now returns to his hometown after spending the last two seasons in Tampa Bay, and before that also had stints in Carolina and Cleveland. Since leaving Atlanta he has been more of a rotational piece than every down player, partially due to injury issues. Despite this Jones is a talented player who should be a more than serviceable backup/sub for Kaden Elliss and Pete Werner on the Saints defense. He will also provide a veteran presence at a position where most of the players beside Werner and Elliss are in their first or second season in the league. Jones is now the first player in NFL history to play for every team in the NFC South and could possibly make his debut in Week 1 of the preseason against the Jacksonville Jaguars on August 15th.

title: NY Giants training camp, practice No. 9: Winners, losers, and a fun finish
summary: WHITE SULPHUR SPRINGS, W.Va. — On Monday, New York Giants coach John Harbaugh said this second week in West Virginia was “the big week of camp.” After going through four grueling padded practices in five days, does Harbaugh think the Giants got out of the week what he hoped they would? “I do,” Harbaugh told […]
full_text: Darnell Mooney running a pass route. | Getty Images WHITE SULPHUR SPRINGS, W.Va. — On Monday, New York Giants coach John Harbaugh said this second week in West Virginia was “ the big week of camp .” After going through four grueling padded practices in five days, does Harbaugh think the Giants got out of the week what he hoped they would? “I do,” Harbaugh told Big Blue View. “One more day. I want to finish strong. I told the guys at the beginning of the week that you’re going to look back after Saturday’s practice and you’re going to see how far you’ve come, how much better you are, how much different you are as a team. “I’m hopeful that they’ll feel that way after tomorrow’s practice. I think they will.” The Giants will practice from 10 a.m. ET to 12:30 p.m., then will depart West Virginia to return to East Rutherford, N.J. The team will have Sunday off, but will return to practice at Quest Diagnostics Training Center on Monday. Winners Abdul Carter — The second-year edge defender is going to be a problem if he continues to play like he did on Friday, and like he has throughout most of camp. Carter had a sack and a pressure early in practice against Andrew Thomas. He also helped blow up a run play for a loss of yardage while working against right tackle Jermaine Eluemunor. The run defense — This is a Harbaugh team. The Giants tried, and tried, and tried some more to run the ball on Friday. The defense — first, second, and third units — was having none of that. The offense has had difficulty finding running lanes throughout training camp, a good sign for a defense that has been a sieve against the run in recent seasons. Why is the defense defending the run so well? “I think it’s just because we want to,” said rookie linebacker Arvell Reese. “We’ve all got the ability to do it, it’s just a want to do it. Getting downhill, you’ve got to want to do that.” The passing offense — For as much trouble as the offense had running the ball, the passing attack was humming. I do not chart quarterback stats, and did miss a handful of Jameis Winston reps. The passing attack, though, was in good rhythm all afternoon. Jaxson Dart had two incompletions in his first three throws. After that, I can find only one incompletion by Dart and one by Jameis Winston in my play-by-play chart. Harbaugh was pleased with the poise Dart showed against a defense that brought heavy pressure with a lot of exotic blitzes. “I would say so. He did. I mean, and he made some good throws. He got us in some good plays,” Harbaugh said. “All three quarterbacks got to some plays versus pressure, which was, that’s great. It’s good to see.” Isaiah Likely, Dalen Cambre, Darnell Mooney, and Calvin Austin all had busy days. Cambre had a highlight catch when he caught a hitch route and spun away from cornerback Colton Hood. Austin put his quickness on display during 1-on-1 drills. These favor the receiver, but Austin easily got open against both Hood and Paulson Adebo. Unfortunately, he dropped a short in-cut after beating Adebo. Odell Beckham Jr. — Even when he has a quiet day, he still gets love from the fans. Yes, the fans love Odell Beckham. #NYG pic.twitter.com/3YaxBgCjis — Big Blue View (@bigblueview) August 7, 2026 Both placekickers — If memory serves correctly, Friday was the first time Ben Sauls and Dominic Zvada kicked on the same day. Sauls went 6 of 7 with makes of 50, 51 and 55 yards. His only miss came from 45 yards after a high snap from long-snapper Ben Mann. Zvada went 6 of 7 with makes from 48 and 51 yards, but a miss wide right from 55 yards. Losers Brandon Allen — The third-string quarterback had six incompletions, by my count, and got intercepted by linebacker Zaire Barnes. Ryan Schernecke — The undrafted free agent right tackle committed one of the offense’s two false starts on the day, and got yanked from the lineup for doing so. ‘Let us finish, coach’ The Giants did an interesting full-field drill starting at the offense’s 1-yard line to end the practice. This was a long session that ended up lasting 14 plays, interrupted by a water break. That is the longest stretch the first units have been on the field in camp, and the only time in two weeks I have seen action interrupted for a water break. There was, of course, some rotation of players during the session. The most interesting part came when the offense reached the defense’s 3-yard line on its 13th play, which by the script was supposed to be the final one. The offense, though, wasn’t having it. They insisted on finishing the drive. “We wanted it. We wanted it, because Harbs was trying to save us,” said rookie guard Sisi Mauigoa. “He didn’t want goal-line stuff, but we wanted it. That shows you how tough and what the mentality of the team is. “We were right there by the goal line. We want to finish. Coach [was] calling the twos in. We’re like, ‘What the hell’?” Harbaugh relented. “They lobbied. I wanted it to be done,” Harbaugh said. “That was supposed to be the last play before that, and they wanted the last play, so I cracked and gave them that last play.” The offense took advantage, with Dart finding Darius Slayton for a touchdown on a rub route. “I wasn’t going to do it,” Harbaugh said. “I was going to stand firm because we’re doing some goal line tomorrow and then I did kind of think, wow, they want to do it. Let’s do it.”

full_text: Malik Nabers | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect WHITE SULPHUR SPRINGS, W.Va — Wide receiver Malik Nabers, slowly working back from his torn ACL, did his usual workload on Friday at New York Giants training camp, doing individual drills and routes on air. He simply looked the best he has this summer doing it. Nabers moved fluidly and was willing to plant and cut hard off his surgically repaired leg. “I’ve noticed that, too,” said head coach John Harbaugh. “I feel like Allie (Allison Boudreau, coordinator of rehabilitation and return to play) she’s worked with him. She’s been working on situations where you’re off-balance, landing off-balance, in unpredictable type situations that you’re going to get rather than just doing normal rehab and then going out there and all of a sudden being surprised by the awkwardness of football. Try to create those as much as you can.” Harbaugh said Nabers will be “working his way back into practice more and more as we go here.” Wide receivers, including Malik Nabers, running routes Friday for the #NYGiants — Ed Valentine (@edvalentine.bsky.social) 2026-08-07T22:04:11.678Z Burns limited New York Giants edge defender Brian Burns was limited at practice. He did some 11-on-11 work, but not not a lot. “Burns is just working through his ankle,” Harbaugh said. “Monitored his reps today.” JMS leaves practice early Center John Michael Schmitz left practice early, with Harbaugh saying “he got his bell rung.” We will have to wait to find out if Schmitz is in the concussion protocol. Skattebo working into shape Running back Cam Skattebo had a limited workload as he comes back from his dislocated ankle. “I think it’s natural. title: NY Giants ‘chess piece’ could play key role in secondary
summary: WHITE SULPHUR SPRINGS, W.Va. — Positional versatility can be a blessing for an NFL player. It can keep him in the league because with roster spots at a premium, coaches value players who can handle a variety of roles in a pinch. It can also be a curse. Versatility can keep a player out of […]
full_text: Ar’Darius Washington | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect WHITE SULPHUR SPRINGS, W.Va. — Positional versatility can be a blessing for an NFL player. It can keep him in the league because with roster spots at a premium, coaches value players who can handle a variety of roles in a pinch. It can also be a curse. Versatility can keep a player out of the starting lineup regularly because he never gets to settle in or compete at a single spot. New York Giants safety Ar’Darius Washington has walked that tightrope during his career. A collegiate safety at TCU, Washington’s NFL career got off to a slow start. Washington went undrafted in 2021, but landed with the Baltimore Ravens. He played in three games before going on injured reserve with a foot injury. He spent most of 2022 on the Ravens’ practice squad, appearing in three games. In 2023, he landed on IR with a chest injury after only two games. Baltimore activated him off IR for the playoffs. During that time, Washington was learning multiple roles on defense and special teams. Whether he liked it or not. “Sometime early on in my career, I wasn’t understanding that,” Washington said during a 1-on-1 interview recently. “I felt like, man, I just want to play one position and just learn that one thing. But the more you can do, the more you can get on the field. You know what I mean? So playing nickel, safety, sometimes dime even. So playing all those positions, you know, you can always be versatile. You can always be on the field. “So as I got later in my career, I was like, okay, so they can use me in many different places.” Giants’ defensive backs coach/pass game coordinator Donald D’Alesio was with Washington in Baltimore last season. He smiled when asked about Washington during minicamp, and called him “a chess piece.” “He’s gonna play safety, he’s gonna play nickel, he can play dime if we need him to,” D’Alesio said. “That’s the beautiful thing about Ar’Darius. In a pinch, he can go play any position on the back end that we would need him to. “His mind’s kinda wired that way. He’s been in the system, obviously, for a number of years. So, that’s how we see Ar’Darius. He’s going to play where we need him to play, when we need to.” The Giants have used Washington in multiple roles already this summer, and he has often been on the field with the first-team defense. If he could choose one position, Washington said it would “definitely” be safety. “I like safety a lot,” he said. “I feel like I make a lot of plays and communicate out there, and I can see things from a different angle than some might, and so I feel like I can help everybody when I’m at safety.” With nickel cornerback Dru Phillips currently sidelined with what head coach John Harbaugh termed “a mild knee sprain”, Washington is likely to be the first option to fill that spot. Washington’s best season was 2024, his only fully healthy one in the NFL. He appeared in all 17 games for the Ravens, starting 10. He played 469 snaps at free safety, 177 in the box, and 166 as the slot cornerback. At 5-foot-8, 177 pounds, he even played 13 snaps at linebacker. Last season, Washington tore his Achilles tendon in May, but returned for the final four games of the regular season. Now, Washington is one of a handful of former Ravens who have followed head coach John Harbaugh from Baltimore. “I know what Coach is all about,” Washington said. “Sometimes you go into a new system, and you don’t understand the coaches and everything like that. “But hey, I know what Coach is all about, and he’s all about winning. So he wanted me to come over here and help bring that culture over here and win. So that’s why I was like, you know what? It doesn’t sound like a bad idea. Let’s do it.“

title: CB Greg Newsome II: ‘No days off’ in Giants’ competitive training camp
summary: The start to the New York Giants 2026 training camp has to have been filled with good news for fans who have been concerned over the state of the defense after 2025. Not only has the defensive front kept the offense from establishing much rhythm at all since the second day of camp, the Giants’ […]
full_text: New York Giants cornerback Greg Newsome II during a drill. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co The start to the New York Giants 2026 training camp has to have been filled with good news for fans who have been concerned over the state of the defense after 2025. Not only has the defensive front kept the offense from establishing much rhythm at all since the second day of camp, the Giants’ secondary has consistently had their hands on passes every day. The Giants didn’t exactly renovate their defense entirely this off-season (outside of defensive tackle), but they did make a few key free agent additions. That includes free agent cornerback Greg Newsome II, who the Giants signed to a one-year deal to (at least) compete for the starting job opposite Paulson Adebo. Newsome has been lost in the discussion of the defense, and has, seemingly, been steady opposite Adebo since the start of camp. After all, if a cornerback isn’t being talked about, he can’t be doing his job poorly. Well, at least until quarterback Jaxson Dart chucked the ball at Newsome after scoring in Tuesday’s practice. On the Jaxson Dart incident One of the highlights, or at least headlines, of Tuesday’s practice was Giants’ quarterback Jaxson Dart throwing the ball at Newsome after scoring a touchdown. Head coach John Harbaugh made his displeasure known and personally flagged Dart for taunting, moving the extra point back 15 yards. Newsome’s response, however, was mixed. Emotions were running high in the heat of the afternoon, but he’s also thrilled that he was able to get the quarterback to lose his cool. “I was mad. But like I said, I’m a guy that chirps,” Newsome said. “I like stuff like that.” Ultimately, the two left the beef on the field and were laughing about it by the end of the day. “So, we were about to post a little selfie because I seen it got on ESPN and stuff,” he said. “So, it was fun. It was funny. I like the aggression. I like that with my quarterback. So, it’s all good. “It’s day whatever of camp, emotions get high. So, it was fun.” On the Giants’ defense The Giants’ defense has been a legitimate problem for the offense so far in camp. When the defensive front isn’t blowing plays up around the line of scrimmage, the secondary is getting their hands on the ball. In fact, the Giants’ secondary has proven to be one of the most competitive positions on the field through the off-season and into camp. “It’s super competitive,” Newsome said. “That’s how you want it. Iron sharpens iron. And we say that all the time, it’s super competitive. Everyone’s looking great. So, it’s definitely been fun to be a part of.” Newsome was familiar with John Harbaugh as the coach of the rival Baltimore Ravens from his time with the Cleveland Browns. What is it like to play for him now? “It’s tough, gritty,‘ Newsome some. “We’re going to work, and I like that. There’s no off days for us in terms of not competing. He’s going to make sure we compete. We’re always doing situational football and things like that. So, it’s been super fun.” It was a bit of a surprise when the Giants signed Newsome back at the start of free agency. After all, while his career got off to a great start as a first-round pick by the Browns out of Northwestern, it stagnated in Cleveland and he wasn’t able to jump-start it after being traded to the Jacksonville Jaguars. Still, it was widely assumed that Newsome would be the Giants’ starter opposite Paulson Adebo. After all, it wasn’t that long ago that Newsome was playing at a high level, and Harbaugh must’ve seen something if the Giants offered Newsome $10 million for the chance to make New York his new long-term home. However, 2023 first-round pick Deonte Banks has been making a real fight of things, and has been making a strong push for the starting job. “Tae Banks is amazing,” Newsome said “He’s one of the best just pure athletes, man-to-man, press corners that I’ve seen. So, he’s been doing an amazing job every single day, getting better every single day. So, I’m super excited because he’s going to help us out this season.” Banks has been clawing out increased reps with the starters over the spring and summer, and even earned a “kudos” for his play during Wednesday’s practices. “I just think when you just watch him [Banks] from OTA’s to now, the guys putting hands on, being physical with guys, there’s not a lot of separation with him,” Newsome said. “And just his athletic ability is fast, he’s strong, he can cover. If you just watch practice, he’s been doing a great job whenever he’s asked to get up there and play man-to-man coverage. So, I think, like I said, I’m pretty sure he’s going to do a lot of great things for us this season.” It certainly seems like we’ll be seeing plenty of man coverage from the Giants’ defense this year. Not only is that the technique in which Paulson Adebo excels, as well as Banks, Newsome believes that’s his strength as well. “With my game, my strong suit I think is playing press man coverage,” Newsome said when the Giants signed him back in March. “That was something that we did in Cleveland all the time was playing man-to-man, getting in people’s face and challenging guys.” Aggressive, challenging man coverage seems to be the name of the game under Dennard Wilson. “Just being aggressive,” Newsome said of what the Giants’ defensive coordinator wants. “Getting up and challenging people. I feel like last year, my first six games in Cleveland, that’s what I was asked to do. I feel like I played at a very elite level. People go watch those games when I was in Cleveland. So, this is something that I’m used to, something that I’m comfortable with. And I think all the corners are comfortable with playing like that, too.” Newsome understands 2026 isw an important year for him. “I think every year is pivotal,” he said. “…For me, I just feel like it’s a fresh start with a new team, with new guys, with a new scheme. And I’m just super excited to just embrace New York, show the fans why they signed me here, why I decided to come here” The Giants’ defense has been consistently disruptive, and at many times dominant, since the second day of camp. “I think for us the sky’s the limit. Like I said, everyone has something to prove this season and I think that’s a key ingredient for success,” he said. “We’re close. We’re in the locker room, staying after, just talking with each other, eating lunch together, going to eat together and things like that. “And we’ve been practicing really well but the thing is we’ve got to continue to build. Obviously, we’re not ready right now for game one but I think if we continue to keep going in the path we’re going, we’ll be ready.”

Kenyon Sadiq, Kingsley Enagbare, T’Vondre Sweat, D’Angelo Ponds and Isaiah Davis are all currently out with injuries. Some are listed as day to day and are expected back shortly. full_text: FLORHAM PARK, NEW JERSEY - JULY 29: Will McDonald IV #9 of the New York Jets, Demario Davis #56 of the New York Jets and Jowon Briggs #91 of the New York Jets during training camp at Atlantic Health Jets Training Center on July 29, 2026 in Florham Park, New Jersey. (Photo by Adam Hunger/Getty Images) | Getty Images Good morning Gang Green Nation! The injuries are starting to pile up for the New York Jets. Kenyon Sadiq, Kingsley Enagbare, T’Vondre Sweat, D’Angelo Ponds and Isaiah Davis are all currently out with injuries. Some are listed as day to day and are expected back shortly. Others are more week to week, but all are currently expected back by opening day. While it’s good that none of these injuries appear to threaten to extend into the regular season, it is less than ideal all these guys are missing valuable reps as the Jets try to install the offense and the defense, as well as sort out the depth chart. All but Isaiah Davis are new to the Jets this year. They need the reps to get integrated into their roles with the team. title: Eagles Training Camp Practice Notes: Backup quarterback battle heating up
summary: Today marked the seventh Philadelphia Eagles training camp practice ahead of the 2026 NFL season. Today’s sweltering session lasted just under 90 minutes. Here’s what I observed down at the Jefferson Health Training Complex! EAGLES PRACTICE NOTES *This unintentionally reminded me of “Sanchez doesn’t look bad at all.” IYKYK. UP NEXT: The Eagles practice again […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - JUNE 2: Tanner McKee #16 of the Philadelphia Eagles looks to pass the ball during OTA offseason workouts at Jefferson Health Training Complex on June 2, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Mitchell Leff/Getty Images) | Getty Images Today marked the seventh Philadelphia Eagles training camp practice ahead of the 2026 NFL season. Today’s sweltering session lasted just under 90 minutes. Here’s what I observed down at the Jefferson Health Training Complex! EAGLES PRACTICE NOTES EAGLES INJURY UPDATES: DID NOT PARTICIPATE: WR DeVonta Smith (hamstring) WR Makai Lemon (hamstring) WR Britain Covey (hamstring) S Cole Wisniewski (hamstring) EDGE Keyshawn James-Newby (ankle) LIMITED PARTICIPATION: OT Lane Johnson (“progressing his workload”) Good to see Lane back after he missed the last four practices. LB Chance Campbell (groin) OG Micah Morris (shoulder) IN-PRACTICE INJURY: C Cam Jurgens visited the medical tent and did not return to practice. Obviously one to monitor. JALEN HURTS UPDATE: Hurts went 9/11 today, according to Eliot Shorr-Parks’ charting . It was a relatively lighter workload for him as a passer with the Eagles working on a good share of run plays. First play in 11-on-11: under-center play-action with Hurts rolling right to complete a short pass to a wide open Elijah Moore, who was in motion prior to the snap. Scheming up an easy completion, what a concept. Hurts’ flashiest completion came on a play where he stood in the pocket and ripped the ball over the middle to Darius Cooper in a tight window. Hurts connected with Dallas Goedert on a curl route at the numbers with Riq Woolen nearby. Hurts hit Goedert again short with Jihaad Campbell trailing. Hurts juked Cooper DeJean in the open field after taking off running on a play where he may have been sacked due to instant pressure from Jalen Carter allowed by Jake Majors, who was filling in for Jurgens. Hurts got Moro Ojomo to jump offside on a hard count in the red zone. All told, a nice showing from QB1 as he turned 28 years old today. Hurts’ teammates sang happy birthday to him during the post-practice team huddle. Between this practice and Wednesday’s session, Hurts is starting to stack some good performances. That’s the kind of consistency you like to see. BACKUP QUARTERBACK BATTLE UPDATE: It was Tanner McKee’s turn to go up first with the second-team offense today. In terms of performance, McKee has been behind Andy Dalton thus far (though it’s been close) but today was the former’s best practice of the summer. McKee ripped a ball to Danny Gray along the right sideline for probably his best completion of camp at the time of that throw. McKee had multiple good connections with Darius Cooper, who continues to shine. McKee completed a nice pass to Cooper over the middle. He found Cooper again with timing and anticipation on a pass along the left sideline. McKee capped off his strong showing with a touchdown ball to Johnny Wilson, who made the contested grab, in the back right corner of the end zone. The bad: McKee had a pass batted down near the line of scrimmage by Smael Mondon Jr. McKee overthrew Gray on an out route to the left side of the field. Dalton didn’t have a bad day, either.* The veteran quarterback connected with Wilson on a deep pass that would’ve set the offense up a little short of the goal line. It did feel like the ball hung in the air a long time but was nevertheless completed. Dalton’s lack of zip/arm strength does stand out at times. Dalton hit Erik Ezukanma and Samari Toure on similar routes to the left side later in practice. I’d still put Dalton a little ahead of McKee for now … but the latter made up some ground on Friday morning. Markel Bell, not Fred Johnson, took first-team right tackle reps again today with Lane Johnson being eased back into practice. Unlike the QB2 battle, Bell and Fred Johnson have not been rotating on and off each day. It seems like the rookie Bell might be pulling ahead of the veteran for at least the backup RT job, if not more. OFFENSIVE LINE VS. DEFENSIVE LINE 1-on-1, NON-STARTERS EDITION: Jake Majors got cooked by Byron Young. Michael Jordan anchored well against a bull rush from Gabe Hall. Myles Hinton shut down Zion Wilson. (No. 78 on offense vs. No. 78 on defense.) Ty Robinson was totally stifled multiple times by either Jordan or Micah Morris (hard to distinguish between No. 79 and No. 76 in the Eagles’ jersey number font.) Wee Willie Lampkin gave up no ground to Zion Wilson. Not sure why the Eagles were rolling with Majors, and not Drew Kendall, as the first-team center after Jurgens left practice. On one hand, it’s not surprising since Majors has commonly repped on the second-team offensive line. But he hasn’t looked good and you would think Kendall would be better served by those reps. Jordan Davis notched a “sack” prior to Jurgens leaving practice. Good pressure up the middle. ELI STOWERS ALERT! I noticed the rookie tight end made a good catch along the right sideline. Nothing fancy but good to actually notice him on a reception beyond five yards. Signs of life. Couldn’t make out who it was but I saw an Eagles defender bounce off Dameon Pierce in the middle of the field on what turned out to be a long run. The Eagles had a period where the first-team offense went against backups on defense. Undrafted rookie safety Kapena Gushiken (Gush, as Vic Fangio once referred to him) did a nice job of punching the ball out of E.J. Jenkins’ control for a fumble. He recovered it as well. Ezukanma had a bad drop. Toure failed to catch a deep attempt that wasn’t an easy play to make but did hit him in the hands. Someone was wearing a Jason Babin jersey at practice. Curious. Special guests at today’s practice: new Sixer Jaylen Brown (who dapped up Saquon Barkley at one point and mostly hung out near Big Dom), Torrey Smith, and Vinny Curry. Always a fun one at Eagles training camp. pic.twitter.com/1YWPbN4jqG — Brandon Lee Gowton (@BrandonGowton) August 7, 2026 *This unintentionally reminded me of “Sanchez doesn’t look bad at all.” IYKYK. UP NEXT: The Eagles practice again tomorrow starting at 10:00 AM Eastern. We’ll hear from Sean Mannion prior to practice around 9:40 AM.

title: Eagles News: Saquon Barkley says getting Dontayvion Wicks was “a steal”
summary: Let’s get to the Philadelphia Eagles news and links … Eagles training camp: 17 winners, 8 losers, and 5 IDKs from the first week – BGNDONTAYVION WICKS. Wicks has been Hurts’ top target with both Smith and Lemon missing time due to hamstring injuries. The former Green Bay Packers wideout looks ready to take on […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PA - AUGUST 04: Philadelphia Eagles wide receiver Dontayvion Wicks #13 runs a drill during the Philadelphia Eagles training camp on August 4th, 2026 at Jefferson Health Training Center in Philadelphia, PA. (Photo by Terence Lewis/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Let’s get to the Philadelphia Eagles news and links … "[Dontayvion Wicks] is a steal… I don't know how we got him." Saquon Barkley LOVES what he's seeing from the Eagles new WR 📈 @Eagles | @saquon | @WicksDontayvion | @heykayadams pic.twitter.com/JXUpy5dKHI — Up & Adams (@UpAndAdamsShow) August 6, 2026 Eagles training camp: 17 winners, 8 losers, and 5 IDKs from the first week – BGN DONTAYVION WICKS. Wicks has been Hurts’ top target with both Smith and Lemon missing time due to hamstring injuries. The former Green Bay Packers wideout looks ready to take on the WR2 role in Philly. He’s done a nice job of getting open and he’s made some tough contested catches as well. Wicks has had some struggles with drops in the past (nine in 2024) but that hasn’t been an issue for him so far in camp (knock on wood). Philadelphia Eagles 2026 preview: Philadelphia returns one of the NFL’s most talented rosters – PFF Dontayvion Wicks is expected to take on a key role following the trade of A.J. Brown. He has been a productive receiver through his first three NFL seasons, averaging 1.60 yards per route run. Wicks has also added value as a run blocker, earning PFF run-blocking grades above 65.0 in two of the past three seasons. That ability should help him stay on the field for an Eagles offense that ranked 11th in the NFL with 478 rushing attempts last season. Analyzing NFL executives’ perceptions of Eagles QB Jalen Hurts – PhillyVoice I can’t fathom how a consensus panel such as this so severely ignores postseason success. Like, don’t results matter, just a little bit? Justin Herbert was in the same draft class as Hurts and has been to the playoffs three times. He’s 0-3 with 2 TDs, 4 INTs, a 64.7 QB rating, and in his last two playoff games the Chargers scored a grant total of 15 points. He’s 6th?! And Hurts is 17? If you think Herbert is just a more talented player, then, eh, OK. But how is there that big a gap? But whatever. Eagles wide receiver Darius Cooper takes pride in doing the dirty work. Will he be rewarded with a roster spot? – Inquirer Cooper is proving in camp that he is capable of more, especially in the absence of Smith and Lemon, who have missed practice time this week with hamstring injuries. But Cooper said he still takes pride in that dirty-work role, and he also expressed an understanding that his coaches will require those responsibilities of him if he wants a spot on the team. “Still got to do the dirty work,” Cooper said. “Got to block on the perimeter. Still got to have that mentality on special teams as well. I’m in the same mindset. Nothing is changing for me.” That mindset isn’t changing because the chip on Cooper’s shoulder hasn’t disappeared. He wasn’t highly recruited as a quarterback coming out of Hazelwood West High School just outside of his native St. Louis. He switched to receiver at Tarleton State, a FCS program in Stephenville, Texas, and became the school’s all-time receiving leader with 3,185 yards in five years. Last year, Cooper became the 12th player from Tarleton State to make an NFL active roster, and the first since Colts and Texans outside linebacker E.J. Speed entered the league in 2019. Roob’s Observations: Another idiotic NFL top-10 ranking – NBCSP WELCOME TO THE TANK BIGSBY FAN CLUB: Tank Bigsby does something every day to remind everyone that he’s a legitimate NFL running back. Bigsby, who averaged 5.9 yards per carry in limited duty last year, is the perfect back-up to Saquon Barkley because he has the ability to go into a game cold and make plays off the bench. He’s even caught the ball well this summer, something he hasn’t really ever done. Bigsby had just 62 catches in 35 games at Auburn, and he has only 11 in 50 games in the NFL. He explained this. Week that he’s just never been asked to catch the ball out of the backfield. “During my career at Auburn, we just ran the ball. When and when I got with Doug Pederson in Jacksonville, just ran the ball. They used me as a running back, they didn’t use me on third down as much. So I feel like as opportunities come, we just take advantage of them and build off of them and show what you’re capable of doing.” This stat tells you everything you need to know about Bigsby: He had just 63 carries last year but 13 of them – over 20 percent – went for at least 10 yards. For the sake of comparison, Barkley had 10-yard gains on 28 of 280 carries – exactly 10 percent of his rushing attempts. Obviously nobody believes Bigsby should be RB1, but he’s one heck of a RB2. He’s also going into the final year of the four-year deal he signed with the Jaguars in 2023, and if he has another limited but productive season it will be interesting to see if there’s a team out there willing to pay Bigsby to play a larger role. But for now, the Eagles are lucky to have him, and remember Howie Roseman got him for a 5th-round pick. 2026 NFL training camp: Early takeaways for all 32 teams – NFL.com With Cooper DeJean playing safety, the Eagles could operate out of a base defense more this season, per DC Vic Fangio, as they respond to the bigger packages offenses are deploying. NFL defensive coaches explain why the 2-high safety trend is here to stay – The Athletic Philadelphia Eagles defensive coordinator Vic Fangio, who is responsible for starting this trend, called a lot of man coverage from two-high last season. An advantage to this is that you don’t give a quarterback a presnap indicator to go to his deep route. Back then, without disguise, a quarterback would be licking his chops as soon as he saw press coverage on the outside with one deep safety in the middle of the field. In this image, the Eagles showed two-high, but safety Reed Blankenship rotated down to cover the tight end in man-to-man coverage. HBCU football returns to Lincoln Financial Field with expanded slate of marquee matchups – PhiladelphiaEagles.com One Philly HBCU Week 2026 will kick off with Virginia Union and Lincoln on Friday, October 30. A rematch between DeSean Jackson’s Delaware State Hornets and Michael Vick’s Norfolk State Spartans will follow on Saturday, October 31. Panthers release OL Saahdiq Charles, WR Ainias Smith from IR – PFT The Panthers waived wide receiver Ainias Smith with an injury settlement and released guard Saahdiq Charles with an injury settlement, the team announced Thursday. […] Smith went on injured reserve Wednesday with an undisclosed injury. The Eagles selected him in the fifth round of the 2024 draft. Smith appeared in seven games, starting one, and totaled seven receptions for 41 yards and one touchdown. He spent all of 2025 on the Panthers’ practice squad. Brandon Johnson: Let go by Seattle – CBS Sports Johnson had just signed with Seattle late last month after spending last season with the Eagles. The 23-year-old could revert to the Seahawks’ injured reserve if he clears waivers. Brian Schottenheimer: Left tackle is still not decided – Blogging The Boys The competition at left tackle is officially over for apparently still going on for the Dallas Cowboys. Brian Schottenheimer said on Wednesday during an appearance on San Antonio’s Sports Star that Tyler Guyton has still not officially won the job. Earlier in the week there were reports that Schotty declared Guyton the winner already, but Schotty told San Antonio that what his point truly meant to be was that Nate Thomas had to play better for it to be a real competition. Schotty reiterated that on Thursday in his press conference before practice. Washington Commanders Week 2 training camp observations, standouts – Hogs Haven Who has struggled? full_text: DETROIT, MI - DECEMBER 04: Donovan Wilson #6 of the Dallas Cowboys defends in coverage during an NFL football game against the Detroit Lions at Ford Field on December 4, 2025 in Detroit, Michigan. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Steelers worked out six players over Thursday and Friday , PennLive’s Nick Farabaugh reported. Only one of those players, safety Israel Mukuamu , has been signed by the team so far. The other names to come to Pittsburgh were edges Xavier Thomas and Andre Carter II, safety Donovan Wilson, and wide receivers Cornell Powell and Isaiah Winstead. Thomas, Wilson and Powell are the most recognizable names. Thomas was a fifth-round pick in 2024 by the Arizona Cardinals out of Clemson. He scored a 6.79 RAS pre-draft as a sixth-year senior with 17.5 career college sacks, but never more than 3.5 in a season. He hasn’t recorded a tackle in an NFL regular season game since his 2.5-sack rookie campaign with Arizona. Wilson, like Mukuamu, is a former Cowboys safety, being drafted in the sixth round of 2019 by Dallas. He spent most of his NFL career being coached by Mike McCarthy. The 6’0, 204-pound defender is primarily a strong safety, with his best year coming in 2022: 101 tackles, five sacks, one interception and two passes defensed. The now-31-year-old started 15 games for the Cowboys in 2025. Powell is another Clemson product. He recorded 882 receiving yards and seven touchdowns in his final collegiate season before going in the fifth round of the 2021 NFL Draft to the Kansas City Chiefs. He scored a 7.59 RAS pre-draft, running a 4.53-second 40-yard dash. Powell has appeared in just three NFL games, mostly on special teams, with no career catches. He had a brief stint on the Steelers’ practice squad in 2025. The Steelers will finish Week 2 of training camp under the lights in an evening practice Aug. 8.

title: Steelers’ DK Metcalf, Michael Pittman Jr ranked outside top 35 receivers
summary: With the NFL season rapidly approaching, the top player lists are coming in at a fast and furious pace. The Pittsburgh Steelers are in an interesting position this season. Mike McCarthy has taken over for Mike Tomlin, reunited with Aaron Rodgers, who is in his final season, and the team added offensive pieces like Rico […]
full_text: May 28, 2026; Pittsburgh, PA, USA; Pittsburgh Steelers wide receiver Michael Pittman Jr. (11) and DK Metcalf (4) participate in OTA drills at the UPMC Rooney Sports Complex. Mandatory Credit: Charles LeClaire-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect With the NFL season rapidly approaching, the top player lists are coming in at a fast and furious pace. The Pittsburgh Steelers are in an interesting position this season. Mike McCarthy has taken over for Mike Tomlin, reunited with Aaron Rodgers, who is in his final season, and the team added offensive pieces like Rico Dowdle and Michael Pittman, Jr. The Steelers desperately needed to upgrade the receiver room and the duo of D.K. Metcalf and Pittman, Jr. is as formidable as it gets. Rodgers will have plenty of options in the passing game. Bleacher Report has released its top wide receiver list and Damian Parson is responsible for ranking the offensive skill position players (QB/WR/RB/FB). The methodology is simple and film based. “Receivers are graded on six categories: hands (25 points), route running, football IQ (20 apiece), athleticism (15), YAC and blocking (10 apiece). Trait scores add up to the grade, and when multiple players received the same score, their ranking was determined by a majority vote among the group.” The tiers are broken up as backup & developmental, replacement level, functional performer, reliable contributor, critical roster piece, high-quality starter, Pro Bowl caliber, All-Pro ability, and franchise cornerstone. Only Ja’Marr Chase is listed as a franchise cornerstone with JSN and Justin Jefferson in the All-Pro tier, but only one point behind Chase. So, where do Pittman, Jr. and Metcalf rank? Both receivers fall into the reliable contributor tier at number 46 (Pittman, Jr.) and 38 (Metcalf). 46 . Michael Pittman, Jr, Age: 28, Overall Grade: 73 “Michael Pittman is a dependable, high-volume possession wide receiver. He is an instinctive player who diagnoses coverages quickly post-snap. Pittman excels working in the middle of the field on in-breakers, where his big frame is an advantage. He welcomes being the glue guy and working in higher-traffic areas and on quick-passing/underneath concepts. Pittman is a willing and effective run blocker at the point of attack, but also looks to block defenders on long breakaway runs. He’s a consistent player with a safe floor and expectations.” The highest grades received for the former Colts receiver are route running (15/20) and hands (19/25). Parson believes YAC isn’t a big part of Pittman’s game and he’s not wrong grading the receiver at 4/10. 38. D.K. Metcalf, Age: 28, Overall Grade: 74 “DK Metcalf is a part of an NFL passing offense that averages under 200 yards per game. He is one of the most physically imposing receivers in the league. He is an established big-body pass catcher with explosiveness. Metcalf’s productivity has tapered off over the last two seasons. Regardless, he poses a dangerous threat to defenses. His speed, acceleration, and strength put defenders in conflict after the catch. He can either run past defenders or run through them for extra yards. Metcalf is still capable of taking over games with above-average quarterback play. He remains a good and quality starting receiver and playmaker.” Parson dinged the receiver duo for the overall offense, but that does have a chance to change with McCarthy as the head coach. Metcalf’s grades are solid to great in nearly each category, but route running (14/20), hands (18/25), football IQ (15/20), and athleticism (13/15) are his best attributes. It was another warm day at team headquarters in Renton, albeit less smoky and hazy than earlier in the week. Much like Wednesday’s practice, the Seahawks were not in pads, and indeed they mixed things up with the 11 vs. 11 sessions. There was first-team offense vs. second-team defense, third-team offense vs. first-team defense, the usual 1s vs. 1s and 2s vs. 2s, plus a lot of situational football like red zone and 3rd-and-long work that often decides actual games. For the second time this week, Field Gulls was on-site at VMAC observing what was just about a three-hour long practice. Myself and fellow Field Gulls staff writer and host of The Hawks Eye podcast , Bryce Coutts, as well as Seahawks Forever podcast host , Dan Viens, filmed an instant reaction video after practice ended with our quick-fire takeaways. full_text: KANSAS CITY, MO - AUGUST 22: Chicago Bears linebacker Power Echols (57) collides with Kansas City Chiefs defensive end Charles Omenihu (90) on August 22nd, 2025 at Arrowhead Stadium in Kansas City, Missouri (Photo by William Purnell/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The training camp roster churn continued on Friday, with the Seattle Seahawks making a change at linebacker. The team announced the signing of 23-year-old linebacker Power Echols, while in a corresponding move, fellow LB Joseph Vaughn was waived to make room on the 90-man roster. Echols, a stalwart on the North Carolina Tar Heels’ defense from 2021 through 2024, went undrafted in the 2025 NFL Draft. He was signed by the Chicago Bears as a UDFA, and spent training camp with the team before he was waived ahead of the regular season. He then joined the Houston Texans’ practice squad toward the end of the regular season, but didn’t receive a futures contract after Houston was eliminated from the postseason. Across 52 games at UNC, Echols totaled 307 tackles, as well as 13 tackles for loss, 2.5 sacks, four interceptions, and a trio of forced fumbles. Despite a strong college career, Echols’ size has worked against him, with his height in the fifth percentile and weight in the 44th percentile among NFL linebackers who have tested at the scouting combine. Vaughn, like Echols, was an undrafted free agent after the 2025 NFL Draft. He was signed to Seattle’s roster on Saturday, but is now back on the market after a short-lived stint with the Super Bowl champions. Seahawks practice starts at 9:45 am PT, so Echols could be out there today.
