title: Tracking 2026 NFL hold-ins: Vea and Tuipulotu
summary: Here is the latest on the Bucs' Vita Vea and the Chargers' Tuli Tuipulotu and where they stand with their deals.
full_text:
The 2026 NFL preseason kicked off with the Pro Football Hall of Game on Thursday , with three weeks of action to follow, but there are two players who are waiting for their contract situations to sort out.

 The start of NFL training camps brought these negotiations to a head. Players can hold out and stay away from camp until their financial situations are addressed, or they can hold in, where they report to camp to avoid fines but skip practice while waiting for a new contract. We're tracking the important hold-ins across the league, with updates from our NFL Nation writers on each situation.

 The list of stars not practicing has gone down to two after Atlanta Falcons running back Bijan Robinson signed a  new historic deal Tuesday, with  Detroit Lions running back Jahmyr Gibbs  surpassing him with a  new contract Thursday.  

 Now,  Tampa Bay Buccaneers defensive tackle Vita Vea  and  Los Angeles Chargers outside linebacker  Tuli Tuipulotu  are the last ones standing. 

 Which player will be next in resolving his contract dispute? Are any of these four willing to miss games once the season begins? Let's examine each situation.

 

 
 Jump to: 
 Gibbs | Robinson | Vea | Tuipulotu 

 
 

 

 Vita Vea , DT, Tampa Bay Buccaneers 
 Status: Holding in, requesting a trade 

 Aug. 7:  Vea still is not practicing because of a back injury and his contract dispute. He also wasn't on the practice field either. However, as of right now, Bowles expects him to travel with the team Monday to joint practices at the New York Jets .

 "Right now, yes, everybody's going," Bowles said.

 Aug. 6: The Buccaneers have "no plans" to trade Vea, according to general manager Jason Licht when asked Thursday about Vea's hold-in. Collin Roberts, Vea's agent, told the Tampa Bay Times this week that he "doesn't see it ending in anything but a trade."

 "We love Vita," Licht added. "We've been engaged with his agent recently. I don't know how it's gonna end, but we've been engaged and that's at least some progress." Vea has been present at the Bucs' facility, taking part in classroom instruction and observing practice from the sideline. He has also been seen helping coach teammates up during positional drills, but he isn't physically participating.

 Aug. 2 update: The star defensive tackle remains sidelined with a back injury, as well as his contract hold-in. Coach Todd Bowles said there is "nothing new" to report on his injury, and he is unsure if Vea will make the trip to the  New York Jets  for a pair of joint practices starting Aug. 11.

 July 31 update: Vea, who stayed indoors to receive treatment Thursday, was back out on the practice field Friday with teammates but was still sidelined with a back injury sustained during the team's conditioning test. Bowles said he does not have a timetable yet for Vea's back.

 July 30 update: While Vea was on the sidelines during Wednesday's first training camp practice and was standing alongside teammates during positional drills, he was not on the practice field Thursday. Bowles said Vea tweaked his back in the team's conditioning test Tuesday and he was getting treatment. Vea did, however, participate in an interview on the "Up & Adams Show," but he did not discuss his contract. Vea is set to earn $17 million this season, but none of it is guaranteed, along with a per-game roster bonus that is capped at $1 million total. Bowles said they are preparing for the season as if Vea will play. 

 -- Jenna Laine, Bucs reporter 

 

 
 

 Tuli Tuipulotu , OLB, Los Angeles Chargers 
 

 Status: Practicing, but still seeking a new contract

 Aug. 6 update:  Tuipulotu participated in team drills during Wednesday's padded practice, his second day in a row after not participating in team drills for the first six days of training camp.

 Tuipulotu looked like himself, bursting by the line of scrimmage to shut down running back Omarion Hampton on one of his first snaps and generating pressure throughout practice.

 Coach Jim Harbaugh originally said that Tuipulotu's absence was being "handled internally," then later said it was a "ramp up." Neither Tuipulotu, his representatives or the Chargers have acknowledged a contract-related absence, but his return to the field signals that whatever matter was being handled internally is resolved.

 Aug. 5 update:  Tuipulotu, who has been a limited participant in practice this training camp amid ongoing contract negotiations, was a full participant in Wednesday's practice. The caveat is that the practice was a walkthrough, so Tuipulotu and the other Chargers players were going at half speed. He still has yet to participate in a non-walkthrough practice 11-on-11 period, but his participation could be a sign that things could be headed toward a resolution.

 Aug. 4 update:  Coach Jim Harbaugh said Tuesday that Tuipulotu's absence from team drills remains part of "his ramp up." Harbaugh stopped short, however, of explaining any further, saying, "I don't know for sure where it's at. If I knew for sure, then I would say for sure."

 After noticing a reporter's facial expression, Harbaugh went on to explain he doesn't know exactly what's happening with Tuipulotu because he is not a medical professional.

 "Am I in somebody's body? A doctor? he said. "A lot of things that hang on my wall, but a medical degree is not one of them."

 Tuipulotu participated in one 7-on-7 rep but did not take part in the remainder of team drills on Tuesday, marking his sixth straight practice with limited participation as his contract situation remains unresolved.

 Aug. 3 update: Tuipulotu again did not participate in team drills, continuing his limited participation as his contract situation remains unresolved. The Chargers, Tuipulotu, and his representation remain mum about Tuipulotu's absence from practice, though it appears to be contract-related. Tuipulotu remains in good spirits and engaged throughout practice. His routine has been the same each day: he participates in individual drills, jokes with teammates, works with a trainer briefly, then watches practice with the team.

 Aug. 1 update:  Coach Jim Harbaugh declined to say whether outside linebacker Tuli Tuipulotu's absence from team drills at practice is contract-related, saying only the situation is being "handled internally" and repeatedly describing Tuipulotu as "ramping up."

 July 31 update:  Tuipulotu continued not to practice amid ongoing contract negotiations Friday. He went through individual drills, worked off to the side with a trainer and watched practice.

 July 30 update: The Chargers outside linebacker did not practice Thursday for the second straight day amid ongoing contract negotiations, but he did more on-field work with teammates than on the opening day of camp. Tuipulotu wore a helmet and jersey Thursday and went through individual drills with the team before working off to the side with a trainer. On Wednesday, he was in a T-shirt and shorts and worked off to the side with a trainer.

 -- Kris Rhim, Chargers reporter 

 

 
 

 Bijan Robinson , RB, Atlanta Falcons 
 

 Status: Signed a new deal 

 Aug. 4 update:  The two-time Pro Bowler and the Falcons reached agreement on a three-year extension worth up to $75 million that now will make him the highest-paid running back in NFL history, sources told ESPN's Adam Schefter and NFL Network's Ian Rapoport.

 Aug. 1 update:  Robinson was again at practice, though not practicing, for the fourth straight day. Robinson left the field at one point during the media video shooting period and then came back when the cameras were off. Otherwise, he was with his teammates on the sidelines like he has been since camp started on Wednesday.

 July 31 update : Falcons coach Kevin Stefanski addressed Robinson's hold-in for the first time Friday morning. He said he was confident the contract situation will be resolved amiably.

 

 On how he is approaching the conflict, Stefanski said: "Just coach the football team."

title: 2026 Atlanta Falcons training camp: Latest intel, updates
summary: Follow our daily updates from Falcons training camp, including intel on QBs, position battles and potential breakouts.
full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. The Atlanta Falcons ' camp is taking place in Flowery Branch, Georgia, and Falcons reporter Marc Raimondi has the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and of course the quarterback room.

 What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at Falcons camp. We will update this file often. How will the QB battle play out between  Michael Penix Jr . and  Tua Tagovailoa for QB1? Who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football? And which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Dive in to all the updates and be sure to check back for more information until the first full week of the preseason begins Aug. 13.

 
 Camp updates for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 

 Latest Falcons stories 
 
 Sources: Falcons, RB Robinson reach 3-year deal worth up to $75M 
 Falcons sign Matthew Bergeron to four-year, $96M extension 
 Falcons' Jalon Walker tore ACL, out for season 
 Wife of DC Ulbrich dies of cancer 
 
 
 

 Friday, Aug. 7 
 Quarterback Tua Tagovailoa hit running back Bijan Robinson on a wheel route that would have gone for a 90-yard touchdown or so during an 11-on-11 session Friday. The series was situational. The Falcons offense was backed up against the opposite goal line and Tagovailoa floated it nicely to Robinson, who had complete daylight.

 It was just another play in another practice this summer here in Flowery Branch, Georgia. But it also felt like more than that, something symbolic. Like a sigh of relief.

 For the first time this training camp, Tagovailoa and Robinson were both full participants in practice. Tagovailoa has been dealing with a tight back and Robinson was a hold-in before signing a three-year contract extension Wednesday that is worth up to $75 million. Robinson got his first carries in 11s Friday.

 
 Quarterback Michael Penix Jr . is still not cleared for 11s, but has looked sharper lately in 7-on-7 work. On Friday, he was 6-of-9 in the red zone, helped out by a diving catch from wide receiver Keelan Marion . 
 Matt Ryan, the team's president of football and former franchise quarterback, threw to wide receivers Drake London and Jahan Dotson separated from everyone else during a drill Friday. 
 

 

 Wednesday, Aug. 5 

 Michael Penix Jr . explained his current situation in the clearest way possible Wednesday.

 "If I can't be on the field," Penix said, "how am I going to be the starter?"

 Penix has been on the field. He has done individual drills and 7-on-7 sessions. But what the Falcons third-year quarterback means is that he has yet to be cleared for 11-on-11 work. And until he does, there cannot be any kind of quarterback competition.

 That is not necessarily news. The Falcons coaching staff made that clear in the spring. But back then there was some expectation Penix would be fully ready for training camp. That has not been the case and Penix said it could be another several weeks before he's good to go.

 Tua Tagovailoa (tight back) took another step toward a full return Wednesday with more work in 11s. He went 5-of-7 passing. At this juncture, it's fair to say Tagovailoa will be the team's Week 1 starter unless something major changes.

 More observations: 

 
 Edge rusher Jalon Walker was officially confirmed as out for the season with a torn ACL after getting injured Tuesday at practice. It's a major blow for a pass rush that was depending him on to make a major impact. He had 5.5 sacks as a rookie last season. 
 Running back Bijan Robinson officially put pen to paper on his three-year extension, which is worth up to $75 million. He is still limited in practice and has not done any 11s as the team ramps him up. 
 

 

 Tuesday, Aug. 4 
 Falcons running back Bijan Robinson returned to practice after a five-day hold-in Tuesday. Robinson got a three-year extension worth up to $75 million and is now the highest-paid running back in the NFL.

 Head coach Kevin Stefanski referred to Robinson's hold-in as "very amicable." Robinson had been at every practice on the hip of running backs coach Michael Pitre prior to actually coming back.

 "He wants to be out there practicing," Falcons running back Brian Robinson Jr . said. "You know he wants to be competing. So, I used to just tell him, 'Yo, take your time, handle your business. Whenever your time comes, it's going to come. I know you want to be out there with us, but we going to hold it down until you come back.'"

 Bijan Robinson didn't do much Tuesday. He worked a bit with the running backs in individual drills and did a play-action drill after practice with quarterback Michael Penix Jr . Pitre said they will work to ramp Bijan up over the next few days based on recommendations by the training and medical staff.

 More observations: 

 
 Quarterback Tua Tagovailoa (tight back) said he continues to make progress and expected to be practicing fully Wednesday. Tagovailoa has eased into 11-on-11 sessions the last two days, but has only thrown seven passes. He was 3-of-4 in 11s on Tuesday. 
 Quarterback Cooper Rush , who signed with the Falcons last Wednesday, got reps with the first-team offense in a two-minute drill near the end of practice. Penix has still not yet been cleared for 11s, but got reps again in 7-on-7 work Tuesday. 
 

 

 Monday, Aug. 3 
 Falcons quarterback Tua Tagovailoa participated in 11-on-11 team sessions Monday for the first time this training camp. Tagovailoa has been dealing with a tight back and was still limited. He did two series, going 3-for-3 passing in 11s with individual drills, as well.

 Michael Penix Jr . (right knee) had his best 7-on-7 session Monday, going 6-of-8 with two drops, working mostly with younger players and reserves. His best throw of camp came on the final play of practice. Penix found  Antwane Wells Jr . for a long touchdown pass down the left side.

 Penix has still not been cleared for 11s. The majority of those reps still went to Jack Strand , followed by veteran Cooper Rush . Strand was 7-of-11 passing in those sessions, while Rush was 3-of-7.

 More observations: 

 
 Defensive coordinator Jeff Ulbrich returned to practice Monday. Ulbrich's wife Cristina died last week after a battle with cancer. "He's a father figure, older brother for me," Falcons linebacker Divine Deablo said. "So, I was glad to have him back out here. I hugged him as soon as I seen him. Everybody just wants to play for 'Brich' at the end of the day." 
 This was the first camp practice with pads. 
 Offensive tackle Wanya Morris and defensive tackle  Da'Shawn Hand  both left practice with apparent injuries. 
 Michael Jerrell , Brandon Walton and rookie seventh-round pick Ethan Onianwa  rotated at right tackle. Free agent signee Jawaan Taylor is not yet cleared to practice after elbow surgery last season. 
 

 

 Saturday, Aug. 1 
 Cooper Rush has only been with the Falcons for a little more than 72 hours, but he is starting to get himself acclimated fairly well.

 The veteran quarterback got reps with the first-team offense for the first time Saturday morning in 11-on-11 team sessions. Overall, Rush was 6-of-10 with a red zone touchdown to tight end  Kyle Pitts Sr .

 The Falcons signed Rush on Wednesday , just before their first practice of training camp. Quarterback Tua Tagovailoa is dealing with a tight back and has yet to do anything but individual work and a walk-through. Michael Penix Jr . is not yet cleared for 11s after right ACL surgery last November.

 Undrafted rookie Jack Strand has gotten the majority of 11-on-11 reps with the first team and still did Saturday. But Rush is clearly starting to ramp up.

 More observations:  

 
 Tagovailoa only did individual work, while Penix did individuals and then a 7-on-7 goal-line session. Penix was 4-of-8 passing, including a touchdown pass to rookie running back Cash Jones .

title: Ranking 10 most interesting recent NFL contract extensions
summary: Jahmyr Gibbs' new deal is the latest in a flurry of extensions shaping the 2026 preseason, and Seth Walder stacked the 10 most notable.
full_text:
Contract extensions sometimes fall under the radar. It's not that they don't make news. It's that they tend to be treated as a checkbox. Is the extension done, yes or no?

 But there's a lot of middle ground. Should the extension have happened? And at what price? Because not every extension is a good decision.

 So with NFL teams seemingly inking players to new long-term deals almost every day in training camp (most recently Detroit Lions running back Jahmyr Gibbs agreeing to a three-year, $67.5 million extension  Thursday with $51.5 million guaranteed), let's go through some of the most interesting deals and rank them from best to worst.

 As always, I'm evaluating the decisions teams make, considering the player in question, the price and the rest of the team's roster, cap situation and time horizon to contention.

 

 
 Jump to an extension: 
 Bergeron | Carter | Flowers | Gibbs 
 Olave | O'Neill | Robinson 
 Taylor | Ward | Wright 

 
 

 

 1. Brian O'Neill , OT, Minnesota Vikings 
 Extension: Four years, $96 million 
 O'Neill has always performed very well and been consistent in pass block win rate. In fact, he finished in the 95th percentile or better for three straight seasons from 2022 to 2024 before dropping back to the 79th percentile in 2025. Conversely, his run block win rates weren't as strong until last season, when he popped into the 87th percentile among tackles.

 At age 30 with only one year left on his contract, extending O'Neill made a ton of sense. That's true for two reasons: (A) offensive tackles can continue to play at a high level well into their 30s, and (B) right now contract costs for good tackles are relatively cheap. Losing O'Neill would really hurt the offense, replacing him would be difficult, and his extension costs only $24 million per year.

 

 The structure of the deal is also favorable. It's a pretty salary-heavy contract with a smaller, fully guaranteed $11.2 million salary in 2027 and then no fully guaranteed salary after that, per OverTheCap.com . In other words, the Vikings bought themselves years of team control with limited downside. That's well worth it.

 
 

 

 2. Darnell Wright , OT, Chicago Bears 
 Extension: Four years, $116 million 
 It was a good sign when Wright posted above average win rates as a rookie in 2023, as most rookie tackles -- even first-rounders -- struggle in Year 1. He capitalized on that promise in pass protection last season, with a 96th percentile pass block win rate to become a key part of Ben Johnson's offense in Chicago. His run block win rate wasn't as good, but Wright got a huge vote of confidence from coaches and executives surveyed by ESPN's Jeremy Fowler this offseason, who ranked the 24-year-old as the sixth-best tackle in the league.

 Signing Wright to an extension makes all the sense in the world, as he should be on the Bears' offensive line for a long time. The Bears did have to pay up; at $29 million per year, Wright ranks second only behind Laremy Tunsil at tackle, per OverTheCap.com . But when adjusting for cap inflation, Trent Williams ' 2021 deal would have cost almost $38 million per year in 2026's cap environment, and Andrew Thomas ' 2023 deal (also entering its fourth year) would have cost $31 million per year today. Wright's deal is still high-end, though.

 

 But given his age, production and the tackle market lagging behind the value of the position, this was a good move by Chicago.

 
 

 3. Bijan Robinson , RB, Atlanta Falcons 
 Extension: Three years, $66.75 million , per OverTheCap.com 
 Ninety percent of resource-intensive transactions involving running backs are going to earn critiques from me, but I'm making an exception here (and with Gibbs below). Robinson is a true difference-maker and the best player at the position. He is coming off a season in which he led all running backs in YAC over expected (and was more than double every player outside of Christian McCaffrey ) while also ranking third in rush yards over expected, per NFL Next Gen Stats. He was second in ESPN's receiver score among running backs last season, behind only McCaffrey.

 And Robinson is only 24 years old. Running backs age quickly, but Robinson is young enough to be able to contribute to the team's next contending window, which is what truly matters. Atlanta has plenty of cap space going forward, so this is a logical way to use some of it.

 

 

 
 

 4. Chris Olave , WR, New Orleans Saints 
 Extension: Four years, $124 million , per OverTheCap.com 

 Extending a player with injury concerns who is coming off a breakout season is generally a red flag. But Olave's contract is an example of how it can be done without putting the organization at too much risk.

 First and foremost, Olave is a heck of a player. He's coming off a 100-reception, 1,163-receiving-yard season (2.1 yards per route run). It was his third 1,000-yard season since being drafted in 2022, and perhaps more impressively, Olave has always shown an ability to get open.

 His open scores (from ESPN's player-tracking based receiver scores ) in each of his four NFL seasons have been 82, 75, 80 and 81, respectively, on a 0-99 scale. That's the type of player a team should want to invest in. And at $31 million per year, the price is totally reasonable. If we adjust for salary cap inflation, Olave's deal puts him on par with  Tee Higgins '  contract from a year ago -- and I'd rather have Olave than Higgins.

 

 The concern with Olave is his concussion history, which he said had him thinking about retirement in 2024 . But the structure of the deal gives the Saints a safety valve. After his $35 million signing bonus, only his 2026 and 2027 salary and roster bonuses are fully guaranteed.

 
 

 5. Jahmyr Gibbs , RB, Detroit Lions 
 Extension: Three years, $67.5 million 
 Paying a top-of-the-market price for Gibbs works for the same three reasons it does for Robinson:

 
 He's a legitimately elite running back. 
 He's particularly dangerous as a receiver, which is what matters most. 
 He's only 24 years old. 
 
 Gibbs' numbers last season weren't quite as good as Robinson's (168 rush yards over expected to Robinson's 249, and 126 receiving yards over expected to Robinson's 201, per NFL Next Gen Stats), but I think these are the best two running backs in the NFL.

 

 While this is top-of-the-market money for a running back today, it's less than what running backs were paid in the past. For example, in 2015, Adrian Peterson and Marshawn Lynch signed deals that were worth the equivalent of $29.4 million and $25.2 million per year, respectively, in 2026's cap environment. Gibbs ranks fifth on this list, but the gap between No. 3 -- where Robinson landed -- and No. 5 in these rankings is small.

 
 

 

 6. Zay Flowers , WR, Baltimore Ravens 
 Extension: Four years, $140 million 
 At $35 million per year, the Ravens invested heavily in the deal for Flowers, but I don't think the price is totally unreasonable.

 Flowers has been excellent through three seasons, averaging 2.4 yards per route run, including 2.8 last year. He consistently gets open, recording at least a 76 open score each season. And that ability to separate and give Lamar Jackson open targets is what the Ravens should be paying for.

 

 Flowers' APY puts him just behind Drake London 's extension signed earlier this offseason and on par with Garrett Wilson 's deal from a year ago if we adjust for salary cap inflation. The one part that surprises me is that the Ravens still had Flowers under contract for two more seasons (as opposed to one each for London and Olave). That should have given Flowers less leverage, which is why I expected him to earn a million or two less per season. Still, at 25 he's a core part of the offense that the Ravens should want secured for years to come.

 
 

 7. Jonathan Taylor , RB, Indianapolis Colts 
 Extension: Two years, $44 million 
 Days after Robinson signed his extension, Taylor got one of his own, moving him back near the…

title: 2026 Buffalo Bills training camp: Latest intel, updates
summary: Follow our daily updates from Bills training camp, including intel on QBs, position battles and potential breakouts.
full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. The Buffalo Bills' camp is taking place at St. John Fisher University in Pittsford, New York, and Bills reporter Alaina Getzenberg has the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and, of course, the quarterbacks room.

 What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at Bills camp. We will update this file often. How will the transition to Jim Leonhard's defense go? Who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football? And which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Dive in to all the updates and be sure to check back for more information until the first full week of the preseason begins Aug. 13.

 
 Camp updates for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 

 Latest news from Bills camp 
 
 Bills safety C.J. Gardner-Johnson carted off with leg injury 
 Josh Allen on Bills' alternate uniforms: 'Stop hating on the jerseys' 
 Bills unveil new 'Nickel City' alternate uniforms 
 2026 Buffalo Bills training camp preview 
 
 
 Friday, Aug. 7 
 The Bills wrapped up training camp at St. John Fisher University with a shorter practice in pads.

 Quarterback Josh Allen said one of his takeaways from the time away from Buffalo is how close the team has gotten.

 "This group from offense to defense is the tightest knit group that I've been around really since I've entered the league," Allen said. "The defense is meshing so well together. Just even when you walk in the dorm room or walk in the cafeteria, guys sitting down, talking, really getting to know each other. 
 
"There's just a lot of love on this team and that'll show on the field."

 Allen pointed to the veteran leadership new OLB Bradley Chubb brings as well as the growth of two-time captain ILB Terrel Bernard  in helping the team get to where it is.

 The Bills now head back to Orchard Park, New York, and camp practice starts with the first football work in the new Highmark Stadium on Saturday night.

 Other observations: 

 
 Two defenders took trips to the medical tent during practice. Rookie defensive tackle Zane Durant went in briefly but returned to the sideline with his helmet. Projected starting nickel Dee Alford was slow to get up after defending a pass by Allen to wide receiver Joshua Palmer . He returned to the sideline without his helmet, and second-year DB Jordan Hancock filled in during the absence, but practice ended quickly afterward. 
 LT Dion Dawkins had a veteran rest day. Backups Tylan Grable and then Jude Bowry spent time with the first-team offense. Bowry dealt with penalty issues from the officials present at the session. 
 No practice for CB Maxwell Hairston , WR Mac Dalena or DB D.J. Miller . Coach Joe Brady said the Bills were being precautionary with Hairston after an injury Thursday. Rookie CB Davison Igbinosun worked with the first-team defense in Hairston's place. 
 Former Bills pass rusher Von Miller has posted photos recently alluding to a desire to re-sign with Buffalo. Bills GM and president of football operations Brandon Beane said, "I talk to Von all the time. We're buds. But yeah, I mean, listen, I love Von. You could name 10 other ex-Bills that if everything lined up right, you wouldn't say no to a guy like that. But beyond that, there's nothing imminent or nothing going." 
 
 
 Thursday, Aug. 6 
 A significant first came from kicker Tyler Bass at practice. Returning after missing the entire 2025 season with a sports hernia, Bass practiced kickoffs and field goals on the main training camp field for the first time this camp. He went 5-of-7, with both misses coming from 45-plus yards. Bass had kicked once in a practice open to the media in the spring.

 Special teams coordinator Jeff Rodgers said earlier in the week that Bass had been kicking outside of open practices and that it was not planned for him to kick in practice until this point.

 "Just the whole organization, I think, Joe [Brady], Jeff ... have done a great job of just integrating me at the right pace," Bass said. "And just letting me be the best version of myself, and that's where I'm seeing a lot of growth in."

 Other observations: 

 
 Safety C.J. Gardner-Johnson (calf) and defensive tackle Deone Walker (left elbow) participated in the individual and team periods of practice. Walker is wearing a brace on his left arm. 
 WR Keon Coleman had an up-and-down day with a nice catch on a pass from quarterback Josh Allen  but also a drop later that left him vocalizing frustration. 
 The splash play of the day came from Allen with a deep pass to recently acquired WR Dante Pettis . If the play had taken place during a game, it would have drawn flags and a review. 
 ILBs Dorian Williams and Terrel Bernard are back participating in 11-on-11 drills, and defensive coordinator Jim Leonhard made it clear there would be roles on the defense during the season for both of those players and rookie Kaleb Elarms-Orr , who has taken advantage of significant practice time due to other injuries. "The physical skill set of those three guys, I think it's going be a lot of fun to work with." 
 
 

 Tuesday, Aug. 4 
 The Bills wore full pads during 11-on-11 drills for the first time in training camp. And with the pads came the fighting.

 Players had to be separated several times, with the back-and-forth talk starting between the offensive and defensive lines even before the team periods. One big altercation came when rookie inside linebacker Kaleb Elarms-Orr didn't realize the play was over and made contact with tight end Dalton Kincaid . The offense did not appreciate the late hit, and coach Joe Brady even had some words after the things calmed.

 One player who was consistently in the middle of the fighting and got involved in that one is offensive lineman Alec Anderson .

 "Well, I didn't enjoy hitting our guy after the whistle, but I enjoyed punching him in the face a couple times and choking him out," Anderson said. "So, that's always enjoyable."

 Veteran edge rusher  Bradley Chubb said that he loved the physicality the team brought.

 "You'd rather say chill than sic 'em," Chubb said. "So, when you got a team full of sic 'ems, that's a good thing. But at the end of the day, we got to make sure we channel our energy in the right place."

 More observations: 

 
 Quarterback Josh Allen and wide receiver DJ Moore connected for arguably the most eye-popping play of camp thus far. Allen found Moore deep downfield with three defenders -- cornerbacks Christian Benford and Maxwell Hairston and safety Cole Bishop -- trailing Moore. After it initially appeared Moore wouldn't catch up to the pass from Allen, the ball landed in the right spot for Moore to stretch out his arms midstride to bring it in. Fellow wide receiver Khalil Shakir said, "[Moore and Allen's] connection has been unreal" and that the play was so beautiful, it feels "fake." 
 
 

 
 Rookie edge rusher  TJ Parker was involved in the beginning of a skirmish. 
 Safety C.J. Gardner-Johnson (right calf strain) worked to the side early in practice. 
 DT Deone Walker  sat out a second straight practice after tweaking his elbow. He said that he was fitted for a brace Monday and hoping to be back practicing Thursday with the brace. 
 The top training camp battles continued to see rotations, including left guard (Anderson/ Austin Corbett ).﻿ 
 

 

 Monday, Aug. 3 
 
 The rain poured down at St. John Fisher University for the third time in the Bills' four training camp practices. The difficult weather lasted the entirety of the team's first practice wearing pads -- which was short-lived.

 The team took off the pads before 11-on-11 drills got underway, another noticeable Joe Brady change.

 "Coming out the first day of pads, and everyone's just adjusting and kind of thinking about all the pads," Brady said.

 Latest Bears news 
 
 Darnell Wright agrees to record deal 
 New Bears safety Coby Bryant out 8-10 weeks with injury 
 Bears CB Johnson views 2026 as 'definitely a contract year' 
 Ben Johnson: Bears motivated to spurn 'regression' label 
 
 
 

 Thursday, Aug. 6 
 The longest practice of training camp to date was also the most physical. The Bears were in pads Thursday for 130 minutes and commenced team periods with old-school 9-on-7 and 9-on-9 running drills. With music blasting across the practice fields closest to Halas Hall, the physical, downhill running session turned up the temperature in practice between the offense and defense with a handful of shoving matches after plays were blown dead.

 "Shoot, we love it," defensive end Austin Booker said. "That's our mentality this year: We're getting off the ball, we're being aggressive and getting in the backfield."

 The intensity carried over to one-on-ones between the offensive and defensive lines. Two days after becoming the highest-paid right tackle in NFL history ( four years, $116 million ), Darnell Wright won all three of his reps taken against defensive end Montez Sweat .

 Braxton Jones , who began practice at left tackle with the first-team offensive line for a fourth straight day, sustained an injury during his second one-on-one rep with Booker. Jones threw his helmet and was visibly upset as he tried to walk it off before heading inside with a trainer. The initial belief is that Jones didn't suffer a long-term injury.

 Caleb Williams finished practice on a high note after the offense struggled with operation issues in 11-on-11. There were multiple false starts, and when Rome Odunze slipped on a route, the ball headed in his direction landed in cornerback  Tyrique Stevenson 's hands for an interception.

 The Bears closed out practice with a two-minute drill. Williams marched the offense 65 yards downfield in 1:41 and went 6-of-6 while connecting with Odunze, Colston Loveland , Kalif Raymond ,  D'Andre Swift and Luther Burden III . Despite having time left on the scoreboard, practice ended immediately after Burden's touchdown in the back of the end zone given the session was right at the 2 hour, 10 minute mark.

 
 Multiple players exited early with injuries including Sweat, who was seen walking into the building under his own power. Defensive backs Dallis Flowers and Gervarrius Owens sustained significant leg injuries. 
 Cairo Santos went 6-for-6 during the field goal period and connected on kicks from 56, 50, 40 and 33 yards. 
 Defensive lineman Shemar Turner , who is on PUP while recovering from ACL surgery, appeared at practice for the first time in training camp and worked with a strength and conditioning staffer off to the side. 
 Kaden Davis continues to impress with his opportunities. The former Division II receiver had several big catches, including a touchdown in the corner of the end zone from QB Case Keenum . Davis punted the ball in celebration and was immediately flagged. 
 Rookie corner Malik Muhammad played nickel during the two-minute drill. He had several reps with the first-team defense. 
 Raymond, a 10-year veteran, believes  Zavion Thomas ' work habits reflect that of an older player. Two nights ago, the rookie wide receiver sent Raymond a series of ankle mobility exercises to help strengthen the muscles in his lower leg and foot. "It's a vet-type mindset to be disciplined and do something like that," Raymond said. "And when he showed me that video, I was just happy to know that that's who he is." 
 Ben Johnson said there is no update on Kyler Gordon (calf), who is on PUP, and when he might return to practice. "We're just continuing to rehab," Johnson said. 
 The Bears signed 10-year veteran safety  Xavier Woods  and worked out nine defensive backs. 
 

 

 Wednesday, Aug. 5 
 One day after becoming the highest-paid right tackle in NFL history, Darnell Wright got ribbed by coach Ben Johnson, who congratulated Wright on his four-year, $116 million extension ($93 million guaranteed) in front of the team before practice.

 Johnson joked that Wright "owed" offensive line coach Dan Roushar a loan. Wright agreed with Johnson's assessment and credited his position coach for helping him reach the point of his career where he's played his way into earning life-changing money.

 "[Roushar's] consistent every day in what he does and what he says," Wright said. "He's consistent in what he's telling you. ... Some coaches I've had in the past or some coaches in the league, they're not very good teachers. They see a guy with talent and blah, blah, blah, but they can't really convey what it is and teach you. You still need to be taught. So I think he is such a good teacher and he does it with such good -- he's not yelling at you, he's not screaming at you, he's not demeaning you, he's telling you what's good about the rep and he's telling you what's bad about the rep so you can see both sides.

 "If you have a coach that tells you just what you did was wrong with the rep so maybe the next rep, you just change everything. Now, you have a different result and you have no consistency to stack on top of each other, where as Dan he shows you what you did good with the rep so you can, you know, keep doing the good things and fix the bad things he tells you."

 During training camp in 2025, Roushar told reporters that he didn't see Wright playing with a consistently high motor. Wright said he appreciated the honesty and path Roushar laid for the right tackle to improve. That constructive criticism paid off as Wright earned second-team All-Pro honors while playing through an elbow injury.

 Wright was the inaugural first-round draft pick by general manager Ryan Poles in 2023. The Bears traded back one spot, from No. 9 to No. 10, which allowed the Philadelphia Eagles to draft defensive tackle Jalen Carter , while Chicago snagged its franchise right tackle.

 Proving to Poles that he made the right decision is something Wright internalized over the first three seasons of his career. Seeing how the investment made by the GM went far beyond a financial commitment motivates Wright to continue to progress.

 "[Poles] really invested in me [by] helping me get more one-on-one time with the coaches, one-on-one time more with the strength staff, one-on-one time more with [assistant strength and conditioning coach] Mark [Phillipi] in there doing core strength," Wright said. "...Even when I was a young player, it's hard for you to go up to a coach and want to demand their time. I know you're a first-round pick and blah, blah, blah, so they would probably be obliged, but sometimes it's hard for a player to approach a coach and want to take all their time when they've got stuff to do ... but he was invested in me at a really early age, beyond what you'd think a GM would do."

 

 
 The Bears were in shells for a practice that lasted 90 minutes and had just a handful of team periods conducted at walk-through speed. 
 The highlight of the morning came during a 7-on-7 period when  Caleb Williams completed 9 of 10 attempts. Wide receiver Kaden…

full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action.  Friday, Aug. 7 
 Cincinnati wants to find bigger gains in the ground game in 2026. There was a healthy amount of that in the limited portion of practice that was inside Paycor Stadium on Friday night.

 Running back Chase Brown reeled off a long run for a TD, which is a good sign for team that lacked explosive rushing plays last season. The Bengals were tied for 24th in the NFL in gains of 10 or more yards on the ground by running backs, according to ESPN Research.

 DT  Dexter Lawrence II  knocked QB Joe Burrow to the ground during team drills inside the stadium. It was a light brush. 
 For a passing offense that has struggled at times in camp, it had a good moment inside the stadium. Burrow connected on a deep throw to WR  Ja'Marr Chase  behind the Cincinnati secondary. 
 
 
 

 Thursday, Aug. 6 
 The offensive tinkering continued on Thursday as the Bengals try to find different ways to put pressure on opposing defenses. Throughout training camp, Cincinnati has had a ton of reps with QB Joe Burrow under center, which is not typically how the Bengals like to operate. But it's clear that finding ways to mix up the offensive formations is a strategy that will be critical to creating a more explosive offense. And offensive coordinator Dan Pitcher is OK with any lumps that are taken during the process.

 "We just wanna have a lot of tools at our disposal," Pitcher said on Thursday. "And that's what we're developing right now."

 
 The offense and defense traded pre-snap victories during an unscripted 11-on-11 drill. First, the defense forced a delay of game. But the offense responded by drawing the defense offsides. 
 Rookie defensive end Cashius Howell continues to turn heads. Howell took reps with the first team and created pressure off the edge. The second-round pick has been one of the camp's biggest stars. 
 Cincinnati appears to be experimenting with its back-up offensive tackles. Cody Ford and Andrew Coker swapped between the left and right sides during second-team reps. Cincinnati is looking to solidify the swing tackle spot behind starters Orlando Brown Jr . and Amarius Mims . 
 

 

 Tuesday, Aug. 4 
 The defense continues its strong start to training camp. That was punctuated by a two-play exchange that started with a pass deflection by CB  DJ Turner  on a deep ball intended for WR Ja'Marr Chase , before safety S Bryan Cook had a pick-six off QB Joe Burrow during a team drill. Coordinator Al Golden's group has looked nothing like the team that has struggled in each of the past two seasons.

 "I think as a defense, we have an edge," Golden said. "We gotta continue to have that edge. We haven't done anything."

 
 Bengals CB DJ Ivey took first-team reps with Dax Hill sidelined. Hill was dealing with a bit of tightness and was limited for precautionary reasons. 
 DT Jonathan Allen was not at practice in what appeared to be a vet rest day. Allen also missed a day last week before quickly returning. 
 Cincinnati released S Isaiah Nwokobia on Tuesday. He had not practiced in back-to-back days. 
 

 

 Monday, Aug. 3 
 The first day of pads belonged to the Bengals' defense. And in what has become a recurring theme, the defensive line was able to bring some good pressure. Boye Mafe continued to affect the quarterback and rookie Cashius Howell had a clean win off the edge against the second-team defense.

 The defense isn't letting any camp success get to their heads. "We haven't scratched the surface, which is the encouraging thing," said linebacker Barrett Carter . "Our floor right now is high. I'm not trying to jinx us or put expectations on us, but we're stacking days, and we just have to keep doing that. We're nowhere near where we can be."

 Dalton Risner and  Orlando Brown Jr . spent a good amount of time decompressing in the locker room talking about how the day went for them. It was a detailed conversation, which Risner said was an example of the group being dialed in this early in camp. 
 Rookie wide receiver Colbie Young made a couple of good catches. The coaching staff has been adamant that the fourth-round pick out of Georgia can carve out a role on this year's offense. 
 

 

 Saturday, Aug. 1 
 Have a day, Boye Mafe . The recent Super Bowl winner was disruptive throughout Saturday's practice. He consistently produced pressure against Joe Burrow and the first-team offense, including getting into a passing lane and forcing an interception .

 It has continued a good first week for the defense. But Mafe, who helped the Seahawks win the Lombardi Trophy in February with the Seahawks, knows Cincinnati has a long way to go.

 "I feel like we're really just setting our standard," Mafe said. "You can't mistake activity for achievement." 

 More observations: 

 
 WR Tee Higgins did not practice today but was a close observer. The team has made it a point to limit his workload to avoid any major soft-tissue injuries, a strategy that worked last season. 
 Former Bengals defensive end Sam Hubbard, who retired after the 2024 season, stopped by Saturday's practice to see his old teammates. 
 Practice started indoors because of rain but eventually moved to the outdoor fields. 
 Cornerback DJ Turner had a good pass deflection on a deep ball intended for Ja'Marr Chase . But was notable was the defensive backs making sure to yell "Ball!" to let Turner know the passes was about to arrive. It was an example of the communication the secondary has displayed during the first week of camp. 
 WR Mitchell Tinsley made a diving catch during a red zone drill that appeared to knock the wind out of him. While he was shaken up a touch, his efforts didn't go unnoticed. Offensive coordinator Dan Pitcher made it a point to give Tinsley props for the effort. 
 

 

 

 Friday, July 31 
 Typically, the Bengals don't practice three days in a row during training camp, but this year, Cincinnati is opening camp with four straight practices. So to break things up, Friday was more of a walk-through as the team managed the workload and tried to avoid major injuries. The Bengals didn't even bring helmets out as they slowed the pace down for a private practice. The team spent a couple of team periods working on red zone drills, which is typically what they do on Fridays during the season.

title: 2026 Cleveland Browns training camp: Latest intel, updates

full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. The  Cleveland Browns  camp is taking place at the CrossCountry Mortgage Campus and Browns reporter Daniel Oyefusi has the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and of course the quarterback room.

 Camp updates for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 

 Latest Browns stories 
 
 What are the Browns looking for in their QB competition? 
 Jerry Jeudy clarifies viral video, says he talked to Browns QBs 
 AJ Epenesa grateful to be Eagle after 'weird' Browns situation 
 Deshaun Watson: Preseason is 'great opportunity' after injuries 
 Deion Sanders gives Browns 'insight' on Shedeur Sanders 
 GM Andrew Berry 'hopeful' Browns can reunite with Jadeveon Clowney 
 Sources: Browns, Grant Delpit agree to 3-year, $48M extension 
 
 
 Friday, Aug. 7 
 The Browns had a lighter practice indoors and in helmets on Friday, as they are set to practice in pads for more than two hours on Saturday. It was still an eventful session, with all the quarterbacks pushing the ball downfield in team drills.

 Deshaun Watson looked his most comfortable attempting deep passes in camp so far. He connected with wide receiver Isaiah Bond for a long gain in 11-on-11s and also found wideout Jerry Jeudy for a 40-yard touchdown in 7-on-7s. Toward the end of practice during a two-minute drill, Watson evaded the pass rush and rolled out to his left before throwing a pass into the end zone that Bond leapt up and caught.

 

 More observations: 

 
 While Watson had some accurate downfield passes, he was also intercepted by cornerback Denzel Ward on an errant pass that went over the head of Bond; it's Watson's eighth interception in nine practices. 
 The Browns signed offensive lineman Jack Conley and cornerback Jeadyn Lukus , claimed defensive tackle Patrick Jenkins , waived wide receiver Jamari Thrash (injury designation) and linebacker, and placed guard Kendrick Green on injured reserve. 
 Rookie safety Emmanuel McNeil-Warren recorded his first interception of camp, picking off Shedeur Sanders after he overthrew tight end Jack Stoll in 11-on-11s. 
 Safety Donovan McMillon intercepted Dillon Gabriel in 11-on-11s on an underthrown deep ball to rookie wide receiver Kole Wilson . 
 Linebacker Winston Reid forced a fumble on running back Raheim Sanders and recovered the ball to end the two-minute drill led by Sanders. 
 Elgton Jenkins , Mason Graham and Teven Jenkins returned to practice, but both Jenkinses were limited to individual drills. 
 Thirteen players did not practice: Joe Royer , Myles Bryant , Michael Burton , Damarri Mathis , Carson Schwesinger , Mike Hall Jr ., Parker Brailsford , Izavion Miller , Elijah Chatman , Zak Zinter , Sam Kamara , Kalia Davis , Maliek Collins . 
 
 
 Thursday, Aug. 6 
The Browns' eighth day of practice concluded the installation of coach Todd Monken's offense. Going forward, Monken said practices would focus more on situational football, "premier plays," and work against defensive looks that Cleveland will see from opponents this season.
 "What we're trying to do is stack as many good plays as we can within what we're asking them to do on a given day," Monken said. "I'd much prefer stacking really good days, but as the head coach, if the offense is stacking really good days, it probably means the defense wasn't stacking a very good day. So, within every practice there's usually give and take, some ebb and flow of practice -- some things you all don't see, and some things that at the moment we don't see until we see it on tape. So it's really about how many plays in a row can we stack?"

 

 More observations: 

 
 Deshaun Watson  and Shedeur Sanders both threw an interception in team drills. Cornerback Tyson Campbell intercepted Watson in 7-on-7 drills, while cornerback Myles Harden intercepted Sanders in red zone 11-on-11 drills. Safety Grant Delpit broke up a pass intended for rookie wide receiver Denzel Boston , which led to the pick. 
 Two plays after his interception, Sanders threw the lone touchdown in team drills when he found rookie receiver KC Concepcion in the end zone after he located an opening in Cleveland's zone defense. 
 Guard Zak Zinter left practice on a cart. 
 Sixteen players did not practice Thursday: Joe Royer , Myles Bryant , Michael Burton , Damarri Mathis , Carson Schwesinger , Mike Hall Jr. , Parker Brailsford , Kendrick Green , Izavion Miller , Elijah Chatman , Elgton Jenkins , Teven Jenkins , Sam Kamara , Kalia Davis , Mason Graham , Maliek Collins . 
 
 
 Wednesday, Aug. 5 
 Quarterback Deshaun Watson had a slow start to training camp but had his best day to date on Wednesday. After two consecutive practices in pads, the Browns practiced in shoulder pads and helmets and ran extensive red zone and goal line 7-on-7 drills. Watson excelled, throwing multiple touchdowns, but he also looked more in sync and confident pushing the ball downfield in other team drills.

 "I think to say who's ahead is a little extreme," Browns coach Todd Monken said before practice. "But we evaluate every day where our roster is, who's where. We try not to knee-jerk react on the one day; that's hard to do. We want every day to go as smooth as it can, and it doesn't, so you have to fight that part of it. We also have to fight; we're in install. We see what you see, and we see a little more in-depth because of the film. But the reality is we're always talking about personnel and the roster; the quarterbacks just happen to be part of that."

 Another observation: 

 
 Sixteen players did not practice Wednesday: tight end Joe Royer (personal), cornerback Myles Bryant and Damarri Mathis , fullback Michael Burton , linebacker Carson Schwesinger , defensive tackles Mike Hall Jr ., Kalia Davis , Mason Graham , Maliek Collins (PUP), Sam Kamara and Elijah Chatman ; centers Parker Brailsford and Elgton Jenkins ; offensive tackle Izavion Miller , guard Teven Jenkins and wide receiver Jamari Thrash . 
 
 
 Tuesday, Aug. 4 
 Quarterback Shedeur Sanders , leading the No. 1 offense in Cleveland's quarterback competition today, led a two-minute drill that ended in a field goal.

 It marked the second straight day Sanders led a successful two-minute drill to end practice.

 "I've been highly impressed over the last four months that I've been around him with how far he's come as a player, and he's only going to continue to get better," Browns coach Todd Monken said. "There's a lot to take in when you're installing. We got through the spring, then we were gone for six weeks, and then you start back up again in a new system. I think you'll continue to see his operation and mechanics improve, and I think that's the biggest part right now is in and out of the huddle, getting to the line of scrimmage, eliminating that anxiety, his anxiety and my anxiety."

 

 More observations from the day: 

 
 Wide receiver KC Concepcion was at practice after avoiding a serious shoulder injury on Monday but was limited to individual drills.

title: 2026 Dallas Cowboys training camp: Latest intel, updates
summary: Follow our daily updates from Cowboys training camp, including intel on QBs, position battles and potential breakouts.
full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. The Dallas Cowboys ' camp is taking place in Oxnard, California, and Cowboys reporter Todd Archer has the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and, of course, the quarterbacks room.

 What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at the Cowboys' camp. We will update this file often. Will Dallas turn around the NFL's worst defense from 2025? Who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football? And which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Dive in to all the updates and be sure to check back for more information until the first full week of the preseason begins Aug. 13.

 
 Camp updates for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 

 Latest news from Cowboys camp 
 
 Cowboys' Dak Prescott not shying away from setting lofty goals 
 Jones optimistic about Cowboys, likes 'what we put together' 
 Source: Ex-Cowboys QB Will Grier returns as offensive assistant 
 Quieter offseason has Cowboys focused on the right things 
 

 

 Friday, Aug. 7 

 After he was tossed from Tuesday's practice for throwing a punch, second-year edge rusher Donovan Ezeiruaku had a conversation with coach Brian Schottenheimer.

 Schottenheimer said it was a "long talk."

 "I just talked to him about [how] we're playing this the way you would play a game. And I said, 'For an incredible player, you run hot'; that's part of his edge," Schottenheimer said. "He's an incredible play-style guy. He plays the game the right way, but at the same time, we have to have a plan that when he gets hot and when he feels his temperature rising, what is the plan?

 "So he and I discussed a couple different options. I think we've got a good thing in place, but again, I don't want to take away the edge that he plays on. But you throw a punch, you've gone over the edge, therefore you're going to get ejected.

 Schottenheimer said Ezeiruaku's reaction was "great."

 In Thursday's practice, Ezeiruaku was as active as he has been, providing pressure off the edge. And he didn't throw a punch.

 
 Thursday, Aug. 6 
 With the Cowboys holding their Military Appreciation Day at training camp Thursday, Dak Prescott was presented with a gift from a fan.

 It was a Cowboys hat with a picture of his brother Jace on the side. At first, Prescott said he just thought it was a normal hat until he saw Jace, who died in 2020 . Prescott's Faith Fight Finish Foundation, which honors his brother as well as his mother, addresses mental health and suicide prevention.

 "That actually means a lot," Prescott said. "I wish I knew who did it because I would've said thank you. I just thought it was a hat. I didn't see it until I go with my daughters [after practice]. 
 
"It's badass."

 

 More observations: 

 
 Coach Brian Schottenheimer wanted to clarify the state of the left tackle competition. Tyler Guyton hasn't been named the starter yet, but Nate Thomas needs to up his level to make sure there is a competition. Guyton took part in Thursday's work with his right elbow taped after he didn't finish Tuesday's practice. Guyton and Thomas had false-start penalties leading to their departures for a play. 
 Tight end  Jake Ferguson is off to a strong start in camp. He and Prescott have had a clear connection on the intermediate and seam throws, and they connected four times Thursday with one completion coming on a "free" play when the defense jumped early that led to a decent gain. 
 Rookie LB Jaishawn Barham did not finish practice because of a groin injury. A source said it wasn't believed to be serious, and Barham was able to return to the field to watch the final parts of the workout. 
 It did not rise to the level of the Donovan Ezeiruaku punch, but cornerback Caelen Carson and rookie receiver Anthony Smith got into a tug-of-war and needed to be separated by teammates. It was brewing with both players after a particularly physical play early in team drills. 
 LB Curtis Robinson had a near interception of a Sam Howell pass down the seam to tight end Brevyn Spann-Ford , reaching high with his right hand to knock it down. The ball nearly fell into Robinson's lap as he landed on the ground. 
 

 

 Wednesday, Aug. 5 
 A year ago at this time, the Cowboys were learning about how  Javonte Williams  fit into their run game. They found out what he did well, as he rushed for 1,201 yards in 2025. Then they rewarded him with a three-year, $24 million contract in the offseason.

 As Williams enters his second season with the Cowboys, offensive coordinator Klayton Adams is looking to expand the list of what Williams does best.

 "Obviously the guy's pretty good on direct runs and he's hard to get down behind the line of scrimmage, but I think that he is a more diverse runner than he probably gets credit for," Adams said. "I think the guy does a really nice job with some of the outside zone stuff, particularly the weak side.

 "He's got really quick feet. He's able to get in and out of cuts really well. And he's one of those dudes that's not scared to run through the smoke, and that's what you're going to have to do on some of the time. I think he's good at a lot of things."

 

 Tuesday, Aug. 4 
 Sometimes coaches can be inventive when it comes to putting players through drills. On Tuesday, wide receivers coach Junior Adams had CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens catching passes off the Jugs machine during a special teams portion of practice while wearing what looked like a mosquito net or beekeeper's hat.

 The goal is to limit the receiver's vision and force him to concentrate longer on the catch. Lamb dropped one pass but figured it out. The first pass went through Pickens' hands, and he was finished.

 Longtime tight ends coach Mike Pope, who had a stint with the Cowboys, said he had 478 different drills for his tight ends. He would throw ice water at shirtless players while wearing a helmet. He had them wear swim goggles to limit their peripheral vision.

 Let's see if Adams has more tricks in his bag.

 More observations: 

 
 Defensive end  Donovan Ezeiruaku was tossed from practice for fighting. Brian Schottenheimer abhors fighting in practice because if a player throws a punch in a game, he gets ejected. A lesson to be learned for Ezeiruaku. 
 With linebacker  DeMarvion Overshown battling a sore leg (a source said it was nothing to do with his surgically repaired knee), rookie Jaishawn Barham worked with the first-team defense next to Dee Winters . 
 Quarterback  Dak Prescott went 13-of-17 in team drills and would have been better if not for drops by Lamb and tight end  Jake Ferguson . He tried to stretch the field once with a throwback down the field to Pickens, who drew a flag on cornerback  Shavon Revel  at the goal line for pass interference. 
 Ferguson had two excellent catches, however, adjusting on a slightly underthrown seam ball from Prescott and later securing a lower pass with one hand before getting it under control. 
 Cornerback  Cobie Durant came up with the defensive play of the day, knocking away a deep ball from Prescott to wideout  Marquez Valdes-Scantling . Safety Alijah Clark was tangled up on the play and limped off to the medical tent and did not return. 
 

 

 

 Monday, Aug. 3 
 No, there is not going to be a playcaller controversy when it comes to the Cowboys this season, but coach Brian Schottenheimer gave the controls to coordinator Klayton Adams for two periods in Monday's practice, including red zone work.

 The result? Four touchdowns in a six-play span, including one to Ryan Flournoy where the receiver wrestled the ball away from cornerback  DaRon Bland for the score from Dak Prescott .

 "[Bland] actually guarded it great," Flournoy said. "I just had to win on that. I dropped slant before that so I had to make it up. Yeah, definitely great defense by DB. I just had to show strong…

title: 2026 Denver Broncos training camp: Latest intel, updates
summary: Follow our daily updates from Broncos training camp, including intel on the QBs, position battles and potential breakouts.
full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. The Denver Broncos camp is taking place in Englewood, Colorado, and Broncos reporter Jeff Legwold has the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and of course the quarterback room.

 What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at Broncos camp. We will update this file often as we track the Broncos' push toward getting to the Super Bowl after falling one game short last season. Who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football? And which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Dive in to all the updates and be sure to check back for more information until the first full week of the preseason begins Aug. 13.

 
 Camp updates for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 

 Latest news from Broncos camp 
 
 Payton to talk to Taysom Hill about interest in Broncos 
 Broncos QB Bo Nix won't be afraid to run on repaired ankle 
 How will Broncos' Sean Payton adjust to not calling plays? 
 Cooper practices Wednesday despite legal troubles 
 

 

 Friday, Aug. 7 
 If Broncos coach Sean Payton checks his phone on his flight to Canton, Ohio, on Friday he isn't going to like some of the messages. It was a rugged day of practice, as wide receiver Marvin Mims Jr ., tight end Nate Adkins and defensive lineman Matt Henningsen left with injuries.

 Mims pulled up after running a deep route and hopped off the field before he went to the locker room. Adkins walked into the locker room with Mims and a trainer while Henningsen, who missed last season with a ruptured Achilles he suffered in last summer's camp, was carted to the locker room with an apparent leg injury.

 That comes in addition to the other injuries the Broncos suffered already this week to wide receiver Jaylen Waddle (leg) and edge rusher Nik Bonitto (ankle/foot). Bonitto returned to practice Friday on a limited basis.

 More observations: 

 
 Payton, several assistant coaches and kicker Wil Lutz left during Friday's practice to head to Ohio for the events surrounding Drew Brees' enshrinement into the Pro Football Hall of Fame. Payton will be Brees' presenter at the Gold Jacket dinner Friday night and at the enshrinement ceremony Saturday. The group had all been with the New Orleans Saints during Brees' career. 
 Defensive coordinator Vance Joseph ran practice after Payton left and will run Saturday's workout in which the Broncos will go through a controlled scrimmage. Joseph spoke to the team at the end of practice as Payton usually does and cornerback Ja'Quan McMillian said he told Joseph "head coach looks good on you." 
 Wide receiver Courtland Sutton practiced fully Friday, while offensive tackle  Garett Bolles , defensive tackle D.J. Jones and defensive tackle Malcolm Roach had rest days. 
 

 

 Thursday, Aug. 6 
 Wide receiver Jaylen Waddle , who left practice Wednesday with what appeared to be a left leg injury, did not practice Thursday and moved gingerly between drills as he watched practice. Coach Sean Payton said after practice Waddle had suffered a "strain" and "I think we'll see him back in the next four to five days."

 The Broncos practice Friday and Saturday before a player's off day Sunday. They have three full practice days next week before a travel day for their Aug. 14 preseason opener in Atlanta. Waddle's status for that preseason opener, which is when Payton typically plays starters at least one quarter, is still a question mark.

 More observations: 

 
 Courtland Sutton , who had been held out the previous two days for rest, participated on a limited basis and is expected to practice fully Friday. Payton said Sutton is not injured, but the rest schedule is "our protocol" for Sutton and that other veteran players in the coming weeks will have similar schedules. Sutton said the team's training staff showed him tracking data from practices late in the season last year to talk to him about trying to pace him better through the season. "Last year I kind of got ran into the ground going into the end part of the season ... just trying to make sure the body stays as fresh as possible as late in the season as possible," he said. 
 Former Broncos coach Mike Shanahan, the franchise's winningest coach, including back-to-back Super Bowl wins to close out the 1997 and 1998 seasons, was at practice Thursday and received a tour of the team's new $178 million facility. 
 

 

 

 Wednesday, Aug. 5 
 Wide receiver Jaylen Waddle left Wednesday's practice and did not return. The Broncos' main offseason addition slowed down during a play in a team period and walked off to the locker room. He did not return to practice. Coach Sean Payton said after the workout that Waddle would be "fine" after the initial exam by the team's medical staff. "But we'll evaluate him ... he had some muscle tightness," he added.

 Payton has said repeatedly "we'll be smart" about returning players to practice after injuries. With the Broncos still nine days away from their preseason opener, Waddle could be held out of some practice time in the remainder of the week. Courtland Sutton was also given his second consecutive off day, so Marvin Mims Jr ., Troy Franklin and Pat Bryant got the bulk of the work with the starters after Waddle left the field. Payton said Sutton would practice Thursday.

 More observations: 

 
 Franklin and Bryant each had explosive plays in team drills Wednesday and Franklin might have had his best day of camp overall. The receiver combination of Sutton, Waddle, Mims, Franklin and Bryant -- if healthy -- looks like it will be the top five, so the Broncos would have to keep six receivers for another wideout to make the 53-player roster at the end of the preseason. 
 The Broncos again showed their cornerback depth, as Kris Abrams-Draine intercepted Bo Nix in an 11-on-11 period. 
 Sam Ehlinger took snaps with the second-team offense during multiple practice periods Wednesday and continues to push Jarrett Stidham for the backup quarterback job. Ehlinger re-signed with the Broncos this offseason after spending 2025 on the practice squad. He turned down multiple chances to sign with a team with an active roster spot a year ago. 
 

 

 Tuesday, Aug. 4 

 Edge rusher Nik Bonitto limped off the practice field Tuesday after he suffered what appeared to be a lower left leg injury in a 9-on-7 run-game drill. Bonitto left the field with a trainer as well as one of the team doctors and did not return. After practice, Broncos coach Sean Payton would say only "he'll be fine, no updates."

 Bonitto has led the team in sacks in each of the past two seasons -- 13.5 in 2024 and 14.0 in 2025 - helping the Broncos lead the league and establish single-season franchise records in each campaign. Jonah Elliss and Jonathon Cooper took most of the snaps with the starters at the edge spots after Bonitto left practice, with second-year man Que Robinson getting more work throughout the day as well.

 It was the second consecutive day the Broncos had a starter leave practice. Center Luke Wattenberg , who dealt with a shoulder injury last season, left Monday's practice and did not practice Tuesday.

 More observations: 

 
 Add Broncos wide receiver Jaylen Waddle to the list of those who have noticed Marvin Mims Jr .'s work this training camp. Mims made another leaping grab Tuesday -- this time in one-on-ones -- and Waddle was quick to praise it all after practice. "Man, Marv -- I'm a big fan of Marvin Mims, I'm not going to lie. He's very explosive, I love watching him work, love being in meetings (with him), picking his brain. Marvin's a big play always ready to happen, you've got to respect that kind of speed."

title: Mrs. Met, Goldy headline inductions into the Mascot Hall of Fame
summary: The announcement was made Friday morning on "Good Morning America," with the five mascots on site to receive the news.
full_text:
On Friday morning, Cocky, Cosmo, Goldy, Miles and Mrs. Met entered the Mascot Hall of Fame , joining a pantheon of some of sports' most famous costumed friends.

 The announcement was made on "Good Morning America," with the five mascots on site to receive the news.

 

 The quintet will make up the 11th Mascot Hall of Fame class, including the inaugural 2005 class, and will join 38 previously honored mascots in the Hall.

 Here's a little more about the five inductees and why they were deserving of making the Hall.

 

 Cocky, South Carolina Gamecocks 
 

 Cocky, representing the South Carolina Gamecocks since 1980, is one of the most accomplished mascots in the game when it comes to trophy cabinets. He's a two-time Universal Cheerleaders Association (UCA) mascot national champion (1986 and 1994), the 2008 NCA mascot national champion and won the 2004 Capital One Mascot Challenge.

 

 
 Cosmo, BYU Cougars 
 

 BYU mascot Cosmo the Cougar made his debut in 1953 by parachuting into LaVell Edwards Stadium, and enters the Hall with a lengthy résumé -- he is the holder of three official Guinness World Records , tops in the record books in double high-fives, back handsprings and consecutive breakdance windmills.

 
 Goldy, Minnesota Golden Gophers 
 

 The University of Minnesota's mascot since 1952, Goldy Gopher is modeled after the 13-lined ground squirrel, a rodent common in Minnesota that bears a resemblance to gophers. Known for his head-spinning celebration, Goldy has won 4 UCA mascot national championships -- in 2011, 2013, 2017 and 2018.

 
 Miles, Denver Broncos 
 

 Miles is the equestrian mascot of the Denver Broncos, best known for climbing to the top of Empower Field at Mile High before the fourth quarter of games. A little-known fact about Miles is that he wears Crocs, a nod to the brand's Colorado roots.

 
 Mrs. Met, New York Mets 

 Just under two decades after her husband, Mr. Met, entered the mascot Hall in 2007, Mrs. Met is joining him. The humanoid baseball who represents the Mets was formerly known as "Lady Met" and was a trailblazer for female mascots in sports. Introduced in the 1960s, Mrs. Met's revival in 2013 after years of inactivity gave the Mets a one-two mascot punch unrivaled in baseball.

St. Brown had a two-point conversion while also converting multiple fourth-downs on a monster day in which his playmaking was consistently on display.  Campbell feels they will continue to get better.

 Running back  Jahmyr Gibbs returned to practice, taking part in the walkthrough portion and stretches for the first time all training camp, before working on the side with a team trainer. However, he didn't participate in any individual drills during the session as he seeks a new deal. A crowd of media members swarmed Gibbs as he strolled off the practice field to enter the locker room after signing autographs, but he carefully avoided reporters and flashed a thumbs-up sign to the group after being asked if he was close to reaching a contract extension soon.

 Tuesday, Aug. 4 
 Tuesday marked Day 2 of padded practices and veteran LB Devin White continued to get acclimated to the defense alongside guys like All-Pro Jack Campbell . White was signed as a free agent on Aug. 1 to add depth after rookie linebacker  Jimmy Rolder went down with a hamstring injury earlier in camp. He has received limited reps in practices so far but has been doing additional conditioning drills on the side with trainers to keep in shape. "Right now, they've got a plan for me and I'm trusting in the plan," White said. "So, whenever they're ready for me to stop doing reps on the side, running and getting more reps in the team period, I'm going to be ready for it."

 More observations: 

 
 Lions RB Jahmyr Gibbs missed his sixth straight practice as his hold-in for a contract extension continues but was on the field watching. Ahead of Tuesday's practice, the Atlanta Falcons reached a record-setting three-year extension with RB Bijan Robinson worth up to $75 million, which now likely sets the stage for Gibbs to reach an extension soon. Campbell feels it's "certainly not gonna hurt" with the process of negotiating. "It's not gonna hurt. But we'll see. Look, I'm anxious to get Gibbs back out there," Campbell said. "Every day that goes by, that's another day that you feel like you miss with him and getting him out there with the guys and him doing his part. But there again, it'll get done when it gets done." 
 LB Malcolm Rodriguez left practice early to be evaluated for an ankle injury. 
 The Lions have placed TE Anthony Firkser on injured reserve list and signed TE Zach Horton . Firkser will miss time with a fractured fibula after being carted off the field in practice on Monday. 
 Lions RB Sione Vaki missed Tuesday's practice after getting poked in the eye and suffering a broken nose during a freak accident at practice Monday, according to Campbell. Vaki will also miss time. "We think he'll be OK," Campbell said. "He's just gonna need a minute here. It's just one of those freak things. Somehow a hand gets through the face mask. It was unbelievable."﻿ 
 
 

 

 Monday, Aug. 3 
 The Lions started padded practices on Monday for the first time in training camp. Head coach Dan Campbell anticipated the intensity increasing with pads on. That sentiment proved correct as players showed more aggression in training for Day 5.

 "I told the players last night that by the end of this week, this roster will begin to separate itself," Campbell said. "This is where we'll find out. We're about to get four really, really good days of pads, and this is Day 1 just to kind of break them in for the other three."

 More observations: 

 
 Star running back Jahmyr Gibbs missed his fifth consecutive practice as his hold-in continues while looking to reach a new deal. However, he was spotted roaming the sidelines for the second straight day, chatting with teammates  Amon-Ra St. Brown , Jameson Williams and Jared Goff on the sidelines. "I think it's good to see. He got a little work inside and to be able to come out and be around the guys, I think that's always gonna be important," Campbell said of Gibbs. "Look, he's still part of us and our players love him. We love him and he's a part of what we do, so it's always good to see him." 
 Injured Lions safeties Kerby Joseph (knee) and Brian Branch (Achilles) were both spotted doing individual rehab/conditioning drills on the side with trainers during practice. 
 Lions rookie LB Jimmy Rolder (hamstring) will be "out for…
