title: Why Packers are connecting with DC Gannon's 'turnt up' vibe
summary: The former Cardinals head coach is bringing a different approach to the defense, and players are buying in.
full_text:
GREEN BAY, Wis. -- There are two Jonathan Gannons on the Green Bay Packers  coaching staff. There's the one underneath the floppy hat and behind the sunglasses who strolls onto the practice field like he doesn't have a care in the world. And the one his players describe.

 And more than one used the same word to do so.

 "He [is] a little crazy, you know," safety Javon Bullard said.

 "He's got like a crazy little energy," safety Evan Williams said.

 

 Other players have offered similar descriptions.

 "Oh yeah, J.G., man, he just turnt up, man," linebacker Zaire Franklin said.

 It sounds like he's nothing like the guy in the infamous, cringeworthy video from a team meeting early in his tenure as head coach of the Arizona Cardinals , during which he asked players whether they drove to the facility or took the bus, seemingly leaving them uninspired.

 "The 'crazy' things ... I don't know who said that, but [I know what] they're probably alluding to," Gannon said. "I do believe that words paint pictures, so there's certain things in the install or certain things when we're going over a tape review, I'm probably using an example that's non-football-related that hopefully hits their brain and they can understand it a little bit better or it kinda cements it in: This has to get done. And I sometimes will use some examples that are probably a little bit out there, so maybe that's what they're talking about."

 

 Whatever the method, Gannon seems to be striking a chord with his new players, many of whom had close relationships with Gannon's popular predecessor, Jeff Hafley. Seemingly no one was more universally liked and respected in the locker room than Hafley, who is now the head coach of the Miami Dolphins .

 So while there has been much talk about how Gannon's scheme (a 3-4 base) differs from Hafley (who used a 4-3), it may be just as important to Gannon to connect with his players like Hafley did.

 Star edge rusher Micah Parsons  spoke glowingly about Hafley after last season, saying, "He's another guy I can't wait to have another year with."

 This was before Hafley got the job in Miami. And when presented with the notion that Hafley could leave for a head coaching job, it was as if Parsons was trying to speak it into non-existence.

 "Nah, Haf ain't going nowhere," Parsons said at the time.

 To be sure, coaches aren't employed to win popularity contests, and being known as a player's coach doesn't always ring true with players.

 "Anytime I need to get cussed out or need a chewing, he's going to be on me," cornerback Brandon Cisse said.

 

 Gannon has been especially popular in the safety room. So far in camp, he has shown a willingness to use three safeties -- usually Bullard, Xavier McKinney and Williams -- on the field together. While Hafley did that with Bullard in the nickel, Gannon appears to have taken it a step further by giving all three safeties more responsibilities and more freedom.

 "I'd probably say the biggest thing right now, obviously we got this three-safety look going on, which we love it right now," McKinney said early in camp. "I think we're gonna continue to love it. I think it's gonna progress and get better as we learn different spots. We're all able to move around and do different things."

 Only Franklin and defensive tackle Javon Hargrave had any previous experience with Gannon. Franklin was on the Colts when Gannon served as their defensive backs coach from 2018 to 2020. Hargrave and Gannon were together in Philadelphia when Gannon was the defensive coordinator in 2021 and 2022.

 Franklin predicted early on that his fellow defenders like McKinney, Parsons and linebacker Edgerrin Cooper would quickly discover what he likes about Gannon.

 "He's gonna bring that fire, he's gonna bring that energy." Franklin said. "I think he recognizes who we have in that room, and he wants the players to play. And I think that's just special.

 "Some guys want to put themselves in that position, and they want their name in the media. Whereas J.G. understands, 'Look, let the players play' -- let us get in the best position, let Cooper and let 'X' be him, let Zaire be him, let Micah be Micah. So that's what's special about it, and you know he's gonna bring that energy for sure. He's gonna make sure we turnt up for sure."

 So even if Gannon seems a little monotonous in public, his players insist that's not what he's like behind the scenes.

 "I feel like you need that as a D coordinator; you need to be a little on edge," Williams said. "If you're a D coordinator, and you're fully stable and emotionally flatlined, I don't need that."

title: 2026 Houston Texans training camp: Latest intel, updates
summary: Follow our daily updates from Houston Texans training camp, including intel on QBs, position battles and potential breakouts.
full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. The  Houston Texans ' camp is taking place in Houston at at NRG Park., and Texans reporter D.J. Bien-Aime has the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and of course the quarterback room.

 What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at camp. We will update this file often. Who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football? And which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Dive in to all the updates and be sure to check back for more information until the first full week of the preseason begins Aug. 13.

 
 Camp updates for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 

 Latest news from Texans camp 
 
 Tank Dell returns to practice for first time since 2024 
 Houston bringing back former No. 1 pick Clowney 
 Texans have 'productive' contract talks with Stroud 
 

 

 Friday, Aug. 7 

 After an off day, the Texans dialed back their intensity as they went through drills without pads, but notably, wide receiver  Tank Dell practiced for the second straight day of training camp, albeit in a limited capacity.

 It's another step in Dell's recovery, with Wednesday being his first time practicing since he suffered multiple torn ligaments and a dislocated kneecap in Week 16 of 2024.

 Speaking to the media for the first time, Dell said he had no fear in the strength of his knee, pointing towards Houston's doctor stating his knee is "100 percent stable." 

 "Trusting the work you put in prior to going out there," said Dell when asked about trusting in his health. "Going out there to put your foot in the ground, trusting the process with the training staff and what they had set out for me. So when I got out here, I wasn't scared."﻿

 

 Wednesday, Aug. 5 

 Wideout Tank Dell made his return to the practice field, participating in limited capacity. It marked the first time he engaged in any sort of team padded practice since Week 16 of 2024 after the 2023 third-round pick suffered multiple torn ligaments and a dislocated kneecap against the Chiefs.

 He caught a few passes from quarterback C.J. Stroud during individual drills and ran full speed routes.

 Dell didn't do much more after that, but this is the step in the right direction. Coach DeMeco Ryans won't rush Dell back and said "Tank is on the right plan." The goal is have him ready for team 11-on-11 contact reps. He still has a ways to go, but this is positive progress.

 Other observation:  

 Wideout Jayden Higgins continue to flash throughout practice. He made another impressive catch with Derek Stingley Jr . in coverage. It was a tightly contested catch but that's always a positive because it's against an All-Pro corner.

 

 Tuesday, Aug. 4 

 Texans wideout Jayden Higgins is starting to blossom as he's entering Year 2. When Pro Bowl wideout Nico Collins  was asked about Higgins' progression he said "He's hooping right now, and I can't wait to see him rock out when it really matters."

 During Tuesday's practice, Higgins made multiple catches with All-Pro cornerback  Derek Stingley Jr . in coverage. One of those receptions occurred during a team third-down period for a 20-yard gain. The other one was during 1-on-1s -- where Stingley tried to aggressively jam Higgins, but he avoided the powerful jab and broke free for an easy toss from quarterback C.J. Stroud .

 Early in camp, Stroud said he expected Higgins to have a "dominant" Year 2, and so far we are starting to see it.

 Other observation:  

 Linebacker Azeez Al-Shaair was slow to get up after a collision with tight end Dalton Schultz . Al-Shaair was fine shortly after.

 

 Monday, Aug. 3 

 This was Day 1 of padded practices, and the defense shined. Quarterback C.J. Stroud  was forced to hold the ball longer than he would like as the secondary coverage was stout.

 Stroud occasionally scrambled more than usual to buy time to make throws and the defensive line forced a few sacks. Safety Calen Bullock intercepted Stroud.

 Also coach DeMeco Ryans used exotic blitzes throughout the day, and the offense sometimes had answers and other times didn't. Ryans deemed the first day in full pads as "successful." 

 Other observation: 

 First-round pick Keylan Rutledge is adding an extra juice of aggression to the unit. He got into a mini tussle with defensive end Danielle Hunter after a successful run play by running back Woody Marks .

 

 Saturday, Aug. 1 
 Saturday's padless practice featured more back and forth from the offense and defense. Some periods the defense dominated and others, the offense was able to counter their blitzing.

 The Texans start padded practices on Monday and that will be a "big part" of the evaluation process for the team according to coach DeMeco Ryans.

 The fourth-year head coach said: "There's a lot of all-stars in shorts," and later added the staff wouldn't be fooled by what players have done without pads.

 Another observation: 

 
 Cornerback Derek Stingley Jr collided with linebacker Henry To'oTo'o and was slow to get up, but he shook it off and was back on the field. 
 

 

 Friday, July 31 
 It was mainly walk-throughs for the Texans. It's a theme that's been consistent for coach DeMeco Ryans throughout the offseason -- where he has focused on helping his team mentally work toward executing deep in the playoffs.

 "I've grown as a head coach," Ryans said in June. "For me, it's more so now about how much smarter can we play as a team. How can we be more elite on our execution? Our communication, can it be louder? Can we echo it more? Can we truly be tied together every time we line up? That's what I've seen when I talk about the process of us this year being better."

 Saturday's practice will be the first day with fans in attendance since training camp has opened. That will be a longer practice with more intensity compared to today's practice that was roughly a little over an hour.

 

 

 Thursday, July 30 
 The passing attack was centered around the quick game time to throw on Day 2 of practice. Quarterback C.J. Stroud was quick and decisive with his throws with all but one of his throws being made under 2.8 seconds, and his only rep over three seconds was when he extended the play and tried to find wideout Jayden Higgins in the back of the end zone.

 It fell incomplete, but the majority of his throws came with precision and decisiveness. Stroud was able to connect a few times with Higgins, who's development in Year 2 will be huge for the offense.

 Other observation:  

 
 Backup cornerback Alijah Huzzie was able to make a nice interception off of backup QB  Davis Mills  -- where took the ball away from the intended receiver. 
 
 
 Wednesday, July 29 
 The Texans were more forthcoming regarding contract discussions than normal. General manager Nick Caserio said there's a "possibility" the team and quarterback C.J. Stroud can reach a contract extension. Stroud isn't focused much on contract discussions; he's letting his agent handle it as he is "keeping the main thing the main thing."

 Stroud is going into Year 4 and is eligible for an extension for the first time in his career. Coach DeMeco Ryans said he doesn't get into a lot of deep discussions with guys when it comes to contract situations.

 But he added, "I truly believe you get the contract by what you do on the field. It doesn't matter what you say, what I say. It's about how you perform on the field, and if you're worthy of getting a contract and you deserve it, it'll happen for you."

 Other observation: 

 
 CB Kamari Lassiter intercepted Stroud with a diving catch and then punted the ball in celebration. That was the most exciting play on a relatively quiet morning.

title: 2026 Jacksonville Jaguars training camp: Latest intel, updates
summary: Follow our daily updates from Jaguars training camp, including intel on QBs, position battles and potential breakouts.
full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. The Jacksonville Jaguars camp is taking place in Jacksonville, Florida, and Jaguars reporter Michael DiRocco has the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and of course the quarterback room.

 What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at Jaguars camp. We will update this file often. How much will we see Travis Hunter on both sides of the ball in camp? Who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football? And which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Dive in to all the updates and be sure to check back for more information until the first full week of the preseason begins Aug. 13.

 
 Camp updates for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 

 Latest news from Jaguars' camp 
 
 Jaguars' Travis Hunter feeling faster after 10-pound weight gain 
 
 
 

 Friday Aug. 7 
 Parker Washington picked up right where he left off at the end of the 2025 season: As the Jaguars' top pass catcher.

 Washington caught passes for 118 yards and a touchdown in the Jaguars' Teal & White mock game on Friday (unofficial stats). He had a 50-yard catch and run and also had a 22-yard reception to go along with his 3-yard touchdown pass, one of three that quarterback Trevor Lawrence threw in the Teal's 19-12 victory.

 "It was nice to see Parker, Jakobi [WR Jakobi Meyers ], B.T. [WR Brian Thomas Jr .] make some plays and just getting the guys trying to spread it around a little bit and go execute," head coach Liam Coen said.

 Washington was thrust into a bigger role in the offense last season because of injuries to Travis Hunter and Thomas and by the end of the season was Lawrence's favorite target. Washington had 19 catches on 29 targets for 347 yards and two touchdowns in the final three games of the regular season. He also had seven catches for 107 yards and a touchdown in the playoff loss to Buffalo.

 Other unofficial stats and notes from the mock game: 

 
 Hunter played 14 snaps on defense and seven on offense. All of his snaps came while playing on the first units. He had no catches on two targets but he did carry the ball for 10 yards on a jet sweep. 
 Lawrence completed 15 of 29 passes for 212 yards and three touchdowns. Washington, Thomas, and RB LeQuint Allen Jr . each had TD catches. 
 RG Patrick Mekari did not participate and RG Walker Little and LG Emmanuel Pregnon and were both injured during the mock game and did not return. LT Cole Van Lanen (knee) and OL Garrett DiGiorgio were already on PUP. This is potentially a problem area if the injuries to Mekari, Little and Pregnon linger. 
 CB Montaric Brown intercepted Nick Mullens to stop a drive in the red zone. CB Keni-H Lovely dropped an interception against Lawrence. 
 Second-year player B.J. Green II had at least two sacks and a tackle for loss. 
 Rookie S Jalen Huskey knocked the ball away from WR Chandler Brayboy and also recovered the fumble. 
 DE Josh Hines-Allen had a veteran rest day and did not participate. 
 

 

 
 Thursday, Aug. 6 
 Talks between the Jaguars and receiver  Parker Washington 's camp on a contract extension remain active, but the fourth-year player out of Penn State isn't focusing on when a deal could get done and isn't upset that an agreement hasn't yet been reached.

 "It's there and it's a conversation, but my focus is just coming out here and I need to make plays for Trevor [Lawrence] ," Washington said Thursday. "So that's my mindset and that's how I'm going to attack it. I'm not going to step on my agent's toes. They can have those conversations. I'm going to come out here and do my job."

 Jaguars general manager James Gladstone said early in the offseason the team was working on extensions with Washington and tight end Brenton Strange . They reached a deal with Strange, signing him to a three-year extension worth up to $48 million in June but have yet to finalize anything with Washington.

 Washington was asked about his reaction to the four-year, $140 million extension  with $108 million guaranteed that receiver Zay Flowers agreed to with Baltimore and said he was happy for Flowers, who was the 22nd overall pick in 2023.

 "The receiver market is a little crazy and you see guys getting their opportunities and getting paid, I mean, that's cool," said Washington, whom the Jaguars drafted in the sixth round in 2023. "But like I said, for me, I just want to go out here and be my best self and just attack it."

 

 More observations: 

 
 OL Emmanuel Pregnon was injured during 11-on-11 and received treatment off to the side. He remained at practice but did not participate in any more team work. 
 S Preston Hodge intercepted QB Joey Aguilar and LB Ventrell Miller punched the ball away from RB Ameer Abdullah and recovered the fumble in 11-on-11 work. 
 The Jaguars will have a mock game on Friday morning at the team's practice facility. 
 

 

 Tuesday, Aug. 4 
 Very good day for the defense on Tuesday in the Jaguars' second day in full pads.

 Safeties Antonio Johnson and Eric Murray and cornerback Jarrian Jones intercepted passes, Jones broke up another in the end zone, and linebacker Branson Combs broke up a pass on the goal line. Cornerback Jabbar Muhammad also had tight coverage on Travis Hunter on a throw into the end zone and forced an incompletion.

 Johnson's interception came off Trevor Lawrence while Murray and Jones picked off Nick Mullens .

 More observations: 

 
 Hunter had 17 snaps (10 defense, 7 offense) in 11-on-11 work. He has totaled 86 snaps (51 defense, 35 offense) through six practices. 
 LB Jared Bartlett was taken off the field after suffering a leg injury, which leaves the team down two linebackers ( Jack Kiser suffered a right knee injury on the first day of camp). The team is also limiting  Foyesade Oluokun 's snaps in team work, so the Jaguars could be looking to add at that spot. 
 RB Chris Rodriguez Jr . did not participate in Tuesday's practice as part of the team's plan to ramp up his participation. Rodriguez, who missed almost all of the spring with a left foot injury, did participate in Monday's practice. 
 DE Arik Armstead had a veteran day off on Tuesday, his second of camp. 
 

 

 

 Monday, Aug. 3 
 Anton Harrison , who has started 48 games at right tackle since being drafted 27th overall in 2023, has spent the past three practices working at left tackle as part of the Jaguars' philosophy of cross-training offensive linemen.

 Coach Liam Coen didn't rule out that being a permanent change, though.

 "If that ends up sticking, then hopefully that's a good thing for us," Coen said after Monday's practice. "And I think he's put together five good practices so far that you're pleased with seeing the consistency."

 Monday's practice was the first in full pads and Harrison won all four of his one-on-one pass rush reps, including two against defensive end Josh Hines-Allen , the franchise's sack leader (61).

 Cole Van Lanen was the team's starting left tackle at the end of the 2025 season and the Jaguars signed him to three-year, $51 million extension in January. However, he has yet to practice because he's still recovering from a knee injury he suffered in the regular-season finale. He is expected to return at some point in camp.

 Walker Little  -- who lost the starting job at left tackle to Van Lanen last season -- had been the left tackle for the first two camp practices and is now working at right tackle.

 

 More observations: 

 
 WR Brian Thomas Jr . has followed up his impressive spring with a good start to camp. He had the play of the day on Monday with a one-handed catch down the sideline in 11-on-11. CB Montaric Brown had sticky coverage but Thomas grabbed Trevor Lawrence 's throw with his right arm while fending off Brown with his left. 
 Relatively quiet day for CB/WR Travis Hunter . He had 13 snaps in 11-on-11…

title: 2026 Kansas City Chiefs training camp: Latest intel, updates
summary: Follow our daily updates from Chiefs training camp, including intel on QBs, position battles and potential breakouts.
full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. The  Kansas City Chiefs ' camp is taking place at Missouri Western State University in St. Joseph, Missouri, and Chiefs reporter Nate Taylor has the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and, of course, the quarterbacks room.

 What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at Chiefs camp. We will update this file often. Can coach Andy Reid get the Chiefs back into the playoffs? Who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football? And which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Dive into all the updates and be sure to check back for more information until the first full week of the preseason begins Aug. 13.

 
 Camp updates for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 

 Latest news from Chiefs camp 
 
 Reid: Mahomes unlikely to play in preseason opener 
 Rookie wideout Cyrus Allen an early star of Chiefs training camp 
 Chiefs' Reid: Eric Bieniemy's wife out of ICU, 'doing great' 
 As training camp opens, Chiefs point to brighter future in 2026 
 
 

 Friday, Aug. 7 

 One player who is having a steady camp for the Chiefs is defensive end Felix Anudike-Uzomah , the team's 2023 first-round pick. For most of this week, Anudike-Uzomah has had his reps with the first-team defense, a result of him replacing Ashton Gillotte , who sustained a strained right hamstring in Monday's practice. Rushing from the left side, Anudike-Uzomah has had several strong 11-on-11 reps in which he has won the one-on-one battle with right tackle Kahlil Benson , an undrafted rookie out of Indiana.

 "His get-off is what jumps out to me," Reid said of Anudike-Uzomah. "He's bringing power with it. It's one thing to run around people, but there's a point, as a defensive end, you've got to physically blow things up a little bit. He's worked hard at that."

 Almost a year ago, the Chiefs had to place Anudike-Uzomah on season-ending injured reserve because of a strained right hamstring he sustained in the preseason -- an injury that required surgery. The Chiefs are hopeful that he can be a reliable contributor in the final year of his rookie contract.

 Anudike-Uzomah shared after Friday's practice that he believes he is the healthiest he's been since he entered the NFL.

 "I feel good, so I'm rolling," Anudike-Uzomah said. "I'm happy to work. Adversity happens with everybody. It's just how you respond."

 More observations: 

 
 Rookie receiver Cyrus Allen , who missed the past four practices with a left shin injury, returned to the field, but he was allowed to participate only in the individual period. "We're just easing him back in," Reid said. "He did a good job when he was out there, so that's a positive." 
 The players who missed Friday's on-field work were Gillotte, right guard Trey Smith (hip), cornerbacks Kristian Fulton (hip) and  L'Jarius Sneed  (rest), linebackers Drue Tranquill (lower back spasms) and Jeffrey Bassa (strained groin), defensive tackle Omarr Norman-Lott (right knee), and receiver Xavier Worthy (sprained right shoulder). "One positive about all these injuries is there's nothing that the guys aren't coming back from," Reid said. He later added of Smith: "We sent him to a specialist just to have it checked out. He's going to be OK." 
 

 

 Thursday, Aug. 6 

 The Chiefs had a light practice Thursday, the first such on-field work after three consecutive days in pads. The most significant change was that backup quarterback Justin Fields had his first 11-on-11 reps with the first-team offense, an indication that he might be the starter when the Chiefs have their preseason opener next Saturday against the Los Angeles Rams .

 "I've been learning a lot since I've been here and I'm excited to learn more, especially [coach Andy Reid] and [quarterback Patrick Mahomes ]," Fields said. "They definitely taught me a lot."

 Reid has yet to share if Mahomes, who has surgery in December to repair the torn ACL and LCL in his left knee, will be held out of the preseason, which would be a first in his 10-year career. During Thursday's practice, Fields spent time completing passes to running back Kenneth Walker III and receivers Rashee Rice , Tyquan Thornton and Andrew Armstrong .

 "I'm ready to get back on the field and in game mode, to be honest," Fields said. "It should be fun for the guys that are going to get out there and especially the rookies."

 

 Wednesday, Aug. 5 
 Rashee Rice , the Chiefs' No. 1 receiver, participated in 11-on-11 repetitions, a positive sign that his acclimation process is going well. In May, Rice underwent surgery on his right knee to remove loose debris that was causing inflammation. Since camp began, the Chiefs have been cautious with Rice's participation.

 Most of Rice's work was during the red zone period, where he had several short receptions, including a bubble screen on the perimeter and a touchdown in the back of the end zone. When Mahomes targeted Rice in the back corner of the end zone, Rice couldn't make a leaping, contested catch against cornerback Nohl Williams .

 It's clear Rice will need time to get into true football shape, as he showed fatigue before the long-drive drill, the final 11-on-11 repetitions. During that period, Rice was held out of the first-team offense's 12 repetitions.

 "He got a lot of good reps today, which is important," Reid said of Rice. "We've just got to ease him back in and just keep working. We know he's a good player. He actually got better as the practice went on, so that was a good thing."

 Other observations:  

 
 Linebacker Drue Tranquill missed his first practice of camp with lower back spasms. During the second half of Wednesday's work, Tranquill did some light strength work off the side with the training staff. 
 The other players who missed Wednesday's on-field session were cornerback Kristian Fulton (hip), linebacker Jeffrey Bassa (strained groin), defensive end Ashton Gillotte (strained right hamstring), defensive tackle Omarr Norman-Lott (right knee) and receivers Cyrus Allen (left shin) and Xavier Worthy (sprained right shoulder). 
 

 

 Tuesday, Aug. 4 

 For the second consecutive day in pads, Kahlil Benson , the undrafted rookie right tackle from Indiana, performed well, even better than Monday, after once again receiving all of the repetitions with the first-team offense.

 In the first 11-on-11 period, Benson showed strong run-blocking skills by executing a double-team to move defensive tackle Khyiris Tonga back. The repetition finished with Benson also blocking linebacker Nick Bolton , which created more space on the right side of the field for running back Kenneth Walker III . A few minutes later, Benson blocked defensive end Felix Anudike-Uzomah in pass protection for quarterback Patrick Mahomes to connect with receiver Tyquan Thornton for a completion for more than 30 yards.

 "He's done great," Walker said of Benson. "We've got pads on now and you get to see how well he's doing out there. He's going to have a great impact on this team."

 Benson's work, on the field and in meetings, has pushed him to have true competition with Jaylon Moore , the five-year veteran, for the starting right tackle role.

 In the final 11-on-11 period, Benson didn't lose any of the five repetitions with the first-team offense. His matchups included Anudike-Uzomah, pass rusher Chris Jones and rookie defensive end R Mason Thomas .

 "We'll give you a chance here to learn, but if you start making [mistakes] consistently, then we've got a problem," Reid said Monday of Benson. "But he's been doing a good job. There's a hiccup here or there, but he fixes them normally."

 More observations: 

 
 The players who missed Tuesday's practice were cornerback Kristian Fulton (hip), defensive end Ashton Gillotte (strained right hamstring), defensive tackle Omarr Norman-Lott (right knee) and…

title: Reid: Mahomes unlikely to play in Chiefs' preseason opener
summary: Although Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes has participated in every part of training camp, coach Andy Reid acknowledged Friday that he will likely not have him play in the team's preseason opener next week against the Rams.

title: 2026 Las Vegas Raiders training camp: Latest intel, updates
summary: Follow our daily updates from Raiders training camp, including intel on QBs, position battles and potential breakouts.
full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. The  Las Vegas Raiders  camp is taking place at Intermountain Health Performance Center in Henderson, Nevada, and Raiders reporter Ryan McFadden has the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and of course the quarterback room.

 What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at Raiders camp. We will update this file often. Who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football? And which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Dive in to all the updates and be sure to check back for more information until the first full week of the preseason begins Aug. 13.

 
 Camp updates for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 
 

 Latest news from Raiders camp 
 
 Maxx Crosby's approaching Raiders training camp with intensity 
 Three-time Pro Bowl guard Andrus Peat announces retirement 
 Cousins gets nod over Mendoza to open Raiders camp 
 What's next for Crosby, WR and CB rooms? 
 

 

 Friday, Aug. 7 
 Friday was an eventful morning at Raiders HQ.

 Las Vegas' eighth practice was highlighted by a scuffle between Maxx Crosby and Kirk Cousins . Other than that, both sides made plays throughout the team's third padded practice.

 Cousins was picked off twice in the red zone. First, Crosby disrupted Cousins' pass attempt, causing the ball to be picked off by safety Jeremy Chinn . On the following play, rookie cornerback Hezekiah Masses intercepted Cousins in the back corner of the end zone.

 Cousins responded well. He connected with tight ends  Michael Mayer  and Brock Bowers on a few big throws in the middle of the field. He was even efficient during the two-minute period near the end of practice, quickly moving the offense down the field into field-goal range.

 Rookie running back Mike Washington Jr . had an explosive run, in which he ran over cornerback Jermod McCoy and continued to sprint down the field for a big gain.

 Fernando Mendoza  was sharp. His performance was highlighted by a touchdown pass to wide receiver Deven Thompkins during the red zone period. Mendoza zipped the ball through tight coverage

 Other observations: 

 
 Wide receiver Jalen Nailor , defensive ends Kwity Paye and Keyron Crawford , tight end Carter Runyon and running back Dare Ogunbowale did not participate in practice. Second-year wide receiver  Dont'e Thornton Jr . left practice early, but coach Klint Kubiak didn't sound concerned about the various absences. With Nailor out, rookie wide receiver Malik Benson took the majority of the first-team reps on the opposite side of Tre Tucker . "We had a few guys nicked up, and we're trying to be cautious," Kubiak said. 
 Jackson Powers-Johnson and Caleb Rogers alternated first-team reps at right guard. Kubiak said it's a part of the plan the team has in place to figure out the best starting offensive line combination. Right guard has been the only position on the first-team offensive line that has had changes. 
 Kubiak clarified that he didn't take the coaching staff to drinks after the Baltimore Ravens backed out of a trade agreement for Crosby. Making a guest appearance on the "Ball in the Family" podcast, hosted by NBA player Lonzo Ball, Crosby recalled Kubiak called him and said the coaching staff was going to celebrate after the announcement was made. "He is in big trouble for revealing that," Kubiak jokingly said. "We haven't gone out as much as a staff. We have been grinding. We probably need to do that more." 
 

 

 Thursday, Aug. 6 

 Tight end Brock Bowers keeps stacking up good practices.

 On Thursday, Bowers was problematic for the defense and made one of the best plays since the start of camp. During 11-on-11, Bowers caught a deep touchdown pass from quarterback  Kirk Cousins , in which he slipped behind the defense and was left completely wide open near the sideline. Bowers stopped running his route and waited until Cousins launched the ball across the field.

 There were multiple occasions where Bowers beat out linebacker Quay Walker to make catches in the middle of the field.

 Outside of Bowers, it wasn't the best morning for the offense. There were quite a few inaccurate throws and dropped passes. Fernando Mendoza recorded his second interception of camp after his pass slipped through  Malik Benson 's hands and cornerback Darien Porter dove to make a catch.

 Aidan O'Connell  also recorded two interceptions.

 The offense didn't do much during the two-minute period. Cousins' pass to Tre Tucker was broken up by rookie cornerback Hezekiah Masses . Cornerback Eric Stokes broke up Cousins' throw to Benson. The offense was penalized twice during that period, as well.

 Other observations:  

 
 Rookie cornerback Jermod McCoy had a rest day and didn't participate in Thursday's practice. Tight end Michael Mayer returned after missing Tuesday's practice with a nose injury. 
 Defensive end Keyron Crawford left practice early after colliding with edge rusher Malcolm Koonce during the team period. Assistant head coach Mike McCoy did not have an update on the rookie's status. 
 The Raiders mixed things up with their starting offensive line for the first time. They had Caleb Rogers and Jackson Powers-Johnson alternate reps at right guard. 
 Rookie safety Treydan Stukes had his first reps with the starting defense. He had a nice pass breakup while working with the second team during the two-minute period. 
 

 

 Tuesday, Aug. 4 

 

 Through six practices, rookie wide receiver Malik Benson has made a strong case for meaningful snaps this fall.

 In a fairly thin wide receiver room, Benson has been a shining star, and that was the case on Tuesday. His and quarterback  Fernando Mendoza 's connection was on point. Mendoza repeatedly completed throws to Benson on crossing and comeback routes.

 During the one-on-one period, Benson matched up with fellow rookie cornerback Jermod McCoy on a few reps, in which the former Oregon pass catcher showed off his footwork and separation ability to make catches.

 Wide receivers Jalen Nailor and Tre Tucker are essentially options one and two in the room. Benson has emerged as WR3, outplaying Jack Bech and  Dont'e Thornton Jr . thus far. For wide receiver coach Zach Azzanni, the biggest improvement he has seen from Benson has been route running.

 "He's gotten a lot better at it," Azzanni said. "He's got a long way to go, but I'm pleased with where he's at because I knew he had the skill set to do it."

 Other observations: 

 
 Tight end Michael Mayer did not practice after injuring his nose on Monday. Mayer, who was not in uniform, observed practice from the sideline. Tight end Carter Runyon was also absent for the fourth straight practice. 
 Offensive line coach Rick Dennison believes starting right tackle DJ Glaze , who struggled last season, still has untapped potential. "He does have great length, and he uses his arm length well, and he's working really hard at it. He's made some progress," Dennison said. 
 Starting inside linebacker Nakobe Dean said his body feels great after not participating during OTAs and mandatory minicamp. He added that his decision to come to Las Vegas over the Dallas Cowboys was because of a "gut feeling" that the Raiders would be a better situation. 
 

 

 Monday, Aug. 3 
 Fernando Mendoza had an up-and-down practice Monday, but coach Klint Kubiak understands the rookie will not be perfect all the time.

 "There will never be a perfect game or practice," Kubiak said. "I think he is doing a good job. I don't expect him to be perfect right now."

 The lowlights of Mendoza's performance included a few off-target throws during the team period and the one-on-one period between defensive backs and wide receivers. In 11-on-11, Mendoza's pass to Malik Benson in the middle of the field was slightly high and put the rookie wide receiver in a bad position…

title: 2026 Miami Dolphins training camp: Latest intel, updates
summary: Follow our daily updates from Dolphins training camp, including intel on QBs, position battles and potential breakouts.
full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. The  Miami Dolphins  camp is taking place in Miami Gardens, and Dolphins reporter Marcel Louis-Jacques has the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and of course the quarterback room.

 What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at Dolphins camp. We will update this file often. Who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football? And which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Dive in to all the updates and be sure to check back for more information until the first full week of the preseason begins Aug. 13.

 
 Camp updates for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 

 Latest news from Dolphins camp 
 
 Dolphins top pick Proctor embracing NFL learning curve 
 Miami, All-Pro LB Jordyn Brooks reach 3-year, $51.3M extension 
 Dolphins, Aaron Brewer reach 3-year, $52.5 million extension 
 Why Miami's rookies can thrive 
 
 

 Friday, Aug. 7 
 Dolphins coach Jeff Hafley has stressed the importance of taking the ball away to his defense, and his players have responded with gusto this summer. Miami's defense recorded four interceptions during Friday's practice, including two by second-year cornerback Miles Battle -- both off quarterback Quinn Ewers . Linebacker Jackson Woodard continued his strong week of practice with a pick-six off quarterback Mark Gronowski , and UDFA safety Louis Moore added to his big play total with an interception as well.

 The Dolphins defense has forced multiple turnovers in nearly every practice this summer. It's a direct result of the team's coaching points on and off the field.

 "One of our assistant linebacker coaches, Wendel (Davis) -- he starts every meeting with taking the ball away," linebacker Tyrel Dodson said. "So he's made excellent emphasis on those takeaway points and we've honed in on it. We've studied different techniques, punching the ball out. Jacob (Rodriguez is) good at it. So we've studied the Peanut punch and all that stuff. So it's looking good."

 More observations: 

 
 Rookie wide receiver Caleb Douglas had an explosive play on a sideline ball from Malik Willis during team drills. The third-round pick appeared to get behind cornerback Jason Marshall Jr and picked up some yards after the catch. 
 Right tackle Austin Jackson returned to practice after missing the past two practices with an undisclosed injury. As a result, defensive end Chop Robinson didn't wreak the same level of havoc he did with Jackson sidelined, but it was a fun matchup to watch. 
 

 

 Thursday, Aug. 6 

 Pressure, pressure and more pressure was the key word for the Dolphins in Thursday's practice. The team shed its shoulder pads, looking to ease back into work following Wednesday's off day, but it didn't stop coach Jeff Hafley's defense from attacking its offensive counterparts throughout team drills.

 Linebacker Jackson Woodard was a constant presence around the ball, while defensive end Chop Robinson continued his strong camp -- albeit against a banged up right side of the Dolphins' offensive line. Thursday also marked another strong performance from rookie linebacker Jacob Rodriguez ; defensive coordinator Sean Duggan said he could tell the game is starting to slow down for Rodriguez and the other rookie linebackers, Kyle Louis and Trey Moore .

 More conversations: 

 
 Running back Jaylen Wright broke of a couple strong runs during team drills. Speaking to the media earlier this week, he sounded calm and at peace with his career to date and ready to attack the best opportunity he's had for regular playing time since entering the league in 2024. 
 Linebacker Willie Gay Jr . intercepted quarterback Cam Miller and returned it for a long gain. We've seen Gay stand out at training camp before, the Dolphins are hoping his momentum carries into game day this preseason, and the regular season. 
 

 

 Tuesday, Aug. 4 
 If you were building a basketball team out of Dolphins players, defensive tackle Zach Sieler -- all 6-foot-6, 300 pounds of him -- might be a choice at power forward. But coach Jeff Hafley said the nine-year veteran is actually more of a point guard on the team's defensive line.

 Despite his 25.5 sacks over the past three seasons, Hafley said Sieler's ability and willingness to take on blockers and open rush lanes for his teammates really pops on tape.

 When asked about the comparison after Tuesday's practice, Sieler said it all comes down to being selfless and a team player.

 "You've got to be a leader, you've got to be vocal -- but you can't be selfish," he said. "The better we do as a unit, the better we'll do as a team ... If someone's making plays one day and you're not, the plays will come. Don't stress, because when you stress and try to force a play, that's when bad things happen."

 More observations: 

 
 Defensive end Chop Robinson goes through stretches where he's simply unblockable -- his speed off the line of scrimmage has given the Dolphins' offensive tackles fits all summer, and continued to do so Tuesday. Fellow defensive end Josh Uche also had a pair of sacks in team drills. 
 Right tackle Austin Jackson , tight end Greg Dulcich and safety Lonnie Johnson Jr . did not participate in Tuesday's practice because of what Hafley described as "day to day" injuries. Neither player is expected to miss much time, but rookie UDFA DT Rene Konga will miss the entire season with an undisclosed injury suffered Monday. 
 Quarterback Malik Willis threw an interception to Zayne Anderson on the first play of the team's red-zone drill, but followed it up the next play with a touchdown pass to running back De'Von Achane . 
 

 

 
 Monday, Aug. 3 
 Malik Willis still isn't scrambling in team drills as the Dolphins want him to focus on making plays from the pocket in training camp, but he's displaying a keen ability to evade pressure and keep his eyes downfield.

 On multiple occasions during Monday's practice, Willis kept a play alive and found a receiver downfield. He spun away from pressure and found a wide open Malik Washington over the middle for an explosive gain, and lofted another off-platform throw to rookie tight end Seydou Traore -- who came down with a one-handed catch for a first down.

 Willis did throw an interception off a tipped pass, but the ball placement certainly could've been better. He also missed a throw to a wide open Caleb Douglas , who got hands on the ball but couldn't come down with it. But Willis has flashed some touch over the past few practices.

 More observations: 

 
 Linebacker Tyrel Dodson returned an interception for a touchdown in team drills, tracking the ball after it deflected off tight end Cole Turner 's hands. In Turner's defense, the ball from Willis was far too low. 
 Cornerback Ethan Bonner intercepted Quinn Ewers ' first pass of the team's game-winning drive drill, again off a deflected pass. 
 Both Willis and Ewers led their groups into field goal range during game-winning drive drills, and both kickers attempted field goals with each unit. Riley Patterson was good from 50 yards before missing from 43 yards, while Zane Gonzalez made both kicks. Both kickers were good from 52 yards on their third attempt. 
 Safety Lonnie Johnson Jr. appeared to suffer a lower body injury after thudding running back Jaylen Wright in team drills. He was attended to on the sideline and didn't return. 
 Tight end Greg Dulcich did not practice Monday for an unspecified reason, and the group's production tapered off without him. 
 Defensive end Chop Robinson blew by right tackle Charlie Heck on back-to-back plays to start the game-winning drill. The first one was credited as a sack, but Willis got the ball off just in time on the second play, hitting tight end Ben Sims over the middle for a first down. 
 

 
 Sunday, Aug. 2 
 The Dolphins' offense woke up in a major way…

title: 2026 Minnesota Vikings training camp: Latest intel, updates
summary: Follow our daily updates from Vikings training camp, including intel on QBs, position battles and potential breakouts.
full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. The Minnesota Vikings ' camp is taking place in Eagan, Minnesota, and Vikings reporter Kevin Seifert has the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and of course the quarterback room.

 What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at Vikings camp. We will update this file often. Who will win the starting quarterback battle between incumbent J.J. McCarthy and free agent addition Kyler Murray ? Who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football? And which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Dive in to all the updates and be sure to check back for more information until the first full week of the preseason begins Aug. 13.

 
 Camp updates for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 

 Latest Vikings stories 

 
 What McCarthy-Murray QB battle means for Vikings' locker room 
 Vikings, O'Neill reach $96M extension 
 Top Vikings storylines after minicamp, from QBs to new GM 
 Will Vikings start Caleb Banks, other rookies on defense? 
 Jefferson says decision on Vikings starting QB 'coach's call' 
 

 
 Friday, Aug. 7 
 NFL training camps can be tediously routine at times, but some days close observers can be surprised.

 Friday, the Vikings changed linebacker Jamal Adams ' jersey number from 54 to 32 and worked him in some of their safety specialty packages during full-team drills. Defensive coordinator Brian Flores is well known for experimenting with personnel during training camp, and it's quite possible that Adams could alternate between linebacker and safety.

 Two other safeties, Jay Ward and rookie Jakobe Thomas , did not appear to be taking part in team drills.

 According to NFL rules, linebackers can wear numbers between 1-59 (and also 90-99). But defensive backs can't wear numbers higher than 49, which necessitated Adams' number change.

 Adams was drafted as a safety by the Jets in 2017, but he moved to linebacker for the Raiders last season. The Vikings signed him on the eve of training camp.

 More observations: 

 
 Quarterback J.J. McCarthy had one of his better days of camp as the competition with Kyler Murray continued. McCarthy hit wide receiver  Dontae Fleming  on a deep out, a route McCarthy has excelled at this summer, and also threw three touchdowns in a four-play red zone sequence. 
 
 

 Wednesday, Aug.5 
 The Vikings haven't won a playoff game since 2019 and have three playoff victories in the past 25 seasons. So during his annual training camp meeting with reporters, co-owner/president Mark Wilf was asked about the patience his family has exhibited during its tenure as owners.

 "We try to be patient as an ownership, and that we know [leads to] ultimate success," he said. "But of course, patience isn't infinite. We understand that, but I feel really good about the direction of this football club and we're going to get to those benchmarks."

 Mark and Zygi Wilf hired general manager Nolan Teasley this spring to work with fifth-year coach Kevin O'Connell. Of their early interactions, Mark Wilf said: "I just think they work well together. I had an opportunity to watch them interact, and I just see how comfortable they are with each other. They have different characteristics but from my perspective, it's working well. And I think coach can focus on what he has to focus on. Nolan can focus on what he focuses on and they share and they collaborate and everyone in the building feels that."

 

 More observations: 

 
 Facing pressure during a two-minute drill, quarterback Kyler Murray made a smart decision: He lofted a jump ball for receiver Justin Jefferson . Predictably, Jefferson extended over cornerback Isaiah Rodgers and safety Theo Jackson to make the catch and scoot into the end zone. Murray also had a key scramble during the drill, keeping the drive alive. 
 Receiver Jordan Addison jammed his thumb Tuesday. O'Connell said tests revealed no serious injury. During practice, Addison was in full pads and ran routes during individual drills. But he did not have a pass thrown in his direction, and he worked out on a side field during team drills. 
 

 

 Tuesday, Aug. 4 

 As members of the 2023 draft class begin getting contract extensions, Vikings receiver Jordan Addison  said Tuesday that he is focused on "being where my feet are."

 Four receivers were drafted between picks No. 20-23 that year, and two of them -- Seattle's Jaxon Smith-Njigba and Baltimore's Zay Flowers -- have agreed to new deals. Addison and the Vikings have had to navigate two arrests and one citation during his time in the NFL, and Addison said: "I'm just putting in the work in right now, going through camp, making sure I'm becoming a better receiver, and I feel like everything is going to take care of itself."

 Addison leads the 2023 class with 22 career touchdown receptions. He ranks eighth with 175 receptions and fourth with 2,396 receiving yards.

 "He loves football," Vikings coach Kevin O'Connell said. "He's a great teammate. Clearly he was a young player when he came into the NFL. I think he's learned, matured and he knows exactly what's out in front of him. He knows what's important to him. I'm proud of his growth and development in that phase as well and I think there's a lot of folks in this building that deeply, deeply care about Jordan and what's best for him on and off the field moving forward, and you can count me as one of them."﻿

 More observations: 

 
 The Vikings had a relatively light practice Tuesday in shells, one day after their first full-pads practice of summer. Quarterback J.J. McCarthy elicited murmurs from fans in the stands after overthrowing three consecutive passes in the red zone against no defense, but he came back later with two strong throws on deep outs to receivers  Myles Price  and Dontae Fleming . 
 

 

 Monday, Aug. 3 
 Neither Kyler Murray nor J.J. McCarthy took a step forward Monday during the fifth practice -- and first in full pads -- of their competition to win the Minnesota Vikings ' starting quarterback job. The pair roughly split first-team snaps during 11-on-11 team drills, with Murray getting 10 and McCarthy eight.

 Murray found Justin Jefferson crossing across the field after evading the pass rush, but he also threw high over the middle to receiver Jordan Addison . On the play, Addison and cornerback Isaiah Rodgers collided in the air, flipping Anderson and sending Rodgers sprawling.

 The practice ended with a rough two-minute sequence for both quarterbacks. In five snaps, McCarthy went 0-for-3 with two tipped passes and an interception on a throw to Jefferson that cornerback Byron Murphy Jr . stepped in front of. Murray took over for two snaps with the second team, going 0-for-2 with a pass behind tight end Josh Oliver on the first and a miscommunication on the second.

 More observations from the day: 

 
 
 Receiver Tai Felton , a third-round draft pick in 2025, made the catch of camp in 7-on-7 drills, leaping high to grab a Murray pass in the back corner of the end zone. Felton has been working as the No. 4 receiver behind Justin Jefferson, Jordan Addison and Jauan Jennings .

 
 
 Cornerback James Pierre returned to practice after sitting out at the end of last week. Rookie running back Demond Claiborne was in full pads but worked out on a side field for players who are rehabilitating injuries."

 
 

 

 Saturday, Aug. 1 
 Quarterback Kyler Murray had by far his best day of training camp Saturday, pinpointing a series of downfield throws in traffic while taking the majority of the Vikings' first-team reps as his competition with J.J. McCarthy continues.

 Murray was on the field for 16 of the first-team offense's 22 snaps in 11-on-11 team drills. McCarthy took the other six. Murray hit receiver Justin Jefferson on a deep dig route over the middle and he threw another…

title: Latest buzz on Vikings' Kyler Murray-J.J. McCarthy QB1 battle
summary: Here is the latest buzz on how  Kyler Murray and J.J. McCarthy have performed in their competition to lead Minnesota's offense.
full_text:
EAGAN, Minn. -- As promised, the Minnesota Vikings have split snaps between quarterbacks Kyler Murray and J.J. McCarthy through the first seven practices of training camp as part of a declared competition. Beneath the surface, however, daily observers have seen plenty of indications that Murray remains the heavy favorite to win the job. 

 Both quarterbacks have produced strong and weak moments over roughly 300 snaps during 7-on-7 and 11-on-11 drills, and each has spent time with the first and second teams. In theory, there is enough time for McCarthy to launch a late run. There have been only two padded practices so far and there will be six more days of on-field work before the Vikings' first preseason game.

 

 But the Vikings have given Murray roughly two-thirds of the snaps with the first-team offense in 11-on-11 drills, a rate that might not carry much meaning for a single practice but is a clear pattern over the course of a week, and he has used them productively. The imbalance can partially be explained by Murray's relative inexperience in the offense, and the need to get him up to speed. But unless it reverses in the coming week, it is hard to imagine McCarthy -- or any player at any position -- winning the job while spending the majority of the most important snaps of camp with the second team. 

 Instead, McCarthy has spent a significant portion of his summer working with the No. 2 offense but against the No. 1 defense. It is a challenging spot but one that NFL coaches have long used to spur development from young players. His passes have skewed more toward the short-range and midrange variety, with less frequent deep attempts than Murray.

 And coincidentally or otherwise, the Vikings have been experimenting with more shotgun and pistol handoffs than they have used in the recent past, particularly in the run game. The Vikings have been the NFL's third-heaviest under-center team in the NFL (47%) during coach Kevin O'Connell's tenure, while Murray's Arizona Cardinals used it at the league's third-lowest rate (18.3%) over his previous seven seasons. 

 During a recent visit with reporters, O'Connell praised both quarterbacks and cautioned against a search for tendencies to their deployment. He did, however, say Murray has "shown improvement every single day" and said it was clear that Murray worked hard to study the offense during his summer break. O'Connell said he was encouraged that Murray has hit some downfield throws but added: "We're just trying to implement our offense. We're trying to really focus on some foundational things that the quarterbacks play a big role in, but it's an all-11 thing right now for sure, regardless of what personnel grouping we're in."

 Let's take a closer look. 

 

 

 Kyler Murray 

 Two factors prompted the initial assessment that Murray was the favorite to win the job. 

 First, Murray was a top-15 quarterback in the NFL during his time with the Cardinals, based on combined QBR of players with enough action plays to qualify. He was not a superstar, but he had established a clear baseline performance, even if he hadn't played in the exact offense O'Connell runs. The amount of ground that McCarthy would have to make up to match Murray's baseline, based on McCarthy's performance in 2025, was substantial.

 Second, the Vikings had already fired general manager Kwesi Adofo-Mensah, who drafted McCarthy. That meant Murray would not need to overcome any organizational inertia that might have favored McCarthy, whom the Vikings used the No. 10 draft pick to select in 2024. 

 Both factors have featured prominently this summer.

 Murray has had his share of the kind of miscommunications that would be expected for a quarterback in a new offense, including several throws that didn't match with the receivers' route. One of them, at the end of a rough two-minute drill Monday, prompted O'Connell to end the practice early. 

 But there have been no indications that Murray is fundamentally uncomfortable with or incapable of what the Vikings have asked him to do, either to the naked eye or in discussions behind the scenes. 

 He has found receiver Justin Jefferson on a series of deep crossing routes, while Jauan Jennings and Tai Felton have caught touchdowns on deep posts, and he has demonstrated a level of touch, arc and accuracy that McCarthy is still working to master. 

 Some might have winced at the jump ball Murray threw toward Jefferson and into double coverage during a two-minute drill Wednesday. But Jefferson jumped over cornerback Isaiah Rodgers and safety Theo Jackson to make the catch, a reminder that some receivers merit riskier throws than others. 

 

 In short, Murray has performed at the level to be expected from a quarterback with his performance profile, within the context of adapting to an entirely new offense. That assessment matches the expectations he expressed when camp first began.

 "I feel great," Murray said July 29. "Really helped me going through OTAs for sure. Having done it once now, obviously this time it's about to be real, but I truly believe that going through OTAs has prepared me for what's to come."

 

 J.J. McCarthy 

 McCarthy has not appeared as frenetic as he did during his worst moments of last season and clearly has a full understanding of the offense. In retrospect, however, the expectation he set out during his own July 29 meeting with reporters has proved prescient.

 Speaking about his pre-camp discussions with O'Connell, McCarthy said: "Conversations were great. Just all about doing my job and doing it to the best of my ability, taking completions, taking what the defense is giving me, making smart decisions, and at the end of the day, just doing my job. Very simple."

 McCarthy's time in full team drills has been notable for the number of occasions that appear designed to get him into a rhythm with a bootleg or another quick, short-range pass. They represent many of his completions over the first week, although one of his interceptions came when linebacker Jake Golday tipped a short pass McCarthy threw while on the run.

 

 McCarthy has thrown some well-placed deep-corner or out routes to receivers Dontae Fleming and Myles Price , but overall his accuracy has been inconsistent. 

 Some of his passes over the middle have appeared late or slightly off target and resulted in incompletions. Earlier in the two-minute drill that O'Connell eventually ended early, cornerback Byron Murphy Jr . stepped in front of a pass to Jefferson on a crossing route for an interception.

 Tuesday, he overthrew three consecutive passes during a red zone period against air -- with no defenders in the drill. On the first, veteran running back Aaron Jones Sr . launched himself into a full-body dive to get closer to the ball but could not make the catch. 

 Reasonable people can argue about exactly where McCarthy is on his developmental timeline. But no objective observer to training camp could say that he has made up the ground necessary to truly challenge Murray. 

 

 Scheme 

 Murray began his time as an NFL quarterback in a shotgun-based Air Raid offense similar to what he used in college. His relative inexperience beginning a play under center, which O'Connell has used in part to build play-action concepts that set up downfield throws, has been cited as one of Murray's potential roadblocks to success in Minnesota. 

 

 But Murray is not the only newcomer to the Vikings' offense. O'Connell hired assistant head coach Frank Smith in part to help diversify his running game, and the frequency with which the Vikings have at least practiced running out of spread formations has been notable. Murray has displayed no observable difficulties under center, and offensive coordinator Wes Phillips said this week that Murray has proved to be "very comfortable playing any which way you want him to play football."

title: 2026 New England Patriots training camp: Latest intel, updates
summary: Follow our daily updates from Patriots training camp, including intel on QBs, position battles and potential breakouts.
full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. The New England Patriots ' camp is taking place in Foxborough, Massachusetts, and Patriots reporter Mike Reiss has the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and, of course, the quarterback room.

 What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at Patriots camp. We will update this file often. Will Drake Maye  start another MVP-like campaign in Year 3? Who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football? And which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Dive into all the updates and be sure to check back for more information until the first full week of the preseason begins Aug. 13.

 
 Camp updates for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 

 Latest news from Patriots camp 
 
 A.J. Brown on injury: 'Thumb out of place, you keep going' 
 Patriots' Brown knows Vrabel's rip comes from 'great place' 
 Kraft: Patriots' Gonzalez has offer to be 'highest-paid' CB ever 
 Too many receivers? A look at the Patriots' crowded WR room 
 
 
 

 Friday, Aug. 7 
 A.J. Brown shared part of what has made his first training camp with the New England Patriots unique from his prior seven NFL seasons.

 "This is my first time going against a defense on a day-to-day basis where the mentality has [picked] up. I believe we need to go against somebody else because we're right at the edge. And that's good for a team, that's really good for a team, but that mentality on both sides of going back and forth, we're toeing that line," he said Friday.

 "That's why I think we're going to be excited for the Colts coming up."

 The Patriots held their 12th practice Friday in humid, 90-degree temperatures, and it featured an intrasquad scrimmage heading into an off weekend. Brown was on the same team as cornerback Christian Gonzalez , which turned down the heat on easily the team's most intense 1-on-1 matchup in camp.

 On Thursday, the two almost needed to be separated after a drill in which Gonzalez had lockdown coverage on Brown, and Gonzalez seemed to be trash-talking in his direction.

 "Every day is a battle with him. It's nothing but respect," Brown said. "Ultimately it's not about me and him. We're competing, all of us are challenging each other, for the greater good of the team."

 For his part, Brown said he's focusing on "crafting" in practice, and if he's doing any talking on the field, it's only to himself. He believes his matchups with Gonzalez have "absolutely" set a tone for the team, which now looks ahead to welcoming the Colts for a practice next Tuesday leading into Thursday's preseason opener.

 "The defense has not been giving us any leeway, and we're not trying to give them any leeway as well," he said. "We're both pushing ourselves."

 More observations: 

 
 Fourth-year WR Pop Douglas had two TD catches in the scrimmage and also hauled in a deep pass from backup QB Tommy DeVito . He looked like the offense's most productive player. 
 DeVito was celebrating his 28th birthday, and as he was signing autographs after a practice in which he looked in command, fans sang to him at the urging of his agent, Sean Stellato. 
 QB Drake Maye had touchdown throws to WR Romeo Doubs (returning after missing two days) and RB TreVeyon Henderson . Maye led a successful two-minute drill to set up a field goal to end practice, which was notable after struggles the day prior in the same situation (2 INTs). 
 One play that got a rise out of the crowd came when rookie QB Behren Morton fired a pass along the left sideline to WR Tejhaun Palmer , and the ball somehow ended up in the hands of RB Myles Montgomery , who had been sprinting up that sideline. The play went for a gain of 40-plus yards. 
 Coach Mike Vrabel served as referee for the scrimmage. He assigned assistants Terrell Williams and Tony Dews as head coaches, Todd Downing and Ashton Grant as offensive coordinators, and Scott Booker and Justin Hamilton as defensive coordinators. 
 Coaches held a draft to split the team up, with Vrabel saying he had just two stipulations -- Maye had to be paired with C Jared Wilson , and WRs Mack Hollins and  Efton Chism III  couldn't be split up (a playful acknowledgement to how close they've become). 
 Starting LT Will Campbell , who wore a brace on his left arm/elbow Thursday, did not participate in the scrimmage, but Vrabel said he expects him back after the weekend. First-round pick Caleb Lomu got some work at LT after spending the majority of camp at RT. 
 Vrabel said it would likely be another week before starting CB Carlton Davis III returns. Davis appeared to injure his hamstring July 28. 
 

 

 
 Thursday, Aug. 6 
 Cornerback Christian Gonzalez and receiver A.J. Brown needed to be separated at one point of Thursday's practice, as the competitive one-on-one matchup between them that has been a highlight of Patriots training camp nearly boiled over.

 The fireworks seemed to be sparked by Gonzalez's trash talk following a red zone drill in which his tight coverage held Brown without a catch. As the Patriots transitioned to a different period of practice, Gonzalez appeared to be chirping in Brown's direction. At first, Brown was walking away, but something appeared to spark him to turn back in Gonzalez's direction.

 Receiver Kayshon Boutte also came over to that area of the sideline and said he was trying to pull Brown away from Gonzalez. Boutte said he heard someone say, "You're a grown man!"

 The battle between Gonzalez and Brown seemed to build throughout the full-pads practice, with Gonzalez gesturing in Brown's direction after covering him tightly in 11-on-11 drills as a long pass from quarterback Drake Maye in that direction was incomplete.

 In the final drill, Brown caught a comeback route on Gonzalez.

 "It's good on good. He's a No. 1 receiver in this league going up against a No. 1 corner. That's how it's going to go," Gonzalez said after practice. "It's football at the end of the day. There's never no disrespect or anything. We're just battling to make each other better.

 "He's going to face corners like that, that are going to yap at him and try to get in his head. And I'm going to face receivers like that, that are strong and are going to come right back at me. It's great work for the both of us."

 

 More observations: 

 
 The practice ended with three straight interceptions as the offense was in a game-ending situation running the two-minute offense. CB Marcus Jones and S Kevin Byard picked off Maye, while S John Saunders Jr. picked off backup QB Tommy DeVito . Coach Mike Vrabel called the team together at that point and ended practice. 
 Starting LT Will Campbell didn't participate in team drills, which thrust 2025 seventh-round pick Marcus Bryant into the top unit over 2026 first-round pick Caleb Lomu . That is due, in part, to Lomu mostly having worked at right tackle. 
 Rookie OLB Gabe Jacas (second round, Illinois) received his first reps with the top defense. 
 With no wind, high humidity and temperatures in the 90s, this was the hottest day of the Patriots' 11 training camp practices. 
 CB Carlton Davis III , WR Cameron Dorner , WR Romeo Doubs and FB Jack Westover did not practice, while starting DT Christian Barmore , top reserve CB Charles Woods and rookie OLB Quintayvious Hutchins left early. 
 Rookie QB Behren Morton (seventh round, Texas Tech) had a surprise waiting for him upon his arrival at practice, as his parents James and Suni made the trip to town from Texas. 
 Third-unit G Caedan Wallace returned to practice. 
 The Patriots had free agent guard Greg Van Roten in for a workout. Guard depth is thin/unproven with Andrew Rupcich (left) and James Hudson III (right) the top backups in practice, while backup C Ben Brown would likely get the first call in the event of injury.

 If the Patriots are indeed…

title: 2026 New York Giants training camp: Latest intel, updates

full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. The New York Giants camp is taking place at The Greenbrier in White Sulphur Springs, West Virginia, and Giants reporter Jordan Raanan has the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and, of course, the quarterbacks room.

 What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at Giants camp. We will update this file often. How will the Giants handle increased expectations and a new coach? Who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football? And which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Dive in to all the updates and be sure to check back for more information until the first full week of the preseason begins Aug. 13.

 
 Camp updates for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 

 Latest news from Giants camp 
 
 Cam Skattebo admits doing 'dumb things,' will save backflips for TDs 
 Nabers 'looked good' in 1st practice since knee injury 
 Giants have spoken with Skattebo after Fanatics Fest flip 
 2026 New York Giants training camp preview 
 

 

 Friday, Aug. 7 
 Wide receiver Malik Nabers looked the best he has this summer during individual drills Friday. He continues to get better -- making sharper cuts, jumping and landing on the affected leg and running crisper routes as he rebounds from a knee injury .

 

 Coach John Harbaugh said he noticed this was the best version of Nabers, who is getting to the final stages of recovery. The next step is for Nabers to "work his way back into practice more and more."

 The expectation seems to be that Nabers will return to live team drills in the next couple of weeks. That would have him trending to be ready for Week 1 against the Cowboys.

 "[Return to play coordinator Allison Boudreau] is working with him, and she's been working on situations where you're off-balance, landing off-balance and unpredictable type situations that you're going to get rather than just doing normal rehab and then getting out there and all of a sudden being surprised by the awkwardness of football," Harbaugh said. "Try to create that as much as you can in a controlled setting."

 More observations: 

 
 The offense had perhaps its best day of camp. On its final drive, the unit went the length of the field with tight end Theo Johnson and running back Dante Miller each making multiple receptions. The series concluded with a 2-yard touchdown from quarterback  Jaxson Dart to wide receiver  Darius Slayton . Dart finished 16-of-19 passing on the day. 
 Malachi Fields on the offense: "It just keeps building over time. We've had almost two weeks now, just getting together, so I think we'll just keep jelling, keep clicking, and we'll just keep building that confidence as we go into the preseason." 
 Cam Skattebo left practice early after stretching out his left leg. Harbaugh described the issue as "working through the football shape part" and didn't think it was serious. C  John Michael Schmitz Jr . left after getting his "bell rung" and is being evaluated, while OLB Brian Burns continues to nurse a minor ankle injury. 
 
 
 Thursday, Aug. 6 
 The Giants shed the pads after three straight days of full contact. Coach John Harbaugh ran a 2½-hour walk-through to give his players' bodies some rest.

 They'll be back at it Friday and Saturday with full padded practices before leaving West Virginia.

 Harbaugh has run a hard training camp to date. The Giants ran over 100 live plays in the heat Wednesday. It has been in stark contrast to the training camps they had under Brian Daboll.

 But the Giants knew this was going to be the case. Harbaugh is known to run a tough camp. Even his practices in the spring don't waste time and have a lot of live periods.

 "Man, it's tough, gritty," cornerback Greg Newsome II said. "We're going to work, and I like that. There's no off days for us in terms of not competing. He's going to make sure we compete. We're always doing situational football and things like that. So, it's been super fun to play. He's a great coach. We're always talking all the time and I'm super excited to play for him."

 More observations:  

 
 CB Dru Phillips has a mild knee sprain and will miss some time. CB Jarrick Bernard-Converse also didn't practice again and is dealing with an "ongoing" knee problem. Harbaugh said the Giants might sign another cornerback. 
 Jaxson Dart doesn't seem too worried about the offense despite the early inconsistency. "We're taking steps each day," he said. "Obviously there are thing that you go out there and maybe it's our first time running something and you have things to talk through. A lot of times we'll have the opportunity the next day to go out there and try to fix it and run it again. So I think the really good thing I'm seeing about our offense is the communication after practices to be able to fix the adjustments the next day. That's really encouraging to see." 
 
 

 

 Wednesday, Aug. 5 

 It was another up and down day for the Giants' offense. It really has been the story of training camp in West Virginia.

 Quarterback Jaxson Dart and Co. were pedestrian again on Wednesday, even against the second-team defense. He threw a pair of interceptions early, before tossing three touchdown passes and rushing for two more in red-zone drills.

 Coach John Harbaugh thought it was a good response after Dart let the frustration get the best of him one day earlier.

 "The football response absolutely was there. Yeah, he stepped up," Harbaugh said. "A lot of third down stuff we did. Fourth down stuff, fourth down in the red zone to win the game, things like that.

 "Yeah, he had a heck of a practice. It was impressive."

 Dart and the first-team offense have yet to fully hit their stride this summer. And there are some built-in excuses. Dart is learning a new offense. He's also without his No. 1 receiver in Malik Nabers , who still isn't taking part in team drills as he recovers from a knee injury. Still, it would be nice to see them put together a complete practice before leaving West Virginia.

 More observations: 

 
 Second day in a row Odell Beckham Jr . had a strong practice. This time he had four catches in live drills. He continues to get open and make it a tough decision for the Giants whether to find a roster spot for the veteran receiver. 
 Outside linebacker Brian Burns , wide receiver Malachi Fields and safety Beau Brade all sat out Wednesday's practice with what Harbaugh called "minor" deals. Wide receiver JuJu Smith-Schuster (knee swelling) returned to practice after sitting out the previous day. 
 Rookie Dominic Zvada went a perfect 10 of 10 kicking field goals. He's now 28 of 31 on field goals at training camp and has to be the leader in the clubhouse to be the Giants' kicker this season. 
 The Giants signed two players: CBs D.J. Jones and David Long. In order to make room, they waived wide receiver Beaux Collins with an injury designation after he was banged up this week and placed defensive lineman Roy Robertson-Harris on injured reserve after tearing an Achilles in the spring. That ends Robertson-Harris' season with the Giants. 
 
 

 Tuesday, Aug. 4 
 In his quest to make the roster, Tuesday was an important practice for Odell Beckham Jr . For the first time this summer he worked with the first-team offense for most of the day.

 Beckham caught a pair of passes and had another would've-been touchdown grab in a strong performance.

 Beckham worked alongside Darnell Mooney and Braxton Berrios on a day when Darius Slayton and Malachi Fields seemed to have their workloads limited. Malik Nabers continues to participate in individual drills but mostly stands around and watches when the team breaks into live periods.

 "Just probably worked out that way [Tuesday]," coach John Harbaugh said of Beckham working with the first team. "He ... I don't know, worked out that way."
