title: 2026 New York Jets training camp: Latest intel, updates
summary: Follow our daily updates from Jets training camp, including intel on QBs, position battles and potential breakouts.
full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. The  New York Jets  camp is taking place at the Atlantic Health Training Facility in Florham Park, New Jersey, and Jets reporter Rich Cimini has the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and of course the quarterback room.

 What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at Jets camp. We will update this file often. Who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football, and which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Dive in to all the updates and be sure to check back for more information until the first full week of the preseason begins Thursday.

 
 Camp updates for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 

 Latest news from Jets camp 
 
 Rookie TE Kenyon Sadiq to miss time after hernia setback 
 Jets' Smith rues being 'distraction' after dispute with girlfriend 
 2026 Jets training camp preview 
 
 

 Friday, Aug. 7 
 

 Geno Smith has a big fan in offensive coordinator Frank Reich, who gushed about his starting quarterback after a sweltering practice.

 "He's a leader of the offense and, make no mistake about it, in every way, shape and form," Reich said. "To me, what has come crystal clear ... the attribute that sticks out to me is his laser focus. This man is laser focused like people don't understand. He comes to work. He comes to work, and he is locked in. And I feel like the whole offense plays off of that. That's a big deal."

 Smith is having a solid camp. He delivered another strong practice (8-for-12 in team drills), hooking up five times with WR Garrett Wilson . August optimism is nice; the bottom line is how the player performs in September and beyond.

 Reich praised Smith's upper-body throwing mechanics, calling them "pure."

 "There's only a couple guys in the league that I would say are pure. Geno's one of them," said Reich, adding that Smith, 35, from a physical standpoint, looks like a 28-year-old.

 Smith has always thrown a pretty ball. The key is eliminating negative plays. He has more interceptions (52) and more sacks (182) than any QB over the past four seasons.

 Other observations: 

 
 The front office has to feel good about the Breece Hall contract extension (three years, $43.5 million) in May. At the time, his average per year ($14.5 million) ranked fourth among running backs. The market has exploded in recent days with extensions for Bijan Robinson , Jonathan Taylor and Jahmyr Gibbs . Hall now ranks eighth in APY. "Man, am I glad we got that done," said Reich, calling Hall a "phenomenal" player. It pays to be proactive. 
 In keeping with the load-management theme to camp, LB Demario Davis , S Minkah Fitzpatrick and DT Harrison Phillips received veteran rest days on Friday. Davis still managed to get involved. During a brief break in the action, he ran out on the field, into the huddle, and gave some quick words to the defense. 
 Coaches never want to see players get hurt, but T'Vondre Sweat 's hamstring injury has opened the door for rookie DT Darrell Jackson Jr . to get reps with the starters. 
 Backup LB Kiko Mauigoa is looking forward to facing his brother, Francis Mauigoa , in the preseason. Mauigoa, a 2026 first-round pick, is slated to start at right guard for the Giants, so the two brothers could cross paths on the field. The family will have to make a decision during the regular season: Whose game will it attend? "I told them, 'We have one home stadium, so they can come every Sunday,'" Kiko said with a laugh. 
 

 

 Thursday, Aug. 6 

 Quarterbacks always wear a red jersey in practice. Geno Smith is taking the red thing to a new level.

 Red contact lenses.

 To reduce the glare on the field, Smith is wearing the red lenses for the first time in his career. They were quite apparent during his weekly news conference, with one reporter joking that the red-eye look was scary.

 "It's actually pretty cool," Smith said. "It blocks out the sunlight and all that, so it's actually pretty cool. It keeps the glare from the sun out of your eyes."

 Smith's former Jets teammate Santonio Holmes, a wide receiver, was known for wearing red contact lenses more than a decade ago. Smith got the idea from Holmes but didn't go red until he consulted recently with eye specialists, who signed off on the idea.

 "It's just something we're trying out, just to see what it's like," Smith said. "I like it, so we've been sticking with it."

 Even though his eyes look red, he's not seeing that way.

 "The entire room is yellow, so it's a yellow tint to everything," Smith said. "But yeah, it's pretty cool. You guys should try it."

 Smith, who threw a league-high 17 interceptions last season for the Las Vegas Raiders , is trying to reboot his career with the team that drafted him in 2013. So far, so good. Teammates and coaches have been impressed with his command of the offense and willingness to take chances downfield.

 His goal is to make opposing defenses see red.

 Other observations:  

 
 Rookie TE Kenyon Sadiq , who suffered a setback in his recovery from hernia surgery, will miss "a couple of weeks," coach Aaron Glenn said. Glenn called it "pretty good news." This was more detail than he provided Tuesday, when he said Sadiq would be sidelined for "a little bit." Glenn reiterated that Sadiq, the second of three first-round picks, will be ready for Week 1. 
 Backup RB Isaiah Davis will miss at least two weeks with a "minor" knee injury, according to Glenn. It should be more reps for Kene Nwangwu , who probably will make the team because of his kick return ability. CB Nahshon Wright has a hip strain. Rookie CB D'Angelo Ponds (calf strain) is close to returning. 
 Rookie QB Cade Klubnik was shaky on Thursday, going 1-for-5 in team drills -- most of which were in the red zone. He was intercepted by backup LB Mykal Walker . This was the second time in camp that the former Clemson star struggled in the red zone. He's been solid in the other practices. 
 One under-the-radar player is former New York Giants S Dane Belton , who made three forced fumbles and one interception last season. The coaches love his ball production. Belton, who came over on a one-year, $4 million contract, is pushing Andre Cisco for a starting job. "No matter where I'm at," Belton said, "I can make plays and help the team." 
 

 

 Tuesday, Aug. 4 

 For months, the Jets have been boasting about their tight-end depth. They will get a chance to show it off in the coming weeks.

 First-round pick Kenyon Sadiq suffered a setback from May hernia surgery and will be sidelined "a little bit," according to coach Aaron Glenn.

 Translation: He probably will miss at least a chunk of the preseason, affording more opportunities for Mason Taylor , Jeremy Ruckert and Jelani Woods .

 Ruckert capitalized Tuesday, making a team-high four receptions in practice. It was a mixed day for Taylor, who had one catch and one drop. He also was the targeted receiver on a Geno Smith pass that was intercepted.

 "I see him breaking out this year," Glenn said of Taylor, a 2025 second-round pick who made a team-high 44 receptions for 369 yards last season.

 The Jets surprised the draft world when they picked Sadiq 16th overall, one year after taking Taylor. Ruckert was a 2022 third-round pick. Yes, they've invested heavily at tight end.

 This year's plan is to use more two-tight end packages, integrating Sadiq's elite speed and versatility into the offensive equation. Those plans will be on hold. While the Jets are "very confident" that Sadiq will be back for Week 1, per Glenn, they will have to adjust on the fly with Taylor, Ruckert and Woods.

 Other observations: 

 
 The starting defense made an interception for the second day in a row. This time it was CB Brandon Stephens , who snared a Smith pass that was deflected downfield. After going interception-less for the…

full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. Who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football? And which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Dive in to all the updates and be sure to check back for more information until the first full week of the preseason begins Aug. 13.

 
 Camp updates for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 

 Latest Eagles news 
 
 Epenesa grateful to be Eagle after 'weird' Browns situation 
 Eagles' Nolan Smith apologizes for 'unacceptable' speeding arrest 
 Eagles, DT Carter agree to four-year, $152M extension 
 Eagles coach Nick Sirianni adjusting to offseason changes 
 
 
 Friday, Aug. 7 
 Right tackle Lane Johnson returned following a four-practice absence for personal reasons. Johnson was originally scheduled to speak after Friday's practice but will likely now talk Saturday, the team said. He was a limited participant as he reacclimates to the grind.

 
"He has a calming presence," defensive tackle Jordan Davis  said of Johnson. "One day, I'm not going to be able to say that I have him in the locker room. It's just very good to have him out here. Everybody knows he's a baller, man. He's a f---ing baller. Lane, man, he's a cornerstone."

 
Rookie Markel Bell continued to get first-team reps at right tackle during team drills. Center Cam Jurgens spent time in the medical tent before heading indoors. Jake Majors took over at center in his absence.

 Other observations:  

 
 The defensive line made life tough for the short-handed offensive front. Jalen Carter ripped past Majors with a swim move to shut down a would-be passing play for Jalen Hurts . He later rose up to deflect a throw. Davis blew up a play in the backfield earlier in the session. 
 Second-year receiver Darius Cooper is making a push for a roster spot. He has enjoyed a strong camp, and that continued Friday with a number of catches, including one from Hurts over the middle with Quinyon Mitchell in coverage. 
 Tanner McKee had perhaps his best day of the summer. He hit Cooper on consecutive attempts before tossing one into the right corner of the end zone for the 6-foot-6 Johnny Wilson , who rose to snag the pass with corner Jonathan Jones nearby. McKee and Andy Dalton continue to split second-team reps. 
 Receivers DeVonta Smith and Makai Lemon missed their third straight practice with hamstring injuries. 
 New Sixer Jaylen Brown visited training camp. He chopped it up with coach Nick Sirianni, Hurts and Smith, among others, and got a nice ovation from the fans as he walked by. 
 Hurts turned 28 on Friday. The whole team sang "Happy Birthday" to him when they huddled after practice. 
 
 
 Wednesday, Aug. 5 
 The Jalen Hurts - Dontayvion Wicks connection continues to shine. The highlight Wednesday came during 7-on-7s with Hurts tossing a precision pass deep down the left sideline for Wicks, who corralled it with defensive backs Jonathan Jones and Andre Sam bearing down on him. Hurts said Wicks was "trying to beat down the door" this offseason to get extra reps in with him and complimented his attack mindset.

 "When you talk about adversity, you learn a lot about the guys around you this time of camp. It's humid, it's sticky, it's hot. You see who's got that anger to them, who's got a little bit of rage in them -- for the best," Hurts said. "He's got it. That's exciting to see."

 

 Other observations:  

 
 Eagles receivers DeVonta Smith and Makai Lemon both missed practice due to hamstring injuries for a second straight day. Right tackle Lane Johnson was absent for the fourth straight practice for personal reasons. 
 The linebacker corps looks to have some good depth to it behind presumed starters Zack Baun and Jihaad Campbell . Jeremiah Trotter Jr . has enjoyed a strong camp. He put himself in perfect position to extinguish a Saquon Barkley toss run. DC Vic Fangio also told reporters not to "sleep" on veteran Chance Campbell when putting together their "lists," seemingly referring to the 53-man roster projections. He has looked solid as well. 
 New offensive coordinator Sean Mannion has dialed up a healthy amount of designed runs for Hurts, generally to good results, including one Wednesday with Dallas Goedert as an escort that produced a chunk gain down the left side. Hurts said it's too early to know how those kind of plays will mesh with the new offensive scheme but the bet here is Hurts uses his legs a little more than last season based off what we've seen at camp. 
 

 
 Tuesday, Aug. 4 
 Eagles receivers DeVonta Smith and Makai Lemon both missed practice with hamstring injuries. The team is not expressing any long-term concern with either player. Still, these are meaningful reps -- especially for a rookie. Lemon missed minicamp as well with a hamstring injury. He has served primarily as the starting slot receiver when healthy but hasn't produced many splash moments to date. It's important Jalen Hurts gets as many snaps as possible with his skill players as the offense breaks in a new system in the post A.J. Brown era.

 Other observations:  

 
 Standout right tackle Lane Johnson was absent (excused/not injury related) for the third straight practice. The team declined to provide further details given that it is a personal matter. Rookie Markel Bell received first-team reps in his absence and appeared to hold his own. 
 With a number of starters missing, it wasn't a big surprise the offense sputtered. Penalties made for a clunky, rhythmless practice with few highlights. 
 It's important to note that new plays are being installed in the early portion of camp, so it makes sense why the offensive operation can look rough in spots. It's no coincidence that the offense's breakout day on Monday was a review of plays that had been installed previously. In other words, patience is required. 
 Linebacker Jihaad Campbell had perhaps his strongest showing of the summer. He sliced into the backfield to stifle a pitch to Saquon Barkley . Moments later, he fired in on a blitz and delivered a hit on would-be blocker Tank Bigsby that sent Bigsby flying to the turf. 
 In that same series, DT Byron Young got free on a pass rush, forcing a Cam Jurgens holding penalty. Between Jalen Carter , Jordan Davis , Moro Ojomo , Young and others, the defensive tackle spot appears to be in superb shape. 
 
 
 Monday, Aug. 3 
 Quarterback Jalen Hurts had his best day of camp to date. It started with a deep sideline throw to Dontayvion Wicks followed by a dot to Elijah Moore down the right seam. Hurts lit it up in the red zone, finding DeVonta Smith for a pair of touchdowns before running in for another score moments later, leading to a leaping celebration with Saquon Barkley and other teammates. There was one notable blemish on the day -- a short pass to Moore that was jumped by Quinyon Mitchell for a pick-six -- but the practice was defined by sharp, on-time throws, including one deep over the middle that led to a highlight diving catch by Darius Cooper .

 Other observations: 

 
 Right tackle Lane Johnson (excused/not injury related) was absent for a second straight practice. Rookie receiver Makai Lemon did not participate in team drills after taking part in individual drills earlier in the session. 
 The second-team defense got work against the first-team offense. Credit linebacker Chance Campbell for sniffing out a Barkley run to the outside and darting into the backfield to make a stop.

title: 2026 Pittsburgh Steelers training camp: Latest intel, updates
summary: Follow our daily updates from Steelers training camp, including intel on QBs, position battles and potential breakouts.
full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. The  Pittsburgh Steelers ' camp is taking place in Latrobe, Pennsylvania, and Steelers reporter Brooke Pryor has the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and of course, the quarterbacks room.

 What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at Steelers camp. We will update this file often. How will coach Mike McCarthy shape this roster and the offense in his first year in Pittsburgh? Who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football? And which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Dive in to all the updates and be sure to check back for more information until the first full week of the preseason begins Aug. 13.

 
 Camp updates for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 

 Latest news from Steelers camp 
 
 'Tempered': Inside Mike McCarthy's new vision for Steelers 
 Steelers' Broderick Jones cleared after eight months (neck) 
 Rodgers: 'Zero debate' 2026 will be last season 
 Jalen Ramsey, Joey Porter Jr. placed on PUP list 
 Steelers revamp wide receiver unit 
 Rodgers reunites with family ahead of final NFL season 
 
 
 Friday, Aug. 7 
 Thunderstorms in the area Friday morning forced the Steelers to adjust their practice schedule. Not only did the team close practice to fans because of lightning in the area, but coach Mike McCarthy also pushed the start time to 11:30 a.m. to give the group as much time as possible to decide between holding practice outdoors or moving to the new indoor facility at St. Vincent College.

 The team managed to squeeze in an abbreviated practice outside between storm cells, practicing for an hour and 45 minutes instead of the scheduled 2 hours and 30 minutes. McCarthy cut out some of the individual work, but he still got in all of the preplanned scheme installations.

 "These two practices yesterday and today, they're the most difficult," McCarthy said Friday morning. "You got four installs already in. You can play games with the first four installs, but now you're adding a second, third down package. We put in short yardage yesterday. Today will be the second red zone package that'll go in. We'll also install goal line. We'll do that thud tempo. We'll do some two-minutes today.

 "This is a really good practice. It gives you everything."

 

 More observations: 

 
 The Steelers seemed to get good news on rookie tackle Max Iheanachor after the first-round pick left practice early Thursday. Though Iheanachor missed Friday's practice, McCarthy said he expected Iheanachor back on Monday. 
 McCarthy said he wasn't pleased with Thursday's practice, specifically saying there were too many mental lapses, including the seven pre-snap penalties he counted. Not among them, though, were the chippy moments and heated altercations between players. "I'd be more concerned if we didn't have that," McCarthy said. "So it's part of football. It's part of the game." 
 
 
 Thursday, Aug. 6 
Rookie first-round pick Max Iheanachor left practice after about an hour and didn't return after appearing to suffer an upper-body injury Thursday. The team's medical staff extensively evaluated the offensive tackle's shoulder and neck area on the sideline, and he eventually walked up the hill to the locker room with an athletic trainer.
 Coach Mike McCarthy talks to the media before practice only, so he's expected to give an update on Iheanachor before Friday morning's practice.

 Iheanachor was making significant progress through the early portions of camp before the injury. In the initial preseason depth chart, he was listed as the second-team right tackle. And though McCarthy was quick to tell reporters not to put much stock in the required depth chart, Iheanachor has consistently been working with the second-team offensive line.

 "Max has had a great start," center Zach Frazier said. "Obviously for any rookie coming in, it's a lot. It's just an NFL offense, but every day he's taking steps. He doesn't really make the same mistakes twice. So he's coachable, and I'm really happy with how he's done so far."

 With Iheanachor out, Broderick Jones took the bulk of second-team reps at right tackle. He was inconsistent in the role as he continues to work his way back from season-ending neck surgery. Though he has been cleared to return to all football activities, Jones, who was the team's starting left tackle last season before his injury, is still regaining his strength and getting back his technique.

 

 More observations: 

 
 DT Cameron Heyward appeared to have a veteran day on Thursday, his first of training camp. 
 Tempers flared several times throughout Thursday's practice -- the first full-length practice of training camp. RB Lew Nichols and DB D'Shawn Jamison got into a scuffle, and WR Ben Skowronek and LB Payton Wilson got chippy after Skowronek shoved Patrick Queen in his helmet after a play in a team period. "People are tired, people are sore," Wilson said. "We're just competing. We love each other. Brothers fight all the time. So someone messes up, we getting into it a little bit, then we'll be in here eating lunch in 30 minutes together." 
 Actor Joe Manganiello, a Pittsburgh native, was at training camp practice Thursday, and he brought his little dog with him. 
 
 
 Tuesday, Aug. 4 
 Midway through an individual period of the Steelers' Tuesday practice, the "Monday Night Football" jingle interrupted the Drake song that had been playing over the speakers on the St. Vincent College practice fields.

 The players paused, processing what they were hearing, then dropped everything and ran to the 5-yard line at the other end of the field. Center Zach Frazier snapped the ball as soon as the first-team offense lined up against the first-team defense, kicking off a series of five quick red zone plays.

 The offense scored just once as Mason Rudolph hit Ben Skowronek in the end zone, while the defense got three stops and was flagged for pass interference in the end zone. As soon as those five snaps were over, the DJ resumed playing Drake, and the players went back to their individual drill stations to finish the period.

 That officially marked the first "Mojo Moment" of coach Mike McCarthy's Steelers tenure.

 "I think that period is awesome because it simulates a real game," defensive lineman Sebastian Joseph-Day said. "Down 14-0, what are you going to do? A sudden change, and now you're on your 5-yard line, you got to get a stop. What do you do? And I feel like that is really going to help us prepare for those moments."

 Named for the Austin Powers movie franchise, the surprise drill Mojo Moment is a midpractice pop quiz. It can come at any time, and it's meant to ingrain the importance of staying ready in the players.

 "If you're prepared, then it's an easy test," safety DeShon Elliott said.

 McCarthy did it during practices in Dallas, too. Elliott remembers waiting out a rain delay against the Cowboys a couple of years ago. The Mojo Moment drill would've come in handy then, he said.

 "You got to sit inside a little bit, and then you got to come back out and get started right now," Elliott said. "So I think that's what he was trying to simulate, just being able to go out there and see who can really [tough it out] when it's time to in situations like that."

 

 More observations from the day: 

 
 Cornerback Jamel Dean had an up-and-down practice. He was burned a couple of times, including by Roman Wilson on a slant in the end zone for a score in an 11-on-11 period. On the very next play, DK Metcalf beat him on a quick out for a score, too. But Dean responded with two pass breakups in the practice-ending two-minute drill, each as he guarded Wilson in tight coverage. 
 Elliott is still working his way back from a season-ending knee injury suffered midway through last season, but he plans to ramp up his practice…

title: 2026 Seattle Seahawks training camp: Latest intel, updates
summary: Follow our daily updates from Seahawks training camp, including intel on QBs, position battles and potential breakouts.
full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. The  Seattle Seahawks ' camp is taking place in Renton, Washington, and Seahawks reporter Brady Henderson has the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and of course, the quarterbacks room.

 What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at Seahawks camp. We will update this file often. What is new with the defending Super Bowl champions? Who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football? And which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Dive in to all the updates and be sure to check back for more information until the first full week of the preseason begins Aug. 13.

 
 Camp previews for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 

 Latest news from Seahawks camp 
 
 WR Tory Horton healthy after cracking tibia last season 
 Seattle Pro Bowl DL Williams confirms deal talks 
 Seattle's Nick Emmanwori has ankle surgery, expected to play W1 
 Who are the Khoslas? Meet the family set to buy the Seahawks 
 
 
 Friday, Aug. 7 
 Wide receiver  Cooper Kupp continued his strong training camp with another touchdown Friday, catching a dart in the end zone during an 11-on-11 period.

 The 33-year-old has not looked his age this summer, moving well and appearing routinely in sync with quarterback Sam Darnold as both enter their second season with the Seahawks.

 Which is to say that Kupp still has productive football left. Whenever he does call it a career, though, coach Mike Macdonald has said he has a job on Seattle's staff if he wants it.

 Kupp is already something of a coach, as the first episode of "Hard Knocks" documented. It showed the 10-year veteran sitting in on quarterback meetings as the conduit of information for the receivers. The episode also featured a film session in which Kupp appeared to decipher an Xs and Os conundrum for Macdonald.

 

 "Being in the same room as Cooper Kupp, it helps us all elevate to his level," receiver Rashid Shaheed said Friday. "Not necessarily to his level, because he's so far beyond what you can expect as a receiver because he's like another coach, as 'Hard Knocks' kind of explained.

 "But Cooper's amazing. Just his knowledge of the game, how he breaks things down in meetings, he's so willing to help and that's what we appreciate about him. You obviously see what he does on the field. He's a triple crown winner, Super Bowl champion for a reason. It's just great to have him around."

 More observations: 

 
 The Seahawks will hold their annual practice at Lumen Field on Saturday evening. Macdonald has said the 5:15 p.m. PT start time is meant to give players -- especially the younger ones -- a sense of what it will feel like to play in primetime. Seattle has six games this season starting around that time. 
 Rookie RB  Jadarian Price  did not practice Friday for undisclosed reasons.  
 
 
 Thursday, Aug. 6 
 Dante Fowler Jr . is a newcomer to Seattle's defense, but he was hardly a stranger when he arrived in May on a one-year deal.

 The 12th-year veteran has known defensive tackle Leonard Williams since 2012, when the two Florida natives took part in the Under Armour All-America Game. Fowler played for Aden Durde in Atlanta and Dallas, when Seattle's defensive coordinator was a position coach for the Falcons and Cowboys. In Dallas, Fowler was a teammate of fellow outside linebacker DeMarcus Lawrence , who took him under his wing.

 Lawrence helped sell Fowler on the Super Bowl champions this past offseason. A year earlier, Fowler had discussions with Durde about potentially signing with Seattle before opting for a second stint in Dallas instead.

 "I just respect the man he is," Fowler said Thursday of Durde. "He got it out the mud. He got it out the hard way. He's from London. He's not from here, and his IQ of football is just impressive. I love his passion, his intent of the game, the way he coaches his players, that's what I like the most. He demands something out of his players. He's not just telling them the X's and O's. He's going to demand it out of you."

 As Fowler was lauding Durde, Seahawks players were heading out of the team's indoor practice facility after a walk-through. Williams, Lawrence and a few other defensive linemen stopped to hype Fowler up, forcing him to pause mid-sentence and laugh.

 "See, that's why I'm happy to be here," he said. "Literally, right there."

 The Seahawks are happy to have Fowler as a less expensive -- even if older -- replacement for Boye Mafe as the speedy complement to the power-rushing styles of Lawrence, Uchenna Nwosu and Derick Hall in their outside linebacker rotation. Mafe, 27, ranked 17th among all defenders last season with an 11.4% pressure rate, according to ESPN Research. Fowler, who turned 32 earlier this week, was 31st at 10.3%.

 Fowler had 3.0 sacks in 17 games for Dallas, which was one more than Mafe had in 20 games, including playoffs. Yet Mafe got a three-year, $60 million deal from the Cincinnati Bengals at the start of free agency, and Seattle landed Fowler on a one-year, $2.5 million deal two months later.

 According to a copy of Fowler's contract that was obtained by ESPN, there's another $2.5 million available in incentives tied to regular-season sacks. He would make the highest of the following amounts: $500,000 for 7.0 or more sacks, $1 million for 9.0 or more, or $1.5 million for 11.0 or more. If Seattle plays in the NFC Championship Game, Fowler will make an additional $500,000 for 9.0-plus sacks or $1 million for 11.0-plus sacks.

 

 More observations: 

 
 After three straight days of practicing for nearly three hours outside in the heat, the Seahawks held a 55-minute walk-through indoors, with rest and recovery in mind. 
 Seattle signed FB Brock Lampe and waived rookie TE Lance Mason , the team announced. Lampe went undrafted out of Northern Illinois in 2025 and spent his rookie season on injured reserve with the Patriots, who waived him last month. He adds depth at FB as Robbie Ouzts remains sidelined. Coach Mike Macdonald said earlier this week that the team is trying to gather more info on Ouzts' injury. He didn't disclose what it is, but Ouzts was listed as having a neck injury during the playoffs last season. 
 

 
 Wednesday, Aug. 5 

 What does it mean to be a technician as a pass-catcher?

 Jaxon Smith-Njigba provided a few examples during an almost-unstoppable performance Wednesday.

 In one early period, as a deep ball from Sam Darnold was on its descent, the NFL's reigning receiving champion and AP Offensive Player of the Year deked an in-phase cornerback by momentarily gearing down, creating enough last-second separation to haul in the pass uncontested. On a later touchdown catch, the Seahawks' new $168.6 million man slow-played his release on a wheel route from the slot, perfectly timing the traffic before accelerating into a void between the corner and safety. He found the end zone again on a quick slant at the goal line.

 Whether he actually did make another highlight-reel grab while falling out of bounds was in question. An official called it incomplete before coach Mike Macdonald overruled him.

 Either way, Seattle's 10th practice of camp was JSN's best.

 "It was great to see him come alive," Macdonald said. "Some of those in high-leverage situations, too. ... There's defensive attention on where he's at at all times, too, so for him to be able to make those plays, it's great for the Seahawks, great for him."

 Smith-Njigba made this kind of dominance almost routine last season on his way to a league-high and franchise-record 1,793 receiving yards, which was the eighth-highest total in NFL history. That was with Klint Kubiak calling the offensive shots. Now it's up to new coordinator Brian Fleury, a first-time playcaller, to find the best way to utilize Seattle's star receiver.

 "He can get open…

title: 2026 Tampa Bay Buccaneers training camp: Latest intel, updates

full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. The  Tampa Bay Buccaneers ' camp is taking place at the Advent Health Training Center in Tampa, Florida, and Buccaneers reporter Jenna Laine has the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and of course the quarterback room.

 What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at Bucs camp. We will update this file often. We are looking at who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football, and which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Dive in to all the updates and be sure to check back for more information until the first full week of the preseason begins Aug. 13.

 
 Camp updates for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 

 Latest new s from Bucs camp 
 
 Bucs GM Licht: 'No plans' for Vea trade, Mayfield still franchise QB 
 Mayfield felt 'disrespected' and 'undervalued' by contract offers 
 History says Vea, Mayfield will play with Bucs this season 
 Vea requests trade from Bucs after stalled talks 
 2026 Bucs training camp preview 
 
 

 

 Friday, Aug. 7 

 Quarterback Baker Mayfield connected with tight end Cade Otton on a slant route for a touchdown during a red-zone period. Meanwhile, cornerback Zyon McCollum intercepted Mayfield on a pass intended for Emeka Egbuka during the two-minute drill.

 That's the kind of back and forth that coach Todd Bowles has coveted after the defense had a dominant day Thursday.

 "I thought the offense started out very well," Bowles said. "I thought it was a lot more give and take today than it was yesterday. The energy was there and the intent was there. We still have some things to clean up. I think both sides made plays. One period, the offense won, one period, the defense won. There was a lot of back and forth, which is what you want to see, trying to make each other better."

 Other observations: 

 
 Starting left tackle Tristan Wirfs still isn't practicing due to a hamstring injury. Bowles added, "If he's healthy, we'd like to work him back in. It doesn't matter how much. We're not just going to throw him in there and give him a whole bunch of reps, but we'll see how he looks in individual [periods]." 
 Running back Kenny Gainwell was excused from Friday's practice because of personal reasons, according to Bowles, as was the case for offensive coordinator Zac Robinson. Bowles said both would be back at practice Sunday as the team has Saturday off. 
 Rookie guard  Billy Schrauth  missed practice as well, with Bowles saying he's "kind of banged up" and "I don't know how long he'll be sidelined, but he should miss a few days." 
 

 

 Thursday, Aug. 6 

 After going three straight days inside the indoor practice facility and having a rest day Wednesday, the Bucs returned outdoors.

 Quarterback  Baker Mayfield  felt the heat from the sun and from the defense, as the pressure got to him several times, and he was flushed from the pocket and forced to throw the ball away as he couldn't find any downfield options because of tight coverage by the secondary. And he was also picked off.

 Backup linebacker John Bullock jumped a route on a pass intended for tight end Cade Otton and returned the interception for a touchdown. Rookie inside linebacker Josiah Trotter , who has made his presence known now that the pads are on, immediately drilled Otton after catching a short pass from Mayfield. Overall, it wasn't a great day for Mayfield and the tight ends, with rookie Keionte Scott breaking up a Mayfield pass intended for Payne Durham .

 Rookie cornerback Ayden Garnes had a pass breakup on a Mayfield ball intended for rookie wide receiver  Ted Hurst III  along the right sideline. Rookie Rueben Bain Jr . also blew up a screen pass to running back Bucky Irving .

 Other observations: 

 
 Outside linebacker David Walker Jr., who missed his rookie season last year with a torn ACL, had a strip sack of backup quarterback Jake Browning and made the recovery at the end of practice. Walker has had a sack just about every practice. "We didn't get to see him in pads last year, but to see him out there and the way he moves -- he moves like an inside backer, but he plays like an outside backer and he's got great power," coach Todd Bowles said. 
 Wide receiver  Dean Patterson  hauled in an impressive deep ball catch working against cornerback Josh Hayes . 
 Wide receivers Emeka Egbuka (soreness) and  Chris Godwin Jr . (rest day on Tuesday), were back in action. Defensive tackle  A'Shawn Robinson  (rest day on Tuesday) and safety Miles Killebrew (knee) were all back practicing. Cornerback Benjamin Morrison (hamstring) was doing individual drills. 
 Wide receivers Jalen McMillan (knee), Tez Johnson (groin) and David Sills V (knee) were not practicing. Inside linebacker Alex Anzalone also sat out with soreness. The status of nose tackle Vita Vea (back) and left tackle Tristan Wirfs (hamstring) are unchanged. 
 Bucs' 12-time captain and future Ring of Honor member Lavonte David, who retired this spring, surprised teammates by coming out to practice. Also in attendance was former Bucs Super Bowl-winning head coach Jon Gruden, who will call the Bucs' second preseason game against the Kansas City Chiefs on Aug. 22. 
 

 

 Tuesday, Aug. 4 

 Tempers flared as the Bucs put on pads for the second straight day -- this time at their annual night practice. Rookie inside linebacker Josiah Trotter , the Bucs' second-round draft pick and son of NFL great Jeremiah Trotter, had multiple tackles for a loss during Monday's first padded practice. He followed that up with a tackle for a loss during 11-on-11s Tuesday.

 Trotter could be seen jawing with starting right guard Cody Mauch , starting left guard Ben Bredeson , starting right tackle Luke Goedeke and backup swing tackle Justin Skule . Fellow inside linebacker Alex Anzalone had to restrain Trotter as he took him to the sideline. Anzalone could also be seen pointing at the offensive line and chirping as they huddled up, appearing to support his younger teammate and directing everyone to get back to work.

 While coach Todd Bowles stopped practice to address the team, he praised the 21-year-old challenging for the starting MIKE role. "He had a heck of a day yesterday and he buckled some guys," Bowles said. "If they start playing like that yesterday, he shouldn't need the extra energy today. He's probably a guy you really don't want to mess with either."

 He added, "Once you put your helmet on and you go on the field, all is fair game as long as you're doing it the right way. He plays with the right temperament and he plays the right way."

 Other observations:  

 
 During one-on-one drills, rookie outside linebacker Rueben Bain Jr . used a nasty hand swipe to blow by starting right tackle Luke Goedeke , drawing gasps from fans in attendance. Mind you, Goedeke is no slouch and is making $22.5 million a year. Bain also had what would have been a sack of quarterback Jake Browning . 
 Rookie wide receiver Ted Hurst III hauled in a Baker Mayfield red zone touchdown in the corner of the end zone with Zyon McCollum in tight coverage. Defensive tackle Calijah Kancey came flying at Mayfield on that play however, and it would have very likely been a sack. Still, it was good work for Hurst, who also caught a 20-yard pass downfield from Mayfield. 
 Wide receiver Tez Johnson left the practice field early to get treatment for what Bowles said was a groin injury that he sustained while running. Wide receiver David Sills V also left practice early, but Bowles did not have specifics immediately after practice. He was, however, seen with an ice pack on his knee.

title: Bucs RB Bucky Irving delivers message to haters ahead of Year 3
summary: Tampa Bay's third-year back said "I've been doubted my whole life."
full_text:
TAMPA, Fla. -- Tampa Bay Buccaneers running back Bucky Irving  has a message for any doubters as he heads into Year 3: "I've been doubted my whole life."

 The 5-foot-10, 195-pound running back from the south side of Chicago is coming off a season in which he averaged just 3.4 yards per carry, and he missed seven games because of shoulder and foot issues. That was after Irving enjoyed a breakout rookie year, when his yards per carry were at 5.4. 

 "I've always been told I'm too small, I'm not fast enough," Irving said. "Things like that -- it motivates me and gives me an edge when I step on the field."

 

 The doubters were there ahead of the Bucs selecting Irving in the fourth round of the 2024 draft after he ran a 4.55-second time in the 40-yard dash at the combine -- tied for 14th among running backs. And they were they when he posted a 29.5-inch vertical, the lowest among running backs.

 He answered them by rushing for 1,122 yards and eight rushing touchdowns as a rookie. And he added 392 receiving yards while helping the Bucs win the NFC South.

 Now he's looking to recapture that form since getting a clean bill of health after offseason shoulder surgery and being a full participant in training camp.

 New offensive coordinator Zac Robinson, who spent the last two seasons in the same capacity with the Atlanta Falcons , called him a "stud" and said he's an "explosive play waiting to happen." That should bode well for an OC known for getting his backs into space.

 "Bucky has been great," Robinson said. "Obviously, the talent speaks for itself. The way he runs the football, his feet are always in the ground, so he's always able to change direction and, obviously, that keeps him so balanced to be able to break tackles. The versatility he has in the pass game and the run game -- he's done a great job. It's been a blast seeing him cut some of these runs and you start seeing it."

 

 The team is moving back towards a more wide zone run scheme, in which offensive linemen move laterally to stretch the defense and the running back must read the block and cut vertically, which suits Irving's one-cut running ability well.

 The Bucs did a lot of that during Irving's rookie season under then-offensive coordinator Liam Coen, before moving away from it last year under Josh Grizzard -- who utilized more power and duo blocking schemes, as well as inside zone.

 They've also added  Kenny Gainwell , the Pittsburgh Steelers ' offensive MVP last year, who matches Irving's skill set while adding some unique attributes of his own. Sean Tucker rounds out the group with a downhill running style and was also used at the goal line last year.

 "I think I'm a big guy in between the tackles, Bucky is a spread-out guy, and both of us do basically the same thing when we get ready to run routes and stuff," said Gainwell, who's listed at 5-foot-9, 200 pounds. "So, I mean, it's just different sizes [and] body types, but at the same time we both have to be ready for what is to come and go out there and attack it."

 The Bucs have some Pony packages where the two could line up together. It was something they utilized under Coen with great success, back when they had Rachaad White paired with Irving.

 

 "I think it's a great thing getting both of us out there, and, you know, him being back balling," Gainwell said. "I'm super excited to see him back on the field. I think it's just great to see us both out there on the field at the same time -- I love it."

 Irving has welcomed the new addition, citing "just having a leader like that in our room" being one of the main benefits.

 "Kenny is an even better person, we all know what he can do on the field," Irving said. "... He's been around some great backs, so just being able to sync up that knowledge. I always say, 'man, it's always good to have two good backs in the room.' We complement one another and [we'll] see how far this thing goes."

 As for Irving personally, he said he was able to grow a lot as a person in his time away from football this year, and it's brought him a different perspective that he believes will translate into his on-field performance.

 "I learned a lot about myself," Irving said. "What this game means to me, I've been doing this since I was 4 years old, and [it was my] first time being hurt. Being able to also know you [are] more than just a football player and just being able to self reflect on things that you can learn outside of football. Just being able to be around my team and know the joy [that] they bring when you [are] around them ... just being able to know adversity is going to come at some point.

 "At the end of the day, it's going to determine how you come out of that. It's going to make you stronger."

title: 2026 Tennessee Titans training camp: Latest intel, updates
summary: Follow our daily updates from Titans training camp, including intel on QBs, position battles and potential breakouts.
full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. The Tennessee Titans ' camp is taking place at the Vanderbilt Health Football Center, and Titans reporter Turron Davenport has the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and of course the quarterback room.

 What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at Titans camp. We will update this file often. We are looking at who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football, and which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Dive in to all the updates and be sure to check back for more information until the first full week of the preseason begins Aug. 13.

 
 Camp updates for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 

 Latest Titans news: 

 
 Extension makes Peter Skoronski NFL's top-paid guard 
 Titans DT Jeffery Simmons throws punch, sent to side field 
 Will Levis: There aren't 32 QBs better than me 
 Titans WRs join Cam Ward in Miami to build chemistry 
 

 

 Thursday, Aug. 6 

 The Titans returned to the field after not practicing Wednesday. The pace was noticeably slower to start, but it livened up during team period.

 The offensive line continues to shuffle, especially along the interior, where Cordell Volson and Jackson Slater are the top contenders for right guard while Austin Schlottmann , Pat Coogan and Andre James are battling for the starting center spot.

 All five players have gotten first-team reps in different tandems. Schlottmann has enjoyed going against Jeffery Simmons during team period because "he's one of the best, if not the best interior defenders in the league." Coach Robert Saleh said they're not close to deciding who will start at this point but expects to be closer to a decision leading into the third preseason game.

 Other observations: 

 
 WR  Elic Ayomanor continues to have a solid camp. He caught a deep pass from Cam Ward on a go route in red zone team period to even the score with Alontae Taylor who broke up a pass on the same route earlier in practice. Ward went to Ayomanor again, but the pass fell incomplete. Ayomanor collided with S  Kevin Winston Jr . as they went up for the pass in what Saleh described as a "bang, bang" play. Ayomanor got up favoring his left shoulder after being down for a bit. He went inside for further evaluation. 
 Left tackle  Dan Moore Jr . returned to practice after leaving team period and walking into the building on his own with a trainer Tuesday. Moore took part in team period and got into a small pushing match with linebacker Cody Barton after one of the plays. 
 JC Latham came out during team period towards the end of practice after taking three reps. Reserve tackle Austin Deculus came on in Latham's place and stayed in when the next group of linemen came in. Latham returned for the final team period and had a couple nice blocks on run plays. 
 The Titans will host a Blue/White scrimmage at Nissan Stadium on Friday night. "We'll play move the ball," Saleh said after practice. "We'll play special teams and it'll flow like a game where you'll see first offense against first defense. We have a full scoring system to make it competitive and as game-like as possible. We'll try to get to like 90 plays." 
 

 

 Tuesday, Aug. 4 

 The middle linebacker competition is heating up. James Williams Sr . has strung three consecutive standout days.

 Williams said he's lost about 20 pounds this offseason. The converted safety looked like a defensive back on a jumping one-handed interception of a Mitchell Trubisky pass during team period. Williams got a pass breakup later in practice when Trubisky went to tight end  Kylen Granson  on an out-breaking route.

 Titans defensive coordinator Gus Bradley spoke glowingly of Williams before practice.

 "We like those guys that have played safety in their career and move them down the linebacker," Bradley said. "That pass coverage part of it, that safety background that he has, I think allows him to be a little bit more instinctive."

 Williams worked alongside rookie linebacker Anthony Hill Jr . mostly. Hill added a couple of interceptions as well, both off Trubisky. One of the interceptions came because Trubisky hit his hand on an offensive lineman's helmet.

 Other observations:  

 
 DT  Jeffery Simmons and OL  Austin Schlottmann with some extracurricular after a play. Simmons swung at  JC Latham in the scrum before Tanzel Smart grabbed Simmons. Coach Robert Saleh didn't like it. Stopped practice and gathered the group for a cool-down talk. Simmons was forced to work on a side field with Brian Bell (strength coach) and wasn't allowed to return to practice. 
 QB  Cam Ward connected with WR  Carnell Tate on a beautiful pass for the play of the day. Tate ran a post and Ward launched a deep pass that traveled at least 50 yards in the air. Tate showed explosiveness as he pulled away from Alontae Taylor to run down the ball for the touchdown. 
 One-on-ones were a little different for WRs/DBs under Saleh. It's more like seven-on-sevens but only allowing man defense. Saleh said he uses this format to facilitate more authentic route running instead of the unreasonably long-developing routes. The offensive line versus defensive line setup was the same as normal. 
 Backup QB  Will Levis and WR  Bryce Oliver connected on two deep passes. Levis worked a play-action pass to Oliver on a deep crossing route. Oliver caught the pass in between the safety and cornerback Keydrain Calligan . Oliver made a jumping catch on a go route from Levis later in the day. 
 LT  Dan Moore Jr . left practice during the second team period. Saleh acknowledged after practice that Moore was hurt, but he didn't have any specifics regarding the injury immediately after practice. 
 

 

 Monday, Aug. 3 

 The first day of pads had a really good pace and tempo. Both the offense and defense did a good job keeping each other off the ground for the most part.

 The defense had big hits from cornerback Nazeeh Johnson and linebacker Sean Brown , and quarterback  Cam Ward had two hiccups throwing across his body while rolling out -- resulting in interceptions.

 Coach Robert Saleh said the throws across the body are non-negotiable, especially the shallow ones. Safety  Amani Hooker came up with the first interception as a result of what Saleh said was a "poor decision" by Ward. Saleh called the second interception an elite play by defensive lineman  Jermaine Johnson II .

 Ward did have a couple of nice spot throws to  Wan'Dale Robinson  between defenders during team period. He also connected with veteran receiver Calvin Ridley on a well-placed pass to towards the sideline.

 Other observations:  

 
 WR  Elic Ayomanor continues to have a solid camp. He beat Micah Robinson at the line of scrimmage and caught a deep pass in the end zone from  Mitchell Trubisky . The two almost connected on another deep pass but Robinson was called for pass interference. Ayomanor caught a pass on a deep in-breaking route from Ward also. Saleh credited Ayomanor for the offseason preparation and confidence he's playing with. 
 Defensive line coach Aaron Whitecotton didn't like the lack of intensity during individual period, so he made the group do pushups. The defensive line goes nonstop during that period. Whitecotton has them do a lot of work on the sled and with bags but at a very fast pace. 
 JC Latham took part in the first team period but worked with a trainer on the third field for the remaining ones. Latham's absence allowed Brandon Crenshaw-Dickson to get some valuable reps as he competes with Austin Deculus for the swing tackle spot. 
 
 

 

 Saturday, Aug.1  
 The Titans hosted fans at training camp for the first time this summer, and they got to see a pretty solid day from quarterback  Cam Ward .

 Ward and Elic Ayomanor connected on a couple of deep passes along the sideline. It's clear Ward…

title: 2026 Washington Commanders training camp: Latest intel, updates
summary: Follow our daily updates from Commanders training camp, including intel on QBs, position battles and potential breakouts.
full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. The Washington Commanders camp is taking place in Ashburn, Virginia, and Commanders reporter John Keim has the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and of course the quarterback room.

 What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at Commanders camp. We will update this file often. Can Washington bounce back from an injury-plagued 2025 season? Who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football? And which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Dive in to all the updates and be sure to check back for more information until the first full week of the preseason begins Aug. 13.

 
 Camp updates for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 

 Latest news from Commanders camp 
 
 Stefon Diggs settles in with Commanders, ups NFL best talk 
 Daniels finds voice, aims to fill leadership void 
 Commanders tab ex-All-Pro WR Wes Welker to coach tight ends 
 
 

 Friday, Aug. 7 

 The Commanders not only introduced a new receiver in Stefon Diggs on Friday, they also welcomed back three key players.

 Corner Trey Amos and defensive end/linebacker Dorance Armstrong were activated off the physically unable to perform list while punter Tress Way was removed from the non-football illness list.

 Amos practiced in full Friday, taking reps with the first group -- he started the first 10 games last season before fracturing his right fibula. He also was dealing with a soft-tissue issue before camp, which is why general manager Adam Peters said they wanted to be "overly cautious."

 Armstrong tore his ACL in Week 7; he posted 5.5 sacks in his first six games. He will participate in individual drills and slowly work his way back into full-team work. He'll play outside linebacker in their base defense and can rush as an end in nickel situations.

 Way, Washington's longest-tenured player, suffered a pectoral injury in the offseason. He's coming off his third Pro Bowl season.

 More observations: 

 
 During a one-on-one drill, receiver Terry McLaurin showed his footwork and hands against corner Rasul Douglas . The play also highlighted Jayden Daniels ' accuracy and their chemistry. McLaurin appeared to be running a fade, but Daniels read the coverage and threw a back-shoulder -- McLaurin quickly adjusted his body and made the catch. However, there would have been strong debate about whether he got both feet in bounds. There might have been a centimeter. 
 Diggs dropped the one pass thrown his way in full-team work, a slant route. Diggs has been credited with two drops in his last 166 targets. 
 Undrafted free agent kicker Drew Stevens continues to have a consistent camp. He made all five of his field goal attempts while Jake Moody missed wide left on two of his -- both were wobbly balls. Moody missed three kicks in practice Wednesday compared to one for Stevens. 
 

 

 Wednesday, Aug. 5 

 Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels has continued to grow more comfortable in their new offense -- and it's showing on the field. He had a strong day Tuesday and another solid one Wednesday.

 He wasn't alone, as backup Marcus Mariota also had a strong day, particularly in the red zone.

 Daniels showcased his dynamic ability in a red-zone drill. There was pressure inside, but he extended the play to his right and connected with receiver Jaylin Lane for a score. Later, in 7-on-7 work, Daniels hit wide receiver  Luke McCaffrey in the back of the end zone, despite good coverage by Mike Sainristil .

 Coaches have said Daniels' growing comfort level can be heard by how he's directing receivers at the line -- focusing on the details of their splits -- or in how he'll remind the center about the snap count as they approach the line.

 All of this is what running back Rachaad White expected when he reunited with Daniels, a teammate for two years at Arizona State.

 "Why I think he's the best quarterback I played with, it's the way he moves, the way he has poise," said White, who played with Tom Brady and Baker Mayfield in Tampa. "Not a lot of guys can do it as well. I've seen him come through in the clutch so many times for us and it was the same in his rookie year. When you've got a guy like that out there and he's so talented and the way he attacks the game, you'll be in every game."

 More observations: 

 
 Guard Sam Cosmi and tackle Laremy Tunsil both returned to practice after sitting out Tuesday. But two defensive players sat out today: linebacker K'Lavon Chaisson and corner Amik Robertson . Last season Washington gave a number of vets planned rest days in camp but they're not doing that this season. However, Quinn will give players recovery days when needed and the previous two practices had been two hours long and intense. 
 Linebacker Sonny Styles closed practice with a hard pop of running back Jacory Croskey-Merritt in a goal-line drill. The defensive players celebrated as if they had just saved a game. One day earlier, defensive lineman Javon Kinlaw said of Styles, "He's coming downhill and he's bringing thump with it. He ain't getting danced out of the hole. You love to see that; he ain't losing his ground on contact." 
 Washington's corners and receivers competed in one-on-one drills Wednesday. On one play, Sainristil faced Terry McLaurin , who beat him off the line -- Sainristil was then flagged for holding after grabbing him. McLaurin still made the catch 
 Mariota had a nice play in the red zone. He fooled the defense with a quick fake pump to an out and then found Nick Nash in the back of the end zone. The fake helped create the opening. 
 Offensive coordinator David Blough likes to call trick plays every practice -- and a variety of them as well. They ran another Wednesday -- media is not allowed to describe the plays -- that worked for a score. Don't be surprised if they become a part of each game. 
 

 

 Tuesday, Aug. 4 

 Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels continues to remind anyone watching practice of what he can do as a passer. Just in case last season caused anyone to forget.

 Daniels, who played in only four full games last year because of injuries, has looked sharp throughout the first week of training camp and Tuesday was no exception.

 Among the highlights:

 
 A deep out to receiver Terry McLaurin in which Daniels threw in rhythm for a nice completion. 
 He extended a play to his right, then threw back to the middle for tight end Ben Sinnott . Daniels kept his eyes upfield and, despite throwing back toward the middle, did not put the ball in danger and Sinnott caught the ball as he slid. 
 Two plays later he threw a perfect ball over a defender to Jaylin Lane , running a post route on the left side. The 5-foot-10 Lane needed to leap to finish the catch, but he jumped too soon and dropped the pass. 
 Daniels found receiver Luke McCaffrey running down the middle of the field for another long completion. A corner was covering McCaffrey and a safety closed fast, but the ball was delivered into the tight window. 
 

 Overall, Daniels, the NFC offensive rookie of the year in 2024, has looked sharp in camp.

 "With him, it's really easy," tight end Chig Okonkwo said. "You just got to be where you're supposed to be and he'll find you with that, with the accurate ball."

 

 Other observations: 

 
 Undrafted free agent Drew Stevens , battling Jake Moody for the placekicking job, has had a good camp thus far. On Tuesday, Stevens made all five of his field goals, ranging from 33-56 yards, while Moody missed two of those attempts. Moody missed from 49 and 56 yards. He also missed from 48 yards to cap one full-team drill, while Stevens didn't miss any of his three attempts to punctuate a series. 
 Right guard Sam Cosmi and left tackle Laremy Tunsil did not practice Tuesday. After a two-hour practice in pads Monday, it was considered a recovery…
